title: 'This is our homeland': Netanyahu responds to Obama accusations that Israel stole Palestinian land
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu responded on Friday to comments made by former US president Barack Obama, in which he accused Israel of taking "land off people" and being "excessive," referring to Israel's treatment of the Palestinian people throughout the country's history.Obama made the comments during a visit to Belfast, Northern Ireland, on Tuesday."The Jewish people are not foreign occupiers in the land of our forefathers," Netanyahu said in a video posted to X/Twitter. "Our history is not a colonial enterprise. Our land is not stolen land. This is our homeland."The Jewish people's right to their own state in their ancestral homeland is non-negotiable. Watch: https://t.co/uMWfObAMaJ— Benjamin Netanyahu - בנימין נתניהו (@netanyahu) October 16, 2026Netanyahu called Obama's Belfast comments a "regrettable statement," emphasizing the connection between the Jewish people and the Land of Israel, noting its biblical name, "Judea.""That's where Jews come from," he said. "And we've been attached to it for thousands of years."The prime minister differentiated Israel from European nations with colonial pasts, saying that the Jews in Israel are not "the Dutch in Indonesia... the Belgians in the Congo, we're Jews in Judea."Obstacle to peace lies with Israel's, America's enemies, Netanyahu saysRegarding the path to a peace agreement, Netanyahu said that the obstacle to peace is not Israel, but rather the enemies in the region shared by Israel and the United States.Specifically, Netanyahu noted the enemies' "refusal to recognize the Jewish people's right to a state of our own, in any boundary."He cited chants of "Death to Israel" and "Death to America," which are common in states like Iran, a shared enemy of the US and Israel."We are the 'Little Satan,' you are the 'Great Satan,'" he said, referencing how such states often refer to Israel and the US, respectively, saying that both countries are "defending our common civilization.""A peace built on illusions will crash against the rocks of Middle Eastern reality," said Netanyahu. "Israel will not gamble with its survival to accommodate those who refuse to accept the facts of history, to accept our right to exist, or who wish to appease terror."We certainly do not; we never will," he concluded.Obama: Palestinians 'understandably' want their 'land back'Obama's comments on Tuesday, made in a conversation with journalist Susan McKay, referred to the Palestinians' reaction to the Jewish people's exerting cultural and military control over the State of Israel by explaining that "those people understandably said, 'This is injustice, and I want my land back.'""The fact is that the Jewish people, for millennia, were oppressed, discriminated against, killed," said Obama at the time. "Europe was responsible for much of it. They understandably sought a refuge.""If the attitude of Israel is, now that we are the strongest, the most technologically advanced in the region, then our security will depend on us simply doing whatever we need and taking whatever we want, and not making any concessions to anyone," he added. "That may work short-term... but you have ceded moral ground if that is the position you take."Obama did introduce nuance into the conversation, according to The Irish Times, saying that the millions of Jews and Palestinians in the region "aren't going anywhere.""The citizenry of Israel has to rethink, to reimagine, how your children and grandchildren are going to live in this region," he said. "Are you just going to be behind walls and wipe out everybody around you, or are you going to find some just way of defending yourself while still acting in an ethical, moral way?"Obama added that the Palestinians must come to understand that they will not "outkill" or "outweaponize the Israelis.""We have to look to other examples of how change comes about," he said, pointing toward "nonviolent strategies." "That's going to take some time."

title: Founder of Indian opposition 'Cockroach Janta Party' group, Dipke, detained ahead of protest
body: Police arrested Indian "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke, according to several media reports on Saturday, after he was detained on Friday ahead of a Delhi rally that drew hundreds of people waving the national flag and demanding the resignation of India's election chief.Broadcasters NDTV and India Today said Dipke was arrested to prevent a breach of the peace and will be called before a Special Executive Magistrate on Saturday.Delhi police did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.The youth-led 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), opposition groups, and student organizations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a voter-list revision that critics say favors Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision, but the Election Commission has denied favoring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enroll. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.Student activist: 'Please, spare the people of India'Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday."Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.Dipke was detained on Friday as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument.Dipke called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.The group and left-wing student organizations had urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.Police officers earlier detained Dipke as he left a houseThe live video on CJP's Instagram handle showed Dipke coming out of a house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, hauled him into a police car and drove away."We are detaining you right now," a police officer could be heard telling Dipke."I have not broken any law right now...how can you detain me?" Dipke asked the police officers as he was taken away.There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention.Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges Modi and the BJP have faced in the prime minister's 12 years in power.A weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the movement earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign over exam paper leaks.

title: Trump press secretary Zacharia admits failing bar exam amid questions about claims she is attorney
body: New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was "let go" from the role, a White House official said on Friday, after US President Donald Trump said he had told her to reconsider the job following public scrutiny."I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters while departing the White House."I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it," he added. "But I would reconsider."Trump said on Friday he is in no rush to name a new press secretary to replace Katie Zacharia, Fox News reported.Fox News, citing a White House official, later reported that Zacharia was "transitioning" out of the role of press secretary. Zacharia started the job on Monday and held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday.Zacharia admits to failing bar exam, not being an attorneyZacharia admitted that she hadn't passed the California bar exam during an interview with Fox News's Sean Hannity on Thursday night. This interview was her first direct confirmation since her credentials came under scrutiny in the last few days.Zacharia's credentials came under question after The Washington Post reported that she had never passed the bar exam in any of the states she lived in, meaning that she is not legally allowed to practice law and is therefore neither an attorney nor a lawyer.Searches of attorney directories in California, Texas, and Washington, DC, under both Zacharia's married and maiden name produced no listings.The Jerusalem Post found that her LinkedIn profile states she earned a Juris Doctor degree, meaning she is not licensed to practice law."You went to Pepperdine Law School, but you did not pass the bar exam, correct?" Hannity asked her."Correct," Zacharia responded, admitting that she wasn't a licensed attorney. Lawyer vs attorney, what distinction is Zacharia drawing?Hannity followed up by asking, "You said you consulted with people who advised you it was okay to call yourself a lawyer but not an attorney, correct?" Zacharia confirmed that was accurate."There's a report out tonight showing 15 social media posts where you identify yourself as an attorney," Hannity said, but Zacharia tried to brush it away, saying that those posts are "just retweets," and adding that she "corrected the record" and "was not endorsing the title." Katie Zacharia crashes and burns on [checks notes] Hannity  If you had the "over" on Zacharia lasting more than one Scaramucci, her epic flame out on Hannity just now won't help your cause HANNITY: You said you consulted with people who advised you it was okay to call yourself a lawyer but not an attorney, correct? ZACHARIA: Correct HANNITY: There's a report out tonight showing 15 social media posts where you identify yourself as an attorney ZACHARIA: I think they were retweets Here's the whole interview:— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 16, 2026Although Zacharia has never practiced or been licensed to practice law in the US, the Post found that she worked as an associate on the international practice team at the Chinese law firm Zhong Lun from 2011-2013. The Washington Post found that Zacharia would not have been able to take the bar exam in China, as she was not a citizen."Why get into this long drawn-out discussion as to the difference between a lawyer and an attorney, when most people won't see the difference between the two," Hannity asked."When I went to go engage in media, I consulted legal professionals on whether or not I could be labeled a lawyer," Zacharia said. "I wasn't providing legal advice; I was giving a general review of the legal circumstances surrounding it."Trump introduced Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her roleDespite Zacharia's claims that she avoids identifying herself as an attorney, Trump specifically called her an attorney in his message announcing that she would be stepping into the role.“Katie is a distinguished Graduate of Pepperdine University and the Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, an attorney, and a frequent Commentator on outlets, including Fox News and Newsmax,” Trump wrote on Truth Social last week.Journalists pressed Zacharia and Trump for more details about her credentials after Zacharia's first press briefing on Tuesday.The White House did not clarify whether or not she is a licensed, practicing attorney.

title: Heavy security at Oyebanji’s second-term inauguration
body: There was heavy deployment of security personnel around the Ado-Ekiti Pavilion, venue for the second-term inauguration of Gov. Biodun Oyebanji, on Friday. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the security personnel, comprising the Nigeria Police Force and the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps(NSCDC) were seen manning strategic locations around the venue. Some of the law enforcement officers were also stationed at designated locations in Ado-Ekiti metropolis as early as 8:00 a.m, while vehicles were subjected to thorough security checks before being allowed into the pavilion. The venue of the inauguration was filled to capacity by the citizens, including members and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) across the 16 Local Government Areas of the state. Among the dignitaries for the inauguration were Vice-President Kashim Shettima; Senate President, Godswill Akpabio; Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele; former Gov. Kayode Fayemi; Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi; former Gov. Segun Oni; and Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State. Others include Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, Gov. AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara; Chairman of the Progressives Governors’ Forum, Gov. Hope Uzodimma of Imo; Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State; and former Gov. Ayo Fayose. The Police Command in the state had on Friday assured residents of adequate security during the inauguration and urged the citizens to remain calm and be law-abiding. The command’s spokesperson, Sunday Abutu, in a statement said the deployment of adequate number of personnel was aimed at maintaining law and order, as well as ensuring the smooth conduct. NAN reports that Oyebanji was reelected during the June 20 governorship election. (NAN) The post Heavy security at Oyebanji’s second-term inauguration appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian combat aircraft, drones strike Ukrainian UAV control posts
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. The crews of Russian combat aircraft jointly with drone operators of the Rubicon Testing Center of Advanced Unmanned Technologies struck Ukrainian UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) control posts and enemy deployment sites in the special military operation area, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"The Defense Ministry of Russia has released video footage of joint combat operations by teams of the Rubicon Center and crews of aircraft of the Russian Aerospace Forces for striking UAV control posts and temporary deployment sites of enemy formations in the special military operation area," the ministry said in a statement.
Rubicon teams confirmed by reconnaissance drones that all the targets had been struck, it said.

Meta’s new terms appear to give it permission to crawl and scrape websites “associated” with the businesses that use its platforms — including online publishers, according to a report from Nieman Lab . The new terms , which go into effect on October 30th, say Meta can use this outside content to “develop, improve, research,” and “train” its AI products.
While Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says that the company is just “consolidating” its commercial and self-serve ad terms, legal experts tell Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” like a site’s robots.txt file . That could potentially allow Meta to bypass a licensing agreement and freely train its AI models on content posted by online publishers.
The new policy applies to business accounts that promote their content across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger:
You authorize us (or any entity acting on our behalf) to use automated software (such as web scrapers, bots, robots, spiders, crawlers, and user agents) and create test credentials to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl the domains, web pages, or URLs (and any content available through them) that are associated with your products or services, or that are made available through your or users’ use of Meta Company Products and services, and to periodically pull updates from such domains, web pages, or URLs. Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.
Roberts pushes back on Nieman Lab ’s reporting, saying “There is no change to how Meta uses web crawlers; any suggestion to the contrary is false… Content owners can still use robots.txt flags to indicate their preferences, as we clearly explain in our developer documentation.” Meta has followed OpenAI in striking AI licensing deals with CNN , Fox News, USA Today , and People Inc., but these terms could give the company access to a much broader swath of content.
“For news publishers, this clearly represents permission to Meta to train AI on any content from their sites and possibly to deploy some of that content, even in competition with the publishers themselves,” James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, tells Nieman Lab .
Andy Stone, Meta’s vice president of communications, writes in a post on X that this change isn’t meant to target news sites. “This update is designed to make sure we’re able to pull accurate information about products for sale on third-party websites when making on-platform ad and content recommendations, not about scraping news sites.”
Businesses that don’t agree to Meta’s new policies “may stop all access or use of our Products for business or commercial purposes,” the terms say. Last month, Meta launched a new Meta One subscription that requires businesses and creators to pay to include links in posts and reels. “Put another way, Meta has begun charging users to post links to the same content that it will be permitted to crawl for free,” Nieman Lab says.
Update, October 16th: Added a statement from Meta and legal commentary.
Update, October 17th : Meta has updated its terms and issued a new statement saying “the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves.” More information can be found in this more recent article .

title: Iran manages to ship some gas, jet fuel despite US blockade, sanctions, data shows
body: Iran has managed to export some liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and jet fuel since July, despite a US naval blockade, shipping intelligence showed and people involved in security said.Tehran has in recent weeks been concealing such cargoes among a growing volume of ship-to-ship transfers by other Gulf producers off Oman, four people in maritime security who track Gulf oil movements told Reuters.The Iranian exports and methodology are reported for the first time here. While a fraction of its former energy exports, the cargoes are rare evidence of petroleum products getting through a blockade that has halted Iran's crude exports.Analysis by US advocacy group United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), which monitors Iran-related tanker traffic using ship and satellite tracking, shows at least eight gas tankers carrying Iranian LPG have left the Gulf of Oman since mid-July.Another tanker carrying Iranian jet fuel reached Myanmar in September, additional satellite imagery and analysis by maritime intelligence group SynMax show.The US imposed targeted sanctions in 2023 on Myanmar's jet-fuel industry, citing military airstrikes on civilians that the United Nations says have killed thousands of people. Myanmar's military government has repeatedly denied targeting civilians, saying its operations are directed against armed groups.Approximately 4.1 million barrels of LPG made it through the blockadeSix of the eight gas tankers and the jet fuel tanker are under US sanctions for transporting Iranian petroleum and petrochemical products, a Reuters analysis of the vessels and sanctions imposed on ships by the US Treasury showed."What we have seen passing is a handful of tankers carrying Iranian LPG, but the overwhelming majority of tankers laden with Iranian products have been redirected by US forces," said Jemima Shelley, senior research analyst with UANI.Shelley said some Iranian LPG tankers transferred cargoes near the Omani coastal towns of Shinas and Sohar, while others waited in the Gulf of Oman before heading past the US blockade, which US Central Command has said sits across the Gulf of Oman near the Iran-Pakistan border.The total amount of these LPG cargoes was estimated at 4.1 million barrels, Shelley said.Shelley said the shipments were driven "more by opportunism" than showing a new trend of Iran trying to export its oil and petrochemicals by using smaller ships.Most of the cargoes sailed to Malaysia's Eastern Outer Port Limits to conduct further STS transfers for likely destinations in China, Shelley said, based on UANI's analysis.The Iranian government did not respond to a request for comment. Myanmar's military-backed government did not respond to a request for comment on whether the country had received Iranian jet fuel.US Military describes blockade as 'ironclad'The US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) said its naval blockade, which was first imposed on Iran-related oil exports on April 13, is "ironclad." The blockade was lifted in June after the US reached a draft understanding with Iran, but it was reimposed on July 14 following the collapse of the agreement.A US military official told Reuters that the passage of a vessel does not necessarily mean it had evaded the blockade. Every ship was assessed individually, including through a review of its papers, and some vessels could be allowed through for humanitarian reasons, the official added.The official said the appearance of a vessel on US sanctions lists is not the only factor to make it subject to the blockade, adding that US forces are also closely monitoring some ships without taking action against them for operational reasons.Centcom said in an update on October 13 that during the three months of the latest blockade, four commercial vessels had been disabled and 135 ships had been turned around by US forces.The US military has turned around ships from Asia and also seized some tankers, previous Centcom statements said.Washington has coupled its blockade with a sanctions campaign aimed at severing Iran's remaining financial links and depriving it of revenue. Last week, it imposed fresh sanctions on 17 vessels involved in transporting Iranian crude, petrochemicals and petroleum products.US Treasury questioned shipping dataA US Treasury spokesperson questioned shipping data suggesting vessels had evaded the blockade, saying ships could spoof their locations or use false identities when loading.Such data "should be taken with a grain of salt," the spokesperson said.The Treasury spokesperson said Operation Economic Outcast, together with the blockade, was "suffocating the Iranian regime."Torbjorn Soltvedt, principal Middle East analyst at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft, said although there was no sign of Washington easing its blockade, worsening economic conditions in Iran could push Tehran to take greater risks."If Iran can move product tankers through, even in small numbers, jet fuel may be a good option. Iran's aviation industry is under increasing pressure from US sanctions, with a growing number of planes grounded, and a potential surplus of jet fuel at Iranian refineries," Soltvedt added.Iranian crude exports fell to zero in September, according to Kpler, the first month without a shipment since the analytics firm began tracking the producer in 2013.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said the blockade prevented most Chinese purchases of Iranian oil and left Iran unable to deliver crude to customers.

title: Northern Bahr el Ghazal moves to collect taxes before polls
body: The caretaker government of South Sudan’s Northern Bahr el Ghazal State will begin collecting annual business taxes and renewing traders’ licences next Monday, ahead of elections scheduled for December, state officials said. The announcement followed a meeting between state officials and business representatives in Aweil to discuss challenges facing traders, including high taxes, business operating conditions and concerns about market prices. Caretaker Minister of Information Dominic Kang Deng said the state governor had directed the finance minister to consult businesspeople on the challenges affecting their operations. Kang said the election schedule had disrupted the usual timetable for renewing traders’ licences and collecting annual taxes, which are normally handled in December. “We met today and discussed tax increases and the challenges facing the private sector to help the people of Northern Bahr el Ghazal State by reducing market prices,” Kang said. He said traders had agreed to renew their licences and pay annual taxes before the elections. Revenue collection would begin next Monday across the state’s five counties and two municipalities, he added. Caretaker Minister of Finance and Investment Garang Yak Kuol said the meeting was part of the government’s annual consultations with traders, but the election timetable had required an adjustment to the revenue collection schedule. “We shall start our revenue collection next Monday and end it in November to leave a gap so that people can access better prices during the festive season as we enter the election period,” Kuol said. He thanked traders for their contribution to the local economy and the livelihoods of Aweil residents, saying they had raised several challenges affecting their businesses. Kuol said the state government would work with the business community to address their concerns and ensure traders’ security during the election period. “The security of businesspeople is paramount, and measures will be put in place to ensure their safety during the election period,” he said. He urged traders to cooperate with the government to support economic growth and maintain reasonable prices for goods. Deng Makol Athian, chairperson of the Northern Bahr el Ghazal State Chamber of Commerce, said traders had agreed to cooperate with the government despite difficulties facing their businesses. He said high taxes were among their main concerns and called for lower rates to help reduce prices for consumers. “We, the business community, have agreed to renew our annual traders’ licences and pay the annual rental taxes to the state government despite the many challenges we are facing. We shall cooperate with the government for the sake of our people,” Athian said. The meeting was attended by the caretaker ministers of Finance and Investment and Information and Communication, the acting mayor of Aweil Town, the Chamber of Commerce chairperson and business representatives from across the state. The post Northern Bahr el Ghazal moves to collect taxes before polls appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones
body: An Xbox controller may be a key part of an unlikely answer to the U.S. military’s struggle with counter-drone defense. As cheap drones proliferate, shooting them down can mean firing multimillion-dollar missiles to destroy aircraft worth just a fraction of that price. The gaming accessory is part of KBR’s Firefly, a mobile high-energy laser weapon system developed by Kord Technologies. Recently, the Pentagon selected the company for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones. The system uses a concentrated beam of light instead of costly missile interceptors, potentially offering a less expensive way to bring down drones. David Zoller Jr., senior director for KBR, said the controller “reduces the amount of time that it takes to train somebody because they already know what that feels like — what all the buttonology is.” The pilot program will place directed-energy weapons at military bases across the country for a yearlong assessment, where service members will operate, maintain and collect data on the weapons. The Pentagon will, in turn, gather information on cost and logistics. KBR subsidiary Kord has marketed Firefly as a palletized mobile laser. The company said the system — part of which looks like a futuristic, modular cell phone camera lens — can operate in temperatures ranging from negative 15 to 35 degrees Celsius. During an August demonstration in Alabama, company officials said that a truck-mounted system needs just a few seconds to down a small drone. Here is how it works: Identify the threat When the radar system detects a potential threat, it sends a cue to the human operator to investigate further. The software also has target list capabilities, so it can help a human identify things that might be threats. The human can use built-in cameras to zoom in on the anomaly — whether that be a bird, plane or drone. The AI capability tracks automatically, but the human behind the joystick makes decisions. The system, Zoller said, “still has a person that decides not just when to fire, but also where to fire.” Engage Once the operator makes the requisite decisions, the system steps in, tracking the threat and aiming the laser at any specific part of the threat. The laser directs “weaponized light” to counter threats by burning a hole through, Zoller said, and can be as specific as aiming at a particular propeller, engine or fuel tank. But Zoller cautions high-energy laser systems are “not a silver bullet.” The Firefly can only engage one threat at a time, so in a drone swarm, the highest threat would need to be prioritized. “As a swarm would come in, I would have multiple systems engaging on the most imminent threat,” he explained.

title: BRADE Supports 400 Students, 17 Teachers in Magbon Segun School Outreach
body: BRADE Group has provided educational materials and classroom resources to 400 students and 17 teachers at Community High School, Magbon Segun, in an initiative aimed at supporting teaching and learning and improving the school environment. The outreach, held on September 24, 2026, featured the distribution of educational materials and customised notebooks to students and teachers, alongside the provision of whiteboards and markers to support instruction across the school’s six classrooms. The initiative formed part of BRADE Group’s 2026 Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) programme, with education identified as a key priority under its Social pillar. Speaking at the event, Dr Kester Awani highlighted the importance of education to the company’s social responsibility agenda, noting that investment in learning helps empower individuals and create opportunities for future growth. He explained that the initiative reflected BRADE’s commitment to supporting host communities through interventions that address practical needs and contribute to sustainable development. The BRADE Group Chairman, Mr Ese Avanoma, delivered a keynote address titled “Learning for a Better Future,” in which he encouraged the students to take their education seriously, embrace continuous learning and recognise education as a pathway to future opportunities. To reinforce the message, the outreach featured an interactive educational quiz based on the keynote address, coordinated by Mr Benjamin Odupitan. A spelling bee competition, facilitated by Ms Happiness Ibeh, also tested students’ literacy skills, encouraged healthy academic competition and provided an opportunity for participants to demonstrate their knowledge. Outstanding participants in the activities were recognised and rewarded for their performances. The initiative was informed by a community needs assessment led by Ms Gbemisola Adeleye, which identified the school’s practical teaching and learning requirements and guided the selection of materials provided. The distribution of classroom resources was coordinated by BRADE Group’s Chief Operations Officer, Mr Robinson Ogholo. The school principal, Mr Aderibigbe Olufemi, expressed appreciation to BRADE Group’s management for responding to the school’s educational needs, describing the intervention as a welcome contribution to the learning environment. He noted that the provision of whiteboards, markers and other educational materials across the school’s six classrooms would support teachers in delivering lessons more effectively and help students engage better with classroom activities. According to him, the donations would provide practical support for teaching and learning while helping to address some of the school’s resource needs. Olufemi thanked the management of BRADE Group for identifying the school as a beneficiary and demonstrating a commitment to educational development through tangible support. He also urged other companies operating within and around the community to emulate the gesture by investing in initiatives that address the needs of schools and other community institutions. He stressed that sustained collaboration between businesses and their host communities could make a meaningful difference in educational development, particularly where schools require additional resources to create conducive learning environments. Speaking on behalf of the students, the school’s Head Boy, Wealth Samuel, thanked BRADE Group’s management for the intervention, noting that the initiative addressed practical needs within the school. He expressed gratitude for the educational materials and classroom resources, saying the donations would support their learning and make classroom activities more engaging. The students also welcomed the opportunity to participate in the quiz and spelling bee competitions, which encouraged them to demonstrate their knowledge, build confidence and appreciate the value of academic excellence. The outreach also featured cultural dances and other engaging activities through which the students entertained the visiting BRADE delegation, adding colour and excitement to the event. The performances provided an opportunity for the students to showcase their talents, celebrate their cultural heritage and interact with the visitors in a lively atmosphere. Through the intervention, BRADE Group combined the provision of educational resources with activities designed to promote literacy, encourage student participation and inspire a stronger interest in learning. The company said it would continue to pursue initiatives aligned with its ESG priorities and core values of integrity, safety, reliability and respect, with a focus on contributing meaningfully to the development of communities in which it operates. The post BRADE Supports 400 Students, 17 Teachers in Magbon Segun School Outreach appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Fiabci-Ghana inaugurated to promote professionalism and global collaboration in real estate sector
body: The International Real Estate Federation (FIABCI), has launched its Ghana Chapter to connect the country’s real estate industry to a global network of professionals, investors and institutions while promoting higher professional standards across the built environment. The ceremony which was under the theme, “Beyond the Individual” also witnessed the inauguration of the Founder and CEO of JL Properties Dr. James Condua Orleans-Lindsay as the Founding President of FIABCI-Ghana. Founded in Paris in 1948, FIABCI is an international business network that brings together professionals from various disciplines within the real estate industry. Its membership spans developers, brokers, architects, engineers, valuers, surveyors, lawyers, financiers, academics, property managers and public-sector institutions. The launch of the Ghana Chapter is therefore expected to strengthen the country’s visibility within the international real estate community and open new avenues for investment, knowledge exchange and professional development. FIABCI-Ghana was jointly established by the Ghana Real Estate Professionals Association and the Ghana Real Estate Developers Association to represent the international federation in Ghana. Delivering his inaugural address, Dr. James Condua Orleans-Lindsay described the formation of FIABCI-Ghana as an important step towards uniting industry stakeholders and connecting Ghana’s real estate sector to global expertise and investment opportunities. According to him, the establishment of FIABCI-Ghana reinforced the growing importance of international collaboration in advancing professional excellence across the built environment. He indicated that the chapter would focus on five principal areas: strengthening advocacy and industry visibility, promoting research and innovation, supporting national development, institutionalising an annual developers’ forum and organising a FIABCI-Ghana International Conference. The chapter, he said would also seek representation on relevant governmental, non-governmental and international boards to ensure that real estate professionals contribute meaningfully to policy formulation and national development. Turning his attention to the country’s housing challenges, Dr. Orleans-Lindsay said the estimated housing shortfall of about 1.8 million units represented only one aspect of a broader challenge requiring coordinated action from the government, private developers, financial institutions and other stakeholders. He called on industry professionals to forge stronger partnerships with the government and relevant institutions to increase housing delivery and improve access to decent and affordable accommodation. “The onus lies on us as industry players to partner the government and all major stakeholders to fill the gap,” he stated. Dr. Orleans-Lindsay, who is also President of the Ghana Real Estate Developers Association, pledged to provide ethical and transformational leadership for the newly established chapter. He cited the redevelopment of the former Achimota dumpsite and quarry into a residential estate as an example of how responsible investment, innovation and efficient land use could transform abandoned spaces and support sustainable urban development. He also pledged that FIABCI-Ghana would pursue strategic partnerships and initiatives that support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and contribute to the transformation of Africa’s housing and real estate landscape. “Our commitment remains steadfast in ensuring the growth and transformation of FIABCI-Ghana and its pivotal role in shaping Africa’s real estate and housing landscape,” he said.

title: Hillel rabbi in Georgia's Emory fired over fiance's Israel criticism, pro-Palestinian posts
body: A rabbi for the Hillel at Georgia's Emory University was fired in August after her fiancé posted criticisms of Israel on social media, the rabbi, Nikki Golomb, told Jewish Currents on Thursday.According to Golomb, she began working at Emory Hillel on July 1 and was fired by the nonprofit that operates Hillels in Georgia on August 3.View this post on InstagramA post shared by Sam Stein (@sam_avraham)“There were no questions, no conversation, nothing about me or my politics or anything I've done,” Golomb said. “It was just about the fact that I am in a relationship with people who are critical of Israel.”Golomb's fiancé, Sam Stein, describes himself as a "protective presence activist and journalist" on Instagram, where he has a substantial following. He posts frequently from the West Bank, including sharing videos of settler violence.“I don't think that Sam's politics are relevant to my job, and they're certainly not relevant to my ability to do the job that they hired me to do,” Golomb said.Before she had been hired, Golomb said that Hillel had told her that Israel and Zionism, and supporting Zionist students, were a major part of the organization and her role in it. "That's something I was prepared to do,” she said, saying that she feels a "deep sense of connection to the land of Israel" despite her fiancé's activism.Hillel concerned Marcus Foundation would pull funding over pro-Palestine postsAccording to Golomb, Hillel's Georgia CEO, Larry Sernovitz, told her that the Marcus Foundation, a major Hillel donor, might cut off its funding if it learned about her engagement to Stein.Golomb also said she was told she would not receive severance pay after her firing.Responding to Jewish Currents inquiries, Sernovitz said that "this employment decision was made in accordance with federal and state law and violated no governmental or organizational policy," adding that the decision had been made "for legitimate, work-related reasons and in accordance with our policies.”Director emeritus of UCLA Hillel, Rabbi Chaim Seidler-Feller, told Jewish Currents that Golomb's firing was "an act of political cancellation and intolerance.”

title: Man Utd have moved on from Martinez outburst, says Carrick
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick insists the club’s squad has moved on from Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club’s hierarchy, saying the defender will be included for Sunday’s Premier League trip to Leeds United. Martinez apologised for the timing of his comments after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, but stood by the substance of his remarks, which questioned the club’s summer investment and singled out director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick said the matter had been addressed and would not distract the team. “He’s released his statement and realised he made a mistake. That’s enough for us to move on with,” Carrick told reporters on Friday. “From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what’s been done is enough to move on.” The United boss rejected suggestions that the episode had damaged the dressing-room atmosphere, despite criticism from former club captains Wayne Rooney, Roy Keane and Gary Neville. “Just because people talk on the outside doesn’t mean that is the truth. I am telling you the truth,” Carrick said. “The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I have seen it for a while.” He added that the players remained united despite the team’s recent results. “We are emotional and care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe you shouldn’t say at that certain time, but it doesn’t distract us from what we are creating here and the environment and spirit within the group,” he said. “It [the squad] is not affected, I am telling you.” Carrick confirmed Martinez would be part of the squad travelling to Elland Road, where United face Leeds on Sunday. The post Man Utd have moved on from Martinez outburst, says Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Timelines for Ukrainian settlement, US interference: Lukashenko’s statements
body:
MINSK, October 16. /TASS/. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko said he is convinced that peace in Ukraine will be achieved either this year or next.
He also said that although the United States considers itself invincible, there are higher powers that "can put the high and the mighty in their place."
TASS has compiled the Belarusian president’s key statements.
Peace in Ukraine will be reached this or next year: "This peace will be achieved. If not this year, then next year. I am absolutely sure of that."
"Russia is stronger, sturdier" and "is able to fight for a long time," but "the economic impact is tremendous": "Who can like and want this? Russians understand this, they are ready for peace."
"If Ukrainians do not agree to a peaceful settlement this year, it will be even more difficult for them next year, and eventually it will become impossible."
Belarus wants the conflict in Ukraine to end as soon as possible and is ready to do its best to help achieve that: "Peace is not only possible but necessary. There will be peace; it will be achieved. We would like the war to end next year, or, even better, this year. We are all for it and will do our best in this regard."
"Various factors are affecting both Russia and Ukraine. But these factors are clearly pushing both Ukraine and Russia toward peace, due to the impossibility of continuing such military operations. For these humanitarian and human reasons, peace is needed there. And it will be achieved."
Vladimir Zelensky once promised to remain in office for one presidential term: "Promises should be kept."
Zelensky must hold a presidential election in Ukraine: "He needs to organize an election."
US President Donald Trump "should not dictate to Ukraine what to do."
The United States considers itself invincible, but there are higher powers that "can put the high and the mighty in their place": "They are all God-loving and devout … And He [God] sees everything and will give them a very hard smack on the head.". That’s why we need to be more careful here. We don’t know for sure, but there are many forces in nature that can put the high and mighty in their place. We must remember that."
Zelensky has become dependent on the United States and Trump: "Why is he [Trump] dictating [Ukraine what to do]? Because Zelensky depends on the United States and Trump. Well, he [Trump] might not well be doing this but first intelligence sharing and then weapons provision to Ukraine - what is badly needed - will be stopped. And maybe, something else, along with weapons."

title: ‘No flying in just for matches’ – Kofi Adams sets conditions for next Black Stars coach
body: Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Iddie Adams has stated that any foreign head coach appointed to lead the Black Stars must be committed to spending substantial time living in Ghana. This follows a disappointing qualifying campaign that saw Ghana suffer a 2–0 defeat to Ivory Coast in Bouaké, followed by a 4–2 loss at home against The Gambia. The results ultimately led to the Ghana Football Association (GFA) and former head coach Carlos Queiroz mutually parting ways. To fill the vacancy, a five-member committee was jointly set up by the GFA and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation to interview candidates and recommend a suitable replacement. Speaking on Citi FM’s Eyewitness News, Adams outlined his key expectations for the next head coach as the search for Queiroz’s successor continues. “In our engagement [with the GFA], we indicated, our coach should also be interested in spending time in Ghana.” “You can’t have a national team coach who visits the country only when the team is coming to play a competition…then you are not a national team coach.” “The coach must spend more time here and maybe go to Europe to also scout there from time to time,” Kofi Adams stated. While the GFA continues its search for a permanent head coach, Black Queens head coach Kim Lars Björkegren is reportedly set to take temporary charge of the team for their upcoming fixtures. He will be assisted by former national team players Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram. The technical team will be tasked with securing Ghana’s first win of the qualifying series when the Black Stars face Somalia in a two-legged tie in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers in November.

title: Israel signs deal for 12 Boeing AH-64E Apache attack helicopters
body:
Israel has signed an agreement with the US government for 12 Boeing AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, introducing the latest version of the type into the Israeli Air Force.
The agreement was signed on October 14 by the Israel Ministry of Defense and the US Department of Defense. Deliveries of the new helicopters are scheduled to begin in the early 2030s.
The acquisition follows US State Department approval in January for a possible Foreign Military Sale to Israel of up to 30 AH-64E helicopters and associated equipment, with an estimated value of US$3.8 billion.
That package included 70 General Electric T700-GE-701D engines, AN/APG-78 Longbow fire-control radars, electronic warfare systems, communications equipment, spare parts, training and logistical support.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The value of the contract for the first 12 helicopters was not disclosed by the Israeli Defense Ministry.
The agreement was concluded after months of discussions over funding and the availability of production positions for the Apache.
According to Israeli media reports, the deadline for completing the acquisition had been extended several times, with Israel facing the possibility that production slots reserved for the country could be allocated to another customer.
The Israeli government approved additional funding shortly before the agreement was signed. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich had opposed the acquisition, arguing that unmanned aircraft could perform some of the missions assigned to attack helicopters at lower cost.
Israel nevertheless decided to proceed with the purchase following operational assessments made after the October 7, 2023 attacks and the subsequent war in Gaza, during which the Israeli Air Force made extensive use of its Apache fleet.
Israel has operated the Apache since 1990, initially receiving the AH-64A, locally known as Peten. The country later acquired the AH-64D Longbow, designated Saraf by the Israeli Air Force.
The fleet currently comprises around 40 helicopters from the two earlier variants. The 12 new aircraft will be Israel's first AH-64Es.
The AH-64E introduces updated avionics, communications and sensors and can exchange information with unmanned aircraft. The configuration approved for Israel also includes Longbow radars and Link 16 tactical data links.
Boeing continues to manufacture the Apache at its facility in Mesa, Arizona. The AH-64E is the current production version of the attack helicopter and is operated or ordered by several countries in addition to the US Army.

title: Romania finally holds Russia responsible for the drone attacks on ships off its coast, and wants a joint NATO command for the Black Sea
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Romania has proposed a joint NATO military command for the Black Sea, as drones hit four merchant ships in 24 hours, three of them off its coast, and its foreign minister said Russia "bears full responsibility." NATO ambassadors will discuss the attacks next week. Russia’s strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have escalated this autumn and reached NATO shores. Drones have attacked at least eight merchant vessels near Romania and Bulgaria since 5 October, two of them inside Romania’s territorial waters. Until now, neither country had named the attacker, and Bulgaria still says it cannot prove who it was. Romania’s patience appears to have run out, and next week’s NATO meeting will show whether the alliance is ready to go further as Russia’s war spills beyond Ukraine’s borders. Acting Defense Minister Radu Miruță wrote on Facebook on 14 October that "the Black Sea needs a joint military command of the NATO riparian states." "The Black Sea incidents, involving drones, sunk ships, and naval mines, oblige us to act, not wait," he wrote, after a call with his Bulgarian counterpart. Leadership and location would rotate among the member states. Romania is ready to host the command on its coast from 2028 and would accept a start on Türkiye's coast until then, he said. He proposed that Romania and Bulgaria send NATO a joint letter backing the idea. The next day, Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu wrote on X that four commercial ships had been attacked over the previous day, including in Romania's territorial waters and exclusive economic zone, and that eight people had died. "Russia is turning the Black Sea into a dangerous area for civilian ships," she wrote. "Killing sailors from commercial ships, both in this region and anywhere in the world, is a crime. Russia bears full responsibility for these developments." Earlier that day, as two tankers burned off Romania's coast, Bucharest had said it was still checking whether drones were involved. Explore further Two tankers burn off Romania’s Sulina as Bulgaria says it lacks proof Russia is behind the Black Sea ship attacks Țoiu said NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte had agreed to convene the allies within days, after he met Romanian President Nicușor Dan and Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev in Brussels. NATO ambassadors will meet next week, France 24 reported . No date has been announced. An escalating drone strike campaign Map: Euromaidan Press Drones have been hitting merchant ships for weeks on the route from Ukraine's Danube and Odesa ports to the Bosporus. Besides the latest strikes off Romania, Reuters counts at least five cargo ships hit near Romania and Bulgaria in the past 10 days, with 23 sailors dead or missing, most of them outside any NATO member's territorial waters. This week the strikes reached Romania's own waters. The Comoros-flagged tanker Yara J was hit inside Romanian territorial waters late on 14 October, off Sulina, the port at the mouth of the Danube. Its crew was unharmed, and it was towed to the Romanian port of Constanța. Early on 15 October drones struck the San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader about a mile outside Romanian waters, also southeast of Sulina. Five of its 12 crew were rescued. Seven were still missing on 16 October, when rescuers returned to search the ship. Two more ships were also targeted, Reuters reported: the Marshall Islands-flagged Sea Destiny , inside Romanian waters according to NATO, and the Tanzania-flagged Dania J , moored at the Ukrainian Danube port of Izmail. Țoiu did not say which ships her eight dead were from, and Reuters still lists the Wine Trader 's seven as missing. A NATO military source told Reuters the drones that hit both tankers came from Russia. The chemical tanker Wine Trader. Photo: VesselFinder Romania's president says too early to say Romania's president has not gone as far as his foreign minister. Dan told reporters in Brussels it was "obvious" that the attacks were Russian attempts to destabilize Romania and Bulgaria and reduce support for Ukraine. But he also said it was too early to say definitively that Russia had launched the drones, according to Politico. Bulgaria, Romania's partner on the command proposal, says it suspects Russia but cannot prove it. Two ships were hit off its coast on 13 October, and one, the HS Dignity , sank. The other, the Chelsea 3 , is Ukrainian-owned. Radev told parliament on 14 October that the attacks worked in Russia's favor and that "logic leads there." "The problem is that we cannot prove it," he told MPs . Sofia summoned the Russian ambassador. Radev also said EU leaders would discuss a moratorium on attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea. Bucharest has blamed Russia for drones before, though over its airspace, not its shipping. On 27 July it expelled a Russian diplomat after prosecutors confirmed that fragments of drones downed on Romanian territory were Russian. Russia, Romania's Foreign Ministry said then, "bears exclusive responsibility." Ukraine ships most of its farm exports across the Black Sea. Euromaidan Press's David Axe has written on how the fight over shipping there has escalated. Explore further Russia is losing the Black Sea grain war it started. Its answer is to sink civilian ships off Romania and Bulgaria

title: Ghana and BRICS: Strategic opportunity, economic imperative or geopolitical gamble?
body: Walk through Abossey Okai, Tema and other industrial enclaves in Ghana and you can already see BRICS in Ghana’s economy: spare parts and machinery from Guangzhou, pharmaceuticals and vehicles from India, gold flowing out to Dubai. Samuel Okudzeto Abalakwa, Ghana’s Foreign Affairs Minister, announced cabinet’s approval for Ghana’s application to join the BRICS, at a joint press briefing with India’s External Affairs Minister during his visit to Accra. The Honourable Minister linked the decision to the President’s “New Economy” agenda and the desire for Ghana to chart its own path without being constrained by the conditionalities of a few international institutions. This announcement formalises a relationship that trade data has been describing for years. The open questions are what formal membership adds, what it might cost, and how businesses should position themselves while the process plays out. The conversation is more relevant now, as Ghana transitions from a period of macroeconomic stabilisation towards one focused on investment-led growth and structural transformation. Understanding BRICS and Why It Matters What began in the early 2000s as an economic acronym coined to describe the fast-growing emerging economies of Brazil, Russia, India and China has evolved into one of the most influential geopolitical and economic blocs in the world. South Africa joined the grouping in 2010, transforming BRIC into BRICS and providing Africa with representation within the bloc. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE later joined, followed by Indonesia in 2025, bringing membership to 11, with Nigeria and several other countries holding partner status. The group’s main institution is the New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai. The bank has approved over 120 projects worth about US$40 billion and admits new members on the condition that the founding BRICS countries’ capital share never falls below 55%. One stated ambition – reducing reliance on the US Dollar – remains a key aspiration yet to be realised. BRICS today is no longer simply a forum for emerging economies. It represents a broader vision for increasing the influence of developing nations within global governance structures. For many countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America, the appeal of BRICS lies not in replacing existing global institutions, but in creating additional options. In an increasingly uncertain global environment characterised by economic fragmentation, geopolitical competition and shifting trade dynamics, diversification has become a strategic necessity. Why Ghana Is Looking Towards BRICS Ghana’s interest in BRICS comes at a pivotal moment in its economic journey. Following years of economic turbulence, debt restructuring and IMF-supported reforms, the Country has made notable progress in restoring macroeconomic stability. Economic discussions are increasingly shifting from stabilisation towards growth, productivity, investment and industrialisation. Internal economic briefings and policy discussions increasingly focus on how Ghana can move from recovery to sustainable private-sector-led growth. At the same time, the global economic environment is changing. Emerging markets are playing a larger role in global trade and investment flows, while developing countries are seeking greater influence within international institutions. Against this backdrop, BRICS presents Ghana with an opportunity to expand its economic options. Government officials have publicly framed the proposed membership as part of a broader strategy to diversify international partnerships and create new avenues for cooperation. This rationale aligns closely with the Country’s broader ambitions around industrialisation, infrastructure development, job creation and economic transformation. The Economic Case for Membership The strongest arguments in favour of Ghana joining BRICS are arguably economic rather than political. Four key areas of potential benefit to Ghana have been highlighted below: Alignment with where Ghana’s trade already goes: This is the strongest economic argument. In 2025, the UAE took 25.9% of Ghana’s exports, India 16.0%, South Africa 10.3% and China 4.9%. All four are BRICS members, which means roughly 57% of Ghana’s export earnings already flow to the bloc. On the import side, China remained Ghana’s largest supplier at about 23% of imports in the fourth quarter of 2025. Membership could institutionalise relationships that are already central to Ghana’s balance of payments, while opening additional channels for exports and investment promotion. Development financing options: Ghana has completed a demanding IMF programme and now engages the Fund through a Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI), a non-financing arrangement that offers technical support and policy guidance. With no IMF money on the table, access to the NDB for infrastructure financing (energy, rail, water, digital) would widen the menu of long-tenor capital at a time when Ghana needs to finance growth. These investments will be essential if the Country is to realise its ambition of becoming a competitive industrial economy. Industrial and technology partnerships: The visit by India’s External Affairs Minister itself showed what is on offer, with plans announced to deepen cooperation in railways, pharmaceuticals, ICT, defence, agriculture and science and technology. If Ghana uses membership to negotiate local value addition, such as gold refining, cocoa processing and pharmaceutical manufacturing, rather than simply more raw commodity exports, the growth dividend could be real. Negotiating leverage: Being in more rooms strengthens Ghana’s hand with every partner, including the Bretton Woods institutions, on debt treatment, climate finance and conditionality, amongst others. Lessons from Africa’s BRICS Experience To understand what BRICS membership could mean for Ghana, it is important to examine the experiences of African countries already within the bloc. South Africa’s journey offers perhaps the most relevant case study. Since joining BRICS in 2010, South Africa has used the platform to deepen trade and investment relationships, expand diplomatic influence and access development financing through the New Development Bank. The NDB’s first South African loan in 2016 supported renewable energy, and the bank has since backed 13 projects there worth around US$9 billion (in current terms), including a loan of up to US$1 billion for water and sanitation infrastructure under the Municipal Infrastructure Grant programme. The lesson is that the NDB can be a meaningful infrastructure financier for a member with a strong project pipeline and capable state entities. The Country continues to benefit from this association, while simultaneously maintaining strong economic relationships with Europe and the United States. Ethiopia, which joined in 2024, presents a cautionary story. At admission, one Ethiopian economist judged that the direct economic benefit would be modest, but that membership would improve investor perception and widen options for development finance. Ethiopian analysts have observed that the country’s trade and investment ties are stronger with individual BRICS countries such as China, Saudi Arabia and India than with the bloc as a whole, and that membership has not offset the AGOA benefits and Western privileges that were lost. The Ethiopian Economics Association also warned that trading in local currencies could worsen forex constraints and complicate Dollar-based trade with other partners, recommending that Ethiopia manages it relationship with both BRICS and the West in the short run to the benefit of the country. Perhaps the most important lesson from these experiences is that BRICS membership itself does not create economic transformation. Membership rewards countries that come with bankable projects and strong institutions, and it does not by itself replace Western market access. South Africa’s gains did not emerge simply because it joined BRICS; they emerged because the country actively leveraged membership to attract investment, strengthen trade relationships and promote national economic priorities. The challenges and considerations While the economic opportunities are compelling, it would be naïve to assume that BRICS membership comes without risks. Western Economic Relationships management is an immediate risk: The European Union, United States and United Kingdom remain among Ghana’s most important development partners, export destinations and sources of foreign direct investment. President Trump has threatened additional tariffs on countries that align with what he describes as the bloc’s anti-American policies. Even though Ghana’s bilateral goods trade with the US is not relatively huge, it matters disproportionately for specific sectors. With AGOA renewal and trade negotiations unsettled, the timing requires careful diplomacy. Ghana’s engagement with BRICS should not be interpreted as a pivot away from the West. Such a framing creates a false choice. The world’s most successful middle-income economies typically pursue diversified international relationships rather than exclusive alliances. The strategic objective should be to broaden Ghana’s options, not narrow them. Trade imbalance and import competition: Concerns have been raised on whether Ghana, as a largely import-driven economy, risks becoming a dumping ground for larger BRICS producers such as China. Trade defence and local-content policies must be reviewed to ensure Ghanaian manufacturers are not squeezed in the pursuit of deeper integration. Choice of membership tier: The membership option being considered is of significant strategic importance. There have been questions around why Ghana is not following Nigeria’s route as a BRICS partner country rather than seeking full membership. Legislators have also asked for scrutiny of the conditions attached to BRICS-linked financing. Partner status or NDB membership alone might be an option to explore, since it delivers most of the financial benefits with less geopolitical exposure. BRICS cannot fix domestic constraints: As critics in the local debate have put it, BRICS cannot improve Ghana’s institutions for us. Membership alone does not guarantee increased exports, investment inflows or financing. Project preparation capacity, procurement integrity, energy sector reforms and the cost of doing business will determine whether Ghana can fully exploit opportunities arising from BRICS membership. Protecting hard-won credibility: Ghana’s recovery is real: its credit rating has risen from restricted default to “B” with a positive outlook after five upgrades, and reserves reached about US$14.5 billion by February 2026, close to six months of import cover. Officials want the PCI to support a path toward investment-grade status. Any perception that Ghana is drifting away from the institutions and investors underpinning that recovery would carry a price in borrowing costs. What Does This Mean for Businesses? For businesses operating in Ghana, BRICS membership should be viewed primarily through a commercial lens rather than a political one. Export-oriented firms may find new opportunities emerging within large consumer markets such as India, China and Indonesia. Agribusinesses could benefit from stronger demand for processed agricultural products, while manufacturers may discover opportunities to integrate into broader emerging-market supply chains. Manufacturers and import substitution businesses should take the dumping concern seriously. Competitive pressures from BRICS imports should be tracked while exploring technology and joint-venture partnerships. Exporters to the US and AGOA users (Apparel, Processed Cocoa, Agro Processing) face the highest near-term risk. Scenarios around non renewal of AGOA and higher tariffs should be modelled, while analysing diversification towards the EU and AfCFTA markets. The Association of Ghana Industries (AGI) and other trade chambers should lead discussions with institutions such as the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) to ensure that the right negotiations are underway to secure favourable terms. Financial institutions should closely monitor developments around trade finance, cross-border payment systems and potential financing mechanisms linked to BRICS institutions. Strengthening compliance frameworks will be key, as banks and other financial institutions may play a role in co-financing or on-lending NDB facilities. Technology companies may also benefit. Several BRICS economies have become global leaders in digital innovation, fintech development and technology-enabled services. Stronger cooperation could facilitate technology transfer, investment partnerships and market expansion opportunities for Ghanaian firms. Businesses should however avoid making major strategic decisions based solely on anticipated membership. The most successful firms will be those that begin proactively studying emerging market opportunities, understanding regulatory environments and building commercial relationships well before any formal accession is completed. What Should Investors Watch? For investors evaluating Ghana, the significance of BRICS membership will ultimately depend less on the membership itself and more on how it influences policy, investment flows and economic reform. Several questions will be particularly important. Will Ghana successfully leverage membership to attract productive investment into priority sectors? Will access to alternative financing accelerate critical infrastructure development? Can the country strengthen manufacturing and export competitiveness? Will policymakers maintain a stable and predictable investment climate? And perhaps most importantly, can Ghana enhance its relationships with BRICS members while retaining the confidence of its traditional partners? The answers to these questions will determine whether BRICS becomes a transformational platform or merely a symbolic affiliation. A Defining Test of Strategic Positioning Ghana’s interest in BRICS reflects a broader reality about the changing structure of the global economy. Economic influence is becoming more dispersed, emerging markets are becoming increasingly important, and countries are seeking greater flexibility in how they engage internationally. In this environment, Ghana’s decision should not be viewed as a choice between East and West, North and South, or old and new alliances. Rather, it represents an attempt to position the Country within a more complex and interconnected global economy. The greatest economic opportunities rarely arise from choosing sides. They arise from cultivating diverse partnerships, maintaining strategic flexibility and aligning international engagement with national development goals. If Ghana proceeds with BRICS membership, success will not be measured by the admission announcement or diplomatic symbolism. Success will be measured by whether the move leads to greater investment, stronger exports, improved infrastructure, more competitive industries and better jobs for Ghanaians. Ultimately, BRICS can provide a platform. Whether that platform becomes a catalyst for transformation or simply another diplomatic affiliation will depend on the quality of Ghana’s economic strategy, the consistency of its reforms and the ambition with which both government and business choose to engage with the opportunity. Author Osei Owusu-Ansah Junior is a strategy and transformation leader with experience across Ghana, Sierra Leone, The Gambia and Liberia. At KPMG in Ghana, he helps organisations navigate complexity, sharpen performance and unlock growth. His expertise sits at the powerful intersection of strategy, operations and enterprise-wide transformation.

title: NSIB recovers missing door as investigation begins into private jet incident
body: By Dickson Omobola Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, has commenced an investigation into an occurrence involving a Challenger 604 aircraft, registration T7-SEI, operated by Triton. The aircraft departed Abuja for Lagos at 16:12 UTC. At three nautical miles, passing 3,500 feet, the crew declared a mayday after the aircraft’s door separated. The aircraft returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22 at 1634 UTC, with nine persons on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers. Director General / Chief Executive Officer, NSIB, Captain Alex Badeh Jr, in a statement, said: “The door has been recovered and secured at the NSIB wreckage hangar. The Bureau has commenced its investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the occurrence. NSIB will provide further updates as the investigation progresses.” The post NSIB recovers missing door as investigation begins into private jet incident appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian MFA comments on Zelensky as ‘incredible disgrace,’ Kiev’s hunt for journalists
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Holding elections in Ukraine is a constitutional obligation of the Ukrainian state, not a demand from Moscow, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said at a briefing.
She noted that Vladimir Zelensky’s life had already led to the collapse of the Ukrainian state.
Zakharova also stressed that Russia demands and will continue to seek condemnation by relevant international bodies of the Kiev regime’s crimes, which have no statute of limitations and include launching a full-scale hunt for Russian journalists.
TASS has compiled the key statements by the Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman.
Holding elections in Ukraine is a constitutional obligation of the Ukrainian state, not a demand from Moscow: "Did Ukraine’s updated Constitution also get adopted at Moscow’s behest? Did some hand from the Kremlin write it? As far as I remember, people in Ukraine, starting with [Vladimir] Zelensky, were very proud of it. What does it say about elections? It is the Ukrainian state’s duty to hold elections on its territory. It is the duty of those elected by the Ukrainian people to ensure that laws are enforced, starting with the Constitution."
Vladimir Zelensky’s life has already led to the collapse of the Ukrainian state: "What an incredible disgrace Zelensky is. Ukraine would collapse if he died? His life has already led to the collapse of the Ukrainian state."
Russia demands and will continue to seek condemnation by relevant international bodies of the Kiev regime’s crimes, which have involved launching a "full-scale hunt for Russian correspondents": "The death toll has already reached dozens."
International organizations not only fail to condemn Kiev’s actions but are unable even to find "words of sympathy": "The leadership of such international bodies as UNESCO, the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has not condemned the Kiev regime’s crimes and has not even found words of sympathy over a number of killings of Russian media representatives."
The silence of officials "effectively fosters an atmosphere of permissiveness and impunity" for attacks on Russian journalists.
The Baltic states have joined Vladimir Zelensky’s favorite game of the meat grinder by deporting Ukrainian refugees of conscription age back to Ukraine: "This is Zelensky’s childhood dream of playing the meat grinder, as his mother described it when recounting the toys little Zelensky used to play with, now put into practice."
After pledging support for Kiev following Vladimir Zelensky’s visit to London, Britain will continue supplying Ukraine with weapons for terrorist attacks on civilians: "Let’s translate this into the language of facts: Downing Street and the British establishment in London will continue to supply the Kiev regime with weapons for terrorist attacks on civilians."
Brussels has maintained its anti-Russian fervor but run out of common sense, having "crushed" it with successive sanctions packages against Russia: "The anti-Russian fervor of the European bureaucracy is, as we understand it, far from exhausted. What has been exhausted is common sense in Brussels. It is completely absent there. It has been crushed by sanctions packages."
The European Union, where "everything is collapsing before our eyes," is finding it increasingly difficult to agree on new sanctions packages against Russia, which, according to Zakharova, shows the weakness of Europeans: "It is becoming increasingly difficult for EU member states to reach agreement on sectoral restrictions that affect their own economies in particular, as well as other areas. As a result, the ‘large-scale’ anti-Russian measures adopted this week, as they called them, turned out on closer inspection to be a mere bureaucratic expansion of the so-called blacklists based on extremely broad wording."
The European Union’s anti-Russian stance offers little prospect for resuming energy cooperation: "At present, judging by their statements and actions, such prospects are unlikely to materialize."
Russia will not prevent peace-minded Europeans from entering the country despite the European Union’s discriminatory policies: "Our country remains open and hospitable. I believe this should be our response. We have no intention of closing ourselves off or restricting those who come to us in peace, with interest, and with a positive, constructive agenda."
Members of the European Parliament who have proposed closing all Russian Houses in Europe are following Nazi methods that "should have been consigned to oblivion": "Doesn’t this remind you of anything? This kind of rabid determination to shut down Russian Houses, which tell people about [Russian culture] when it matters to them and they want to learn about it. It reminded me of something. These are the very same patterns they used to shape their policies not so long ago, in the first third of the 20th century. Remember the play Schlageter? It was written by a playwright who was a Nazi."
Russia views the proposal to close all Russian Houses in Europe as another example of rabid and thoughtless Russophobia.
Russian citizens traveling abroad need to remain vigilant amid what Zakharova described as a "worldwide hunt for Russians" by US intelligence agencies.
Threats to expel Russian Ambassador to Moldova Oleg Ozerov, as well as the routine summoning of the diplomat to the Moldovan Foreign Ministry accompanied by "a show involving the conspicuous placement of drones on the steps," are absolutely unacceptable.
Such rhetoric "demonstrates that Oleg Ozerov’s opponents have absolutely no real grounds for accusing him of disrespecting his host country," and that they are therefore resorting to "blatant lies, groundless accusations and sheer rudeness."
"Fortunately, people in Moldova itself understand the real value of their authorities’ anti-Russian statements. Independent political analysts note that the country’s residents see the real threat to statehood in the destructive policies of Moldova and [Maia] Sandu’s team, which is systematically turning the republic into yet another anti-Russian foothold."

title: MARTAC USVs Gain Real-Time Machine Vision from SEA.AI
body: MARTAC has integrated SEA.AI machine vision on its unmanned surface vessels. The system classifies contacts in real time at the sensor, so USVs understand their surroundings without anyone watching a video feed. SEA.AI press release MARTAC has integrated SEA.AI maritime machine vision on its unmanned surface vessels (USVs). The system classifies vessels and objects in real time at the sensor, so a USV operating far beyond its operators’ line of sight gets usable situational awareness without anyone watching a video feed. MARTAC, a Florida-based manufacturer of high-performance autonomous maritime platforms, selected SEA.AI as part of its sensor integration architecture. The integration covers ISR, security, and patrol mission profiles. SEA.AI announced the partnership with MARTAC on 13 October 2026. Why radar and AIS leave a gap in maritime domain awareness SEA.AI picture Radar resolves a contact’s position and radar cross-section, but not what the contact is. AIS is voluntary, routinely manipulated, and missing on any platform that chooses not to broadcast. In today’s grey zone environment, these limits carry operational weight because threats are designed to exploit them: dark vessels, spoofed identities, and fast-attack craft that look like surrounding traffic until the moment they act. How SEA.AI turns a camera feed into actionable information Electro-optical and thermal cameras have long been part of maritime sensing. The weak point is what happens after the image is captured.
