On an autonomous platform, a conventional camera produces video, and that video is useless without an analyst watching it continuously. SEA.AI runs AI inference at the sensor level. Its electro-optical and thermal system classifies each contact in real time and outputs vessel or object type, heading, and proximity as actionable information, with no human review of imagery. For a USV beyond visual range of its operators, this separates genuine situational awareness from a data stream nobody has time to interpret. Built for missions beyond the operator’s reach MARTAC T38 USV (Credit: MARTAC) In May 2026, MARTAC’s T38 Devil Ray completed a record 8-day fully autonomous mission off the coast of California. It navigated multiple real surface contacts in open-ocean conditions, without crew or escort, more than 400 nautical miles from shore. At that range and in Sea State 5 conditions, no remote operator can review imagery in time. The vessel has to detect and understand its environment on its own, and that is the capability SEA.AI brings. “We built SEA.AI in 2018 around a conviction that the camera alone was never going to be enough at sea. The intelligence had to be in the system, not in a person watching a screen somewhere. That requirement has only become more urgent as autonomous platforms move from trials into operational deployment.” Marcus Warrelmann, CEO, SEA.AI “Operators have sensors, platforms, and more data than their teams can process. What we add to a MARTAC vessel is not another feed to monitor, it is a system that watches, understands, and reports. This partnership with MARTAC puts that capability where it matters: on proven platforms, in real missions.” Diogo ArredaManaging Director US, SEA.AI “Our platforms are built to carry whatever sensors the mission requires, and we evaluate every integration on one basis: does it make the vessel more operationally capable? SEA.AI’s machine vision, that classifies contacts autonomously and in real time, is a direct solution for closing a real gap. That is why it is on our platforms.” Jim HarveyChief Technology Officer, MARTAC SEA.AI machine vision, proven at sea since 2018 SEA.AI pioneered maritime machine vision in 2018. Its systems combine optical and thermal sensors with artificial intelligence to detect what radar and AIS often miss: persons overboard, marine mammals, unlit vessels, small craft, containers, semi-submerged logs, and other floating hazards, day and night, in real time. The technology is built on more than eight years of real-world data gathered at sea. More than 1,300 systems are in service worldwide, across recreational, commercial, and security operations, at sea and from fixed installations. – End – The post MARTAC USVs Gain Real-Time Machine Vision from SEA.AI appeared first on Naval News .

title: SML vs GRA: Court grants preservation order in dispute over US$500 million investment
body: The High Court (Commercial Court 3), Accra, presided by Her Lordship Justice Doris Awuah Dabanka-Bekoe on Friday granted a preservation order in favour of Strategic Mobilization Ghana Limited (SML), directing the preservation of the company’s equipment installed at all 25 fuel depots across the country, pending the determination of the company’s ongoing legal dispute with the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA). The equipment covered by the preservation application includes Automatic Tank Gauges (ATGs), ultrasonic flow meters, Remote Terminal Units (RTUs), satellite equipment, power shelters, solar systems, cables and other technical infrastructure deployed by SML in the performance of its contractual obligations to the GRA. These installations formed part of the technological systems that SML says it used in the delivery of the various measurements, audits, and verification services undertaken by the company. The application for the preservation order followed a civil action instituted by SML against the GRA after the company received a letter from the Authority requesting that it remove its equipment installed at the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company Limited (BOST) depot. In an interview, Cephas Boyuo, Esq., Corporate Lawyer of SML, described the court’s decision as a step in the right direction, expressing confidence in the company’s case and its prospects of recovering its investment. He indicated that SML was confident that, just as the court had granted the preservation order to protect the equipment pending trial, it would ultimately uphold the company’s claim for more than US$500 million after hearing the substantive case. According Lawyer Boyuo, the preservation order represents an important development in protecting the company’s interests while the parties await the determination of the substantive dispute. He expressed confidence that the evidence and legal arguments to be presented at trial would support SML’s claim for the recovery of its investment outlay. Lawyer Boyuo further stated that following receipt of GRA’s letter requesting the removal of its equipment, SML commenced legal proceedings against the Authority, seeking recovery of its investment outlay, estimated at over US$500 million, in connection with the services it provided under its contractual arrangements with the GRA. The company has said its contractual services included transaction audits and external price verification, downstream petroleum measurement audits, upstream petroleum measurement audits, and solid minerals measurement audits, and that these services formed part of SML’s engagement in the measurement, monitoring, verification, and auditing of activities within the petroleum and solid minerals sectors. The preservation order seeks to maintain the existing position regarding the equipment while the court considers the substantive issues raised by the parties. It is intended to safeguard the subject matter of the litigation and prevent the removal or interference with the equipment from prejudicing the proceedings, subject to the precise terms of the order. According to lawyer Boyuo, the dispute concerns both SML’s protection of its installed equipment and the recovery of what the company says is a substantial investment it made in fulfilling its contractual obligations. The company maintains that it is entitled to recover its investment outlay, and proceedings will therefore provide an opportunity for SML and the GRA to argue out their respective positions on the contractual relationship, the investments, and the circumstances surrounding the request for the removal of the equipment.

title: My Word: The Nobel non-Peace Prize - opinion
body: Once upon a time, the Nobel Peace Prize was founded to award genuine efforts to further world peace. Or so the legend goes.Last week's announcement that the 2026 prize is being awarded to South African judge, and strident critic of Israel, Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, proves how far it's come – in the wrong direction.Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge, served as UN high commissioner for human rights from 2008 until 2014 – a position she used to promote an anti-Israel agenda – and last year she oversaw the publishing of a UN-commissioned report that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Hamas, the Iranian-backed terrorist organization that literally committed an act of premeditated genocide during the October 7, 2023 invasion and mega-atrocity, in which 1,200 people were murdered in southern Israel and 251 abducted to Gaza, barely merited a mention. The focus is on Israel, always on Israel. It's part of the technique of delegitimization and demonization, with the aim of eventual elimination of the Jewish state.What did Navi Pillay do?In 2021, the UN launched an unprecedented, open-ended war-crimes probe against Israel. The “UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in Israel” (COI) is tasked with submitting a report twice a year, in addition to the mandated sessions on Israel held by the UN Security Council every three months. Having uniquely granted the Palestinians “perpetual refugee” status, the UN needs to subject Israel to perpetual blame.Pillay chaired the three-member COI, despite having already called for the boycott and sanctioning of Israel. She was joined by two members with equally problematic backgrounds, Miloon Kothari and Chris Sidoti. The three resigned last year, apparently fearing they could face US sanctions like UN Special Rapporteur for Palestinian rights Francesca Albanese, another UN official with a proud anti-Israel bias.The Norwegian Nobel Peace Prize committee announced its decision on October 9, as Israel was deep in a week commemorating the barbaric frenzy of terrorist murders, rapes, and abductions three years ago – the worst attack on Jews since the Holocaust.Pillay beat a list of contenders reported by Time magazine to have included, among others: Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms (acting to provide relief in the war that few notice because Israel can't be blamed), and Mykola Kuleba, co-founder of Save Ukraine, an organization dedicated, among other things, to reuniting Ukrainian children kidnapped and held by Russia during the ongoing war.Israel's Foreign Ministry dropped the diplomatic language to post on social media: “If there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn't just be a contender. She'd be a frontrunner. Her role in the relentless, politically motivated demonization of Israel and promotion of the genoLIE speaks volumes.“Awarding Pillay the Nobel Peace Prize isn't a recognition of justice. It's the grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice.“Now that the Nobel committee has rewarded the biggest lie of the 21st century, Joseph Goebbels is certainly applauding from hell.”Chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov posted on X: “Maybe next year they will award the Chemistry Prize to a Hamas bomb maker.” Kasparov later clarified that he knows that the peace prize is granted by Norwegian committees while the other Nobel awards are given by Swedish institutions – but the joke's on all of us.In 2012, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the European Union – another body that collectively promotes a Palestinian narrative at Israel's expense. The irony that Norway isn't even a EU member state was pointed out by Swedish editorial writer Henrik L. Barva, a brave supporter of Israel, Ukraine, and Taiwan.I first met Barva, along with a very mixed group of international journalists, on a press tour of Taiwan (the Republic of China) to celebrate Double Ten Day, the October 10 national day. We were together when the decision to award the prize to Barack Obama was announced in 2009, before he had even taken office, and had fun thinking up other Nobel categories in which he could have won the award, including literature for his books and the prize for physics, for defying the laws of nature and becoming the first superman to be elected president of the US.As it happened, Obama missed the chance to further world peace by failing to support the courageous Iranian Green Movement protesters trying to overthrow the Iranian regime in 2009, and later promoting the disastrous Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action nuclear deal. The results are still being felt globally today.When the 1994 peace prize was given to Yasser Arafat (along with Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres) for the Oslo Accords, I didn't find it funny.I attended this year's festive Taiwanese national day reception hosted by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Tel Aviv last week. Chief representative Ya-ping (Abby) Lee noted the reception also marked 30 years since Taiwan's first direct presidential election, and highlighted a shared commitment to democracy and freedom. She also emphasized, “Taiwan's global role in technology and the potential for closer cooperation with Israel in innovation and AI, while reaffirming our support for Israeli communities recovering and rebuilding.”Taiwan was ousted from the UN in 1971 and replaced with the People's Republic of China. Hence, democratic Taiwan – an economic powerhouse with much to contribute to the fields of health and technology, for example – is unable to share its knowledge through UN bodies, while Communist China – still threatening to invade Taiwan – has a permanent seat (alongside Russia) on the UN Security Council.JUST AS I wasn't shocked by Pillay's Peace Prize award, I was not surprised by the announcement last week that the Palestinian Authority elections had been postponed – yet again. The PA had promised several countries, including France, that it would hold elections in return for gaining recognition as “The State of Palestine” last September. (The UN also recognizes the borderless, failed state.) The elections – the first in 20 years – were scheduled to be held next month. They have been tentatively rescheduled for September 11, 2027, but don't hold your breath.The date 9.11 will be forever remembered for the jihadist attack on the US rather than Palestinian democracy and good governance. PA head Mahmoud Abbas, now in the 21st year of his four-year term, also pushed off the presidential elections, blaming Israel, of course, for the delay.Israel, unlike the Palestinian territories, is gearing up for elections on October 27, but democracy is no guarantee of winning praise, let alone awards, as both Israel and Taiwan can testify.US President Donald Trump blasted the decision to award Pillay the prize he has been eyeing for years, but he didn't stand a chance. If he wasn't considered worthy of the award for creating the Abraham Accords in 2020, peace agreements that have proven themselves over the years, then he won't get it now, after tackling Iran.In 2024, reported peace prize contenders included the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, probably for the same reason that Pillay won it this year – dedicated criticism of Israel. It obviously wasn't for creating peace.Guterres gracefully complimented Pillay on her award, saying: “It has shown that the force of law must prevail over the law of force…”Law professor Yuval Elbashan met Pillay in Nepal in 2009 and wrote in Israel Hayom this week: “Even then, in our personal conversation, she revealed hostility toward the very idea of a Jewish state in the Land of Israel, in which she saw an exact reflection of South Africa's apartheid regime.”He called this year's peace prize “evidence of the deep anti-Israel politicization that has spread through international institutions… The anti-Israel stamp of approval has become a springboard to the biggest prize of them all.”Elbashan also noted that Pillay “is now leading the push to redefine the legal definition of 'genocide' so that it fits and encompasses Israel's actions in Gaza. She is doing so as an ad hoc judge… in Gambia's case against Myanmar at the International Court of Justice in The Hague. “She isn't crafting this new legal test for the Rohingya people. She is crafting it to convict Israel.”With winners like Pillay, world peace and justice are the losers.

title: Middle Israel: From Caesar to Netanyahu, Israel prepares to enter a post-charisma era - opinion
body: Theodor Mommsen was infatuated.Julius Caesar, wrote a future Nobel laureate in The History of Rome, was “a statesman genius,” one so “perfect” that such a figure emerged only “once in a thousand years,” like the “consummate beauty” that even the most gifted painter “can only be silent” in its face.Written in 1856, it was the kind of partiality that historians are expected to avoid, reflecting a German nationalist’s thirst for a charismatic leader who would unite his politically splintered people. That great leader would be far wiser, bolder, and more visionary than ordinary people. Charisma, the gift of natural leadership, would make that superhero deliver what no one else could achieve.A similar attitude inspired Zionist historian Joseph Klausner’s depiction of the Messiah as “Judaism’s Ubermensch,” a superhero “far greater and stronger than the multitude, a personality to which all willingly submit.”Inspired by Mommsen’s portrait of Caesar, Klausner painted Hasmonean King Alexander Janneus not as the Judean despot that rabbinical memory recalled, but as “a great king… dedicated to his country’s expansion and the spread of its faith.”WWII produced fascist nightmares that tainted the charismatic leaderSuch thinking was legitimate, even common, among German-educated intellectuals for generations – until World War II. The fascist nightmare produced a new breed of historians who realized that charisma is not necessarily a gift, and in fact can become a curse.Writing in his acclaimed Caesar: A Biography, historian Christian Meier shrank Mommsen’s superhero into an opportunistic politician who had no coherent vision of Rome’s future, and thus did not shape the great events in which he played a central role. Instead, Caesar was now portrayed as a shrewd tactician who responded to events that were shaped by forces larger than himself.For Jewish graduates of the 20th century, suspicion of charisma goes without saying, even though charisma also did us good, most memorably when David Ben-Gurion used it to win war, and when Menachem Begin used it to deliver peace. Now, however, the Jewish state is in the process of shifting from an era of charisma to an era of anti-charisma.How long this transition will last is anyone’s guess, but for an Israel crushed by Benjamin Netanyahu’s overbearing charisma, the post-charismatic era’s emergence will not be one day too early.Israel has already had two post-charismatic eras, and their results were surprisingly good.The current age of charisma began in 1996, when Netanyahu first became prime minister. Though there were other prime ministers during the subsequent decades, Netanyahu shaped the era. And Netanyahu, even his rivals agree, led by charisma.Netanyahu was more handsome, eloquent, and brash than any of his opponents. None could work a crowd, manage a press interview, phrase a political slogan, engineer a journalistic photo, or deliver a televised speech more effectively than he could.In turn for all of this, and as has so often happened with charisma, these merits came coupled with a soloist’s failure to consult, or even just tolerate the presence of, other able people. The charismatic leader thus gradually became not merely the government’s leader, but the government itself.How will Israel fill Netanyahu's big shoes?That is why people now wonder, after surveying his potential successors: how will they get into his big shoes? It is the same question people asked in 1963, when David Ben-Gurion stepped down after leading Israel’s creation, and that is what people asked in 1983, when Menachem Begin stepped down six years after unseating Ben-Gurion’s successors.In both cases, the question was even harsher than it is now, not only because Ben-Gurion and Begin were so much larger than Netanyahu, but because their successors were even less charismatic than the men who may soon replace Netanyahu at the State of Israel’s helm.Levi Eshkol was an unassuming, bespectacled, balding, and grandfatherly man who loved to tell Yiddish jokes and looked like a tailor who had just emerged from a Lower East Side sweatshop. Whether in his intellectual curiosity, literary diet, historical insight, political vision, or rhetorical ability – he was no David Ben-Gurion.Similarly, Yitzhak Shamir was no Menachem Begin. Begin spent decades in the public limelight, delivering fiery, eloquent, and unwritten speeches in mass rallies, and heading the opposition for nearly 30 years. Shamir spent most of the same years in the opaque labyrinths of the Mossad. Short, stocky, bushy-eyebrowed, introverted, and ineloquent, he was charisma’s antithesis.Even so, this pair of antiheroes did incredible things.Eshkol built the army that struck the greatest military victory in Jewish history. Before that, as finance minister in the 1950s, he built an economy that was the fastest-growing in the world, alongside Korea and Japan. And as prime minister, he inspired national reconciliation, first by ordering an official funeral for his party’s historic nemesis, Ze’ev Jabotinsky; then by canceling Israel’s military rule over its Arab towns; and finally, by bringing Menachem Begin into the government that won the 1967 Six-Day War.Similarly, the uncharismatic Shamir led four million Israelis’ successful absorption of one million immigrants from the fallen Soviet Union. While at it, he airlifted Ethiopian Jewry. In the interim, he managed, with great poise, Israel’s precarious situation during the First Gulf War. And before all that, he and his arch-rival, Labor’s Shimon Peres, jointly saved a hyper-inflationary economy from collapse.Shamir and Eshkol registered all these achievements not despite, but because of their lack of charisma. Their grayness only made them positively humble, focusing on the issues rather than on themselves, harnessing rather than fearing talent, and inspiring business-minded teamwork instead of spending their days thinking of the next photo op, soundbite or speech.Now, as the post-Netanyahu era steadily approaches, this is what Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett offer, and what a traumatized Israel demands.www.MiddleIsrael.net The writer, a Hartman Institute fellow, is the author of the bestseller, The Jewish March of Folly (Yedioth Books 2026), now available in English on Amazon.

title: Spotify brings audiobooks to Ghana
body: Spotify has announced that audiobooks are rolling out to listeners in Ghana from 14 October. The launch is part of Spotify’s global expansion of audiobooks from 22 markets to more than 180 by the end of 2026, bringing books to more than 750 million people who will be able to stream or purchase them on Spotify. From the trotro ride across Accra to the late-night wind-down, audiobooks fit into the everyday moments listeners in Ghana already fill with music and podcasts. In Ghana, Spotify Free and Premium users can add Audiobooks+, a monthly add-on that includes 15 hours of audiobook listening for GHS 20. Only the time spent actually listening counts, and hours reset every billing cycle. Want more time? Listeners can buy a 10-hour top-up for GHS 24, or buy an individual title to keep. “Books change how we see the world, and the people in it. For a lot of people, audiobooks are how they find their way back to reading, on the commute, on a walk, or at the end of a long day. Bringing audiobooks to more than 180 markets means millions more people can discover that, and authors and publishers can reach readers they’ve never been able to reach before,” said Owen Smith, VP of Audiobooks, Spotify. Features made for everyday listening Page Match: Read a few chapters in bed, then pick up the story on your morning commute, right where you left off. More than one million readers have used Page Match to move between print, ebook and audio. Now listeners can simply scan a book’s ISBN barcode and use page numbers to find their place. Page Match works in over 30 languages. A home for books: A dedicated Audiobooks space in the app to search, browse and discover, with recommendations based on what each listener loves across music, podcasts and books. Never lose your place: Spotify saves your progress across the more than 2,000 devices it’s available on, so you can start on your phone and carry on in the car or on a speaker. Sleep Timer: Set a timer for night-time listening so the story stops when you drift off. Listen offline: Download audiobooks to listen without a connection, just like music and podcasts. A bigger stage for Ghanaian authors Spotify believes authors should find the largest possible audience, which is why all of its audiobook partnerships are non-exclusive. Through Spotify for Authors, local publishers and self-published authors in Ghana can upload their audiobooks and reach listeners in more than 180 markets, with insights into who is listening. The catalogue in Ghana will keep growing as new partners join and local authors upload their work. A world of stories Three years ago this fall, Spotify brought audiobooks into Premium to build a better home for book lovers, authors and publishers. Over the past year, monthly audiobook listeners grew nearly 40% and listening hours climbed more than 30%. Since launching just over a year ago, Audiobooks+ has grown to more than one million subscribers. How to get started Update to the latest version of the Spotify app and open the Audiobooks hub, or search for any title. Choose a book and add Audiobooks+ Manage your plan at spotify.com/account .. Press play. Pricing and access models vary by market.

title: Flick confirms return of Barcelona duo Raphinha, De Jong
body: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick announced that star attacker Raphinha and midfield lynchpin Frenkie de Jong have recovered from injury and could face Real Betis on Saturday. The Catalans boast a 100 percent record in all competitions this season but face a tough test in La Liga in Seville against third-placed Betis. During his pre-match press on Friday, German boss Flick revealed the timely return of two of Barcelona’s biggest names. “If you ask him, he’ll tell you he’s ready to start, but we’re taking things step by step. We have a lot of games in a short space of time and we need to manage that,” Flick told reporters of Raphinha, who has scored 14 goals in eight outings for Barcelona this term. The 29-year-old Brazilian picked up a knock on recent international duty and was unavailable for Barca’s wins over Getafe in the league and Galatasaray in the Champions League. Dutch international De Jong, 29, has not featured this season due to a knee issue sustained during the World Cup. “He gives us another option in midfield and we’ll see how he progresses,” Flick said. “He’s training well and is ready to get some minutes. He looks very focused and he’s a top player.” The return of the pair will likely take some of the creative and goalscoring burden off Lamine Yamal’s young shoulders. The 19-year-old world champion has played the full 90 minutes in eight of the 10 competitive matches played by Barca this season, and in the other two he was substituted after an hour of play. “He’s a special player,” Flick said. “We have to manage his minutes, but the important thing is that he enjoys playing. That’s how things are at the moment and I don’t want to interrupt that.” After this weekend’s trip to La Cartuja, Barcelona face a daunting visit to twice-defending Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday before hosting Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid in El Clasico five days later. AFP The post Flick confirms return of Barcelona duo Raphinha, De Jong appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: GPL 2026/27: ‘We are the team to beat’ – Medeama boss Tanko ahead of Samartex clash
body: Medeama SC Head Coach Ibrahim Tanko has expressed confidence ahead of a table-topping fixture against FC Samartex in the Ghana Premier League. The defending champions aim to maintain their commanding start to the season as they square off against FC Samartex on matchday 7 of the Ghana Premier League. Tanko’s side sit at the top of the table with 14 points from six matches, while Samartex are three points behind in third place looking to close the gap on their rivals. As the only unbeaten team in the league, Tanko voiced readiness and assurance ahead of the away fixture noting that it puts a target on their back. “We just had six games and we didn’t lose a game so definitely we are one of the teams that everyone would like to beat. “We are preparing very well. We know the venue we are going to is very tough to play at. They have a very good team with a very good coach behind them.” He stated. Medeama face Samartex on Sunday October 18 as they aim to secure a crucial away victory to build on their dominant start to the campaign.

title: Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say
body:
The shooting occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School.
The mass shooting at a Bend, Oregon, elementary school on Thursday that left three children and one teacher dead took place inside a special needs classroom, authorities said at a news conference, identifying some of the victims and the suspected shooter.
Three boys, ages 5, 8 and 11, and the teacher died at the scene, police said. At a news conference on Friday, authorities identified the teacher as 25-year-old Megan Lambert, and one of the boys as 5-year-old Rhoam Summer. The names of the other two children killed are not being released at the request of their families, police said.
The suspected shooter, a 16-year-old armed with a twelve-gauge shotgun, was fatally shot by a community member who saw the teen going into the Silver Rail Elementary School and pursued him inside, according to Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz.
In another "heroic" act that may have saved lives, he said another teacher tackled the shooter to the floor and tried to take the gun away from him.
A 7-year-old girl and a 54-year-old teacher were wounded in the gunfire and were taken to the hospital with critical injuries, police said. The child was in serious but stable condition on Friday, and the teacher -- identified by her family as Becky Drury -- suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries, police said.
Police identified the suspected shooter on Friday as Griffin J. John II, a Bend resident who formerly attended Silver Rail Elementary School. The suspect had been a special needs student at the school, school officials confirmed. He was not currently enrolled in the school district, according to the police chief.
Preliminary information indicates the 16-year-old suspected shooter used a pump-action shotgun believed to be purchased by his mother, multiple sources told ABC News.
"How the suspect got the weapon and ammunition remains part of the active criminal investigation, and I will not be able to address any of that portion today," Krantz said at a press briefing on Friday.
A motive also remains under investigation, police said.
"It will require substantial investigative time to continue that, but that is the answer we're seeking as well," Krantz said. "We may never get that full answer, but we want it."
The incident began unfolding shortly before 1 p.m. PT Thursday, police said.
At 12:59 p.m., police received a call from a driver who reported being shot at multiple times by a person with a long gun, the police chief said. The vehicle was struck three times.
Shortly afterward, the Deschutes County dispatch center began receiving multiple 911 calls that a shooter had entered Silver Rail Elementary School. The school was directed to go into lockdown at 1:01 p.m, Krantz said.
The shooter "forced" his way inside the school by shooting at the glass panes of locked doors multiple times, according to the police chief.
"The suspect went directly into the classroom, immediately to the left of the entry doors, where he fired as many as 15 rounds overall," Krantz said.
Officers arrived on the scene at 1:02 p.m., police said.
All of the shooting victims were located in that special needs classroom, he said. The suspect was also shot in the classroom and died at the scene, he said.
A Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun was located near the suspect, who had approximately 44 remaining rounds of 12-gauge ammunition, according to the chief.
Police said the shooter was fatally shot inside the classroom by a 36-year-old community member who had seen the teen firing at the truck and then followed him into the school, Krantz said.
His family on Friday identified him as Kaylub Giamanco, a father with two daughters who attend Silver Rail Elementary School.
Giamanco -- a lifelong Bend resident -- was driving near the school when he heard the commotion and ran inside, according to his family, who said he regrets not being able to save more lives. His family confirmed he has a concealed carry permit.
"He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," the Giamanco family said in a statement.
Police also commended another teacher who threw her cellphone at the shooter after he entered the classroom. The police chief said the teacher then "tackled him and fought to take the firearm from him," and that she "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed." The police chief did not identify the teacher, and noted that she was uninjured.
Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek thanked teachers, staff and first responders who rushed to the scene and thanked the community member who she said "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life."
Following the shooting, police said they evacuated the school room by room. A reunification site for families was set up at a nearby church.
Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook called the shooting an "unthinkable tragedy" and said, "We are heartbroken. We are horrified."
Thousands of community members gathered for a candlelight vigil Thursday night at Drake Park in Bend. A makeshift memorial has also grown outside the elementary school, with mourners leaving flowers, candles, toys and stuffed animals.
Kotek ordered flags at Oregon public institutions to be flown at half-staff on Friday from sunrise to sunset in remembrance of those who lost their lives at Silver Rail Elementary School.
Classes, activities and athletic events at all Bend-La Pine Schools were canceled Friday, school officials said.
"A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure. What happened today should never happen," Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said at Thursday's press briefing. "Like so many in our community, I'm struggling to make sense of a loss that feels unimaginable."
A school resource officer was not at the elementary school at the time of the shooting, a police spokesperson said, noting that he officer oversees multiple schools and was at a nearby campus at the time.
The shooting sparked a large police presence as law enforcement and first responders raced to the school. Over 150 law enforcement officers and first responders have been involved in the investigation, police said.
"Everything they were doing seemed highly trained and highly prepared for this," Caleb Weis, who was riding his motorcycle near the school at the time, told ABC News.
"I didn't see as many phones out recording as you see on many other occasions, just a kind of a shock factor and an immense amount of respect for the law enforcement, first responders," he said.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency was on the scene assisting in the investigation. Agents with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives were also responding, according to a source.
Some parents who heard the sirens came to the school and anxiously awaited information.
"There's really no way to prepare for something like this," one father told ABC Bend affiliate KOHD.
ABC News' Alyssa Pone and Lisa Sivertsen contributed to this report.
Editor's Note: Police have corrected their initial spelling of the 25-year-old teacher's name. The correct spelling is Megan Lambert.

title: Russia’s Medvedev beats US’ Paul to advance to Shanghai Masters semifinals
body:
SHANGHAI, October 16. /TASS/. Russia’s Daniil Medvedev defeated Tommy Paul of the United States to make it to the semifinals of the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) tournament in Shanghai, China.
The 5th seeded Medvedev won the match 6:3, 1:6, 6:3. Paul was seeded 15th.
In the semifinals, Medvedev will face Rafael Jodar, seeded 12th.
Daniil Medvedev, 30, is currently the 6th-ranked player in the world. He has won 24 ATP singles titles, spent 16 weeks as the world's number one player in 2022, and helped Russia win the ATP Cup and Davis Cup in 2021. Russia’s top-ranked tennis player has reached six Grand Slam finals, winning the 2021 US Open, and won the ATP Finals title in 2020.
Tommy Paul, No. 18 in the ATP rankings, boasts five ATP titles.
The Shanghai tournament is an ATP Masters 1000 event, with only the Grand Slam tournaments and the ATP Finals ranking higher in prestige. The total prize pool is $9.4 million. Monaco’s Valentin Vacherot won the title last year. Russian players Nikolay Davydenko (2009) and Medvedev (2019) have also won the tournament.

title: Zelenskyy, Orbán agree to resume high-level talks, bilateral visits
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar discussed a number of important bilateral issues at a meeting in Brussels, including Ukraine's accession to the European Union, trade and agricultural products. They also "agreed to resume joint work and exchange visits."
"I met with Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar. We spoke one-on-one about key issues on our bilateral agenda and Ukraine's progress toward EU accession," Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram on Friday.
The president thanked the prime minister "for his principled steps and for the opening of two more negotiating clusters." According to Zelenskyy, work is now underway to open the two remaining clusters by the end of the year.
"We discussed the diplomatic situation and efforts to end Russia's war. I am grateful for his solidarity with Ukraine and our people, and for his readiness to work together for peace. We also discussed opportunities for cooperation between Ukraine and Hungary, trade, and issues related to agricultural products," the president said.
"Ukraine always stands for good-neighborly relations and mutual strengthening. We agreed to resume joint work at various levels and to exchange visits. Our teams will work out the dates," Zelenskyy wrote.
As reported, following his meeting with Zelenskyy, Magyar said Hungary was ready to provide diplomatic assistance to secure a ceasefire as soon as possible and establish lasting peace in Ukraine.
"I assured the president of Ukraine of my full solidarity in the face of Russia's inhumane aggression against his country, which has been going on for almost five years. I told him that Hungary is ready to help by all possible diplomatic means to achieve a ceasefire as soon as possible and establish lasting peace," Magyar wrote on Facebook on Friday.
He also said that following the meeting, the parties had agreed to continue consultations at the ministerial level, with particular attention to the situation of national minorities in both countries. Magyar welcomed the political agreement between Hungary and Ukraine on strengthening the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia and described the Verkhovna Rada's adoption of a law on the educational rights of national minorities, along with the start of its implementation, as a first step toward restoring mutual trust.
Magyar also thanked the Ukrainian parliament for its September resolution on crimes committed against Hungarians in Transcarpathia in 1944-1946, particularly forced labor and mass deportation.
"We agreed that it is in both countries' interests to put political and economic relations on a new footing," he said.

title: Parliamentary Select Committee on Health assesses progress of work on KATH maternity block
body: The Parliamentary Select Committee on Health has inspected work on the ongoing Maternity and Children’s Block project at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) in Kumasi to assess its progress and engage stakeholders on measures to facilitate its completion. The inspection, led by the Committee’s Chairman, Dr Mark Kurt Nawaane, focused on the current state of the project and the challenges affecting the timely completion of the facility. The Project Manager, Emmanuel Fobi Asabre, briefing the Committee, said work on the project had been suspended because of outstanding payments owed to the contractor. He said before the suspension, procurement of materials and equipment for the project had reached 75 per cent, while physical construction stood at 56 per cent. Mr. Asabre explained that the project had experienced two major suspensions, largely due to delays in settling claims submitted by the contractor. The interruptions, he said, had contributed to delays and additional costs, while raising concerns about the validity of warranties and the condition of some materials procured for the project. Despite the challenges, he said the contractor had continued to maintain the site during the suspension periods. He added that essential materials and equipment, including air-conditioning systems, electrical components and building façade materials, had already been procured and were being stored pending the resumption of construction. Mr. Asabre said the contractor was awaiting the settlement of outstanding payments and further engagements with relevant stakeholders to return to the site and continue work. The Chief Executive Officer of the KATH, Dr Paa Kwesi Baidoo, underscored the importance of the project to the hospital’s efforts to expand and strengthen specialised maternal and paediatric healthcare services. He said the facility represented a significant investment in the future of healthcare delivery at the hospital, particularly for mothers, children and families who depended on KATH for specialised medical care. Dr Baidoo stressed the need for sustained collaboration among stakeholders to resolve the outstanding issues and facilitate the resumption and eventual completion of the project. Dr Nawaane described the Maternity and Children’s Block as an important healthcare infrastructure project whose completion would significantly improve maternal and child healthcare delivery at the hospital. He said the Committee recognised the importance of the facility to KATH and the numerous patients who relied on its services. “From the update provided, it is clear that substantial work has gone into the project, including the procurement of essential materials. “We wish to encourage continued engagement among the relevant stakeholders to address the outstanding challenges, particularly those affecting payments and the resumption of construction,” he said. When completed and operational, the facility is expected to strengthen KATH’s capacity to provide specialised maternal and child healthcare services and contribute to efforts to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality.

title: Feds investigating letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to congressional offices
body:
Federal law enforcement officers said they are working to intercept the letters.
The FBI, U.S. Capitol Police and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating "multiple letters containing suspicious substances that were mailed to various addresses nationwide, including multiple Congressional offices," according to a notice sent to Senate staff on Thursday and described to ABC News.
Preliminary information suggests there are over 100 letters circulating in the U.S. mail system that apparently contain white powder, law enforcement sources told ABC News.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer was one of the lawmakers to whom an intercepted letter was sent, according to a person familiar.
The district office of Connecticut Democratic Senator Chris Murphy was also sent a letter, but it was intercepted by postal service authorities, according to a statement from his office.
"Due to those efforts and various safety protocols, the Senator and staff were not in immediate danger. Our office is grateful for the investigators involved in this incident, and we intend to continue close coordination as the investigation continues," Murphy's office said in a statement.
ABC News confirmed that Democratic lawmakers Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand and Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester were also sent intercepted letters.
"This afternoon, a suspicious piece of mail was sent to my New York City office and was safely intercepted by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service," Gillibrand said in a statement Thursday. "I am deeply grateful to the postal inspectors for protecting my staff."
“Senator Blunt Rochester’s office was sent a letter with a suspicious substance. The letter was intercepted by Capitol Police and taken for investigation. Thanks to existing safety protocols and the swift action taken by the officers, neither the Senator nor her staff are in any immediate danger," Blunt Rochester's office said in a statement.
The Senate Sargent at Arms warned in the notice that some letters could make it to congressional offices.
The Senate Sargent at Arms recommended treating any suspicious letters with caution, and that suspicious letters contain multiple postage markings, according to the notice.
Additionally, the House Sergeant at Arms sent a notice to members warning of these letters sent around the country, but for safety, offices could forward the district mail to the Capitol complex for rigorous screening.
"The Office of the Sergeant at Arms (SAA) has been made aware of reports of letters containing suspicious white powder substances received by public officials throughout the United States," according to the notice described to ABC News.
The Capitol Police referred ABC News to the FBI for comment.
The FBI confirmed in a statement Thursday that it was working with the U.S. Postal Inspection Service in a probe over "a series of suspicious mailings sent to various addresses nationwide, including Secretary of State offices and their related election offices."
Those mailings also "contained an unknown substance," according to the FBI.
Election offices in at least 15 states have reported receiving or being the intended recipient of suspicious mail, as of Thursday evening.
"We are also working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters. The FBI and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service will continue to safeguard the public and secure elections for American citizens," the FBI said in a statement.
It is unclear whether these letters are connected to the letters recently sent to Secretaries of States offices around the country.

title: Tatarstan interested in Indian IT specialists, medics, welders
body:
KAZAN, October 16. /TASS/. Tatarstan is interested in English-speaking engineering and technical personnel, IT specialists, healthcare professionals and highly qualified welders from India, Elmira Zaripova, the republic’s Labor, Employment and Social Protection Minister, said at the second Russia-India business forum "TIME."
"Today, we have compatible skills. India represents not only workers but also English-speaking technical and engineering personnel, specialists in IT and healthcare, and highly qualified welders. I’d like to note that welders from India are familiar with Russia’s federal standards, especially in manual arc underwater welding. That is, they are familiar with our standards, and this too brings us closer together," Zaripova said at the session titled, "Labor Market: problems and prospects."
According to her, Tatarstan has an almost zero unemployment rate: its approximately 3,000 unemployed citizens account for less than 0.2% of the labor force, and there are 14 to 25 jobs per unemployed.
In 2026, Tatarstan obtained a quota to attract more than 3,000 workers from India, and in 2025, the republic granted over 600 work permits to Indian nationals, Zaripova noted. More than 1,000 Indians are officially employed in the region. The median age of an Indian worker is 29, an age in which people have long-term carrier plans. In addition, there are around 1,300 Indian students at universities, mostly medical and technical ones, in Tatarstan.
"The prospects include the harmonization of standards for the recognition of qualifications. Otherwise, a specialist trained in the country of origin will not be employed here, primarily in fields such as welding, engineering, medicine and IT. This is an objective that is pursued at the federal level too," Zaripova concluded.
The second Russia-India business forum "TIME" is being held at the Centre of Unique Craftsmanship (TSUM) in Kazan from October 14 to 17. TASS is the event’s general media partner.

title: CSTO to contribute to peace, stability in Central Asia — Secretary General
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) Secretariat aims to promote the formation of a new Eurasian security architecture, and the organization will continue to contribute to ensuring peace and stability in Central Asia, CSTO Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov said at the CSTO, CIS, and SCO conference on security in Central Asia and Afghanistan.
"The CSTO Secretariat is committed to promoting the formation of a new Eurasian security architecture based on ensuring equal and indivisible security for all states. We will continue to contribute to ensuring peace and stability in Central Asia. We are ready to strengthen cooperation with all partners who share our principles and goals," Masadykov stated.

title: Aircraft loses door shortly after take-off from Abuja
body: By Dickson Omobola A CL60 aircraft operated by Triton Aviation has made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after its crew reported that a door had opened in flight. The aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI, departed Abuja for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, at 4:17 yesterday. The aircraft, according to the serious incident report, was about three nautical miles from the airport and passing 3,000 feet when the crew made a “MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY” distress call at 4:20. The crew reported that a door had opened in flight, prompting air traffic control to direct the aircraft back to Abuja for an emergency landing on Runway 22. The report stated: “At 1620 UTC, APP-RADAR informed Tower DWCO52 a CL60 with registration marking T7SEI that departed Abuja at 1617 UTC runway 22 to DNMM at 3 nautical miles outbound, passing 3000ft made a MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY call. DWC052 reported an open door in flight. Radar vectored the aircraft back to land using runway 22. “16:22 UTC, Fire watch room and Medical team informed to be on standby. Information pertaining to the flight passed to the fire watch room. Fire watch asked to position at A4 and A5. “At 16:29 UTC, Abuja Tower was in contact with DWC052, and the crew asked Tower if they could see their door opened. “The Duty Air Traffic Controller, DATCO, used the birocular to view the aircraft but was unable to view the door because of the position of the aircraft, and the crew was advised. “At 16:34 UTC, DWC052 landed safely on runway 22. On landing, the fuselage of the aircraft was clearly visible to the DATCO and the door was missing from the aircraft. DWC052 was taxied to the International apron extension. At 16:40 UTC DWC052 reported marshaller insight and was parked by the marshaller.” The media team of the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, confirmed the serious incident. The team said: “ Yes, it happened. The investigators are there. We will be releasing an official statement shortly.” The post Aircraft loses door shortly after take-off from Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: FM Sybiha: Ukraine will respond proportionally to Russian attacks on its energy sector
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha made this statement in an interview with Ukrinform.
“If we see that Russia is striking our facilities, there will be a proportional response. We are ready for a ceasefire, but Russia must be compelled to agree to it,” Sybiha emphasized.
He also noted that Ukraine is working to strengthen its air defense, specifically exploring the possibility of developing its own ballistic missile and obtaining a license to manufacture it.
“All these areas are being explored. We are also looking for many other solutions,” Sybiha emphasized.
According to the minister, the U.S. position remains a key factor in the supply of anti-ballistic interceptors to Ukraine.
“We have the PURL program in place, and we are ready to purchase these weapons [from the U.S. ], and we are ready to increase the procurement budget. Therefore, the decision regarding additional interceptors lies with the American side,” the Ukrainian foreign minister stated.
As reported by Ukrinform, U.S. President Donald Trump criticized Ukraine’s decision to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, claiming that they allegedly contribute to keeping global energy prices high.
On October 15, President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times that Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian oil refineries because Russia continues to attack Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.
Oil prices rose over the course of the week amid uncertainty regarding supplies from the Middle East and a larger-than-expected drawdown in U.S. oil inventories.

title: 3 children, 1 teacher dead in Oregon elementary school shooting, police say
body:
A 16-year-old shot his way through locked doors to get into an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher. He was then shot by a person at the scene who followed him inside, authorities said.
The suspect was found dead inside the school minutes after the shooting was first reported, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.
The three children killed were aged 5, 8 and 11. Another child, 7, and a teacher, 54, were injured and taken to the hospital in critical condition, he said.
The first 911 call came just before 1 p.m. from a person in a vehicle outside Silver Rail Elementary who reported being shot at by someone with a long gun, Krantz told reporters. Further 911 calls came from inside the school, and officers arrived on scene within minutes, police spokesperson Sheila Miller said.
The attacker, who police identified as a Bend resident, was shot and went down inside the school shortly after officers arrived, she said.
Police said they did not know if the shooter knew anyone at the school or whether he had attended.
Children were taken by bus to a nearby church serving as a reunification center for families. Parents hugged, kissed and held their kids’ hands as they walked to their cars, with some bringing along favorite stuffed animals or other comfort items from home.
The school in Bend, which is about 200 kilometres southeast of Portland, had 459 enrolled students as of last year, according to the Oregon Department of Education. The school serves students in kindergarten through fifth grade.
The high-desert city has ballooned in population over the past three decades and is a tourism and outdoor recreation hub near Mount Bachelor.
Classes, sports and extracurriculars were canceled Friday for all 32 schools in the Bend-La Pine district.
The shooting was the 28th mass killing in the U.S. this year, according to a database maintained by The Associated Press and USA Today in partnership with Northeastern University.
The attacker used a pump-action shotgun that was purchased by his mother, according to a law enforcement official briefed on the shooting. The official spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to publicly discuss the investigation.
At a news conference, Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek said her heart was “absolutely broken” and thanked the civilian who pursued the shooter.
“To the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life: Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well,” she said.

title: DPO Removed After Suspected Cultists Renovated Police Outpost In Rivers
body: The Rivers State Police Command has relieved the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in charge of Abuloma Division and the Divisional Officer overseeing the Abuloma Police Outpost, and ordered a full investigation, following reports that suspected cultists renovated the outpost. In a press release signed by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Agabe Kaborlo, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, the Command said it had taken cognisance of a trending social media report and a circulating video alleging that suspected cultists renovated the outpost and visited the facility on Thursday, October 15, 2026, to celebrate the completion of the project. The Command condemned any action or association capable of compromising the integrity, discipline and professional standards of the Nigeria Police Force, or of conferring legitimacy, recognition or acceptance on suspected cult groups or other unlawful organisations. It stressed that police facilities are public institutions established to protect citizens and enforce the law, and must not become platforms through which criminal groups seek public validation or influence. Under the leadership of the Commissioner of Police, CP Olugbenga Adepoju, the Command said it maintains zero tolerance for criminality and for any conduct that undermines public confidence in the Police. It said that the two officers have been queried and relieved of their duties pending the outcome of investigations. The commissioner also ordered a full investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and the veracity of the allegations. The probe will seek to determine the identities and backgrounds of the individuals or groups who financed or facilitated the renovation; the police officers who authorised or approved the project; whether due procedures were followed; whether any officer breached professional standards or compromised the integrity of the Force; and the extent of any involvement by police personnel. The command said it welcomes legitimate community support for improving police facilities, consistent with Section 26(1)(d) of the Nigeria Police Act 2020, which provides for gifts and contributions to the Police General Fund. However, it insisted that such support must not compromise police independence, professional standards or security. The investigation, it said, would establish whether the necessary approvals were obtained and appropriate checks conducted on those who financed or facilitated the renovation, adding that no donation or assistance confers immunity from investigation or prosecution. The command reiterated that it would not condone unprofessional conduct, compromise, or any form of improper association with criminal elements by any police officer, and that all personnel are expected to uphold the highest standards of discipline, integrity and accountability. It said it remains committed to professionalism, transparency, the protection of lives and property, and the fight against cultism and organised crime, and promised that appropriate disciplinary and legal action would be taken against anyone found culpable, in line with the outcome of the investigation and extant laws. The post DPO Removed After Suspected Cultists Renovated Police Outpost In Rivers appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Dubai Police arrest eight over alleged illegal driving licence scam
body: Dubai Police have arrested eight people suspected of running a network that allegedly supplied people with driving licences, the recipients of which could then bypass the usual training and tests involved to get behind the wheel on UAE roads. For Dh10,000 ($2,720), the suspects would procure a driving licence from a neighbouring country for customers who had never travelled there. This allowed buyers to take advantage of the UAE's international driving licence exchange rule, which allows eligible holders to convert the licence directly into a UAE one. Dubai Police's General Department of Criminal Investigation made the arrests in co-ordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA). Police said the suspects used offices belonging to transaction-processing companies in the UAE to approach potential customers and promote their services. Customers were given licences from a neighbouring country without the need to travel there, take driving lessons or pass mandatory driving tests. These licences could then be presented to Dubai's RTA for exchange under international agreements between the UAE and other countries. Dubai Police warned that driving lessons and tests help ensure motorists have the skills and knowledge needed to drive safely. Bypassing these requirements and allowing unqualified people to drive could put other motorists, passengers and pedestrians in danger. Anyone who pays for a driving licence obtained through illegal means may face penalties and legal action. The force said exchanging a fraudulently obtained international licence for a UAE licence does not make the original licence legitimate or remove responsibility for any wrongdoing. Anyone seeking a driving licence is advised to follow official procedures and deal only with authorised entities. Residents are also urged to report individuals or companies offering licences through unlawful means.

title: Israel picks between 'secular democracy or theocracy' in election, chess master Garry Kasparov says
body: When Israelis head to vote on October 27, they won't just be picking the next government; they will be deciding whether Israel becomes "a secular Hebrew democracy, or a rigid, rabbinical theocracy," Garry Kasparov, a Russian chess grandmaster, political activist, and writer, wrote in an op-ed for the New York Times published on Thursday."Just as Abraham Lincoln observed that the government could not persist 'half slave and half free,' Israel cannot go on half theocratic and half secular," Kasparov, whose father was Jewish, argued."Americans resolved that contradiction over four years of brutal civil war. Israel's election on Oct. 27 offers a bloodless way out of this morass," he wrote."Democracies are built on compromise," Kasparov said. "But sometimes a compromise can turn dangerous."Growing up in the Soviet Union shaped Kasparov's view of Israeli democracyHe explained that his upbringing in the Soviet Union shaped his perception of both the US and Israeli democracies. "I see this dynamic at play in two democracies with which I closely identify: the United States and Israel.""As a young Soviet with a Jewish father, I grew up to become a staunch supporter of Israel, an outpost of liberalism surrounded by illiberal, Moscow-backed Arab states," Kasparov wrote."While I rejected the anti-Americanism and anti-Zionism of the Communist regime under which I was raised, I also sought a textured understanding of the United States and Israel."Israel faces a breaking point, risk of permanent rupture"I learned early on that the United States had reached a breaking point just 84 years after independence. America's founders included men who owned slaves and men who did not. They could not both midwife the union and challenge the 'peculiar institution.' This guaranteed the birth of the United States but cursed the young nation with an affliction that nearly caused a permanent rupture."Kasparov believes that Israel is also facing this affliction and risk of permanent rupture. Rather than the divisive issue being slavery, the divisive issue that Kasparov says has placed Israel at this crossroad is the haredi (ultra-Orthodox) draft to the IDF. He clarified in the NYT that "There is, of course, no moral equivalence between the haredim, as the ultra-Orthodox are called in Israel, and slave owners."He cites then-prime minister David Ben-Gurion's original agreement with the haredim as the thing that set in motion the aforementioned split. In 1948 Ben-Gurion approved a temporary agreement with haredi yeshiva students, granting 400 people an exemption from army service to study Torah. Today, upwards of 50,000 people evade IDF draft to study Torah."The pact haunted their descendants and today is sustained by a nationalist far right and an unscrupulous prime minister willing to bend the law to stay in power," Kasparov said.Haredi draft is 'corroding' Israel's social compact"In Israel today, ultra-Orthodox political power is corroding the social compact that holds the country together.""Israelis of Ben-Gurion's generation may not have understood the kind of foundation they were laying," Kasparov argued. "They may have presumed they were simply handing out draft exemptions to a few hundred young men. Many of the American founders similarly expected slavery to peter out over time.""Instead, slavery expanded significantly after 1776, just as religious influence in Israel exploded in the decades following 1948. The draft exemption became especially infuriating to secular Israeli Jews after Oct. 7 and the war in Gaza."The haredi draft is not the only way Kasparov thinks that religious influence is corruptive to Israel. He argues that their power over Israeli law, from marriages, divorces, and funerals to transportation and public services on Shabbat, is "toxic" and unfair to the millions of Israelis who do not observe Shabbat."The ultra-Orthodox parties in the Knesset are so single-minded that it seems they will support anyone, no matter how clouded by accusations of misdeeds, who preserves their special privileges," Kasparov wrote in the NYT. "This is how the haredim have become indispensable accomplices and supporters to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition."Netanyahu's relationship with the haredim in Knesset"Without the ultra-Orthodox, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would not have backing for many of his authoritarian endeavors," he argued, and similarly, "Without Mr. Netanyahu, the ultra-Orthodox would lose their protected status."Despite his comments that Israel is choosing between secular democracy or rigid theocracy, Kasparov added that he does not want religion and culture to be suppressed. "When I was growing up in the Soviet Union, Communist thugs enforced atheism and suppressed Jewish culture. This is not what I want for Israel.""I simply believe in equality before the law and an Israel that embodies its founders' aspirations of being a 'light unto the nations,' rather than an international pariah held back by far-right and religious special interests," Kasparov wrote."Israel's election on Oct. 27 offers a bloodless way out of this morass."

title: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says
body:
Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said.
Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest.
“He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote.
Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy.
Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted.
The legal news Telegram channel Slovo Zashchite reported that Kynev suffered two fractures to his shinbone after being beaten during his arrest and was taken to the hospital at Moscow’s Matrosskaya Tishina detention center. His lawyer, Mikhail Biryukov, previously said he could neither confirm nor deny that account.
The Medved detention center, in Moscow’s Yuzhnoye Medvedkovo district, previously held opposition politician Ilya Yashin while he was under investigation for spreading “false information” about the Russian military, the investigative outlet Agentstvo noted .
Other former inmates include police rights activist Vladimir Vorontsov, former monk Nikolai Romanov and Andrei Bykov, the former head of the Federal Penitentiary Service’s research institute.
Yelena Masyuk, a former member of the presidential human rights council, previously documented allegations of extortion and abuse at the facility, including beatings by fellow inmates and cases in which prisoners were driven to suicide.
Kynev remained in Russia and had regularly commented on the Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections before his arrest.
He estimated that turnout would have been around 40% and the ruling United Russia party would have won no more than 35% of the vote without electoral fraud. He also warned that the party’s record haul of 349 seats could backfire.
A specialist in Russian regional politics and elections, Kynev previously taught at the Higher School of Economics and headed independent election monitor Golos’ analytical department.
The Justice Ministry designated him a “foreign agent” in February 2026, accusing him of spreading false information about government policies and the electoral system, as well as cooperating with an organization designated “undesirable.”

title: Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating protests
body:
Prominent student leader Neha Bora, center, shouts slogans as she is detained by the police during a youth demonstration demanding the resignation of the country's election chief Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, Friday, Oct. 16, 2026. Vipin/AP hide caption
NEW DELHI — Thousands of Indians thronged a bustling thoroughfare in the heart of the capital, waving the national flag and demanding the resignation of the country's election chief, the latest show of public dissent against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
The protesters rallied in Connaught Place, one of New Delhi's busiest commercial districts, responding to a call by the youth "Cockroach" movement, whose leader Abhijeet Dipke was detained by police ahead of the demonstration. Protesters spanning generations joined the rally, reflecting broad public anger and intensifying pressure on the country's top election official.
Protests by the youth and opposition parties have intensified over an ongoing review of voter lists that has removed more than 130 million names since last year. Critics say the exercise is politically motivated, threatens to disenfranchise millions more, and has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims. They have demanded the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar.
Student activist Neha Bora, center, shouts slogans during a youth demonstration demanding the resignation of the country's election chief Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, Friday, Oct. 16, 2026. Prabhat Mehrotra/AP hide caption
The Election Commission and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration deny the allegations and say the revision is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries.
Friday's protest was part of a growing campaign that has put Modi's government under pressure and comes a week after a police crackdown on protesters in New Delhi.
The demonstrators vastly outnumbered the security personnel lining the road, while columns of riot police stood watch.
Police had earlier asked people not to join the rally and offered to let a small group gather to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem. In anticipation of the protests, authorities also closed Central Park, a green space surrounded by Connaught Place's white colonial-era buildings, on Friday and Saturday.
Modi has not publicly commented on the protests. Some of his party leaders have dismissed the demonstrators as "anarchists" and suggested, without offering evidence, that they are backed by foreign powers.
Police detained Dipke, the founder of the "Cockroach" movement, ahead of the demonstrations. He had urged supporters unable to travel to New Delhi to raise the flag and demonstrate in their own communities.
Security personnel patrol ahead of a tricolor (Indian flag) waving protest called by the youth "Cockroach" movement demanding the resignation of India's election chief in central New Delhi, India, Friday, Oct. 16, 2026. Channi Anand/AP Photo/Channi Anand/AP hide caption
A live video posted on the movement's Instagram account showed Dipke leaving a house and heading toward the street, where police officers intercepted him. After a brief exchange, officers hauled him into a police vehicle and drove away.
"Waving the tricolor (Indian flag) is not a crime," he told reporters Thursday.
The "Cockroach" movement began as an online satirical campaign this summer after India's chief justice compared unemployed young people to parasites. Many young Indians embraced the remark, adopting the cockroach as a symbol of resilience. It has since expanded into a nationwide protest movement of young people. Protests led by the group forced the resignation of Modi's education minister in July, a rare setback for the prime minister, who has been in power for more than 12 years.
It remains unclear whether the protests will grow into a wider political movement. Modi's government remains electorally strong, and anger over voter lists may not necessarily translate into support for the opposition, which has used the issue to criticize his Hindu nationalist government.
