title: Team digitally traces Polish Revolutionary War hero’s West Point contributions
body: Nearly 250 years after 30-year-old Tadeusz Kościuszko established himself as one of the Continental Army’s most brilliant — and much-needed — combat engineers, West Point and three members of Poland’s Foundation for the Virtualization of National Cultural Heritage teamed up to ensure Kościuszko’s legacy endures. The three-man team traveled from Kościuszko’s native Poland to use 3D scanning, aerial photography and other digital technology to digitally document Revolutionary War-era sites and artifacts associated with the Polish-American hero, according to West Point . As West Point’s earthwork fortifications and landscapes face continual erosion, the project, titled “Tadeusz Kościuszko at West Point: The Digital Heritage of the Polish-American Hero of Freedom,” seeks to preserve the physical traces of the Polish Revolutionary War hero’s contribution to buttressing West Point from the invading British forces. From Sept. 14 to 29, the Polish team comprising Piotr Bialobrzycki, Damian Kuc and Jerzy Pajo worked to create “3D digital records of the sites as they exist today,” with the project providing “a benchmark for future conservation while eventually allowing people around the world to virtually explore historic resources at West Point… [and] create a precise and lasting digital record of Kościuszko’s material heritage at West Point,” a news release reads. Project director Bialobrzycki led the terrestrial laser scanning of eight heritage sites at West Point, while Kuc, “the project’s lead specialist in 3D scanning and modeling, used structured-light scanning to document cannons, commemorative plaques, elements of the Kościuszko Monument, the Great Chain and selected artifacts, including Kościuszko’s sword at the West Point Museum,” according to West Point. For his part, Pajor used his background in professional photography to document the sites with multimedia and gigapixel imagery, which will eventually support virtual walkthroughs of the historic site. “We wanted to use this moment to demonstrate that the Polish contribution to the American Revolution was concrete and consequential,” Bialobrzycki said. “Its traces can still be read in the terrain, fortifications, monuments, documents and historical objects at West Point.” Kościuszko’s journey from Polish tutor to war hero was non sequitur — all thanks to an unsuccessful attempt to elope with a lord’s daughter back in Poland. After discovering his brother had spent all the family’s inheritance, Kościuszko was hired to tutor Louise Sosnowska, a wealthy lord’s daughter. The pair fell in love and attempted to elope in the fall of 1775 after Lord Sosnowski refused Kosciuszko’s request. According to the Smithsonian , “Kosciuszko told various friends, Sosnowski’s guards overtook their carriage on horseback, dragged it to a stop, knocked Kosciuszko unconscious, and took Louise home by force.” Broke, heartbroken and perhaps fearing repercussions for his actions, Kościuszko set sail across the Atlantic in June 1776. Upon arriving in Philadelphia, John Hancock appointed him a colonel in the Continental Army that October, and Benjamin Franklin hired him to design and build forts on the Delaware River to help defend Philadelphia from the British navy, according to the Smithsonian. The Pole oversaw the damming of rivers and flooded fields to stem a British pursuit following their victory at Fort Ticonderoga in 1777. This action bought time for the patriots to regroup and prepare for their first major victory of the war — Saratoga. Fortifying Bemis Heights overlooking the Hudson, Kościuszko’s design contributed to the surrender of Gen. John Burgoyne and precipitated the French’s entry into the war. From there, Kościuszko oversaw the defense of West Point, with his fortifications so thorough that the British never deigned to attempt an assault. At war’s end, he was promoted to brigadier general, with Thomas Jefferson praising the Pole : “As pure a son of liberty as I have ever known.”

title: No MMDCE can say they don’t see galamsey – Local Government Ministry
body: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, says Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives can no longer pretend they do not see illegal mining happening in their areas. He described the sector Ministry as perhaps the most culpable for looking the other way while galamsey destroys lives. “Every piece of land falls within a district, municipality and metropolis. I am here to support the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources who has been battling with this situation,” he said. Speaking at a briefing ahead of the Green Ashanti Initiative to restore the Jimi River and degraded lands at Tasleman near Obuasi, the Minister announced a firm intervention to force local authorities to take ownership. “We have put together a conference that we will soon invite all MMDCEs to attend. The reason is that no MMDCE can tell me that they don’t see what is happening within their jurisdictions, and so we at the Ministry of Local Government are perhaps the most culpable when it comes to looking the other way and allowing this level of deprivation to take place,” said Mr. Ayariga. The Minister said the fight against galamsey can no longer be left to one Ministry. “We want to step up our game and make it not just the responsibility of the Ministry of Lands. When this goes on, it is equally the responsibility of the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs. We want to share the blame with him. “Everybody has taken him on over what has happened, but it happens within the geographical space that is managed by a set-up that is the local government authority, and so it can’t just be the responsibility of the Minister for Lands. It is the responsibility of the traditional leaders who own the lands and all of us. It is time for us to own up and do our part to support the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources,” he said. Current data shows 120 of Ghana’s 261 MMDAs are directly affected by illegal mining, with the government identifying 44 critical hotspot areas requiring permanent security presence. In the Western Region alone, 12 out of 14 districts are under siege. The worst impacted river systems are the Pra, Ankobra, Offin, Tano, Birim and Densu – rivers that serve millions. The Jimi River, which was inspected by the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, on the same day, has had its course diverted by illegal miners at Tasleman, causing siltation that threatens the Jimi Dam, which supplies water to over 200,000 people in Obuasi and Adanse. Beyond rivers and farmlands, the Minister’s concern comes as health data show devastating human impact. The briefing formed part of the 153-hectare Jimi Land Reclamation and River Watercourse Rehabilitation Project, a pilot under the Green Ashanti Initiative. The project is led by the Ashanti Green Initiative and supported by AngloGold Ashanti. It seeks to restore the diverted Jimi River, reclaim degraded lands in six stages, and create alternative livelihoods through the cultivation of trees. The tour was led by Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, who warned that “we may get the money, but we will die after the environment is destroyed.” It included the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah.

title: ‘Close to our best’ – Kompany defends Bayern players after consecutive draws
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has defended his players after consecutive draws, insisting the German champions are close to finding their best form. Bayern drew 2-2 with Augsburg in the Bundesliga before a 3-3 draw away to Viking in the Champions League. They had to come from behind in both matches, raising questions about their finishing and defending ahead of Saturday’s home game against RB Leipzig. But Kompany pointed to Bayern’s attacking output as evidence that the team is making progress. “We want to attack,” he said at Friday’s pre-match press conference. “In the last two matches we shot 50 times on goal. If we do a few things better, then we are not too far from our very best version.” Kompany said his players remained “sharp and motivated” and were relishing a demanding run of fixtures. After Leipzig, Bayern face Arsenal in the Champions League, Bundesliga leaders Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund, with a German Cup tie against Magdeburg also on the schedule. “These moments that some people think might be difficult, we say these are the best moments you can have in your career,” he said. “If you win these matches, then you have created some moments.” The coach added that Bayern’s players were pushing themselves in training and would have to show their response on the pitch. On the defensive concerns, Kompany said the team had discussed what needed to improve and was ready to move on. “We’ve got a process. We discuss things as a team or with individuals. It’s important to draw a line under things quickly,” he said. “Now we go to the next game.” Kompany expects a difficult test against Leipzig, who he said were arriving in Munich with confidence and had dangerous wide players and attackers. Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer had not trained ahead of the match because of a foot issue, while Aleksandar Pavlović trained normally on Thursday. Kompany said Pavlović would be available if he completed another full session. The post ‘Close to our best’ – Kompany defends Bayern players after consecutive draws appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian Tu-22M3 long-range bombers conduct planned flight over Baltic Sea
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Russian Tupolev Tu-22M3 long-range bombers conducted a planned flight over international waters of the Baltic Sea accompanied by Su-35S and Su-30SM fighter aircraft, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Tu-22M3 long-range bombers of the Russian Aerospace Forces conducted a planned flight in the airspace over neutral waters of the Baltic Sea. Su-35S and Su-30SM aircraft of the Aerospace Forces provided fighter support during the flight," the ministry said in a statement.
The flight lasted over four hours and at some stages of the flight the Tu-22M3 long-range bombers were escorted by fighter jets of foreign states, it said.
The crews of Russia’s long-range aircraft regularly perform flights over the neutral waters of the Arctic, the Northern Atlantic, the Pacific Ocean, the Baltic and Black Seas, the ministry said.
"The aircraft of Russia’s Aerospace Forces perform all the flights in strict compliance with the international rules of using the airspace," the ministry stressed.

title: What Albertans need to know about voting in the referendum
body:
The provincial referendum has 10 questions about immigration policy, constitutional reform, and whether Alberta should remain in Canada or hold a binding, second referendum on quitting the country.
Advance voting locations opened Tuesday and close Saturday night.
Over 1,400 polling stations will be open Monday from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Here’s what to expect when you go to vote:
Get familiar with the ballot questions ahead of time, which are on the Elections Alberta website. Officials say it will help avoid confusion and delays.
They say they’re expecting a record turnout of between 80 and 85 per cent of Alberta’s nearly three million electors.
You have as much time as you want to fill in the 10 ballots, but officials estimate it will take most people about two minutes.
You should get a “where to vote” card in the mail ahead of time if you’re registered. Otherwise, visit Elections Alberta’s website to find out where to vote.
You must vote in your electoral division during advance voting or at your assigned location on Monday.
You’ll need one government-issued ID with your correct name, current address and photo, such as a driver’s licence. You can use two pieces of ID that both have your full name, with one showing your current address.
There are 50 forms of acceptable ID listed on Elections Alberta’s website that can be one of those two pieces, from a library card or a hunting licence to a bank statement or vehicle registration.
Elections Alberta says it will accept expired forms of ID, including a certificate of Indian Status Card, provided it still has the correct name.
Another option, in special circumstances, is to bring an attestation form signed by an authorized person such as a First Nation band manager or a student housing staffer.
A voting officer will ask you to sign a declaration that confirms your eligibility — including that you are a Canadian citizen, at least 18 years old and that you normally reside in Alberta.
There are 10 ballots, in different colours for easy identification. You can mark some of them, all of them or none. Your choice.
The ballots go into separate boxes to make it easier to count them and to lessen the chances of a mistake spoiling one long ballot.
What if I’m still in line when the polls close at 8 p.m.?
Stay in line. Don’t leave. You will be allowed to vote.
By law, the votes need to be counted by hand within 48 hours.
Question 10 — about separation — is to be counted first. Officials say early results are to be released after 8 p.m. Monday, with the final count announced in the early hours Tuesday.
The results of the other nine questions should be completed and announced by Wednesday.

title: Michael Carrick says Man United have already 'moved on' from Lisandro Martinez outburst
body: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said the team has addressed Lisandro Martinez's controversial remarks about the club's management and moved on from the controversy. United defender Martinez had to issue an apology on Thursday for criticising ​the ​club's hierarchy following their ​Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, highlighting the lack of investments and singling out United director of football Jason Wilcox. Martinez then held talks with the manager and ⁠senior officials, before issuing an apology. Carrick said the chapter is now closed. “It's done really,” Carrick said on Friday. “We've moved on from that. It was one of those things. He has come out and acknowledged the situation and as a group we have moved on. “It is really not a drama for us as a group. The boys have trained really well, there was a really good feeling around training this morning. “From the outside [you are] after some big information about big discussions but it was pretty simple. We all understood the situation and what it meant. He made his statement and acknowledges that it was a mistake from him and that was it really.” 🗣️ "It was pretty simple." Michael Carrick on discussions with Lisandro Martinez that led to an apology from the defender. pic.twitter.com/JSWGOx9TbY — Sky Sports News (@SkySportsNews) October 16, 2026 In his apology, Martinez said he got carried away in his post-match interview. “Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager,” Martinez said in an Instagram post. “It was a very positive conversation where we were able to exchange ​views ⁠and speak openly about what ‌happened after Tuesday's game.” Martinez said that his frustration following the defeat had got the better of him and apologised for choosing the wrong moment to air his feelings. “Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity,” he said. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

title: Turkey and Morocco Lead Fuel Supplies to Russia as Seaborne Imports Fall 44%
body:
Turkey and Morocco became Russia’s largest suppliers of seaborne oil products in September, as total imports fell 44% from August’s record, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).
Russia imported 234,000 metric tons, down from 416,000 in August. Despite the decline, September remained the second-highest month in the think tank’s data, which extend back to January 2022.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The figures cover seaborne shipments and do not establish that Russia’s domestic refining capacity has recovered.
Turkey supplied 55% of September’s imports. Four cargoes loaded at the southern port of Mersin carried 130,000 tons of fuel worth €94 million ($106 million), according to CREA.
Three cargoes contained gasoline and one contained diesel. The total was about three and a half times the 37,000 tons shipped from Mersin in August.
Russia supplied 89% of Mersin’s seaborne oil-product imports in the first half of 2026. CREA said some of that fuel might now be returning to Russia amid its domestic shortages. The loading port does not, by itself, establish where a cargo was refined.
Morocco was Russia’s second-largest supplier, shipping 96,000 tons in September, up from 70,000 in August and 39,000 in July.
All three September cargoes contained gasoline, according to Kpler shipping data cited by CREA. They were loaded at the Horizon terminal in Tangier and unloaded at St. Petersburg and Murmansk, with Gazprom and Surgutneftegas among the listed buyers.
Russia received no seaborne oil-product shipments from India in September, compared with 160,000 tons in August. However, a 40,000-ton cargo arrived from India in early October.
South Korean deliveries fell to 8,000 tons in September from 95,000 in August. None had arrived in October as of Oct. 13, CREA said, linking the slowdown to threatened legal action against South Korean exporters.
Kyiv Post previously reported on questions over South Korea’s fuel shipments . Seoul subsequently said the shipments were not prohibited , while investigating the trade.
The latest report’s August figures differ from earlier estimates cited by Kyiv Post. Its September comparison uses an August total of 416,000 tons.
CREA also identified seven September shipments to EU ports from refineries processing Russian crude, despite the bloc’s ban on products made from Russian oil, which took effect on Jan. 21, 2026.
Six shipments came from India and one from Turkey. Italy received three, Romania two, and Spain and the Republic of Cyprus one each.
The refinery’s use of Russian crude does not establish that every exported cargo contains Russian-derived fuel. CREA identified the shipments as requiring scrutiny under EU guidance.
Refineries in India, Turkey and Brunei that process Russian crude exported €1 billion ($1.12 billion) of oil products to sanctioning countries in September. CREA estimated that €295 million ($332 million) of those products were refined from Russian crude. Recipients included the EU, Australia, the US and New Zealand.
The findings come after Washington’s Oct. 9 agreement to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports , which drew objections from European governments. Kyiv Post has examined the proposed supplies against fuel consumption . September’s lower import total alone does not establish how much additional diesel Russia can produce or export.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: We can’t have criminal justice system run by criminals – Adebayo
body: By John Alechenu Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has vowed to overhaul Nigeria’s criminal justice system if elected in 2027. Adebayo said the system as presently run helps rich criminals and corrupt public officials escape justice while jailing the poor for petty offences. He spoke on Thursday in Lagos at an annual lecture organised by the Committee for the Defence of Human Rights, CDHR, themed “Understanding Human Rights Beyond Emotions and Personal Interests.” His address, titled “The Counter-Intuitive Architecture of Human Rights,” was delivered on his behalf by his Campaign’s Chief Media Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, at the Airport Hotel, Ikeja. “It’s just unfortunate that those who administer Nigeria’s criminal justice system are often adjudged, rightly or wrongly, criminals by the society,” Adebayo said. The SDP Candidate further said, “This diminishes trust in the system and consequently creates a dangerous culture of self-help because the current system helps rich criminals and corrupt public officials to escape justice while the innocent or a petty criminal who steals a one thousand naira bread is sentenced to 10 years in jail. The one who steals trillions from the treasury is taken to and from court in luxury jeeps. “Our administration will overhaul Nigeria’s criminal system in a way that ensures equal delivery of justice, punishes criminals and protects the innocent and the poor. We cannot have a criminal justice system run by criminals.” Adebayo argued that human rights must be protected especially when it is unpopular to do so, noting that rights are not rewards for virtue but structural safeguards against arbitrariness. Citing John Adams’ defence of British soldiers in the 1770 Boston Massacre, Jewish lawyers defending Nazi sympathisers, and defence counsels at the Yugoslavia war crimes tribunal, he argued that defending due process for “monsters” protects the innocent. “The true metric of a society’s commitment to human rights is not how it treats its saints, but how it treats its perceived monsters,” he said. He also challenged civil society to move beyond what he called “prebendal activism” and confront out-of-school children, electoral manipulation and clampdown on protests. “If Chief Gani Fawehinmi were alive today and Babangida were to suffer unjust treatment, Gani would be the first to stand in his defence,” Adebayo said. He accused the current administration of building a “comprehensive rigging machine” ahead of 2027 because it cannot win on performance. The post We can’t have criminal justice system run by criminals – Adebayo appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Pres. Pezeshkian meets with Georgian PM in Yerevan
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 16 (MNA) – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met and held talks with Prime Minister of Georgia Irakli Kobakhidze in Yerevan on the sidelines of 17th Summit of Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
During the meeting, Pezeshkian and Kobakhidze discussed host of issues, including bilateral ties, recent developments between the two countries and also issues of mutual interest.
Referring to the clear position of martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyed Ali Khamenei on the prohibition of development of nuclear weapons, the Iranian president stressed, “Iran is not pursuing nuclear weapons, and we consider the destructive propaganda against our country to be lies.”
Pezeshkian said Iran has always been prepared for negotiations, but warned that attempts to force the country into submission would fail. “They (enemies) think they can make us surrender, but we will not bow to coercion,” he stated.
Addressing US sanctions against Iran, the president said the measures are outside the bounds of humanitarian principles. He also described the attacks carried out against Iran in recent months as “unjustifiable and inhumane.”
Pezeshkian also emphasized the need to expand economic, cultural and tourism relations between Iran and Georgia through practical measures. He said the two countries need to develop an operational plan with a clear timetable to translate their shared goals into concrete action.
For his part, Kobakhidze said Georgia has a clear position on relations with neighboring countries and opposes any foreign interference in their internal affairs.
Referring to the cultural and geographical commonalities between Iran and Georgia, the Georgian prime minister said friendship and cooperation are the guiding principles of bilateral relations.

title: Russian Drones Kill Kharkiv Market Traders, Plunges City Into Blackouts
body:
Russian drones killed two traders at a Kharkiv market and struck critical infrastructure on Friday, Oct. 16, leaving 280,000 consumers without power as attacks hit four districts of Ukraine’s second-largest city.
The dead were a 71-year-old woman and a 58-year-old man, Kharkiv regional Gov. Oleh Syniehubov said. Mayor Ihor Terekhov identified both as market traders.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Officials reported 19 people affected by the attacks. Ten were hospitalized, including two in serious condition. The figures were released as further strikes were being reported across the city.
Medics resuscitated a man wounded near the heart following the morning attack on Kharkiv, Viktor Zabashta, director of the regional emergency medical center, told reporters, according to Suspilne Kharkiv.
He described the man’s condition as critical and said more than a dozen other injured people needed medical care, most for shrapnel wounds.
Eleven ambulance crews responded, Zabashta said. One woman with multiple shrapnel wounds declined hospitalization, though medics were trying to persuade her to accept further treatment.
Drone impacts were reported in the Osnovianskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, and Industrialnyi districts during the morning.
Mayor Terekhov said an attack on critical infrastructure cut electricity to 280,000 customers. The initial reports did not specify when power would be restored.
At about 11:57 a.m., another drone struck the roof of a civilian business in the Nemyshlianskyi district, injuring two people.
A separate Russian drone attack hit a shopping center in central Sumy on Friday morning, injuring three people, the regional State Emergency Service said. The strike damaged the building’s roof and facade.

title: Abu Dhabi scientists use AI to develop pain killer 'more effective than morphine'
body: Researchers in the UAE have used artificial intelligence to develop a pain killer that they believe could be more effective than morphine. Insilico Medicine , a clinical-stage biotechnology company with scientists working in Abu Dhabi's Masdar City, created the pill to treat acute and chronic pain. The drug, known as ISM9528, has produced promising during results initial trials and the next step is to test it on humans. Nine out of 10 potential drugs that reach the human testing stage fail to be approved , health experts say. But there has been cause for optimism among the Insilico team. “To see a non-opioid candidate outperform morphine in preclinical models is unprecedented,” Alex Aliper, president and co-founder of the company, told The National . Insilico believe the drug could be used as an alternative to opioid medication, reducing the risk of dependence and addiction. When asked about reported side effects, Mr Aliper said it was "so far, so good". Tests showed a "very clean profile on several species in preclinical studies – we will conduct an extensive safety evaluation in further clinical trials". The company said the global pain medicine market was worth more than $100 billion. There is a significant need for effective non-addictive treatments, it added. “If you have a safe, non-addictive way to treat pain, that’s a game changer,” Mr Aliper said. The Insilico team in Abu Dhabi are also in the early stages of developing a drug that they hope could be used to treat a number of cancers, including glioblastoma, which aggressively attacks the brain. The researchers work at Insilico’s AI and drug discovery centre in Masdar City. Most of the company’s AI team is based in Abu Dhabi, with other offices in Boston, Montreal, Hong Kong and Shanghai. “Developing ISM9528, a potential treatment for pain, right here in Abu Dhabi demonstrates how the UAE's thriving innovation ecosystem has made huge leaps over the past few years," said Ahmed Al Suwaidi, Insilico’s associate director of strategic partnerships and business development for Middle East. The company is using "advanced locally based AI capabilities to develop ground-breaking, real-world medical solutions that address a critical global health care challenge", he added. Insilico’s executives described the development of the two drugs as a significant regional milestone, as the discovery of novel medicine had historically been concentrated in a small number of countries. They said the Abu Dhabi team showed how the UAE could expand drug discovery capabilities and develop medicine for global use. Insilico was founded in 2014 and began developing its AI platform that year. It launched the first end-to-end AI-driven platform Pharma.AI, in 2020. The platform helps researchers identify biological mechanisms linked to disease, select a target and design molecules that could act on it. Researchers then synthesise selected molecules and test them in labs and preclinical models. New horizons The company said it normally took about 12 to 18 months after starting a project to nominate a preclinical candidate, compared with about five years in traditional drug discovery processes. A preclinical candidate is the term for a potential new drug chosen to undergo safety testing, before being tested on humans. Insilico said it was on track to nominate about one candidate a month this year, while large pharmaceutical companies typically nominate four or five a year. The National reported this month about how the company was working to develop a drug to tackle blood cancer. The company believes the use of AI helps to reduce the number of research cycles and narrows down which molecules to make and test. “It’s like having a more precise way to model biology and chemistry at your disposal,” Mr Aliper said. “You have an intelligent system designing molecules for you, with your guidance.” Insilico estimates that its approach could bring the cost of early drug discovery down from tens of millions of dollars to millions. Mr Aliper said that could make it more viable to pursue treatments for rare diseases that have attracted less investment. But AI does not shorten the human trial process, the company added. Clinical trials can take about a decade to complete, depending on the disease, and are subject to regulatory review. “The analogy we use is there is a highway,” Mr Aliper said. "You can overtake cars on the highway, move really fast, but when you reach downtown, that is clinical trials. You need to move with the speed of traffic.”

title: Ghana, Germany explore stronger partnership in technical and vocational education
body: Minister for Education Haruna Iddrisu has held discussions with German Ambassador to Ghana Frederik Landshöft on strengthening bilateral cooperation in education, with a particular focus on Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). The meeting focused on opportunities for international partnerships to improve skills training and equip young people with practical competencies that match the changing demands of the labour market. Both sides discussed the importance of collaboration in preparing students for employment and addressing skills gaps across various industries. Mr Iddrisu emphasised the role of strategic partnerships in advancing Ghana’s education agenda, improving learning outcomes and strengthening employability through industry-relevant training. He highlighted the need for education and skills development programmes to respond to the practical requirements of employers and the wider economy. According to the Ministry of Education engagement reaffirms Ghana’s commitment to working with Germany and other international partners to expand opportunities for skills development and improve the quality of technical and vocational education.

title: AMA urges motorists and road users to comply with traffic regulations
body: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has urged motorists and other road users to observe road traffic regulations and exercise caution to ensure safety on the roads, following the completion of repair and paving works on a section of Kwame Nkrumah Avenue in Accra’s Central Business District (CBD). The appeal follows the completion of sectional repair and paving works on the Lava U-turn and the stretch of Kwame Nkrumah Avenue between the Derby Avenue junction and the Selwyn Market Street junction in Accra’s Central Business District (CBD). The rehabilitation followed concerns over severe abrasions and potholes that had developed along the busy stretch, slowing vehicular traffic and creating potential safety risks to pedestrians and other road users The Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, inspected the completed works as part of efforts to improve road safety, ease traffic congestion and enhance mobility within the city’s commercial centre. Speaking after the inspection, Mr Allotey emphasised the importance of regular road maintenance, explaining that well-maintained roads were essential for supporting commercial activities, reducing travel delays and ensuring the safety and convenience of the public. The Assembly consequently called on motorists, commercial drivers, pedestrians and other road users to comply with traffic regulations, exercise caution and use the rehabilitated sections responsibly to preserve the road surface and minimise the risk of accidents. The completed works are expected to improve traffic flow around the Lava U-turn and adjoining junctions, which serve as important access points for commercial vehicles, traders and other road users within the CBD. The Mayor was accompanied during the inspection by the Metropolitan Co-ordinating Director, Mr Douglas N.K. Annoful, and the Metropolitan Director of Finance, Mr Abeeku Amissah. Before the commencement of the works, the Assembly announced the temporary closure of the affected sections to facilitate essential repairs and paving aimed at restoring the road surface and improving its durability. The rehabilitation forms part of the AMA’s broader efforts to address infrastructure challenges across the metropolis and provide a safer, more accessible and orderly environment for businesses and the travelling public.

title: Sam George urges One Million Coders participants to complete all three levels
body: Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has urged participants in the One Million Coders Programme (OMCP) to complete all three levels of the training to improve their employability and access a wider range of job opportunities. He made the appeal on Thursday, October 15, 2026, during a visit to the Ho Community Information Centre in the Volta Region to assess the programme’s progress, engage learners and identify challenges affecting implementation. The visit was attended by Volta Regional Minister James Gunu, the Administrator of the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communications (GIFEC), Tanko Rashid Computer, and officials from the Ministry and GIFEC. Mr George explained that the programme is structured into three progressive stages: Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced. He noted that although some learners might be eager to seek employment after completing the introductory level, employers increasingly require more advanced technical skills. He therefore encouraged participants to progress through the full course to strengthen their competencies and improve their prospects in the competitive digital job market. The Minister said completing all three stages could open up opportunities for participants both in Ghana and internationally, including remote work with foreign companies. He urged learners to remain committed to the training, stressing the importance of acquiring the advanced skills needed to meet the growing demand for digital talent.

title: Starlink speeds in Ukraine restored after brief restrictions – Zelenskyy
body:
Starlink speeds in Ukraine are recovering following the introduction of restrictions, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

"Is the speed recovering? Yes," Zelenskyy said at a press briefing in Brussels on Friday.

At the same time, the president said that the reduction in Starlink speeds had prevented Ukrainian forces from intercepting some Russian jet-powered drones that attacked civilians.

"We use specialized interceptors that move at high speed. Interceptor drones that operate specifically using Starlink... And when the speed was reduced [Starlink's speed], we were unable to shoot down some of the jet-powered Shahed drones," Zelenskyy said.

According to him, the jet-powered drones were traveling at speeds of more than 400 km/h, while Starlink speeds had been reduced to 78 km/h.

The president also added that, because of the restrictions, Ukraine had been unable to use Starlink to strike military targets in temporarily occupied territories.

title: Five Things To Know Today
body: 1. Nigeria’s inflation falls to 14.63%, but food prices remain elevated Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.63% in September, down from 15.39% in August, according to figures released by the National Bureau of Statistics on Thursday, October 15. The annual rate was 20.98% in September 2025. Month-on-month inflation also slowed to 0.06%, compared with 0.71% in August. However, food inflation remained relatively high at 19.59%, underlining the continuing pressure on household budgets. Why it matters: The latest figures indicate that consumer prices are rising more slowly. They do not mean that prices have returned to previous levels. Food and energy costs remain especially important to household purchasing power. Watch : The Central Bank’s response, movements in petrol and food prices, and whether the decline in inflation continues into the final quarter of 2026. 2. Borno military base attacked as Tinubu orders intensified security operations Security sources have reported that 15 soldiers and five members of the Civilian Joint Task Force were killed during an attack on a military base in Mairari, Guzamala Local Government Area of Borno State. The attack occurred on Tuesday night. The military has not independently confirmed the reported casualty figures. Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu chaired a National Security Council meeting on Thursday, directing security agencies to intensify operations against terrorists and kidnappers, rescue abducted Nigerians and ensure a secure environment for the 2027 elections. Defence Minister Christopher Musa said the President also instructed security personnel to remain politically neutral. Why it matters : The reported military casualties underline the continuing security challenges in the North-East. Protecting voters, candidates and election officials is also becoming an immediate operational priority. Watch : Official confirmation of the Borno casualties, further military operations and the security arrangements being developed for the January elections. 3. APC releases nationwide campaign timetable; Tinubu to attend rallies in 12 states The All Progressives Congress released its presidential campaign timetable on Thursday, October 15, confirming that President Bola Tinubu will personally attend rallies in 12 states, while other party leaders will represent him elsewhere. The campaign begins in Kaduna on October 24, followed by Rivers on November 7, Plateau on November 14 and Oyo on November 21. The President’s other scheduled appearances include Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos. The timetable follows Wednesday’s inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council and the publication of an expanded membership list that includes prominent politicians from outside the ruling party, notably Nyesom Wike, Chukwuma Soludo and Ademola Adeleke. Why it matters: The timetable establishes the ruling party’s nationwide campaign programme. The inclusion of politicians from other parties also places attention on the nature of cross-party political cooperation ahead of 2027. Watch : The Kaduna campaign launch, the roles played by the newly named council members and the opposition parties’ campaign schedules. 4. Federal Government and NLC disagree over minimum-wage negotiations A fresh disagreement has emerged between the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress over when negotiations for a new national minimum wage should begin. Labour Minister Muhammad Dingyadi says the existing ₦70,000 minimum wage, introduced in 2024, is not due for review until June 2027. However, NLC President Joe Ajaero argues that negotiations should begin immediately to allow sufficient time for a new agreement. In correspondence made public on Thursday, October 15, the NLC maintained that preparations should begin by October 17, citing the statutory review timetable and the increasing cost of living. The government maintains that an immediate review would be premature. Why it matters : The disagreement comes amid organised labour’s demands for lower petrol prices and additional measures to protect workers’ purchasing power. Watch: Whether the government agrees to establish a tripartite negotiating committee, further exchanges between the parties and the possibility of industrial action. 5. Presidency says National Policing Bill will reach lawmakers within two weeks The Presidency says a proposed National Policing Bill is almost ready for submission to the National Assembly. Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila disclosed on Thursday that a presidential working group had substantially completed work on the legislation. However, the related constitutional amendment required for state policing faces a separate hurdle. Reports indicate that only a small number of state assemblies have approved the amendment, against the constitutionally required support of at least 24 states. The Presidency says consultations with governors are continuing, while remaining issues in the proposed legislation are being resolved. Why it matters: State policing would significantly change Nigeria’s security structure. The proposed legislation must address operational responsibilities, funding, oversight and safeguards against political interference. Watch : Submission of the bill, the progress of the constitutional amendment and the positions taken by state legislatures. The post Five Things To Know Today appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Communications Minister announces 2,800-site telecom expansion during Volta visit
body: The government plans to construct 800 new cell sites and upgrade 2,000 existing ones nationwide within the year, the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has announced during a two-day working visit to the Volta Region. He gave the assurance during a courtesy call on the Paramount Chief of Akoefe, Togbega Drake Tsigbe IV, at Akoefe Kpodzi in the Ho Central Constituency. The minister also inspected a newly constructed Rural Telephony Project (RTP) facility at Akoefe Gadza to assess progress in extending telecommunications services to the community. Major telecommunications investment Mr. George said the 2,800-site programme represented a significant expansion of the country’s telecommunications infrastructure compared with developments over the previous five years. The initiative covers new cell towers and upgrades to existing facilities operated by major mobile network operators, including MTN and Telecel. He further disclosed that the additional network spectrum released over the past two years exceeded the total allocated during the preceding two decades. Spectrum provides the radio-frequency capacity needed to transmit calls and data, and the increased allocation is expected to support faster internet speeds and better network performance. Collaboration to improve network services The minister commended traditional leaders and community members for supporting engineers working on telecommunications projects across the region. He said their advocacy, alongside that of Members of Parliament, had helped prioritise underserved communities. The Ningo-Prampram MP added that relevant ministries were coordinating telecommunications cable deployment with road construction projects to minimise service disruptions caused by fibre-optic cable cuts. Mr. George expressed confidence that the investments would deliver more reliable mobile services, particularly in underserved communities. As the facilities become operational towards the end of the year and into early next year, more residents are expected to benefit from improved network coverage and greater access to digital services.

title: Impunity fuelling sexual abuse in Ghana – Angela Dwamena-Aboagye
body: The Executive Director of the ARK Foundation, Dr Angela Dwamena-Aboagye, has identified impunity and the failure of institutions to hold perpetrators accountable as key factors fuelling sexual abuse in Ghana. She said people entrusted with positions of authority often exploit their power because they believe they can escape punishment, allowing sexual violence to persist. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show during a discussion on the alleged sexual abuse case involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, Dr Dwamena-Aboagye said the problem was compounded by society’s failure to take sexual violence seriously. “Even if you do it, nobody will bring me to book. That’s a very common expression. Take me anywhere,” she said, describing the attitude that emboldens some perpetrators. Her comments follow a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, which revealed that municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures had received reports concerning alleged sexual abuse by the Obuasi SHTS headmaster months before his suspension. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye said the abuse of authority was particularly troubling when those responsible for protecting children became the alleged perpetrators. Responding to a question about how a headmaster could violate a student entrusted to his care, she said the abuse was linked to the power such individuals exercised over those under their supervision. “As far as this person is concerned, you know, I’m in a position of trust. I have people with me. I can exercise my power over them, not only as a headmaster, as an adult over a child, people put in my trust. The next thing that fuels this is the impunity,” she said. She said that such conduct could continue when perpetrators believed their positions would shield them from accountability. “This is severe abuse of trust. And it happens also because of the impunity that is enabled by the kind of responses that our institutions give.” She said institutions must confront the culture of impunity that allows perpetrators to believe they can act without consequences. “Impunity enables this kind of behaviour. And until we’re able to tackle that impunity through assistance, it won’t stop,” she said. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye criticised the wider societal attitude towards sexual violence, saying victims often suffer serious consequences that are not fully understood by those around them. “Let me just put it plainly, we don’t take this matter seriously,” she said. “Sexual violence is something that a lot of societies do not take seriously. And Ghana is one such example.” She said the failure to appreciate the effects of sexual abuse often influenced how allegations were handled by families, schools and other institutions. According to her, victims can experience psychological, physical, economic, social and spiritual difficulties, yet their experiences are sometimes dismissed or treated lightly. “Until we get rid of the mindset by understanding the nature of the act, what it does to the victims, how they struggle psychologically, physically, economically, socially, even spiritually, with acts like that, we would always continue to treat it with kid gloves,” she said. She also expressed concern about parents who settle sexual abuse cases without adequately considering the experiences and welfare of the victims. “People describe sexual violence as the living death. We don’t understand it,” she added. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye said the response to sexual violence was not solely a problem within educational institutions, but reflected attitudes across society and the institutions expected to protect victims.

title: Belgium to deliver 10 F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine by end of year — PM
body:
BRUSSELS, October 16. /TASS/. Belgium intends to transfer ten F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine by the end of this year, Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever said following a meeting with Vladimir Zelensky on the sidelines of the EU summit in Brussels.
"Ukraine urgently needs operational jets (…), and we can help with that. <...> We will supply ten [aircraft] this year," the Belga news agency quoted De Wever as saying.
The Belgian prime minister noted that the schedule for the transfer of military equipment had been pushed back due to delays in the delivery of American F-35 fighters to Belgium, which are intended to replace the F-16s currently in service with the country’s air force.
Belgium has promised to deliver its first two F-16s to Ukraine in 2024, and then to transfer all remaining operational aircraft in phases. In June 2026, Belgian Defense Minister Theo Francken announced plans to transfer seven F-16 fighter jets by the end of this year. To date, deliveries have not begun due to delays in receiving the F-35s.
The Belgian F-16s are, on average, about 40 years old. The Belgian Air Force has about 200 aircraft on its roster, however, according to local media estimates, no more than 40 remain operational.

title: Douglas Alexander welcomes defence skills investment boost
body:
The  Colleges in the East and West of Scotland will upskill young people, enabling them to benefit from good, well-paid jobs in Scotland’s growing defence sector.
Scotland already benefits from over £2 billion a year in MoD spending, which supports more than 12,000 jobs.
Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander today welcomed the Scottish Government’s decision to match fund the UK Government’s £10 commitment to create two Defence Technical Excellence Colleges (DTECs) in Scotland, as part of a £50 million Scottish Defence Growth Deal.
The DTECs will help provide young people with new specialist pathways into high-skilled, well-paid careers in defence engineering, advanced manufacturing and maritime technology are coming to Scotland.
The colleges will be located to support Scotland’s defence clusters in the East and West of the country and will benefit from the engineering and innovation centres previously announced as part of the Scottish Defence Growth Deal.
Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander said:
In March we announced a £10 million commitment to develop two Defence Technical Excellence Colleges in Scotland. I’m pleased that the Scottish Government has now agreed to match fund these colleges to give our young people the skills they need to secure high-skilled, well-paid careers in Scotland’s defence sector in the years to come.
Scotland is a defence industrial powerhouse and is already benefiting from increased UK Government investment as we deliver a defence dividend for Scotland, creating new skilled jobs, new training places and new opportunities for communities while keeping us and our allies secure. It is crucial that we continue to develop the skilled workforce needed to support this growing sector.
Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, Luke Pollard MP said:
Finally matching DTEC funding is welcome news for Scottish careers.  The colleges will provide routes into high-skilled, well-paid roles in the defence sector which is crucial to the work of keeping the UK safe around the clock.
This is an important part of our £50 million Defence Growth Deal - announced back in March - to boost growth opportunities for Scotland that supports our Armed Forces.
Industry analysis suggests there could be demand for up to 50,000 additional defence jobs across the UK by 2034/35.
Scotland already benefits from over £2.5 billion a year in Ministry of Defence spending, which directly supports 12,200 jobs.
The Scottish Secretary launched the UK Government’s Defence Growth Deal on 12 March, committing £10 million towards the creation of two DTECs — one in the East and one in the West of Scotland — as part of a wider £50 million deal.
The offer remained conditional on the Scottish Government providing match funding. More here:
https://www.gov.uk/government/news/scotland-set-for-skills-and-innovation-boost-as-50-million-defence-growth-deal-unveiled
Scottish Government Innovation minister Alyn Smith on October 15th confirmed that Holyrood ministers would “partner with the UK Government” on the project.

title: Pezeshkian meets with Armenian PM in Yerevan
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 16 (MNA) – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met and held talks with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pshinyan in Yerevan on Friday on the sidelines of 17th Summit of Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
During the meeting, the two sides explored avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries in all areas.
Emphasizing the need for a comprehensive roadmap for cooperation, the Iranian president said a strategic plan between the two countries could help deepen relations across various fields. He stressed that Tehran is determined to expand ties in all areas and called for translating agreements and discussions into practical results.
“Through cooperation, we must bring these issues to fruition in practice,” Pezeshkian said, noting that significant steps had already been taken. He expressed hope that the initiatives would have a long-term impact and produce tangible results.
Addressing US sanctions against Iran, Pezeshkian stressed that the country could not be isolated through such measures. “The US must know that Iran, relying on its people and in coordination with its neighbors, will continue to engage with the world with strength,” he said.
He added that Washington has created problems not only for Iran but also for the international community, warning that continued pursuit of the same course would worsen conditions for everyone. The US, he said, should choose dialogue based on reason rather than coercion.
Pashinyan, for his part, referred to Iran’s cultural heritage and long history, saying Armenia seeks peace and stability in the region and is working to expand relations with neighboring countries on a daily basis, with the aim of promoting mutual development.
The Armenian prime minister described the expansion of trade and economic ties with Iran as significant and highlighted the considerable potential for bilateral energy cooperation. He said Yerevan is seeking to further strengthen relations with Tehran in that sector.

title: Trump’s Betrayal of Ukraine and the Free World
body:
When Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky addresses the international community, he speaks for a nation fighting for its sovereign existence on the active front line of European democracy, holding back Russian anti-Western imperial ambitions.
Whatever his domestic shortcomings may be, his leadership and diplomacy during a wartime state of siege are backed by the courage of a people refusing foreign authoritarian subjugation with its genocidal traits.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
But what he encounters from US President Donald Trump and his political entourage is not strategic solidarity but transactional disdain – an impulse to treat Ukraine’s survival as a disposable bargaining chip both abroad and in American domestic politics.
While continuing to ingratiate himself with authoritarian Russian war criminal Vladimir Putin, Trump has gone so far as to call for Zelensky’s removal.
This posture is far more dangerous than ordinary campaign rhetoric, or crude lack of diplomacy. It signals a retreat from the post-1945 rules-based international order, an implicit repudiation of NATO, and an open invitation to revanchist powers to redraw sovereign borders by force.
Trump’s antagonism toward Kyiv is neither accidental nor isolated; it is the cornerstone of a transactional worldview that views democratic alliances with contempt, authoritarian leaders with deference, and Zelensky and his country as an insubordinate nuisance.
Trump’s recurring threats to halt military assistance and force Kyiv into an immediate, lopsided settlement with Vladimir Putin reflect an instinct to accommodate Moscow while abandoning a democratic partner under fire.
For a political figure who frequently presents himself as a master dealmaker, demanding that the victim of aggression concede territory and sovereignty looks less like shrewd negotiation than preemptive surrender for reasons that are still unclear but suspect.
His isolationist claim that supporting Ukraine is a peripheral distraction from core American interests rests on a profound strategic error. Ukraine is not asking for foreign troops; its forces are actively degrading the conventional military capability of Moscow –historically, and today even more so, the primary security threat to Europe.
Abandoning Ukraine would shatter Western deterrence worldwide. Authoritarian regimes in Beijing, Tehran, and Pyongyang are closely watching Washington’s resolve. If the United States forces Kyiv into capitulation, it will demonstrate to China that Western democratic stamina is fleeting – drastically increasing the risk of an invasion or blockade of Taiwan, a crisis that would inevitably threaten global trade and risk pulling American forces into a Pacific war.
In Europe, a Russian victory would place Moscow’s forces directly along the borders of Poland, Romania, Moldova, and the Baltic states, elevating the risk of a miscalculation that could trigger NATO’s Article 5 and require direct American military intervention.
Moreover, and what is often overlooked, the economic reality of security assistance contradicts populist talking points: most allocated funds remain in the United States, expanding domestic manufacturing capacity and replacing aging military stockpiles with modern systems.
Trump’s record demonstrates that this hostility toward Ukraine is part of an established global pattern: accommodating authoritarian adversaries while antagonizing historic partners.
While autocrats in Pyongyang, Moscow, and Beijing have enjoyed personal deference, democratic allies face continual coercion. Trump has repeatedly subjected Canada, the European Union, and NATO members to punitive tariffs and questioned collective defense arrangements.
This is not hard-nosed negotiation; it is the strategic unraveling of the Western alliance. When foreign policy is reduced to personal leverage and real-estate transactionalism, strategic alliances cease to be treated as enduring commitments.
This transactional approach to statecraft cannot be separated from the continuous political spectacle used to deflect scrutiny from unresolved ethical and legal questions at home.
Let’s be clear. Trump is calling for Zelensky’s replacement while Russia intensifies its drone and missile attacks on Ukraine. After almost five years of all-out war against Ukraine, Russia has failed to break the spirit and resistance of its indomitable people. Now the current US president is colluding with Putin even more brazenly than before in calling for Kyiv’s de facto capitulation.
Could anyone have imagined Washington pursuing such a nefarious policy and siding – as it has been doing under Trump, Rubio, Vance, Hegseth, and co. – with anti-democratic countries in the UN and elsewhere?
But fortunately, this abysmal situation may not continue indefinitely.
Ukraine’s faith in the American project rests not in single political figures but in the institutional resilience and moral clarity of its people – and in the principles of liberty, national sovereignty, and the rule of law deeply woven into the American identity.
As key electoral tests approach, the world looks to the American citizenry to reaffirm that the United States remains a beacon of freedom, rather than an accomplice to autocracy.
The democratic world cannot accept betrayal as the new norm. For the West, the choice is stark: stand firm with those defending democracy today or prepare to pay a vastly higher price tomorrow. The US appears to be signaling that it may have already chosen not to remain with its allies, that it has become something else.
Meanwhile, left with the stark choice, or rather, ultimatum, of “to be, or not to be,” Ukraine will continue to fight for its existence, with or without those who turn their backs.
Fundamental change should begin in Washington, not Kyiv.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.
Bohdan Nahaylo, Chief Editor of Kyiv Post since December 2021, is a British-Ukrainian journalist, author and veteran Ukraine watcher based between Kyiv and Barcelona. He was formerly head of Amnesty International's Soviet Union unit, a senior United Nations official and policy adviser, and Director of Radio Liberty’s Ukrainian Service.

title: The battle for Israel: As Netanyahu rallies the Right, Eisenkot makes his move for power
body: As the election nears, Netanyahu targets right-wing alternatives, while Eisenkot seeks the commanding lead that would make him the opposition's undisputed PM candidateThink of Israel as one big cruise liner. Considering the country's hyper-stressed reality, that may require some imagination, but bear with it for a moment.On the starboard side of the ship, the right side, are all the voters in the pro-Netanyahu camp, split into different halls and ballrooms.The Likud occupies the biggest hall, with smaller rooms for Shas, United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, and the Religious Zionist Party.On the port side, separated from starboard by a hallway with doors leading to both sides, are the rooms of the anti-Netanyahu camp.Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar has the biggest room there, followed by Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad, with smaller rooms for the Democrats and Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu.In the hallway itself stand Ofer Winter's People of Israel party and Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha's reservist-economist party. Behind the ship, in a separate tugboat, sail the two Arab parties.As the cruise liner steams toward its destination, Election Day, just 11 days away, representatives of the two sides shout the expected accusations across the hallway.From one side: “You are responsible for the worst disaster in Israel's history and are leading the country toward catastrophe.” From the other: “You will join forces with those in the tugboat and establish a Palestinian state.”But the more consequential action is taking place on each side of the ship.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu looks down the hallway, trying to persuade Winter's and Hendel's voters to abandon them and come to his side of the ship. Over on the port side, Eisenkot is trying to expand his already large ballroom at the expense of the rooms occupied by those sharing his side of the liner.Netanyahu intensifies campaign to consolidate right-wing votersThose two maneuvers are dominating the final stretch of the voyage to Election Day. And what is a sure sign the campaign has entered that final stretch? Netanyahu's sudden ubiquity on the airwaves.After months when the prime minister's interviews were largely reserved for foreign media, ABC, CBS, Fox News, and various podcasts, he showed up in Israeli studios this week, and not only on Channel 14.Granted, on Tuesday he was, again, on Channel 14, where a “home crowd” greeted him rapturously. But the next day he was on Channel 11, and in between he appeared on Army Radio.His message had two parts: the election is perilously close, and right-wing voters cannot afford to gamble.The first is familiar. Netanyahu has sounded the same alarm in numerous campaigns, warning his voters that victory is slipping away. On Channel 14, he anticipated the obvious response: people would dismiss this as his traditional gevalt campaign. This time, he insisted, he really is worried. The race is tied, he said.And where, precisely, did he see right-wing voters gambling?Once you cut through the familiar warnings about Eisenkot joining forces with Ahmad Tibi and the election determining whether a Palestinian state will be established, a much smaller target comes into view: Winter's party.Netanyahu's relentless attacks on the retired brigadier-general stand out in this final stretch. At a time when he might be expected to concentrate his fire on Eisenkot and Bennett, he is devoting considerable energy to a small party standing in the hallway.Netanyahu said he had tried to persuade Winter to join the Likud and, when that failed, to team up with another small right-wing party. That, too, failed, so now he is going after him mercilessly.In one of the anti-Winter messages he put out this week, Netanyahu charged that Winter would take right-wing votes and carry them over to Liberman on the port side of the ship.“It's no coincidence that a senior figure on Liberman's list, Yulia Malinovsky, says that ultimately Winter will join a government with Liberman. That's what will happen. That's the plan,” Netanyahu said.Then came a blistering comparison with Bennett, who formed a government in 2021 with Yair Lapid's Yesh Atid and Mansour Abbas's Ra'am.“If he walks like Bennett and talks like Bennett, he's Bennett. Vote Likud, vote Right. Winter is not right-wing. Winter is Bennett 2. We mustn't squander the Right's votes. Don't vote for Winter.”Winter's coalition conditions complicate Netanyahu's election strategyNetanyahu's concern is twofold.First, Winter's party will fail to cross the 3.25% electoral threshold, sending votes cast by people on the Right down the drain. Of the 19 major polls taken since October 1, the party crossed the threshold in 11, including four of the seven taken in the last week.That is enough to keep Winter in the race, but hardly enough to reassure Netanyahu that the votes will count.The second concern is that Winter will cross the threshold, then peddle his seats elsewhere.Winter and others in his party say they will recommend Netanyahu to the president as prime minister. But they also say they will not join a government in which the haredi parties hold the balance of power unless those parties agree to a widespread haredi conscription law.But what if Netanyahu does not accept those conditions? Asked precisely that in a Channel 12 interview on Saturday night, Winter replied, rather inelegantly, that Netanyahu could essentially “go take a hike.”Nobody owns me, he declaredWinter did not explicitly rule out joining an Eisenkot or Liberman government. He did, however, rule out sitting with Yair Golan, because “he smears Israel abroad.”For Netanyahu's campaign, that left an opening wide enough to drive a campaign bus through.A recommendation is one thing; a commitment to join a government is another. Winter is offering the former, with conditions attached to the latter. Netanyahu wants right-wing voters to hear that distinction and draw the conclusion he is supplying: Winter could be Bennett all over again.The pressure has extended to billboards and signs in areas where candidates on Winter's list live. Davidi Ben-Zion, eighth on the list, withdrew, reportedly telling colleagues that pressure on his family, including negative posters strategically placed near the bus stops his children use, had become too much.Netanyahu's concerns also extend to the other party in the hallway: Hendel and Zelekha's.In the Channel 14 interview, Netanyahu went after Zelekha, whom Netanyahu – as finance minister – appointed accountant-general in 2003. Despite the party's appeal to right-wing voters, Netanyahu charged that Zelekha had voted for Meretz in the past and participated enthusiastically in anti-government protests on Balfour Street in Jerusalem and Kaplan Street in Tel Aviv.He also attacked Zelekha on his home turf, the economy, challenging his credentials as a free-market champion.Hendel and Zelekha's party crossed the threshold in all seven major polls taken this week. But unlike Winter, they have not pledged to recommend Netanyahu. Hendel says the party will use its leverage to establish a broad Zionist government without the Arab and haredi parties.Given the coalition arithmetic, how that government would come together remains an enigma. Like Winter, Hendel is clearer about his conditions than about how he would assemble a government that meets them.But Netanyahu doesn't need their coalition plans fully worked out to worry about them. He needs the voters attracted to those parties back in his camp.Eisenkot seeks commanding lead to establish opposition leadershipAcross the ship's hallway, Eisenkot has a different calculation.His campaign to make Yashar the largest party is aimed, in part, at voters already on his side of the boat. He wants them to leave the other rooms and enter his ballroom.For Netanyahu, the immediate task is to consolidate the camp. For Eisenkot, it is also to establish who commands it.That is why the leaders of the other parties in his bloc are less than enthusiastic about his strategy. A voter moving from Bennett, Liberman, or Golan to Eisenkot does not enlarge the bloc. It enlarges Eisenkot.The bigger Yashar is, and the wider its lead over the Likud, the stronger his claim to form the next government – even if his bloc falls short of 61 seats.Eisenkot repeated one phrase this week: Netanyahu must not be allowed to win by losing. By that, he means Netanyahu must not remain caretaker prime minister through another cycle of inconclusive elections simply because no one else can form a coalition.In a Yediot Aharonot interview this week, Eisenkot said, “If you [Netanyahu] think you will do to me what you did to others in the past – meaning, remain in office at the head of a caretaker government – that will not happen.” When Israel held five elections in under four years, from April 2019 to November 2022, Netanyahu served 19 months as caretaker prime minister over two stretches.Eisenkot considers minority government to prevent Netanyahu remaining in officeOne route Eisenkot envisages to prevent a repeat of that scenario is to bring a minority government to the Knesset for approval and secure the support of a majority of those voting.A government does not need 61 members to win such a vote; it only needs a majority of those in the plenum casting a vote. This scenario would be made possible, for instance, if the Arab parties simply don't vote.Once this minority government is approved, Eisenkot can then attract defectors from the other side of the ship. A substantial lead over the Likud would give that effort greater public legitimacy.There are other considerations, too.First, in the unlikely event that a rotation agreement with the Likud became a serious possibility, a decisive lead in seats would bolster his claim to go first as prime minister.More immediately, the larger Yashar becomes, the harder it would be for Bennett or Liberman to argue that someone else should lead the bloc.The four parties in the “change bloc” have yet to agree on a mechanism to determine their prime ministerial candidate after the election.Eisenkot has said, logically enough, that the leader of the party that wins the most votes should be the bloc's candidate. Since Yashar currently leads the bloc by a considerable margin, that formula would obviously favor him.It remains unclear, however, whether the others are prepared to accept this. But the wider the gap, the harder it would be to explain why the leader of a much smaller party should get the top job.Eisenkot is campaigning both against Netanyahu and for an outcome within his own bloc that would make his leadership hard to challenge.Both Netanyahu's and Eisenkot's maneuvers make sense.Netanyahu wants to prevent right-wing votes from being lost or carried into another government. Eisenkot wants to ensure that, if there is an opportunity to replace Netanyahu, he will be the one to seize it.But both maneuvers have their limits. For Netanyahu, keeping his passengers together does not guarantee enough support to retain command. And for Eisenkot, having the biggest ballroom on one side of the ship does not guarantee enough support to become captain of the whole vessel.

title: Tinubu celebrates aide Basheer Lado at 60
body:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Basheer Lado, his special adviser on National Assembly Matters (Senate), on his 60th birthday on 16 October.
The president described Mr Lado, a former senator, as a dependable public servant and accomplished legislator who served in the Senate for four years before becoming his liaison officer in the National Assembly’s Upper Chamber.
President Tinubu said Mr Lado’s experience in lawmaking and public administration has continued to benefit the nation, particularly by fostering cordial relations between the Executive and the Senate.
The presidential aide represented Kano Central Senatorial District in the 7th National Assembly from 2011 to 2015. In the Senate, he served as vice chairman of the Senate Committee on Works.
President Tinubu remarked: “In the several capacities he has found himself, Senator Lado has been very impactful. As Senator, Lado facilitated the Kundila Bridge, popularly known as Gadar Lado, among other projects for his constituents in Kano.
“As Federal Commissioner at the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons and as Director-General of the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), Lado helped protect vulnerable Nigerians, confronting human trafficking and advancing the welfare and rehabilitation of displaced persons.
“His humanitarian gesture is further reflected in his Ladon Alheri Foundation, particularly in education, healthcare, women’s economic empowerment, rural water supply and support for disadvantaged communities.
“As Senator Lado attains 60, I commend his commitment to public service, loyalty to our Renewed Hope administration and invaluable contributions to strengthening democratic governance in Nigeria.
“I congratulate him on this milestone and wish him good health, wisdom and strength as he continues to serve our nation.”
Bayo Onanuga Special Adviser to the President (Information & Strategy) October 15, 2026

title: NUGS condemns alleged sexual abuse by Obuasi SHTS headmaster, calls for prosecution
body: The National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) has condemned the reported sexual abuse of a female student by the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, calling for a swift and impartial investigation into the allegation and prosecution if the claims are established. In a press statement signed by its President, Rashid Ibrahim Esq., on October 16, NUGS described the allegation as deeply troubling, stressing that school authorities have a responsibility to protect students from harm rather than expose them to abuse. “NUGS strongly condemns the reported sexual abuse of a female student by the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. The allegation is deeply troubling, especially because school authorities are expected to protect students, not expose them to harm,” it said. The union said the reported incident highlighted broader concerns about sexual harassment, intimidation and the abuse of authority faced by female students in senior high schools and tertiary institutions. “Many girls in Senior High Schools and female students in tertiary institutions continue to face sexual harassment, intimidation and abuse of authority, sometimes at the hands of people entrusted with their care,” the statement said. NUGS stressed that “no student should have to endure such experiences in the course of pursuing an education”, emphasising the need for schools and universities to provide safe environments for learning. The union called on the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the relevant investigative authorities to act swiftly and conduct a thorough and impartial investigation into the allegation. It further urged the authorities to prioritise the welfare of the affected student by providing the necessary counselling and support while protecting her identity and dignity throughout the investigative process. According to the statement, measures must also be put in place to ensure that the student is not subjected to intimidation, victimisation or any form of retaliation for reporting the alleged abuse. On accountability, NUGS called for criminal prosecution if investigations establish that the allegation is true, insisting that individuals in positions of authority must be held accountable under the law. “If investigations establish that the allegation is true, we call for the headmaster to be prosecuted in accordance with the laws of Ghana,” the statement said. The union added that administrative sanctions should not be used as a substitute for criminal prosecution where investigations establish that an offence has been committed. “Where criminal conduct is established, administrative sanctions alone must not replace the prosecution required by law,” it stated. Beyond the reported incident, NUGS urged the GES and tertiary institutions to strengthen existing mechanisms for reporting sexual abuse and ensure that students can report misconduct without fear of retaliation. READ ALSO: Minister orders suspension of Obuasi SHS headmaster over alleged sexual misconduct following JoyNews investigation “We also urge the Ghana Education Service and tertiary institutions to strengthen systems for reporting sexual abuse and ensure that students can speak up without fear of retaliation. “it added. It also called for reports of sexual misconduct to be treated seriously and addressed promptly to protect students and promote accountability within educational institutions. The union reaffirmed its support for the affected student and others who may have experienced sexual harassment or abuse, including those who have remained silent because of fear. “NUGS stands in solidarity with the affected student and all students who have suffered sexual harassment or abuse, including those who have remained silent out of fear,” the statement said. The union maintained that schools and universities must be places where students feel safe, respected, and protected, urging the relevant authorities to take the necessary steps to address the allegation and strengthen safeguards against sexual misconduct. Meanwhile, the Minister of Education has directed the immediate suspension of the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, following allegations of sexual misconduct involving a female student.

title: Working with Austin Abrams on Whalefall made even Josh Brolin uncomfortable
body: Austin Abrams has a way of making you care about a character before you quite understand him. There is something familiar in his awkwardness and flaws, even when he is keeping much of himself hidden. It helped him stand out in last year’s Weapons , and has become harder to overlook as he has moved into leading roles in Resident Evil and now Whalefall . The latter gives him an extraordinary situation to make believable. Playing a young diver swallowed by a sperm whale, Abrams spends much of the film alone, trying to escape before his oxygen runs out. It is the young man himself who holds our attention – his fear, his frustrations and the unfinished business with his father that brought him into the water. What sounds like a premise built for a couple of hours of high-concept fun becomes something unexpectedly moving. Directed by Brian Duffield and adapted from Daniel Kraus’s novel, Whalefall follows Jay Gardiner, played by Abrams, who goes diving off California’s coast to recover his father’s remains.
