title: How Bakassi Boys arrested ‘Issakaba’ distributor, accosted Sam Dede — Lancelot Imasuen
body:
Nollywood filmmaker Lancelot Oduwa Imasuen revealed that the Bakassi Boys arrested the distributor of his 2001 film, Issakaba, in Aba, Abia State, and confronted its lead actor, Sam Dede, over its portrayal of the vigilante group.
Mr Imasuen said the group took issue with the film’s portrayal of its activities and questioned how the filmmakers obtained details of its operations.
The filmmaker recalled the incidents in an interview with Channels Television while discussing Issakaba Returns, the forthcoming sequel to the action franchise.
“That was one of the most unbelievable moments of my life. The distributor in Aba was then arrested by them, the Bakassi Boys,” he said.
“They were dealt with, and they felt like the film went too far. They were asking, how did we know about them? Sam Dede was accosted in Aba while travelling to Port Harcourt.”
Mr Dede played Ebube, the leader of the fictional Isakaba Boys, whose campaign against criminals formed the centre of the film’s story.
Mr Imasuen said the production drew directly from events unfolding in southeastern Nigeria at the time, adding that he and his collaborators followed the vigilante group’s activities before its operations became increasingly entangled in political interests.
“They were not fallacy; they were true. Before the infiltration of the actual people that created that, we followed the story tenaciously as it was played in real time. We were making the movie,” he said.
The filmmaker said the team understood the risks of dramatising the activities of a group known for confronting suspected criminals through methods that attracted both public support and controversy.
“When political actors started taking advantage of them, we could have localised it and said, ‘Oh, it’s just chiefs’, but we knew what we were talking about at that time,” he said.
“Our fears then were real. We feared they might come to us. ‘ But the success that trailed the release of that film then, we couldn’t just stop.”
He said the decision to continue making the film was driven by more than its commercial prospects.
“The success was not about, ‘Oh, there was money to be made.’ It was about the reality that was with us,” he said.
The 2001 film was produced by Chukwuka Emelionwu and Moses Nnam.
The controversy surrounding Issakaba reflected the film’s connection to one of southeastern Nigeria’s most contentious security developments in the late 1990s: the emergence of the Bakassi Boys.
The vigilante group emerged in Aba in 1998 amid growing concerns about armed robbery and insecurity. It subsequently expanded its influence across parts of the South-east, earning support from residents who viewed it as a response to violent crime.
However, its methods, including the treatment and killing of suspected criminals without due judicial process, also attracted criticism over allegations of extrajudicial killings and human rights abuses.
The group’s activities provided the backdrop for Issakaba, which transformed the real-life security crisis into a supernatural action thriller built around vigilante justice, traditional beliefs and the fight against criminal gangs.
Mr Imasuen said the film’s idea followed the success of his earlier production, The Last Burial, produced by the late Chukwuka Emelionwu of Kas-Vid International.
The original film featured several actors who were prominent in Nollywood during the home-video era.
The cast included Sam Dede as Ebube, Chiwetalu Agu as Odiwe, Pete Eneh as Mbanefo, Amaechi Muonagor as Igwe, Susan Obi as Lolo, Mike Ogundu as Nwoke, John Okafor as Amazuru, Andy Chukwu as Danga, Zulu Adigwe as Akuku, Diewait Ikpechukwu as Odogwu, Tom Njemanze as Idoko and Uche Ndigwe as Osita.
Other actors included Emeka Nwachukwu, Emeka Ani, Remmy Ohajianya, Fabian Adibe, Steve Eboh, Cynthia Okereke and Stella Ikwuegbe.
Several original cast members, including Pete Eneh, Amaechi Muonagor, John Okafor, and Zulu Adigwe, have since died.
Released as Nigeria’s home-video industry expanded rapidly, Issakaba drew on public anxieties about armed robbery, insecurity, and the perceived limits of conventional policing.
More than two decades after the original film, Mr Imasuen is returning to the franchise with Issakaba Returns, which is scheduled for nationwide cinema release on 13 November 2026.
Production began in 2024, with principal photography completed in Asaba, Delta State. Mr Dede returns as Ebube.
Mr Imasuen returns as director, and the sequel brings together veterans of the original production with a new generation of Nollywood actors.
The announced cast includes Chidi Mokeme, Nosa Rex, Iyabo Ojo, Regina Daniels, Alex Osifo, Charles Okafor, Mark Angel, Phyna, Francis Onwochei, Ben Olaye, Chudi Kashimawo, Yekini “Itele” Ibrahim and Sanni Danger.
Returning cast members include Mr Dede, Mr Agu, and Mr Ogundu.

title: Zelensky: Europe has enough PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles to defend Ukraine this winter
body:
The head of state made this remark during a briefing in Brussels, according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“Will the Europeans support us? Yes. As for the quantity [of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles], I don’t know yet. But I do know some things about certain countries. Are there enough PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles in Europe for Ukraine to get through the winter? Yes. According to the figures I announced—the number we would like to receive for the winter—Europe has those numbers,” he said.
Zelensky noted that today’s winter support package for Ukraine primarily involves PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles. He informed European representatives of the minimum number of missiles Ukraine needs.
“No one expects that two missiles will be used to shoot down a single ballistic missile from Russia, as is standard practice... We’re talking ‘one-for-one’—about the minimal, scarce resources we need. To be honest, all leaders have this package,” said the head of state.
He also expressed hope that the development of the “Freyja” anti-ballistic missile system would be completed.
“May God grant success to the engineers of dozens of countries; we will overcome this technological barrier and build our own anti-ballistic missile system. I want to emphasize that it must be quick to produce and more affordable. We will certainly share it with all our European partners—and beyond—with those who need this protection and the corresponding security,” he said.
The president added that Ukraine has “good agreements” with Germany, which have secured support packages for 2027–2028.
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukraine has received confirmation of new energy, humanitarian, and defense aid packages from at least five partner countries.

title: Child protection must be the state’s responsibility, not NGOs’ burden – ARK Foundation Boss
body: The Executive Director of the ARK Foundation, Dr Angela Dwamena-Aboagye, has called on state institutions to take greater responsibility for educating children about sexual abuse and establishing effective reporting systems, saying civil society organisations cannot be expected to shoulder the burden indefinitely. She said safeguarding policies must be integrated into the daily operations of schools and public institutions to ensure children know where to report abuse and what action will follow when they speak up. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show during a discussion on the alleged sexual abuse case involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Dr Dwamena-Aboagye questioned why non-governmental organisations continued to bear much of the responsibility for educating communities about sexual abuse and laws protecting children. “How long can the ARK Foundation or FIDA or AWLA or whatever go around sending laws to schools, to communities, teaching, training, sensitising? How long?” she asked. She said state institutions should have incorporated such education into their policies and established systems to ensure sustained implementation, rather than relying on occasional campaigns by civil society organisations. “By now, our state institutions should have picked this up in our policies and start running with it,” she said. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye argued that integrating safeguarding into institutional practices did not necessarily require substantial financial resources but demanded commitment and effective systems. She said children should know where to turn when they experienced or witnessed sexual abuse and be confident that their complaints would trigger an established process. “Where children know that if this happens, I can go here, I can see this person, this is the system that will be kicked into place. And it will go through until the end, and we get a resolution or whatever it is,” she said. She stressed that child protection should not depend on the availability of an NGO to intervene or whether a case had attracted public attention. “This doesn’t take money. It takes commitment. It takes systematising. And then once it is into the system, it starts running,” she added. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye also called for a change in attitudes that discourage children from reporting abuse, including the tendency to blame victims for failing to resist their abusers. She noted that power imbalances between children and adults in authority could make it difficult for students to report misconduct, particularly when they feared punishment or other consequences. She said clear reporting procedures and sustained education would help children understand their rights and identify trusted people who could assist them. Her comments follow a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, which revealed that municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures had received reports concerning alleged sexual abuse by the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, months before his suspension.

title: Sudan’s Burhan seeks to ease US pressure with peace overture, analyst says
body: Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan’s letter to US President Donald Trump appears aimed at easing mounting American pressure and buying time amid Sudan’s deepening political, economic and military crisis, political analyst Awab Azzam al-Bushi told Radio Tamazuj. Burhan, who heads Sudan’s Transitional Sovereignty Council and commands the army, said on Thursday that he had sent Trump a letter affirming his government’s readiness to work with relevant parties to achieve a just and lasting peace that preserves Sudan’s sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and the dignity of its people. The message comes amid US-led efforts to secure a humanitarian truce in Sudan, strained relations over Washington’s ceasefire proposals and US sanctions linked to the alleged use of chemical weapons. US senior adviser Massad Boulos also met Burhan in Egypt earlier this month as diplomatic efforts to end the war intensified. Al-Bushi said the letter should be understood in the context of these pressures, arguing that Sudan’s military leadership is seeking to ease tensions with Washington and reopen channels of communication with the US administration. “In my assessment, Burhan’s letter reflects the mounting political, diplomatic and economic pressure on Sudan’s leadership,” al-Bushi said, citing the country’s economic crisis and growing political and military challenges. Al-Bushi linked the timing of the letter to a proposed US-Sudan economic and investment partnership bill introduced in the US House of Representatives on October 13. The proposal links cooperation in agriculture and mining to tangible progress in protecting civilians and achieving political stability in Sudan. Burhan’s message is a significant political signal, al-Bushi said, suggesting an attempt to contain US pressure and gain more time amid mounting domestic and international challenges. “The timing is an important political indicator,” he said. “It suggests an attempt to contain American pressure and gain more time.” Peace rhetoric and military strategy Al-Bushi questioned whether Burhan’s message signals a genuine shift towards ending the war, pointing to what he described as a gap between the army leadership’s diplomatic statements and its domestic rhetoric and military conduct. “There is a contradiction between Burhan’s external rhetoric about peace and his domestic discourse and actions, which remain focused on military victory and the continuation of fighting,” al-Bushi said. “Peace requires practical decisions and a genuine willingness to make political concessions,” he added. The analyst said the credibility of Burhan’s message would depend on whether it was followed by concrete steps to end hostilities and pursue a sustainable political settlement. Actions will test commitment Al-Bushi said the key test of Burhan’s commitment to peace would be his willingness to engage constructively with diplomatic initiatives and take practical steps towards a humanitarian truce. “The real test of Burhan’s seriousness is the extent to which he is prepared to engage positively with these initiatives, rather than simply declare his support for peace,” he said. “What we are witnessing may be an attempt at political manoeuvring and to buy time under mounting internal and external pressure,” al-Bushi added. Sudan’s war erupted in April 2023 between the Sudanese army, led by Burhan, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), commanded by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, following a power struggle over the military’s future and plans to transition to civilian rule. The conflict has triggered a major humanitarian crisis, displaced millions and derailed Sudan’s transition to civilian government. The post Sudan’s Burhan seeks to ease US pressure with peace overture, analyst says appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: CODEO calls for Emelia Agbenyo’s resignation over partisan ties
body: The Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) has called on Emelia Affi Agbenyo to resign as Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC), citing concerns about her past political activities and their potential impact on public confidence in the Commission’s impartiality. In a statement, CODEO also urged President John Dramani Mahama to demonstrate consistency with his previously stated position on electoral reforms by calling on Ms Agbenyo to step down. Ms Agbenyo was sworn in as Deputy Chairperson of the EC on October 12, 2026. CODEO, which comprises more than 41 member organisations, said publicly documented evidence of her involvement in the National Democratic Congress (NDC)’s 2024 election campaign raised concerns about the perceived independence and credibility of the electoral management body. The coalition stressed that the EC’s integrity depends not only on the actual neutrality of its commissioners but also on public confidence in their impartiality. According to CODEO, the NDC announced Ms Agbenyo in August 2024 as one of its sectoral spokespersons for the party’s election manifesto under the governance portfolio. The coalition said Ms Agbenyo also identified herself on LinkedIn as a spokesperson for the governance sector during the NDC campaign. CODEO further cited social media posts it attributed to Ms Agbenyo during the 2024 election campaign as evidence of her political engagement. It said that on September 20, 2024, she shared a video featuring then NDC presidential candidate John Dramani Mahama, accompanied by the party’s campaign song, Asempa by NACEE, and hashtags including #voteforchange2024. The coalition also referenced a post dated October 31, 2024, in which Ms Agbenyo shared a photograph of Mr Mahama with the caption: “To salvage our democracy, to restore good governance, reset our nation on the path of thriving democracy.” CODEO said another post on her X account on December 2, 2024, expressed opposition to the then government over what she described as its treatment of citizens and the imposition of a nuisance levy. The coalition argued that such political engagements could undermine public perceptions of the EC’s neutrality. It clarified, however, that its concerns were not about Ms Agbenyo’s professional qualifications or technical competence but the need to protect the Commission’s institutional credibility. CODEO said it had consistently advocated a broader and more consultative process for appointing EC members since the departure of the Commission’s former Chairperson, Dr Kwadwo Afari-Gyan. It cited its objections to the appointment processes involving former EC Chairperson Charlotte Osei in 2014 and the appointments of Jean Mensa, Dr Bossman Asare and Samuel Tetteh in 2018. The coalition also recalled that, in 2023, it joined STAR-Ghana Foundation and the Civic Forum Initiative to call for the resignation of Dr Peter Appiahene over concerns about his alleged partisan affiliation with the New Patriotic Party (NPP). According to CODEO, that appointment attracted criticism from several groups, including the NDC, whose then presidential aspirant, Mr Mahama, called for urgent reforms to the EC appointment process. The coalition said the appointment of another person whose political engagement had been publicly documented raised questions about the role of the Council of State in advising the President. It argued that the Council of State needed to establish transparent processes through which citizens could assess how it discharges its constitutional responsibilities. CODEO also cited Afrobarometer findings indicating that public trust in the EC reached its lowest levels in 2024, arguing that concerns about perceived partisan influence had affected confidence in the institution. CODEO recalled that in March 2023, Mr Mahama, then in opposition, criticised the appointment of persons he described as “known party activists” to the EC. He also called for an amendment to Article 43(2) of the 1992 Constitution to require parliamentary approval of new commissioners. CODEO Press Statement on Newly Sworn-in Deputy Chairpersons15thOct26 Download The coalition said the position was relevant to the circumstances surrounding Ms Agbenyo’s appointment and urged the President to apply the principles he advocated while in opposition. It maintained that safeguards for the independence of electoral institutions should be upheld regardless of which political party is in power. In response to the appointment, CODEO outlined four key demands. First, it called on Ms Agbenyo to resign as Deputy Chairperson of the EC to protect public confidence in the Commission’s impartiality and credibility. Second, it urged President Mahama to demonstrate consistency with his previous position by calling on her to resign. Third, it called on the government to pursue reforms that would make future appointments to the EC transparent, merit-based and capable of commanding confidence across the political divide. Finally, it urged the Council of State to establish processes that would enable citizens to access information on how it performs its constitutional duties. CODEO reiterated its call for a review of the appointment process for the leadership of the EC, citing recommendations by the Constitutional Review Committee for an open, competitive and merit-based system. The proposed reforms include a restructured Council of State, involvement of the Public Services Commission and prior parliamentary approval of appointments. However, CODEO said the government’s position paper rejected the proposed changes to the existing appointment arrangement, although it indicated that the President could adopt transparent and merit-based procedures. The coalition urged the government to reconsider its position and pursue reforms that introduce independent scrutiny, clear selection criteria and meaningful parliamentary oversight. It said such measures would help address concerns about actual or perceived political influence before appointments are made, rather than waiting for controversies to emerge. CODEO concluded that the independence of the EC must be protected not only through constitutional provisions but also through a commitment by political leaders to ensuring that the country’s electoral management body remains independent and impartial.

title: Ukraine in talks with EU to create separate track for dialogue with Russia – Zelenskyy
body:
Ukraine is negotiating with its European partners to establish a separate European track for dialogue with Russia aimed at achieving a diplomatic settlement to the war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

"I believe Europe is taking certain steps to establish its own channel in Europe that would, of course, primarily represent our interests and enable us to find a format for engaging with the Russians. Therefore, I think all of this will definitely happen," Zelenskyy said at a press briefing in Brussels on Friday.

According to him, the emergence of such a format would not rule out other negotiation processes, as they could take place in parallel. He added that he also sees parallel processes taking place on the U.S. side.

"My vision is that I would very much like to see several tracks. This would make it possible to move toward a diplomatic settlement of this war. We are holding relevant talks with the Europeans," the president said.

title: The first vibe-coded gun is here
body:
Since gun-rights activist and alt-right-friendly agitator Cody Wilson made the first 3D-printed firearm 13 years ago, he’s helped usher in a chaotic era of untraceable ghost guns. Now he’s claiming another first: “the first AI-made gun.” It’s called the WASP.
I stood about 20 feet away as Wilson and his sidekick clamped the WASP to a DIY test mount outside Defense Distributed headquarters in Austin, Texas. The 3D-printed .22 caliber handgun is, in reality, little more than a pistol barrel attached to a spring-loaded plastic box. Its rudimentary design bears a resemblance to Wilson’s single-shot 3D-printed “Liberator,” albeit with some quintessentially AI-generated oddities, like a wacky, bubbly grip that doesn’t quite fit a human hand. It was aimed toward a shallow green slope in the backyard of a semi-residential neighborhood. A long black string ran from its trigger to Wilson, who sat crouched about 10 feet back behind a police riot shield.
“Three. Two. One.” I braced for a thunderous crack, but instead heard only a loud click. The world’s first AI-generated gun had misfired.
“This didn’t happen last time,” Wilson, annoyed, reassured me as he carried out some quick troubleshooting. The gun’s striker had hit the cartridge, he said, but failed to set off the primer. I quietly took another step back. After some more fiddling, Wilson declared the WASP ready for a second chance. This time, pulling the string produced a sharp bang, about as loud as a firecracker. Downrange, a cardboard target had a hole ripped through its top left corner. His colleague had suggested using a life-size cutout of Joe Biden, but Wilson shot that down as “too on the nose.”
The safety test completed, Wilson then unclamped the WASP, slipped on a protective glove, took aim at the cardboard target, and squeezed the trigger himself. Another bang. This time, a miss, slightly high. The AI gun, today at least, was two for three in terms of shots successfully fired.
[Image: A hand-drawn target in the backyard of the Defense Distributed headquarters in Austin, Texas. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0630.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
With the smell of gunpowder still lingering, I asked Wilson the obvious question: Why make this functionally suspect firearm in the first place? We’re in Texas, where buying a conventional gun is often easier than getting a driver’s license. He paused, taking issue with the premise.
“I would argue that what we’ve made is not an AI-generated gun, but an AI that can generate guns.”
His supposed AI gunsmith is a custom model he calls GatGPT. But instead of generating pasta recipes or travel plans, this unfiltered model answers questions about firearms. It’s trained on DEFCAD’s expansive library of gun files and can help enthusiasts pick out the exact parts they need for a build. Launched in 2012, DEFCAD (another Wilson-led project) is the world’s largest online repository of digital gun and component files. Gun safety advocates and lawmakers have argued sites like DEFCAD aid the proliferation of “ghost guns,” firearms made partly or entirely of components without a serial number. Wilson, meanwhile, has called access to firearms “a fundamental human right.”
Under US federal law, licensed gun makers are required to include serial numbers on the frames or receivers of guns they sell. Wilson and others in what’s referred to as the 3D2A movement say gun files aren’t actually guns, they are computer code, a form of protected speech. That core argument, whether or not gun codes are protected speech, has been argued in court cases for over a decade, with many often citing or involving Wilson. It’s possible the issue will wind up before the Supreme Court.
Now, Wilson claims, AI can also come up with its own unique designs. The results have a bizarre, surrealist quality emblematic of early generative art to the tune of Will Smith slurping spaghetti.
The WASP’s entire development, Wilson claims, from its name to safety tweaks (an early grip design could have cost someone a finger), resulted from a natural-language dialogue between the model and its human user. In other words, it’s essentially a vibe-coded gun. Though mostly a proof of concept, the WASP nonetheless fires real, lethal rounds and doesn’t have a serial number. Wilson believes AI-generated guns like this will only improve as GatGPT ingests more data, and as users engage with it.
But the WASP also poses another pressing public safety issue. Producing 3D-printed guns has gotten easier over the years, but it still fundamentally requires some technical know-how. Now, however, a novice armed with GatGPT could plausibly make a gun with only a handful of prompts. That’s exactly the kind of barrier-lowering that critics of 3D-printed guns, like Everytown, have spent years warning about.
“[Wilson] admits the goal here,” Everytown senior vice president for law and policy Justin Wagner told The Verge. “He wants to lower the barrier to entry so anyone, regardless of their background check status or legal eligibility [can] own a gun. He wants anyone to be able to design and manufacture weapons, and that’s dangerous.”
Everytown has played a prominent role in advocating for a pair of recently passed laws in New York and California that will require 3D printer manufacturers to install firearm-blocking software that can detect guns or gun parts and stop them before they are ever printed. (Experts have questioned how and if these methods would actually work.)
Wilson didn’t specifically cite evading detection as a reason for building an AI gun maker, but the development comes on the heels of his recent efforts to complicate firearm-blocking technology that New York and California will require in future 3D printers. In August, Wilson began rolling out a tool called Hochulization (a jab at New York Gov. Kathy Hochul) that he says subtly alters a file’s underlying hash, which functions as a kind of digital fingerprint. By late September, Wilson claimed to The Verge that users had already “Hochulized” files more than 26,000 times, with some users applying the treatment more than once. It’s one of the many ways Wilson has planted a flag in the evolving battle over how to regulate 3D-printed guns.
The core idea behind that “self-defense measure,” as Wilson calls it, is to stymie a purely hash-based gun detection system by rendering it unable to keep up with constantly changing hashes. A new AI-generated gun design also wouldn’t immediately be recognized in a gun detection database, since it didn’t exist yet. More sophisticated gun detection software goes beyond simple hashes and uses AI to try to predict whether a file is likely a gun or gun component before it prints. It’s unclear whether this type of software, which is still being developed, would reliably detect a sufficiently strange-looking AI-generated gun design.
“Individuals who intentionally aim to thwart safety regulations put themselves and New York communities at risk, which is why Gov. Hochul remains committed to combating emerging threats and the production of ghost guns and illegally manufactured guns, and strengthening regulations that keep New Yorkers safe,” Hochul spokesperson Jess D’Amelia told The Verge.
Defense Distributed’s AI didn’t just log on one day and suddenly decide to build a gun. It started with a specific request from a human to riff off an existing design. An employee asked the model to build a new gun based on a design called “Ergo Harlot,” itself a variation of the more popular “Harlot” model. Like the WASP, the Harlot is a compact single-shot handgun that fires a .22 caliber round. The AI prompter, according to chat logs viewed by The Verge, framed the assignment as a “challenge” and told the AI model its entry “must be completely and fully functional and have a unique design.”
Chat logs show the AI model responding with a plan for a new design called the WASP and submitting it for approval. The AI didn’t explain its name choice, though Wilson suggested it bears some physical resemblance to the insect. When I asked whether it’s possibly an abbreviation for “white Anglo-Saxon Protestant,” he said it isn’t.
The AI model listed six key changes it made to the inspiration design, including a slightly longer barrel than the Harlot’s and a grip made of three grooved, circular lobes. Once a Defense Distributed employee approved the model’s plan, the logs show it checking and testing each component, much like how an AI coding agent such as Anthropic’s Claude Code works through a checklist when vibe-coding an app. The team then printed the WASP in its office on a Bambu Lab printer using standard plastic filaments, along with a handful of common metal parts for the firing pin and barrel. Wilson said the print took about six hours.
So is the WASP actually a good gun? Ashley Hlebinsky, a firearms historian and founder of consulting firm The Gun Code, told The Verge that it’s hard to judge without handling it, but several design choices stand out as odd. Most notably, the AI appears to have started making a trigger guard (the loop that normally protects a shooter’s finger) but doesn’t finish it, leaving the trigger exposed, for no apparent reason. The gun also seems to borrow from what are called modern “beavertail” grip designs. But bizarrely, the AI appears to have inverted its grip.
“It reminds me of times when I’ve prompted AI to draw a picture of a gun and it gets most of the way there but then has some weird parts missing,” Hlebinsky said. “It has an obvious futuristic, sci-fi appearance that reminds me of Marvin the Martian’s ray gun.”
Jonathan Ferguson, keeper of firearms and artillery at the Royal Armories Museum in Leeds, England, was more critical when asked if the WASP seemed functional.
“Functional? From a legal perspective, if it successfully fires a shot without a breech explosion, it’s a viable firearm, but so are two lengths of steel pipe with a firing pin and cap attached to the rear of one,” Ferguson told The Verge. “From a technical perspective, I would not call this a ‘sound’ or ‘good’ firearm. It does not appear to be comfortable to hold or easy to aim and, based on the test firing, seems to be only marginally functional.” If anything, Ferguson noted, he expected generative AI in 2026 to do a better job at designing a reliable firearm. “There are vestigial sights that can’t work, an open trigger guard, [and a] weirdly shaped grip.”
“This certainly is a development, [but] I don’t think it’s necessarily that novel. It’s another way to 3D print a gun,” Wagner said. “A victim of a mass shooting who was shot by a ghost gun told me when you get shot, it doesn’t matter if it’s a ghost gun, a 3D-printed gun, or a gun that got bought over the counter. They’re all just as lethal,” he added.
Wilson is confident his AI’s design will improve, both in terms of functionality and aesthetic uniqueness, as the DEFCAD database grows. More gun files will help, but he expects the biggest gains will come from users chatting with the model and pushing it to refine its choices. (GatGPT is currently in limited early access.) Eventually, he predicts, constant back-and-forth between users and AI could dramatically speed up the pace at which new 3D-printed gun designs appear.
“This is all just spontaneous parallel thinking,” Wilson said. “I think you’ll see those cycles faster now because of AI.”
“It’s like you’re speedrunning the available possibilities, the materials, the platforms, the concepts,” he added.
A skeptic would say the WASP’s origins as essentially a remix of a previous designs makes its claims to true originality shaky. Like many half-baked AI movie scripts or janky generative art, the WASP conjures up the familiar feeling of AI slop, made manifest in the real world. Even Wilson admits it looks a bit like a “Fortnite gun.”
Still, Wilson maintains the WASP is fundamentally an AI creation and one that he’s ultimately not responsible for, even though his team’s prompts led to its creation. That position aligns with a broader argument Wilson’s made for the better part of a decade in legal skirmishes with the State Department and local lawmakers: that gun files are protected speech. In fact, Wilson said he doesn’t necessarily consider the WASP a gun at all until it’s printed and fired.
“This thing lives first as a digital organism,” he said.

title: External management for companies, Trump’s words about Zelensky: Kremlin briefing
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. External management for a range of companies from unfriendly countries and US President Donald Trump’s remarks about Vladimir Zelensky were among the key topics of Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov’s daily briefing on Friday.
TASS has summarized the Kremlin spokesman’s key statements
Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold an international phone call this evening.
The introduction of external management for a number of companies from unfriendly countries that has taken place, can be described as a continuation of an existing trend: "This is a continuation of a trend. All those companies are from unfriendly countries, and their origin was one of the factors taken into account when the decision was made."
External management is being introduced primarily for companies from countries that are unfriendly in the full sense of the word, that are unlawfully holding Russian assets and expropriating Russian property: "This refers to countries that are participating in the unlawful holding of Russian funds, Russian assets, and are taking part in the unlawful expropriation of property belonging to Russian companies."
Russia shares US President Donald Trump’s assessment that Vladimir Zelensky is reluctant to take responsibility and pursue peace: "Zelensky’s reluctance to take responsibility and engage in peaceful settlement efforts is an obvious fact. We completely see eye-to-eye on this with President Trump."
Discussing a way out of the Ukraine conflict without the current Kiev regime would be impossible: "Even with all the desire, discussing anything without an operational Ukrainian leadership is impossible.".

title: National Ballet School, divinity college students among those affected by OSAP pause
body:
A recent pause on financial assistance payments to private post-secondary institutions in Ontario is affecting divinity schools, Canada’s National Ballet School and many others, with students feeling unfairly swept up in what they describe as a trawling net-like policy.
Colleges and Universities Minister Nolan Quinn announced last week that the province had tasked KPMG with auditing Ontario Student Assistance Program usage at career colleges, and that preliminary findings were of such concern that he referred the matter to the Ontario Provincial Police.
While the audit is ongoing, Quinn said, OSAP payments to private post-secondary institutions would be paused. Quinn said he is “working on” securing low-interest loans for affected students at financial institutions, but he has not indicated a timeline.
Many career college students have said they are worried about the pause, with no clear end in sight and with some students relying on that financial aid to cover not just tuition but living expenses while they study.
The broad nature of the pause affects all private post-secondary institutions, including private universities, chiropractic and naturopathic medicine colleges, and performing arts schools such as Canada’s National Ballet School.
Alessia Di Palma is in her last year of the ballet school’s five-year joint teacher training program with York University, and said she does not want to have to leave school when she is so close to finishing, but at the moment doesn’t know how she will pay her rent, even though she works two jobs while going to school.
“I’m heartbroken,” she said. “My heart sunk when I found out because it’s unfair that I’ve had this funding for four years and then the fifth year it’s just gone now because of something that didn’t even have anything to do with me.”
Initial concerns stemmed from activity at a few schools, Quinn’s office says, but evidence of “systemic issues” has come up in recent weeks.
“At this time, we do not have assurances from the audit team that the issues are not more widespread, leaving us with no choice but to pause OSAP payments to all private institutions to protect taxpayer dollars and hold bad actors accountable,” spokesperson Bianca Giacoboni wrote in a statement.
“We understand this is creating uncertainty for students and are working quickly to develop options for low-interest, third-party loans facilitated by financial institutions to help students through this period of transition.”
At the ballet school, programs are mostly at the secondary level, but it does have a post-secondary teacher training program that is affected by the OSAP pause. About half of those students rely on that aid to pay their tuition, said executive director John Dalrymple.
The government has chosen the bluntest and most harmful way of dealing with the root of the problem, he said, and it is especially disappointing that Quinn enacted the pause before securing those third-party loans.
“The fact that now all of these students who are working multiple jobs to make ends meet, who are at the very beginning of their career, are now left holding the bag to figure out how to finance something that the government had already assured them they qualified for and they were going to receive, I think is unconscionable,” he said.
Theological schools like McMaster Divinity College, affiliated with McMaster University, are also affected by the pause. Ambrose Thomson, the school’s registrar and director of student services, said students are beside themselves.
About 10 per cent of the non-profit institution’s revenue is dependent on OSAP-paid tuition, he said. McMaster Divinity College is relatively well-positioned to weather that storm, Ambrose said, but not all schools are so lucky.
“The impression I get is that the government knows full well what the impacts are,” he said.
“They’re not stupid. All I can assume is that at the highest levels where these decisions were made, they’re actually willing to allow career colleges and other schools to shut their doors … I think they’re trying to look like they’re doing something in the face of 300-whatever million dollars that they were not smart enough to pay attention to.”
Data obtained by The Canadian Press through a freedom-of-information request showed large increases in OSAP usage at a relatively small number of career colleges from 2020-21 to 2024-25.
The seven career colleges that had the highest OSAP usage in 2024-25 received $385 million in provincial grants – the same amount that went to students at all of Ontario’s publicly funded colleges that year.
Career Colleges Ontario has raised concerns since 2023 about what it calls potentially “suspicious activity” with OSAP usage at a few schools.
Deanna Hutten, a second-year master’s student in McMaster Divinity College’s counselling and spiritual care program, is borrowing money from family and working 10 more hours per week at her marketing job to make up for her OSAP being on hold.
The single mother to a one-year-old daughter who hopes to work in hospital chaplaincy said it is frustrating to be lumped in with some suspected bad actors.
“It definitely feels very unfair,” she said.
“They had known about this since 2023 that there were people kind of (allegedly) fudging the system, and now we as private career – not even career colleges, but private institutions – are kind of being swept into that field or that group of people, even though we’re not a part of that.”
At the Toronto Film School, there is also “tremendous uncertainty and anxiety” for many students, said president Andrew Barnsley. He is calling for prompt reinstatement of OSAP for eligible students, or at least a clear, expedited timeline to resolve the pause.
“The OSAP pause is deeply disappointing, and our greatest concern is the impact on our students who made significant commitments to their education with the reasonable expectation that financial assistance would be available,” he wrote in a statement.
“Many students have rearranged their lives, reduced or left employment, made child-care arrangements and, in some cases, relocated to Toronto in order to pursue their studies. They need to know whether they can meet their financial obligations, including life essentials like rent or food, and continue the programs in which they have already invested time, money and effort.”

title: Stop Obuasi SHTS head from contesting Juaben chairmanship amid sexual abuse allegations – Kojo Asante to NDC
body: The Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships at the Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Dr Kojo Asante, has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to prevent the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School from contesting the Juaben constituency chairmanship amid allegations of sexual misconduct. He says the allegations against the headmaster should be thoroughly investigated before political considerations are allowed to take precedence over accountability and the protection of children. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Friday, October 16, Dr Asante described the reported institutional failures surrounding the case as “mind-boggling”, questioning why concerns allegedly raised over an extended period did not trigger decisive action. His comments follow a directive by the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, for the Ghana Education Service (GES) to suspend the headmaster over the allegations. Dr Asante said he was particularly concerned that the headmaster could be allowed to pursue a political position while serious allegations remained unresolved. He cautioned against allowing political interests or pressure from constituents to undermine the need for a proper investigation, arguing that the allegations should be sufficient to prompt serious scrutiny of his candidacy. The CDD-Ghana official said he was deeply troubled by the potential lifelong psychological consequences of the alleged abuse on the affected students, urging the public to consider the harm the reported incidents could cause. He also questioned the effectiveness of the school’s oversight structures, including the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA), teachers, school management and other local stakeholders, given reports that the concerns had persisted for about a year. “It is a system failure that is mind-boggling,” he said, expressing concern that it took an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni to bring the matter to national attention. Dr Asante argued that the failure to act decisively on earlier reports could have exposed more students to harm, insisting that the case required a comprehensive investigation beyond the immediate circumstances of the student unrest. He stressed that allegations of sexual assault constitute a criminal matter and should not be treated solely as an administrative issue by the GES. According to him, the police must investigate the allegations, while the relevant authorities ensure that students are protected from potential further harm. He also questioned whether previous investigations had adequately examined the allegations that reportedly prompted the students’ protest, arguing that the inquiry should not focus exclusively on the unrest. Dr Asante said the underlying concerns must be addressed and those found culpable held accountable to prevent similar incidents. He warned that the case reflected a broader problem of accountability in Ghana, questioning how institutions could be expected to enforce responsibility at the highest levels of government if alleged misconduct at the school and municipal levels was not addressed effectively. “If we cannot hold a headmaster in Obuasi responsible and accountable for criminal conduct, how are we going to be holding a president responsible?” he asked. He called for a decisive response from the education authorities, law enforcement agencies and relevant political actors, stressing that protecting children and ensuring accountability must take precedence over partisan interests.

title: Donations Manager
body:
The Kyiv Independent – Ukraine’s biggest English language publication is hiring a Donations Manager. The Kyiv Independent is Ukraine’s main English-language news outlet. It was founded in November 2021 by a team of reporters and editors who were fired from the Kyiv Post for defending editorial independence, in partnership with a media consultancy company Jnomics. Today it’s a team of around 100 people based mostly in Kyiv. Publishing in English, we serve as Ukraine’s voice in the world and the world’s window into Ukraine. The Role As Donations Manager, you will lead the Kyiv Independent's relationships with its private supporters: individuals who have chosen to support us with donations, big or small. You will build and maintain these relationships through a steady flow of communication: listening with care, knowing how to turn goodwill into long-term support for some of our most ambitious projects. Success in this role means a growing community of donors who feel close to the Kyiv Independent and choose to stay with us. Responsibilities:
It’s a full-time position in the Kyiv office or remote (upon agreement).
Thanks for taking the time to apply to work with the Kyiv Independent. If you are among the qualified candidates, you will receive an email from a member of our hiring team to schedule an interview. Please note that while we would like to meet with all applicants, we may not have the opportunity to do so due to the volume of applications we receive.

title: Coal market is recovering, Russian presidential advisor says
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Coal will continue to be an attractive method of electric power generation, Advisor to Russian President Anton Kobyakov said.
"Coal has again become an attractive method of generating electric power and will continue to be such further on. Talks that coal will soon leave [the market] are clearly exaggerated," Kobyakov said.
The coal market is recovering now, he noted. East Asia is the main market at present, the advisor added.

title: ‘Thirty-three governors cannot be wrong,’ Onanuga says of Tinubu’s support
body: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, has defended the President’s economic record, citing the support of 33 governors and claiming that food prices have dropped and foreign investors are returning to Nigeria. Onanuga made the remarks in a post on Friday while reacting to a clip shared by Arise TV on X featuring Obafemi George, a member of the Media and Strategic Communications Committee of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council. He criticised television anchors for questioning Nigeria’s economic progress under Tinubu, accusing them of promoting the opposition’s narrative that nothing had improved since the President assumed office in 2023. “TV anchors keep pushing the opposition’s narrative that nothing has changed, positively, indeed, massively, since 2023. Their position has become so ridiculous that they keep parroting the old narrative, and now they question the NBS data on receding inflation. I will advise them to revisit the markets,” he wrote. The presidential aide claimed that the price of a bag of rice had fallen from about N120,000 to below N50,000, adding that it sold for N45,000 in his hometown. Onanuga also cited Nigeria’s foreign reserves, access to foreign exchange for businesses and the ability of Nigerians to use naira cards abroad as signs of economic progress under Tinubu. He said the country’s foreign reserves were approaching $60bn and argued that businesses could now obtain foreign exchange to import raw materials and equipment. The presidential aide further disputed claims that returning investors were mainly portfolio investors, saying foreign direct investment was bringing capital into the economy and creating jobs. “These facts are clear to anyone not blinded by partisanship and hatred for the leader who has laid a solid foundation for the economy and is poised to take the nation to a higher level of shared prosperity,” he added. The post ‘Thirty-three governors cannot be wrong,’ Onanuga says of Tinubu’s support appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Afghanistan urgently needs peace, stability — CSTO Secretary General
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Kabul is in dire need of peace, stability, and economic development, Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov said at a conference hosted by the CSTO, Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), and Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) on security in Central Asia and Afghanistan.
"Afghanistan is in dire need of peace, stability, and economic development. And under current conditions, breaking the vicious cycle of poverty, halting drug trafficking, terrorist activity, armed conflict outbreaks, and other threats is possible only through pragmatic, coordinated, and phased international cooperation with this country," Masadykov said.
The CSTO secretary general said that in this context, efforts between the CSTO, the CIS, and the SCO need to be better coordinated "to promote the peace process in Afghanistan." "The Taliban government has proven that it is a long-term political force in the country," he concluded.

title: Iran Army Navy identifies violating oil tanker in east Hormuz
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 16 (MNA) –Iran Army Navy has announced that an oil tanker violating maritime restrictions caught fire in a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz after switching off its tracking systems and attempting to navigate through the area.
The Army Navy of the Islamic Republic of Iran emphasized that uncoordinated movements within restricted routes and zones result in insecurity and pose significant risks to other vessels.
A few hours ago, as part of ongoing monitoring of the eastern Strait of Hormuz, surveillance teams from Iran’s Army Navy detected and identified a violating oil tanker that had caught fire within an unauthorized zone.

title: 'Egypt will never pose a threat': Netanyahu questioned Egypt's military expansion, Sisi says
body: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi revealed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had previously expressed concern over Egypt's military buildup, directly questioning why Cairo continued to expand its armed forces and purchase weapons.Speaking at a Thursday graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Police Academy in New Cairo, Sisi emphasized that Egypt's military expansion is not directed against Israel but is intended to safeguard national security and preserve peace in an unstable region."Netanyahu is responsible for his country, and he knows very well that Egypt will never pose a threat," Sisi said."On one occasion, he asked me, 'Why are you arming yourself?' He asked me that question. He said, 'Why are you buying weapons?'"Sisi says Egypt's military strength poses no threat to IsraelAccording to Sisi, he responded by urging Netanyahu to view Egypt's military capabilities in the same way Cairo views Israel's military strength."I told him, 'I have never viewed Israel's strength as a threat to me, and I believe you should also approach us with the understanding that Egypt's strength does not pose a threat to you.'"Sisi explained that Cairo considers a strong military essential to maintaining stability and protecting the country's security interests."We live in a turbulent region, and we need to be strong to preserve the peace we enjoy, not only with Israel but with the entire region," he said.According to the Egyptian president, Cairo's security doctrine is based on developing strong military and police forces capable of deterring threats and safeguarding the achievements of peace.Sisi says Netanyahu rejected Palestinian statehood as path to regional stabilitySisi also linked his remarks to Egypt's diplomatic relations with Israel and the Palestinian issue, saying he had repeatedly told Netanyahu since 2013 that establishing a Palestinian state would contribute to regional stability and Israel's integration into the Middle East."I told him that the opportunity to establish a Palestinian state would bring real stability to all of us," Sisi said."There would be genuine integration of Israel into the region. He was not convinced. He was not convinced."The remarks come amid growing Israeli concerns over Egypt's military buildup and the deployment of forces in the Sinai Peninsula, alongside public tensions between Cairo and senior Israeli officials.Sisi reiterated that Egypt remains committed to its peace agreement with Israel and has no "hidden ambitions" regarding Israeli territory.

title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Kojo Asante calls for taskforce to review protocols for handling sexual abuse in schools
body: The Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships at the Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Dr Kojo Asante, has called for a taskforce to review protocols for handling sexual abuse allegations in schools, following reports of alleged sexual misconduct at Obuasi Senior High Technical School. He says the case exposes serious weaknesses in the systems designed to protect students and highlights the need for clear procedures to ensure that allegations are reported, investigated and addressed promptly. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Friday, October 16, Dr Asante described the alleged institutional failures as “mind-boggling”, questioning why concerns reportedly raised before the student unrest at the school did not trigger decisive action. His comments follow a directive by the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, for the Ghana Education Service (GES) to suspend the headmaster over allegations of sexual misconduct. Dr Asante said the reported experiences of the affected students were particularly disturbing because of the potential lifelong psychological harm associated with sexual abuse. He questioned why several layers of oversight, including teachers, school management, the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) and local authorities, had allegedly failed to ensure an effective response to the concerns. According to him, the allegations reportedly persisted for about a year, yet it took an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni to bring the matter to national attention. He said the situation raised serious questions about whether existing reporting and accountability mechanisms within the education system were working effectively. Dr Asante argued that a review of the protocols should establish how school authorities must respond when allegations of sexual abuse emerge, including the steps required to protect students from potential further harm. He stressed that sexual assault allegations constitute potential criminal offences and should not be treated solely as administrative matters. “Administratively, that’s all you can do, but this is a criminal matter, and you have to bring in the police to investigate,” he said, calling for law enforcement agencies to be involved in investigating such complaints. He also expressed concern that previous interventions by the police and the Bureau of National Investigations (BNI), as he recalled, had not produced a satisfactory outcome. Dr Asante further insisted that investigations into the Obuasi case must examine the allegations that reportedly prompted the students’ protest rather than concentrating exclusively on the unrest itself. He said the reasons behind the protest and the students’ reaction were separate from the underlying allegations and both required appropriate attention. The CDD-Ghana official warned that failing to investigate complaints thoroughly and hold those found culpable accountable could allow similar incidents to recur. He also criticised what he perceived as a dismissive response to serious allegations, questioning whether Ghanaian society had become too accustomed to reports of abuse to demand decisive action. Dr Asante said the case reflected a broader accountability problem, arguing that institutions must demonstrate that misconduct will not be overlooked, regardless of the position held by the person accused. He called for the authorities to ensure that the allegations are properly investigated, the affected students are protected, and measures are introduced to prevent similar incidents in other schools.

title: Boeing Announces Winners of National Aeromodeling Competition
body:
DELHI, India, Oct 16, 2026. Boeing announced the winners of the 11th annual Boeing National Aeromodeling Competition, one of India’s largest and most popular aeromodeling programs designed for aspiring aerospace engineers. This year, the competition drew more than 1,179 students representing 115 institutions across India.



46 finalists from 14 teams were selected for the finale held at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi. Three teams were declared winners of the competition.

Salil Gupte, President, Boeing India & South Asia, said, "Now in its eleventh year, this competition has continued to grow into India’s largest aeromodeling platform, giving students an opportunity to turn their passion for aviation and engineering into hands-on experience. I congratulate all the participants and winners and thank our academic partners for their continued collaboration.”

The zonal rounds of the competition were held at IIT Kanpur, IIT Gandhinagar, IIT Madras, and Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT) Bhubaneswar.

The competition, sponsored by Boeing, and conducted in partnership with IIT Kanpur, IIT Gandhinagar, KIIT Bhubaneswar, IIT Madras, and Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer (FITT)-IIT Delhi began in 2013 to engage aerospace engineers in building industry solutions. Participants design, build, test, and fly fixed-wing aircraft models under defined performance, safety, and mission criteria.



This year, the students were given a challenge to focus on a “collaborative humanitarian airlift mission” that evaluated aircraft design, flight stability, payload integration, and coordinated mission execution across paired teams.

Over the years, Boeing has strategically invested in helping nurture talent for the aerospace sector in India. Its programs, including Boeing University Innovation Leadership Development (BUILD), past programs such as the Boeing HorizonX India Innovation Challenge and the Accelerated Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AME) Apprenticeship program have continued to empower entrepreneurs and are helping build a skilled workforce for the country’s aerospace and defence sector.

title: Day 1: Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair underway in Ho as firms showcase housing solutions
body: The Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair is underway at the Ho Sports Stadium in the Volta Region, with 19 institutions and businesses showcasing property options, building materials and services to help prospective homeowners and individuals planning to build make informed decisions. The three-day event, which opened on Friday, October 16, and runs until Sunday, October 18, brings together players in banking, real estate, construction, building materials, telecommunications, security and technology. Visitors have the opportunity to interact directly with exhibitors, explore available products and services, and seek information to guide their homeownership, property investment and construction plans. Republic Bank is engaging visitors on financial solutions relevant to their housing and other financial needs, while real estate and property development companies, including Nestas Homes Limited, Adonai Estate Limited and TDC Ghana Limited, are presenting opportunities in the property sector. Construction and building-materials suppliers are also showcasing products and services for different stages of building projects. They include Lipe Builders & Contractors, which operates in the construction sector; Akwaaba Building Materials, a supplier of building products; Interplast, which manufactures plastic piping and related products; Vol-link Roofing System, which specialises in roofing solutions; and Sintex Tanks, a provider of water-storage products. DoorMaster is also represented with door and access-related solutions, while Virtual Security Africa offers security solutions for properties and premises. Telecommunications company MTN is participating alongside C Techi GH Limited, Waylead Company GH Ltd, Ayuda App, Rhoyak Ventures, Simef Gold Limited and Lesh Fortune Ltd, extending the range of businesses visitors can engage with at the fair. The event provides a platform for prospective homeowners, property investors, contractors and people preparing to undertake building or renovation projects to ask questions, compare available options and obtain information directly from service providers. It also offers participating businesses an opportunity to connect with potential customers and showcase their products and services to residents of Ho and surrounding communities. With the fair currently underway and continuing through Sunday, members of the public are encouraged to troop to the Ho Sports Stadium to explore the exhibitions, engage participating companies and discover solutions that could support their housing and construction needs.

title: Children aged 5, 8 and 11 killed in US school shooting before suspect shot by bystander
body: A 16-year-old has shot dead three children and a teacher at a primary school in the US state of Oregon before he was killed by a bystander, police said. The suspect, who has not been named, forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary School in the city of Bend on Thursday afternoon by shooting at locked doors, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz confirmed. The teenager was shot dead by a community member who “pursued him into the school and engaged him”, Krantz said. Police arrived three minutes later. The three children killed were aged five, eight and 11. A seven-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to a hospital in a critical condition. It is unclear if the attacker had any links to the school. “We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy,” Steven Cook, the top administrative official of the local school district, said in a statement. “No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing.” Police said the attacker was a local 16-year-old boy, but they did not release any further details on him or the identity of the victims. They were alerted to an active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary at 12:59 local time (19:59 GMT), Bend Police Department spokeswoman Sheila Miller told reporters. The first call came from a person who said that an unknown suspect was shooting into their car with a long gun, police said. Photos released from the scene show a red truck with bullet holes. Minutes later, the local county dispatch received 911 calls reporting that the attacker had entered the school. Police said he shot at locks on the doors in order to force his way inside. Local media reports suggested the school received new classroom doors in 2022 which can be locked with the flip of a switch. A bystander saw the shooting begin to unfold, pursued the attacker into the school and shot him dead, police explained. Three minutes later, officers first arrived at the scene. They confirmed that the attacker had been killed, and then searched the school. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek praised the bystander who “heroically intervened” to stop further loss of life. A local newspaper reporter told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that the school was in lockdown during the shooting and that students were able to communicate with parents outside with their Apple watches. Michael Kohn, a reporter with Bulletin newspaper, said the incident had left the parents stunned. “This is a neighbourhood school. Parents are stunned. It’s just something you don’t expect to happen in Bend, Oregon. It’s a mountain town,” he said. Teacher Kathy Sheil Smith described to CNN affiliate KPTV how she tried to keep the children calm after spotting the gunman approach the school. “The looks on their faces was really hard to see,” she said. “Some kids were praying, some kids were consoling other kids. I’m sure that every teacher at the school thought ‘Today is the day that I am going to die,'” she added. Schools in Bend will be closed on Friday. Officials said the community needed time to heal. Around 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary School, which has more than 40 adult staff members, police said. According to the K-12 School Shooting Database, there were 235 shooting incidents at American schools last year and at least 140 so far this year. A person under the age of 18 cannot buy a firearm in Oregon. The state does allow juveniles to possess one with the permission of their parents but only for certain uses like hunting. Officials would not say exactly what type of weapon was used in the attack or how many rounds were fired. Multiple law enforcement sources told CBS News the suspect used a shotgun. Oregon has passed a broad range of gun safety laws in recent years, placing it 12th out of 50 states in terms of their strictness, by gun control advocacy group Everytown for Gun Safety.

title: Russian troops liberate 12 communities in Ukraine operation over week — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated 12 communities in the Kharkov and Zaporozhye Regions and the Donetsk People’s Republic over the week of October 10-16, including two communities during the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Last week, Battlegroup North units took control of the settlements of Lukashovo, Lobanovka, Reznikovo, Kupino, Nefyodovka and Chernoye and yesterday they established control of the settlements of Varvarovka and Nikolayevka in the Kharkov Region through active and decisive operations. <…> During the week, Battlegroup Center units liberated the settlements of Novotroitskoye, Petrovskoye and Lidino in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said in a statement.
"Over the past week, Battlegroup East units continued their advance deep into the enemy’s defenses and liberated the settlement of Nikolskoye in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry reported.
Russian troops delivered one massive and seven combined strikes by precision weapons and unmanned aerial vehicles on Ukrainian military-industrial facilities, logistics and telecommunications centers and ammunition depots over the week, the ministry reported.
"On October 10-16, 2026, the Russian Armed Forces delivered one massive and seven combined strikes, hitting military-industrial enterprises, logistics and telecommunications centers, transport infrastructure facilities used to support the Ukrainian army’s operations, sites producing and storing unmanned aerial vehicles, ammunition and materiel depots, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries," the ministry said.
Russian troops delivered strikes over the week, degrading some infrastructure facilities of Ukrainian ports used to receive and store military supplies, it said.
"In addition, some infrastructure facilities of Ukraine’s ports used to receive, store and distribute military cargo were degraded," the ministry said.
Russian troops struck 15 dry cargo ships involved in the delivery of Western weapons and military hardware to the Ukrainian army over the week, the ministry reported.
"During the week, 15 dry cargo ships involved in the delivery of Western weapons, military hardware, fuel and equipment for the needs of the Ukrainian army were hit," the ministry said.
Russia’s Battlegroup North thwarted all the Ukrainian army’s attempts during the past week to break out of the encirclement in the Kharkov Region, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units continued tightening the ring of encirclement of enemy formations in the northeast of the Kharkov Region and expanding the outer area of control. <…> All the enemy’s attempts to break out of the encirclement were thwarted," the ministry said.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted more than 1,675 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed five enemy armored combat vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the week, the ministry reported.
During the past week in the Kharkov and Sumy Regions, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of six mechanized brigades, two motorized infantry brigades, two airmobile brigades, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army, four territorial defense brigades and a National Guard brigade," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 1,675 personnel, five armored combat vehicles, 82 motor vehicles, three field artillery guns and eight electronic warfare stations in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the week, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted more than 1,550 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed 18 enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the week, the ministry reported.
"During the past week, Battlegroup West units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and two territorial defense brigades," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 1,550 personnel, 18 armored combat vehicles, 94 motor vehicles, 12 field artillery guns and 11 electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the week, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 1,155 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed nine enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the week, the ministry reported.
"Over the past week, Battlegroup South units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade, a mountain assault brigade, an airmobile brigade, an unmanned systems brigade of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and a territorial defense brigade," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 1,155 personnel, nine armored combat vehicles, 198 motor vehicles, 13 field artillery guns and two electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the week, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted more than 2,740 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed 37 enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the week, the ministry reported.
Over the past week, Battlegroup Center units "inflicted losses on formations of four mechanized brigades, a jaeger brigade, an airborne brigade of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and three National Guard brigades," the ministry said.
Overall, the Ukrainian army lost more than 2,740 personnel, 37 armored combat vehicles, 76 motor vehicles, 11 field artillery guns and 11 electronic warfare stations in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the week, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 1,695 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed seven enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the week, the ministry reported.
During the past week, Battlegroup East units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade, an assault brigade, three air assault brigades, three assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and two marine infantry brigades," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 1,695 personnel, seven armored combat vehicles, 53 motor vehicles, three field artillery guns and two electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the week, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 240 Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the week, the ministry reported.
"Last week, Battlegroup Dnepr units improved their tactical position and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a mountain assault brigade, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade," the ministry said.
"As many as 240 [Ukrainian] military personnel, an armored combat vehicle, 116 motor vehicles, five artillery guns and nine electronic warfare stations were destroyed," the ministry reported.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 5,695 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and four Flamingo cruise missiles over the week, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down seven guided aerial bombs, two rockets of the US-made HIMARS multiple launch rocket system, four Flamingo long-range cruise missiles, a Neptune long-range missile and 5,695 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 263,235 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,251 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,790 multiple rocket launchers, 36,738 field artillery guns and mortars and 74,686 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.
