title: Europe Must Tackle Dependency On Starlink, EU Leaders Say
body: EU leaders grappled Friday with how to tackle Ukraine’s dependence on Starlink satellite communications supporting its battlefield operations, as Kyiv was rocked by disruptions to the US-owned system. The bloc’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Europe did not have a readily available alternative to technology controlled by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, as she arrived at an EU summit where the issue will be high on the agenda. “Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine and unfortunately in (the) short term Europe can’t replace this capability,” Kallas said before the talks, where Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was also in attendance. Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink’s military-grade satellite service, for its battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and interceptor drones. It also uses SpaceX’s parallel Starlink civilian satellite system, but not for offensive operations. Musk has shifted stance on Ukraine several times since Russia’s invasion in 2022. Kyiv reported restrictions on its use of the Starlink system this week. Musk said any disruption was the responsibility of the US government, not his SpaceX firm. Kallas said the European Defence Agency had mapped all the “critical capabilities” that Europe was missing and needed to fulfil, adding Europe needed to fill these gaps “as soon as possible”. European leaders echoed the urgency for Europe to build its capacities. “Starlink is the key for Ukraine actually to fight or fight back,” Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs told reporters. “It takes time for us to have the same capabilities. We do have, but not enough. So this is strategically something we have to discuss today.” Zelensky was taking part in the leaders’ talks with Ukraine and Europe’s own security and defence on the agenda. Also addressing the Starlink issue, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said he had discussed with French President Emmanuel Macron Thursday “how we, as Europeans, can provide more of these kinds of services in the not too distant future”. Speeds were slower on the system on Wednesday, affecting connectivity, according to Ukrainian officials, who have suggested Washington was behind slower speeds reported on some Starlink internet terminals. British defence minister Wes Streeting also said he discussed Starlink with his US counterpart Pete Hegseth Thursday. “It’s not yet clear to us in the UK what happened, why the service interruption occurred. But I am reassured, and was reassured directly by Secretary Hegseth, that the service has been restored,” he told the BBC Friday. The post Europe Must Tackle Dependency On Starlink, EU Leaders Say appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ship fuel squeeze persists despite accelerating crude exports via Strait of Hormuz — Vitol
body:
NEW YORK, October 16. /TASS/. Accelerating crude supplies through the Strait of Hormuz aren’t translating into higher production of shipping fuel, Vitol’s Asia head Kieran Gallagher said.
"Many are looking to increased crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz as a silver bullet, but more crude does not necessarily mean more high-sulfur fuel oil," Gallagher was quoted as saying by Bloomberg.
"Refining margins are exceptionally strong and refiners have been maximizing throughput to capture those returns," he added, referring to refiners prioritizing other products such as diesel.
The supply squeeze has driven prices of ship fuel in Singapore, its biggest supplier globally, to the highest level since April, according to data provider ClearLynx.

title: 2027: Tinubu afraid to face Nigerians, has no business seeking re-election — ADC campaign
body: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has accused President Bola Tinubu of being afraid to face Nigerians, saying his reported decision not to campaign across all 36 states ahead of the 2027 election amounts to contempt for the electorate. The council said the move could give its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, an advantage, arguing that Nigerians deserve a leader willing to defend his record, answer questions and explain his plans for the country. The ADC-PCC Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, stated this while receiving a delegation of youths under the aegis of Young Voters for Atiku (YVA). Ologbondiyan said a president seeking re-election should be prepared to meet voters and account for his performance, rather than rely on official engagements as a reason to avoid nationwide campaigning. “What President Tinubu has done is a clear act of contempt against the Nigerian people. The APC is known for its contempt for Nigerians. How can a man who wants to be re-elected as president, after failing woefully, say he does not want to visit the people he seeks to govern? It is an aberration of norm,” he said. He rejected the argument that official duties could prevent Tinubu from campaigning nationwide, citing former Nigerian presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari, as well as American presidential candidates Donald Trump and Kamala Harris. “Saying that he (Tinubu) will be attending to official assignments is untrue, fake, deceitful and insincere. Didn’t former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari attend to official duties while campaigning for their return tickets? Didn’t Donald Trump campaign? Didn’t Kamala Harris campaign? Why is Tinubu’s case different?” Ologbondiyan queried. He further alleged that public anger over hunger, poverty, insecurity and economic hardship explained the president’s reported reluctance to engage voters across the country. “He knows Nigerians are hungry and angry. He knows that the average Nigerian finds it difficult to eat and to be secure. He has failed on all fronts, so he is afraid to face Nigerians. He is running away from the reality he created,” he said. Ologbondiyan urged young Nigerians to reject the APC in 2027, warning that another term for the ruling party would prolong the hardship citizens were experiencing. “I appeal to every young Nigerian to reject them. Let us collectively reject hunger, reject poverty, reject hardship and reject insecurity. The APC has brought only pain to Nigerians. It is time to say enough is enough,” he said. He described Atiku as physically fit and mentally alert, saying the former vice-president was prepared to campaign across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He also pledged that an ADC government would pursue economic recovery, wealth creation, improved security and better living standards. “Atiku Abubakar will bring back subsidy to reduce cost of petroleum products, create wealth, end hunger in our land, secure our nation and restore our battered economy. He has the experience, the capacity and the compassion to rescue Nigeria. He is fit, ready and prepared to lead Nigeria out of this present predicament,” Ologbondiyan added. The ADC-PCC also claimed that the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council had strengthened its own political standing, alleging that the event attracted no endorsements from ADC members or sympathisers. The post 2027: Tinubu afraid to face Nigerians, has no business seeking re-election — ADC campaign appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Muted Response by NATO to First-Ever Russian Drone Attack vs. Cargo Ship in Romanian Territory
body:
Reaction to deadly military drone attacks by Russia against civilian cargo ships in the territorial waters of NATO member state Romania – a theoretical act of war – was cautious, with senior officials in Bucharest and Brussels on Thursday declaring it “unacceptable” and “deplorable,” but not invoking Atlantic Alliance collective defense articles against the Kremlin.
Romanian interim Defense Minister Radu Miruță , in comments published by the mainstream Digi24 news platform, said that there was “no certainty” that Russian drones had struck two tankers near the Romanian port town Sulima in the Danube Delta, and stated his office was coordinating with the Bulgarian Defense Ministry to send a joint letter of concern to NATO headquarters about the incidents.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to Romanian and Ukrainian news reports military drones breached the NATO air frontier at about 3 a.m. on Oct. 14 to hit the Comoros-flagged oil tanker Yara well inside Romanian territorial waters. It had been anchored about 8-10 nautical miles (14.8-18.5 km, or 9.2-11.5 statute miles) from Sulima. A fire breaking out following the drone’s detonation was extiguished and the Yara’s crew of 17 abandoned ship without incident.
At approximately the same time a drone or drones attacked and set afire the San Marine-flagged tanker Wine Trader as she stood at anchor without cargo some 12-14 nautical miles (22.2-25.9 ķm, or 13.8-16.1 statute miles) to the south-east of Sulima. Five crew were rescued and seven thought lost amid difficult sea conditions.
Miruță said that Romanian air defenses had not seen those particular aircraft coming.
“On the radars of the Ministry of Defense and the Coast Guard, this drone was not seen coming towards the ship that suffered this fire, which is now extinguished. The ship (Wine Trader) is heading to the Port of Constanta, where checks will be made when it arrives. If it was a drone, the technical expertise should observe this and then this aspect will be certain,” Miruță said in part. “More checks will be made to confirm whether it was a drone, if it was something else.
“Drones have no business in Romanian airspace, whether they hit a ship or not. This should not be something we get used to, but it should be something we respond to diplomatically,” Miruță said .
By international convention an attack against civilian shipping in territorial waters of a sovereign state, if launched by another state, is a definable act of war. The internationally-recognized extent of a country’s territorial waters is 12 nautical miles, a standard used by NATO member states.
NATO’s Article 4 gives member states the right to consult and request assistance in case of a threat to its territorial integrity. Article 5 of the NATO stipulates that an armed attack against any NATO state constitutes an armed attack against all NATO members and could trigger the use by NATO of armed force in collective defense.
Romanian interim Foreign Minister Oana Țoi in comments on her personal X channel that Russia bears “full responsibility” for turning the Black Sea into a war zone and called its attacks against ships and sailors passing through those waters “a crime.” Toiu said her government’s stance was that discussions with NATO fellow members was the best way to prevent Russian attacks in the future.
“We are coordinating closely with our allies and partners. We will intensify our efforts to strengthen NATO’s collective capacity to respond effectively to such incidents and to strengthen its deterrence and defense posture,” Țoiu said. “We continue to call for a ceasefire in the Black Sea, to eliminate risks to civilian ships and to restore safe navigation on this essential maritime route for global food trade.”
Unitățile aeriene și navale ale Gărzii de Coastă (GdC/MAI) și ale Inspectoratului General pentru Situații de Urgență (IGSU/MAI) sunt implicate activ în operațiunile de căutare și salvare, în vederea găsirii membrilor dați dispăruți ai echipajului navei care a fost atacată în…
Russia during the first two weeks of October has intensified its naval strike campaign against cargo shipping transiting the Black Sea economic exclusion zones (EEZ) of NATO member states Bulgaria and Romania.
Confirmed incidents include the sinking of a cargo ship (2 crew dead 11 rescued) off Romania’s coast on Oct. 5, the sinking to one merchant ship and heavy damage to a second off Bulgaria’s coast on Oct. 6 (at least 10 crew lost, 18 rescued, some injured), a cargo ship in Bulgarian EEZ waters hit by drones and abandoned on Oct. 12 (all 15 crew rescued) and a cargo ship sunk in Romanian EEZ waters the same night (5 crew rescued, at least 11 missing).
Overnight on Oct. 13-14, one night before the Sulima strikes, according to a Romani Defense Ministry statement, Russian drones entered Romanian airspace and overflew Sulima port.
NATO air defenses launched F-18 fighters that failed to intercept the reported two or three drone encroachers, which returned unharmed to Ukrainian airspace. In air battles over Ukraine, that same night, Ukrainian air defenses claimed successful intercept and destruction of 115 out of 128 Russian military drones.
Defense Minister Miruță, commenting on the Oct. 14-15 violation of Romanian airspace by Russian drones for the second night running, explained to Romanian taxpayers it’s not so easy to locate a hostile drone and destroy it.
“The Black Sea is twice the size of Romania. Expecting that everything that flies, at any point in the Black Sea, will be detected and intercepted is an unrealistic expectation,” the civilian head of Romania’s armed forces said. “There are very frequent situations in which we see these drones, we track them, some disappear from the radar. The radar image does not provide details about the reason why they disappeared. Maybe they ran out of fuel, maybe they entered an area where our radars can no longer see because of the distance. There are many possibilities.”
On the night Oct 14-15, in airspace over Ukraine, Ukrainian air defenses claimed successful interception and destruction of 536 out of 580 Russian military drones.Union leader Adrian Mihălcioiu, President of Romania’s Seafarer’s Union (Sindicatul Liber al Navigatorilor) in Thursday televised comments called on the government to review its rules of engagement and access procedures for civilian shipping. He said the Sulima strike marked the first time in the Russo-Ukraine War that Russian weaponry had hit a ship in Romanian territorial waters with loss of life and that Russian attack was intentional. The Romanian state and its allies should take action to give effective protection to mariners, he said.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte on Thursday held a meeting in Brussels with President Nicușor Dan and Bulgarian PM Radev about Black Sea security and Russian attacks on commercial shipping and maritime free trade. Rutte in subsequent comments to media said that NATO has already strengthened its eastern-flank posture and, “will continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed.”
No activation of Article 4 was announced. Rutte’s official comment did not mention Russia by name.
Good meeting with 🇧🇬 Bulgarian PM @RumenRadevPM and 🇷🇴 Romanian President @NicusorDanRO about security in the Black Sea & the latest attacks on commercial shipping. NATO has strengthened our posture along the eastern flank including with increasing counter-drone capabilities.… pic.twitter.com/O0aBdNFMWN
Stefan Korshak is the Kyiv Post Senior Defense Correspondent. He is from Houston Texas, is a Yalie and since the mid-1990s has worked as correspondent/photographer for newswire, newspapers, television and radio. He has reported from five wars but most enjoys doing articles on wildlife and nature. You can read his weekly blog on the Russo-Ukraine War on Facebook, Substack and Medium. His new book on the 2022 Siege of Mariupol is available on Amazon UK and Amazon US .

title: Famine Affects Southern Madagascar, Braces For Looming El Nino
body: With scrawny arms and bellies swollen by malnutrition, a dozen children waited for a meal at a World Food Programme centre in an arid area of southern Madagascar scarred by famine and bracing for the looming El Nino. Flour porridge simmered on a stove at the site that opened in the small town of Ifotaka the year after a 2021–2022 famine then described by the United Nations as the first in the world caused by climate change. A staff member had to slip away: she had just learned of the death of a malnourished two-year-old. Even before the full impact due in the coming months of the El Nino warming pattern, which experts have said is on course to be the strongest on record, people in Madagascar’s far south are already going hungry. The World Meteorological Organization has warned of “increased drought risk” in southern Africa as the months-long phenomenon begins in October, with countries across the planet — from Brazil to India — also vulnerable. In Madagascar, international aid cuts and spiking inflation caused by the Middle East war add to the threat of severe hunger. A general view of the riverbed of the Mandrare River in southern Madagascar’s Anosy region on September 23, 2026(Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP) Ifotaka — an inland town of wooden shacks and corrugated iron huts — was the epicentre of the 2021–2022 “kere”, as periods of hunger are known here. Around 30,000 people in the surrounding region of sandy soil and bristling cacti suffered from a life-threatening lack of food. To survive, they boiled pieces of cactus and scraps of animal hide. Fragile Climate Context “There has been a dramatic increase in climate-related events in Madagascar,” WFP country director Tania Goosens told AFP. “In 20 years, there have been 35 cyclones, eight floods and five severe droughts,” she said, triple the climate events of the previous 20 years. “So we’re really in a very, very fragile context,” Goosens said. In the nearby coastal village of Manindra, where the ocean taunts people working dry land, rainfall was normally expected from late September, said 46-year-old farmer James Tsirimalaza. “Unfortunately, there’s no rain,” he said. Anticipating a crisis, the Save the Children NGO has doubled its normal budget for Madagascar, country representative Tatiana Dasy told AFP. By April next year, 39 percent of children under the age of five will be suffering from acute malnutrition in Madagascar’s “Grand South”, according to predictions by the UN-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC). Children suffering from malnutrition play as they receive nutritional care at the Learning Center for Nutritional Rehabilitation and Early Childhood Development (FARNE) in central Ifotaka, on September 24, 2026(Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP) This amounts to nearly 270,000 children. The conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran that is driving up the price of oil and fertiliser will only add to the risks, it warned in July. These increases will “directly affect the costs of transport, pumping, fertilisers, fuel for fishing, agricultural inputs and food prices,” it said. Annual food inflation in the large Indian Ocean island stood at 10.4 percent in July, compared with 6.8 percent in January. ‘Even Worse’ An hour away in a 4×4 vehicle — which no local owns — the hospital in Amboasary-Atsimo has recorded six deaths this year of malnourished children with medical complications. In 2022, when the famine continued until harvests in early May, 15 children died there. On a wall, the logo of USAID — the US foreign aid agency dismantled in 2025 — is a reminder that international help is also drying up. The US funds covered patient transportation and health training via humanitarian agency Medecins du Monde, but ended two months earlier, an official told AFP. A general view of parched land showing deep surface cracks following several consecutive weeks without rainfall in southern Madagascar(Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP) The WFP predicts around 3.7 million people in Madagascar will experience “crisis-level food insecurity”, Goosens said. “We haven’t seen that in the country before, so it’s even worse than in 2021–2022.” The programme aimed to support 720,000 people this year, but funding had barely reached half of what was required, she said. Waiting For The Sun At the WFP office, Eva Razafindrazaka held her grandson, being treated for malnutrition, and explained she could not water her crops because they were too far from the communal water point. “But those who have solar pumps can,” the 51-year-old said. As cattle were returned to their enclosure for the night, a farmer struggled to transport solar panels on a wheelbarrow, its wooden wheels sinking into the sand. “If I leave them, I won’t find them again,” said Manjomaro Andrianantenaina, 25. He only got the panels the day before. A general view of a planted field in Anjamahavelo in southern Madagascar, on September 23, 2026.(Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP) Drilling a well with a solar-powered pump cost him more than two million ariary (about $450), unaffordable to most in the region where more than 90 percent of people live below the poverty line of $2.15 per day, according to the World Bank in 2023. “I used to worry about the lack of rain when it was hot,” he said. “Now I wait for the sun so I can pump water from underground.” AFP The post Famine Affects Southern Madagascar, Braces For Looming El Nino appeared first on Channels Television .

title: 2027: Spanish group, Fact Check Nigeria train journalists on indigenous-language reporting
body:
A Spanish organisation, Fundación para la Internacionalización de las Administraciones Públicas (FIAP), and FactCheck Africa have trained journalists on reporting electoral issues in indigenous languages ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general election.
The training, held in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, focused on addressing translation gaps and other language-related challenges that could affect the accuracy and inclusiveness of electoral information reaching diverse communities.
The three-day programme, which ran from 13 to 16 October, was the first of a two-part southern and northern series, with the second part scheduled to hold in Abuja.
The workshop, organised under the European Union Support to ECOWAS in Peace, Security and Governance (EPSG) Project, brought together journalists from different media platforms and states, including Lagos, Enugu, Edo and Oyo.
FIAP is a Spanish public-sector organisation that specialises in promoting public administration through international cooperation programmes and projects.
Mustapha Lawal, an official with FactCheck Africa, in his opening address said the aim of the programme is to train media professionals to provide accurate and inclusive electoral coverage in indigenous languages ahead of the upcoming elections.
Mr Lawal noted that the programme will address the “translation gap” and nuances lost when translating English electoral terms into local languages.
He said participants will create an unofficial language register to standardise electoral terminology across various indigenous languages.
“This three-day workshop is to help us see how we can come together to create an official language register, not particularly officially, but a step to making it official across many different languages that we have in the room,” Mr Lawal said.
He said they will also work together to improve the accuracy of reporting to prevent misinformation and disinformation caused by poor translation.
Mr Lawal emphasised that the participants will ensure inclusive reporting that respects vulnerable communities and avoids accidental offence through linguistic nuance.
During the three-day training, media professionals were taken through indigenous language ecosystems, electoral concepts and terminologies, misinformation and verification, and electoral glossary and style sheets.
Also, participants had practical sessions where they translated real-world electoral information into their local languages, including Yoruba, Ibibio and Igbo.
The facilitators cut across academic and media organisations including Nsikak Idiong, a professor of journalism, political communication and media studies from the University of Uyo.
Kingsley Alozie, a freelance journalist, expressed delight in participating in the programme to scrutinise electoral reportage.
Theresa Donatus, a journalist with the Daily Times, noted that her reporting will help citizens make informed choices about their civic duties.
“One of my key takeaways is that effective electoral communication goes beyond sharing information; it requires accuracy, context, inclusiveness, and responsibility,” Ms Donatus said.
Also, Ezinne Alozie, a broadcast journalist with Darling FM, said language is a “universal currency and a form of identity.”
She said it is important that when information is passed through any means, it is thoughly factchecked.

title: White House ordered limits on Ukraine’s military satellite service — Reuters. Who made the decision remains unclear
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); White House officials instructed Pentagon leaders to limit Starshield, SpaceX’s military-grade satellite service used by Ukrainian forces, Reuters reported on 15 October, citing three officials. The report came a day after a senior US official told Axios the Trump administration had nothing to do with the alleged Starlink restrictions. Ukrainian forces rely on US-controlled satellite technology for battlefield operations and for intercepting Russian drones aimed at Ukrainian cities, so the latest restrictions have raised questions about how reliably they can depend on it. Senior US official denies president requested restrictions Asked about the order, a senior US official replied, “No such request was ever made by the president.” The White House did not respond to questions about whether other administration officials might have made the request. Ukrainian officials contacted the White House, State Department, and Pentagon on Tuesday and Wednesday and were told it was a White House decision. European allies question Starlink restrictions European officials raised concerns about the restrictions. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul criticized the throttling and said Ukraine must continue to receive full support, Spiegel reported on 15 October. Wadephul said Germany had questions for the US, noting that Germany finances part of the Starlink technology used in Ukraine. On 16 October, UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had assured him in a face-to-face meeting that Starlink was back up and running, the Guardian reported . However, a Ukrainian Defense Ministry source said that military-grade terminals were working in motion again, but only at speeds of up to 160 km/h. New data-speed restrictions disrupted drone missions The military Starshield package previously had no data-speed restrictions, Ukraine’s 7th Rapid Response Corps told Novynarnia. Ukrainian officials said that after the restrictions were imposed, terminals disconnected when drones exceeded 160 km/h and sometimes at 80 km/h. The Corps also reported 10–20-second connection drops at 110–120 km/h on the Huliaipole front, which made drones harder to control. One unit had to cancel some missions. The restrictions came as US President Donald Trump pressed Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries, blaming them for soaring energy prices ahead of November’s midterm elections. Ukraine suspects SpaceX imposed the restrictions to pressure Kyiv over the refinery strikes, but that motive has not been confirmed. title: Russian attacks kill at least 3, injure 53 across Ukraine, as Moscow hammers energy infrastructure
body:
At least three people were killed and 52 others injured across Ukraine over the past day, as Russian attacks targeted energy infrastructure in several oblasts, regional authorities said on Oct. 16.
In western Volyn Oblast , Russian attacks injured two people and left 370,000 people without electricity, regional governor Roman Romaniuk said. Russian attacks with jet-powered Shahed-type drones across 20 locations destroyed civilian and critical infrastructure, the governor added.
Ukraine's Air Force said Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with 149 Shahed-type drones, 108 of them jet-powered. The Air Force said it neutralized 114 of the Russian drones, 108 of them jet-powered, across 24 locations.
In Kyiv , a Russian drone crashed in Kyiv's Pechersk District on Oct. 15, injuring seven people and causing damage to a residential building, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Three of the injured people were hospitalized, Klitschko said . The Russian drone crashed near a five-story residential building, damaging the facades of nearby buildings, as well as setting a car on fire, he added.
In Kyiv Oblast , two people were injured over the past day, according to regional governor Tymur Tkachenko . One person was injured during a morning attack in the Fastiv District that also damaged eight residential buildings on Oct. 14, while another person was injured after a Russian attack in the Buchan District on the morning of Oct. 15.
In Kharkiv Oblast , three people were injured in Russian attacks over the past day, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said. Among the three injured was a 105-year-old woman, Syniehubov said. Russia attacked the oblast with glide bombs, missiles, and FPV-drones across four settlements, the governor added.
In eastern Donetsk Oblast , Russian attacks over the past day killed one person and injured six others, according to regional governor Vadym Filashkin . One person was killed and three injured in Kramatorsk, while three others were injured in Sloviansk, Filashkin said. Russian attacks also damaged private houses, infrastructure, shops, and cars.
In Cherkasy Oblast , Russian attacks on the city of Uman injured five people, regional governor Ihor Taburets said. Three injured people were hospitalized, and a Russian attack elsewhere led to a fire in a warehouse, the governor said.
In southern Kherson Oblast , two people were killed and six others injured over the past day, regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin said. Russia struck the oblast with artillery fire and drones, Prokudin said, damaging residential areas and social infrastructure.
In Rivne Oblast , seven people sought medical help after a Russian attack on civilian infrastructure, including residential buildings, according to regional governor Oleksandr Koval . None of the seven injured had to be hospitalized, Koval said.
A Russian attack on Ternopil Oblast , injured five people on Oct. 15, as Russia attacked the city twice, setting fire to a business building, according to regional governor Taras Pastukh .
In northeastern Sumy Oblast, six people were injured in Russian attacks over the past day, the Sumy military administration said. Russian troops carried out 70 attacks on 38 settlements, using artillery, mortars, FPV-drones, UAVs, and glide bombs, the administration said.
In southern Odesa Oblast , four people were injured in Russian attacks over the past day, according to regional governor Oleh Kiper . Russia struck private houses, a manufacturing enterprise, as well as energy infrastructure, the governor added.

title: Kosmos Energy, Eni, TotalEnergies and AGL Win Big at African Energy Awards
body: Kosmos Energy Ghana and its CEO, Andrew Inglis, were among the top winners at the 2026 African Energy Awards. Eni, TotalEnergies, and Africa Global Logistics (AGL) were also recognised for their work in entrepreneurship, petroleum production, exploration, renewable energy, and logistics. The awards were presented during African Energy Week in Cape Town, South Africa, celebrating achievements across Africa’s energy sector. Kosmos Energy Ghana received the CSR Project of the Year award for its Kosmos Innovation Centre, and Mr Inglis was given the Mohammed S. Barkindo Lifetime Achievement Award. Eni was named Exploration and Production Leader of the Year, TotalEnergies won Power Africa Developer of the Year, and AGL was recognised as International Service Provider of the Year. Kosmos Energy was recognised for supporting entrepreneurs The CSR award recognised Kosmos Energy Ghana’s support for entrepreneurs through the Kosmos Innovation Centre, which provides mentorship and business development assistance to businesses in Ghana’s agriculture and energy value chains. The initiative aims to help entrepreneurs build commercially viable businesses, strengthen their capacity, and create employment opportunities. Kosmos Energy is a major investor in Ghana’s petroleum industry through its interests in the Jubilee and Tweneboa-Enyenra-Ntomme (TEN) fields. The company is still investing in these fields as Ghana works to reverse declining oil production and attract new investment in its petroleum sector. This recognition shows how private-sector investment can support businesses beyond just oil and gas. For Ghana, it also raises questions about the measurable impact of corporate social investment programmes on business survival, revenue growth and job creation. Kosmos CEO receives lifetime achievement award Mr Inglis was honoured for a career spanning more than four decades in the energy industry. He joined Kosmos Energy in 2014 after spending 30 years at British Petroleum (BP), where he rose to become Chief Executive Officer of its Exploration and Production business. At Kosmos, he has overseen investments in major African energy developments, including the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim liquefied natural gas project involving Mauritania and Senegal, which achieved first LNG production in 2025. His leadership has also been associated with continued investment in Ghana’s Jubilee and TEN fields. The award comes as Ghana seeks to extend the productive life of existing petroleum fields, encourage additional drilling and strengthen domestic natural gas supplies. For the country, sustaining investment will be critical to improving oil production, supporting energy security and maintaining investor confidence. Eni recognised for exploration successes Italian energy company Eni received the Exploration and Production Leader of the Year award for discoveries across its African operations. These discoveries include the Algaita-01 well in Angola’s Block 15/06 and the Murene South-1X well in Block CI-501 offshore Côte d’Ivoire. The Murene South-1X well is part of the larger Baleine development, which started production in 2023. ENI’s operations in Ghana include its flagship integrated oil and natural gas project located off the west coast of Ghana, which utilises the John Agyekum Kufuor floating production, storage, and offloading (FPSO) vessel and an onshore gas plant in Sanzule (Western Region). TotalEnergies wins renewable energy award. TotalEnergies won Power Africa Developer of the Year for its Hydra hybrid energy project in South Africa. The project combines a 216-megawatt solar plant with a battery energy storage system that can store 500 megawatt-hours of electricity. According to the awards announcement, the facility should generate more than 400 gigawatt-hours each year, enough to power over 200,000 homes. AGL recognised for logistics services Africa Global Logistics was named International Service Provider of the Year for its integrated logistics network covering ports, rail, road transport and warehousing. The company supports energy projects from construction to production, moving equipment, materials, and energy products between sites and international markets. Formerly known as Bolloré Africa Logistics, AGL joined the MSC Group in 2022. This recognition shows how important efficient logistics are for cutting costs and supporting energy infrastructure development. The awards highlight the importance of investment in petroleum production, entrepreneurship, exploration, renewable energy and logistics.

title: Citadel system shows high efficiency when neutralizing enemy drones — Defense Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Russia’s state-of-the-art Citadel anti-aircraft artillery system uses minimal shells to take out uncrewed boats, as well as lightly armored vehicles and drones, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"With a high degree of automation, the use of AI, and a modular architecture, the system can effectively engage unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), uncrewed boats, and even lightly armored vehicles with minimal ammunition consumption," the ministry said in a statement.
It specified that the Citadel 30-mm automatic cannon uses shrapnel shells with programmable detonation timing to destroy enemy drones. In addition, the ministry noted that the system includes a control post for coordinating the operation of firing modules and other equipment, a surveillance radar station, firing modules, and a munition package.

title: Russian Lawmakers Propose School Fees for Central Asian Migrants’ Children
body: Russia relies on millions of workers from Central Asia, but lawmakers want to charge some of their children, typically aged 15–17, for the final two years of public schooling. The move comes after tougher enrollment rules that have left thousands of migrant children struggling to attend Russian schools. The proposal, submitted to the government by deputies from the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR) on October 14, would require foreign citizens and stateless people to pay for education in grades 10 and 11 . LDPR leader Leonid Slutsky argued that migrant families should bear the costs of educating their children in Russian upper-secondary schools, allowing public funds to be redirected toward Russian students. The party claimed that more than 130,000 foreign children attend grades 10–11, costing the state over 37 billion rubles (about $440 million) annually. However, these figures contradict data from Russia’s Ministry of Education analyzed by the data project Tochno , which found approximately 130,000 foreign pupils and another 3,000 stateless pupils enrolled across all school grades in 2025–26, with only 4% of foreign pupils attending grades 10–11. That would put the number of foreign pupils in the final two grades at roughly 5,200, casting doubt on the LDPR’s estimated savings. Growing Pressure on Migrant Families The proposed fees follow a series of Russian restrictions that have already made it more difficult for Central Asian families to educate their children in Russia. Since April 2025, foreign children seeking admission to Russian schools have been required to demonstrate sufficient Russian-language proficiency and provide documentation establishing their legal residence. Enrollment among children from Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Kyrgyzstan fell by 27% in the 2025–26 school year, from approximately 122,000 to 89,000. In January 2026, Tajikistan’s Minister of Education and Science Rahim Saidzoda reported that approximately 9,000 Tajik children had returned from Russia during 2025 following difficulties continuing their education there. Kyrgyzstan’s membership in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) raises a separate legal question. The EAEU treaty recognizes the right of migrant workers’ children to receive education in the country where their parents work, subject to that country’s legislation. However, it does not explicitly guarantee free tuition, leaving unclear whether children of workers from EAEU member states would qualify for exemptions. For migrant families, the immediate consequences would depend on the eventual tuition charges and exemptions. Some parents might choose vocational education for their children after grade nine, while others could leave them with relatives in their home countries rather than incur additional schooling expenses in Russia. Additional education costs could discourage migrant workers from bringing their families to Russia, even as the country continues to rely on Central Asian labor. Central Asia’s Dependence on Remittances The proposed fees would affect families whose earnings are often vital to their home countries’ economies. Tajikistan is the most dependent on remittances relative to the size of its economy, Kyrgyzstan relies particularly heavily on earnings from Russia, and Uzbekistan receives the largest remittance inflows in absolute terms. According to The Times of Central Asia ‘s Central Asia Balance Sheet , which draws on World Bank data, personal remittances received were equivalent to 57.7% of Tajikistan’s gross domestic product (GDP) in 2025, 17.6% of Kyrgyzstan’s GDP in 2024, and 14.3% of Uzbekistan’s GDP in 2025. Russia remains the dominant source of remittances for several Central Asian states. It accounted for approximately 93% of Kyrgyzstan’s remittances in 2025 and 72.4% of Uzbekistan’s in the first quarter of 2026. Russian border statistics recorded approximately 1.9 million work-related entries by citizens of Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Kyrgyzstan during the first half of 2026, although this represented a 15% decline from a year earlier.

title: Tehran plans to invite Gazprom to develop gas fields in Iran
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. Iran plans to invite Gazprom to develop gas fields in the Islamic Republic, Iranian Deputy Oil Minister, CEO of the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) Saeed Tavakoli said at Russian Energy Week.
"Yes, we plan it," he said when asked a respective question.
Speaking about joint gas production, the official said that Tehran and Moscow "have no specific program in this regard." "Iran will employ the potential of Gazprom and other Russian companies in accordance with the terms of contracts currently under discussion," he noted.
"We hope that the agreement on transportation of Russian gas to Iran will be brought to the stage of practical implementation," the deputy minister added.
In 2022, the National Iranian Oil Company and Gazprom signed a memorandum on strategic cooperation.
The Russian Energy Week (REW) International Forum is taking place from October 14 to 16. It is being held with the support of the Government of the Russian Federation, the Ministry of Energy of the Russian Federation, and the Government of Moscow. The Roscongress Foundation organizes the forum. TASS is the information partner of Russian Energy Week.

title: No ammonia leak threat in Volyn region after Russian strikes – official
body:
Rescuers in Volyn have fully mitigated the consequences of the Russian strike on the town of Manevychi, Head of the Regional Military Administration Roman Romaniuk reported.
"There is no risk of any ammonia leak on the enterprise's territory. Generally, the tank storing the ammonia was not damaged. Only minor distribution pipes were damaged, and this is not critical at all. A protection system was triggered, making a direct ammonia leak into the air impossible. Therefore, there is no threat whatsoever to local residents," Romaniuk stated on We – Ukraine TV channel.
As reported, as a result of the strike on the territory of the Agrofrukt LTD enterprise in Manevychi, one person was killed and eight were injured. A fire broke out on the premises.
Agrofrukt LTD, with 100% of its capital owned by Polish citizens, is part of Polko Group. It is a leader in Ukraine in the export of organic berries and cooperates with local farmers, purchasing products from them. As of 2021, such plantations were located in five districts of Volyn region, covering a total area of about 30 hectares. According to Opendatabot, the company's revenue for 2025 amounted to UAH 344.526 million, which is 1.22% less than in 2024, and its net profit was UAH 7.12 million, down 2.4% from the previous year.

title: Turkey Issues Navtex for Live-Fire Exercise South of Kastellorizo
body: Turkey has challenged Greece’s maritime authority south of Kastellorizo after issuing its own Navtex for a multinational live-fire exercise scheduled for October 19. Turkey has issued a maritime safety notice for a multinational live-fire exercise south of the southeastern Aegean island of Kastellorizo, hours after Greece published a similar notice for the planned military activity. The exercise, named Eunomia , has been planned since last spring and is organised under the Quadripartite Initiative involving Greece, France, Italy and Cyprus. The Turkish notice, transmitted by the Antalya Navtex station, disputes Greece’s authority to issue maritime warnings for the area, claiming it falls under Turkish jurisdiction and that Antalya is the competent station to issue the relevant notices. The move adds to ongoing tensions between Athens and Ankara over maritime jurisdiction in the eastern Mediterranean. Live-Fire Exercise Scheduled for October 19 The Eunomia exercise is scheduled to include live firing between 0400Z and 1000Z on October 19 , within a designated maritime area south of Kastellorizo. The Turkish notice also refers to multinational aeronautical activities planned across a wider area later that day. The exercise brings together Greece, France, Italy and Cyprus through the Quadripartite Initiative, a framework for regional cooperation that includes military activities and coordination among the four countries. Electricity Interconnector Route Also in Focus The maritime area covered by the Greek and Turkish notices lies along the planned route of the French research vessel Abeille Marengo . The vessel is expected to conduct surveys connected to the planned Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnector cable, once Athens issues the relevant Navtex. The project, known as the Great Sea Interconnector, is intended to establish an electricity link between Greece and Cyprus, with plans to extend the connection to Israel. The overlapping notices come as the project continues to draw attention to maritime jurisdiction and the competing positions of Greece and Turkey in the eastern Mediterranean. The October 19 exercise will take place amid renewed diplomatic and strategic sensitivities in the region, with Greece, Cyprus, France and Italy cooperating through Eunomia. The post Turkey Issues Navtex for Live-Fire Exercise South of Kastellorizo appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Navantia to modernize Angola's Mandume-class patrol vessels
body:
Spanish shipbuilder Navantia has signed a contract to repair and modernize two Mandume-class patrol vessels for the Angolan Navy.
The contract, signed with Simportex, the Angolan state-owned company responsible for procurement for the Ministry of Defence, involves the modernization of the patrol vessels Golfinho and Atlântico, built at the Spanish state-owned Empresa Nacional Bazán - now Navantia - in the early 1990s.
In addition, the contract includes training for a number of officers of the Angolan Navy in Spain, as well as two years of life-cycle support and knowledge transfer to the Navy to enable the maintenance of the vessels in Angola.
The work will take place at the San Fernando (Cádiz) shipyard.
This order from the Angolan government marks another step forward in Navantia’s international defence market for its Repairs and Services business area, particularly in Africa.

title: Foxtrot gang's teenage hitman jailed for 20 years over UK murder plot
body: A Norwegian teenager who flew to the UK to carry out a murder on behalf of Iran-backed criminals has been jailed for 20 years. Johannes Natland, 19, was hired by the Foxtrot crime network to carry out a “hit” on an unknown target in exchange for £21,000 ($28,000). The network, along with its founder, Kurdish-born gangster Rawa Majid , has been placed under sanctions by the US and the UK for carrying out attacks on Jewish and Israeli targets on behalf of Iran , using teenagers recruited through social media apps. It is known for hiring teenagers for attacks that Europol has called "violence-as-a-service". In sentencing Natland, Justice Cheema-Grubb said: "The Foxtrot network is an organised crime group which has developed an arm's-length method of recruiting young people to carry out violent crimes. You were recruited to travel to England to kill an unidentified target." She said Natland, from Stavanger in south-west Norway , must spend a minimum of 13 years in custody. He was arrested in ⁠a hotel room in Huddersfield, northern ​England, ⁠in March ‌2025 with two firearms and ammunition in ​his possession. He imitated holding a firearm and pretended to shoot one of the officers, who recovered £2,000 in cash from the room. Natland admitted possessing a semi-automatic pistol, a revolver and ammunition, but denied conspiracy to murder and claimed he did not intend to ​carry out the ‌plan. But he was ⁠convicted in July ​after a retrial and ​was sentenced ‌at London's Woolwich Crown Court to ⁠detention for 20 years. The case was the first recorded instance of the network organising an attack in Britain. "Natland was arrested just hours before he was due to carry out an assassination here in the UK," said Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London. “Natland was clearly being tasked by someone in the Foxtrot network, an organised criminal group ... orchestrating violence against Jewish and Israeli targets in Europe on behalf of the Iranian regime. “The intended target of this specific assassination has never been identified, and we found no evidence of any direct link to Iran in this case. However, as recent events have shown, CTP will seek to proactively disrupt any attempts by hostile states to carry out criminal acts in the UK." She said criminal proxies were “one of the tactics increasingly used by foreign states seeking to cause harm" to the UK. "They often recruit people online with promises of significant financial reward," she added. "But the reality is that those carrying out these tasks are viewed as disposable assets by those directing them. They are used when convenient and abandoned when circumstances change.” Natland was the latest ⁠young adult to stand trial in Britain over serious criminal acts allegedly carried out after being recruited ​online for money, often as an unwitting proxy for a foreign state. This week, the head of the UK’s domestic intelligence service, Ken McCallum, said MI5 had made more than 50 arrests in the past year specifically linked to Iran operations. Frank Ferguson, head of the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division, described Natland’s actions as a “calculated plan to kill for money” and said the case showed how organised crime networks operated “across borders and exploit young people to carry out serious violence”. The court heard Natland had been recruited when an individual referred to as Agent 47 used social media to contact a figure with the username Generalen to ask for someone to carry out an assassination in the UK. In the message, Agent 47 told Generalen that there was €25,000 ($24,306) “in the pot”. Swedish police believe Agent 47 is Ali Shehab Ahmed , a senior figure in the Foxtrot network, who was arrested in Sulaymaniyah in Iraq in December.

title: Russia to discuss energy agreements with Africa at forum later this month — minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. The Russian Energy Ministry will discuss the implementation of agreements in the fuel and energy sector with African partners at the upcoming Russia-Africa forum, Minister Sergey Tsivilyov told reporters at Russian Energy Week.
A delegation from Russia visited Africa not long ago and held first meetings of intergovernmental commissions with the Central African Republic, Togo, and Niger, he said, adding that intergovernmental commissions with Mali and Burkina Faso are also working. "Those were not formal meetings: each [meeting of the] commission produced a list of specific projects, timelines, and those responsible for them. At the Russia-Africa forum, we plan to continue our dialogue with African partners and discuss the implementation of agreements reached in detail," the minister noted.
The Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum will take place in Moscow on October 28-29.
The Russian Energy Week (REW) International Forum is taking place from October 14 to 16. It is being held with the support of the Government of the Russian Federation, the Ministry of Energy of the Russian Federation, and the Government of Moscow. The Roscongress Foundation organizes the forum. TASS is the information partner of Russian Energy Week.

title: Europe increasingly recognizing threat of Russia’s ‘shadow war’ – FM Sybiha
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said this in an interview with Ukrinform .
“I see that our partners have a deeper understanding of the situation in Ukraine. I see greater recognition of the need to define a new role for Europe in international discussions. Our European colleagues are aware of the risks of further Russian escalation. I see that they understand that Russia’s actions in Europe have gone far beyond hybrid warfare. I have even heard them use the term ‘shadow war’ to describe the war Russia is waging against Europe, and they understand that it must be countered,” the Foreign Minister said.
Sybiha stressed that Ukraine, through its military, economy and combat experience, provides Europe with strategic advantages, and that cooperation between the two sides benefits both.
“Military officials are the most aware of Ukraine’s role and importance from a security perspective. They understand that Ukraine’s armed forces, economy and experience give Europe strategic advantages, and that our cooperation is a two-way street,” the minister said.
According to Sybiha, European partners recognize Ukraine’s achievements in the defense industry and on the battlefield and have demonstrated sustained support. At the same time, they expect Kyiv to put forward concrete proposals that would help strengthen Ukraine in the face of continued military risks.
At the same time, Ukraine’s top diplomat warned of the growing influence of populist and radical forces in Europe that exploit anti-Ukrainian and anti-immigrant rhetoric.
“We are now facing a very challenging period: more than 50% of Europe’s population will vote in elections next year. We are witnessing an era of populism and the growing influence of radical forces seeking to exploit anti-Ukrainian and anti-immigrant rhetoric. Each country has its own particular circumstances, but this rhetoric is based on manipulation,” Ukraine’s top diplomat stressed.
He noted that misleading claims – for example, that aid to Ukraine is causing cuts to social spending in European countries – can influence public opinion. Therefore, Sybiha emphasized, Ukraine must work with its partners to debunk disinformation and explain to European societies why supporting Kyiv is essential for the security of the entire continent.
As Ukrinform reported, Ukraine is urging its partners to maintain sanctions pressure on Russia without interruption and continually introduce new restrictions to increase the strain on the Russian economy and force Moscow to negotiate.

title: Police Confirm Abduction Of Catholic Priest John Otache In Benue
body: The Benue State Police Command has confirmed the kidnapping of a Catholic priest, Rev. Fr. John Otache of Otukpo Diocese. In a phone chat, the spokesperson of the Benue Police Command, Aondongu Peter, said the priest was abducted on Tuesday. He noted that the police are making frantic efforts to rescue the priest. Otache is the Parish Priest of St Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume. Meanwhile, the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo, in a statement issued on Thursday and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor, Rev. Fr. Joseph Itodo, said Otache was kidnapped on Tuesday, 13th October, 2026, along Otobi Amejo-Ajegbe Road in the Ohimini Local Government Area of Benue State while returning from Otukpo. “It is with great sadness that we write to notify you of the kidnapping of one of our priests, Rev. Fr. John Inalegwu Otache. He is the Parish Priest of St Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe – Awume. The unfortunate incident occurred on Tuesday, 13th October, 2026. Fr. John was going home from Otukpo when he ran into the kidnappers along Otobi Amejo–Ajegbe Road in Ohimini LGA, Benue State,” the statement read in part. The Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo, Most Rev. Michael Ekwoyi Apochi, expressed regret at the incident and called on all faithful and people of goodwill to pray for the quick and safe release of Fr. John as efforts are intensified to secure his freedom. “The bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo, Most Rev. Michael Ekwoyi Apochi, is deeply pained by this sad development and has earnestly requested all Christ’s Faithful in the Diocese and all people of goodwill to pray for the quick and safe release of Fr. John as we intensify efforts to ensure his release,” the Diocese of Otukpo said. This is the second time a priest from St Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume, has been kidnapped. The post Police Confirm Abduction Of Catholic Priest John Otache In Benue appeared first on Channels Television .
