title: Livestock Experts Warn Farmers Against Indiscriminate Use of Antibiotics
body: Livestock experts in Bauchi State have warned farmers against indiscriminate use of antibiotics in animals, saying the practice could fuel antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and pose risks to animal and human health. They gave the warning at the maiden Bauchi Livestock Stakeholders’ Engagement and Capacity Building Forum held at the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) Secretariat in Bauchi. Speaking at the event, the State Chairman of the Nigerian Association of Animal Health and Husbandry Technologists (NAAHHT), Salisu Abubakar Buba, described animal health technologists as essential workforce for the implementation of livestock extension services and vaccination campaigns. He said the absence of animal health technologists at abattoirs, livestock markets and border posts poses serious risks to meat safety, disease surveillance and the control of zoonotic diseases. Importation, insecurity threaten Nigeria’s food sufficiency Nigeria’s unfinished food security battle On his part, Dr Muhammad Sani Mu’azu, a lecturer at the Federal Polytechnic Damaturu, Yobe State, stressed the need for proper regulation of antimicrobial use in livestock production. He warned that giving animals drugs and antibiotics without proper guidance could endanger human lives because people consume animal products. In a presentation titled “Combating Antimicrobial Resistance in Food Animals: The Role of the One Health Approach in Securing Bauchi’s Animal Protein Value Chain”, Provost of the Bauchi State College of Agriculture, Dr Ahmed Isah Ahmed, described antimicrobial resistance as a major threat to human and animal health. He explained that the misuse of antibiotics in livestock could increase animal deaths, treatment costs and production losses, affecting farmers’ incomes and the safety of animal products. Ahmed called for a ‘One Health’ approach that brings together human and animal health professionals, farmers, environmental scientists and policymakers to tackle the problem. He urged livestock farmers to use antibiotics only when necessary and under veterinary supervision. He also recommended improved farm hygiene, vaccination, biosecurity, animal nutrition and proper record-keeping to reduce the need for antibiotics. Others who presented papers at the event were Dr. Abdullahi Mohammed of the Federal Polytechnic Bauchi and Dr. Idi Saidu of the Bauchi State College of Agriculture. The forum was organised by NAAHHT, in collaboration with the Bauchi State Ministry of Livestock Development, the L-PRES Project, MHWUN Bauchi State Council and the Centre of Excellence for Integrated Farming System at Federal Polytechnic Bauchi. With the theme, “From Farm to Fork: Building a Resilient, Productive Livestock Sector under One Health in Bauchi State”, the forum brought together government officials, academics, farmers, traditional rulers, development partners and students to discuss ways to improve livestock production and animal health. In a communiqué issued at the end of the forum, NAAHHT called on the Bauchi State Government to employ animal health technologists and other livestock professionals to address staff shortages across the state’s 20 local government areas. The association also called for the full implementation of the reviewed 100% Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) for animal health technologists in the state and urged the Head of the Civil Service to intervene in the salary deductions affecting the workers in September 2026.

title: Reforms and financing assurances from partners are prerequisites for receiving EFF tranche – IMF
body:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) welcomes the efforts of the government and the Verkhovna Rada to reinvigorate reforms in Ukraine. Resuming these reforms is a key condition for the successful completion of the combined second and third reviews of the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) program by the end of this year. A second essential condition is the provision of financing assurances from partners, stated Mateusz Szczurek, Director of the IMF’s European Department.
"We plan to conduct the second and third reviews of the program by the end of this year. Naturally, this depends on the resumption of reforms, as well as on the provision of financing assurances by partners," he said during a press conference held on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok on Friday, according to an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
Szczurek emphasized the critical importance of adopting legislation and implementing other measures related to revenue mobilization and public administration, as these are vital for securing further donor financing, starting as early as 2026.
Regarding new assumptions and the potential need to revise the EFF program, the IMF European Department Director pointed to the Ukrainian government’s draft state budget for 2027, currently submitted to parliament, which is based on the assumption that the war will continue for a longer period.
"This, of course, increases the financing requirement for 2027 (...) As for the structuring aspects, that is a topic for discussion during the combined second and third reviews of the program, so we will provide details once they are made public," noted Szczurek.
During this year’s IMF Annual Meetings, held from October 12–18, the Ukrainian delegation is discussing with the Fund the implementation of the new four-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) program, valued at $8.1 billion, which was approved at the end of February this year. This program is part of a broader $136.5 billion external financing package for the 2026–2029 period, based on the baseline scenario.
In July, the IMF completed the first review of the program and disbursed a second tranche of approximately $690 million, bringing the total funding received under the new program to $2.2 billion. At the same time, it was noted that some of the program’s structural benchmarks had not been met by their respective deadlines. Following the first review, the EFF program was updated to include eight additional structural benchmarks, seven of which are fiscal in nature.
Discussions are currently underway to combine the second and third program reviews, with the aim of presenting the matter to the Executive Board before the end of this year. This would coincide with the approval of a combined third and fourth tranche disbursement, totaling approximately $1.65 billion.
"Bringing this to the Board depends on receiving sufficient and credible financing assurances to cover the projected funding gap, on terms that are consistent with maintaining Ukraine’s debt sustainability," IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack stated in early October.
Finance Minister Marchenko noted that, ahead of the expected IMF mission visit in November, it would be desirable to secure confirmation for all sources of the $52.6 billion in external financing required for the 2027 state budget; currently, about $32.6 billion of that total still awaits confirmation.
According to Marchenko, Kyiv expects the European Union to fulfill its commitment to cover two-thirds of Ukraine’s external financing needs for next year as well—a move that would increase confirmed funding by approximately $17.5 billion. As for the remaining balance of roughly $15 billion, the minister explained that there are several potential sources to cover it, including bilateral financing, guarantees, and programs with international financial institutions.

title: LNG plants outside Persian Gulf compensate just two-thirds of shortfall
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. New LNG capacity outside the Persian Gulf has compensated for only two-thirds of the lost Qatari and UAE volumes, Advisor to the Russian President Anton Kobyakov said at a press conference during the Russian Energy Week forum.
"Before the conflict of the US and Israel with Iran, nearly 20% of global LNG supplies passed through the Strait of Hormuz. Yes, new capacities outside the Gulf are somewhat mitigating the problem today; between March and June, they compensated for approximately two-thirds of the lost Qatari and UAE volumes," he said.
"But not entirely. Although everyone understands that the beneficiaries of this situation are, to a large extent, American companies, operators and builders of new and expanding pipelines," he added.
The Russian Energy Week international forum is being held in Moscow on October 14-16 with the support of the Russian government, the Russian Ministry of Energy, and the Moscow government. Roscongress Foundation is the event organizer. TASS is the information partner of the forum.

title: Gunmen abduct Catholic priest
body:
A Catholic priest, John Otache, has been kidnapped along the Otobi Amejo-Ajegbe Road in Ohimini Local Government Area of Benue State, the police and the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo have confirmed.
Mr Otache, who is in charge of St Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume, was abducted on Tuesday, 13 October, while returning from Otukpo, according to a statement by the Diocesan Chancellor, Joseph Itodo.
The Police Public Relations Officer in Benue, Peter Aondongu, also confirmed the abduction, saying efforts were ongoing to rescue the priest.
“I can confirm that. It happened on Tuesday. He has not been rescued yet, but our teams are still making efforts to rescue him,” Mr Aondongu told Vanguard.
The Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo, Michael Apochi, appealed to Christians and other people of goodwill to pray for the priest’s safe release.
“The Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo, Most Rev. Michael Ekwoyi Apochi, is deeply pained by this sad development and has earnestly requested all Christ’s faithful in the Diocese and all people of goodwill to pray for the quick and safe release of Fr John as we intensify efforts to ensure his release,” the statement said.
The diocese also urged prayers for other people held by kidnappers across the country, expressing hope for their speedy and safe release.
Vanguard reported that the abduction was the second involving a priest serving at St Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume.
The abduction comes days after the Catholic Diocese of Gboko announced the indefinite closure of Catholic institutions in Ihugh, another community in Benue State, citing repeated attacks, arson and concerns vvover the safety of its personnel.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Diocese of Gboko, in a pastoral letter dated 12 October, ordered the closure of St Winifred Secondary School, St Winifred Nursery and Primary School, St Thomas Hospital and Salus Mudi Care Centre, as well as St Winifred Parish.
The decree, signed by the Bishop of Gboko, William Avenya, and the diocesan chancellor, Marcellinus Wende, also directed the withdrawal of priests, consecrated persons and other diocesan personnel from the affected institutions.
The diocese said student hostels at St Winifred Secondary School had been burnt on four occasions between October 2025 and October 2026. It also cited repeated burglaries and other criminal incidents involving church properties.
The diocese said it had engaged community leaders and security authorities but had not secured the lasting safety guarantees required to keep its institutions operating.
Although the two incidents occurred in different parts of Benue State, they have raised fresh concerns about the security of Catholic personnel and institutions in the state. The available reports do not establish a connection between the priest’s abduction and the attacks cited by the Diocese of Gboko.

title: Washington Post photojournalist wounded in clash between Israelis, Palestinians in West Bank
body: Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was wounded during a Friday altercation between extremist settlers and Palestinians in the West Bank, with the IDF confirming the account later on Friday.Footage seen by The Jerusalem Post appears to show Levine kneeling on a path in a press jacket and helmet, as colleagues run over to carry her to safety.Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine after reportedly being wounded during an altercation between extremist West Bank settlers and Palestinians, October 16, 2026. (credit: Section 27A via Walla)Police launched an investigation into the incident after receiving an IDF report of the West Bank clashes, according to an Israel Police spokesperson.Palestinian media reported that Levine was beaten, sustaining fractures and cuts in the violence near Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah. Israeli sources have not independently verified this.Levine, speaking from a hospital bed, said that she had been kicked "about 50 times," adding that if she hadn't been wearing her black jacket and helmet, she "probably wouldn't be here at all, because they just kept kicking me again and again."After about 10 minutes, they tried to make me get up; they pushed me back to the ground and continued kicking me," she said. "I tried to hold on to my cameras and my side bag, but in the end they just ripped everything from me and kept kicking me."According to the IDF, soldiers initially fired warning shots into the air in an effort to disperse the crowd upon arriving on scene, eventually targeting an individual who approached them with a sharp object.PMO: 'Serious questions remain,' facts 'unclear'The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) condemned the attack in an X/Twitter post later on Friday, noting that the facts "remain unclear and are under investigation.""Israel unequivocally condemns violence against anyone - Jews, Arabs, Christians, or journalists," the statement read. "Those responsible will be held accountable."The Prime Minister's Office: The facts surrounding the confrontation near Abu Falah, during which Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was allegedly assaulted, remain unclear and are under investigation. Israel unequivocally condemns violence against anyone—Jews, Arabs, Christians or journalists. Those responsible will be held accountable. But serious questions remain. Reports indicate some 200 Arabs and far-left activists confronted approximately 40 Israeli youths. Footage shows masked individuals on both sides hurling objects, amid reports of fireworks fired at Jewish youths. Other footage appears to show Levine knocked down and immediately helped to her feet by the same unidentified individual. The investigation must establish the facts, including who initiated the violence. We will not allow disputed incidents to be exploited to demonize the hundreds of thousands of law-abiding Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria. The facts must determine the conclusions. Not the headlines.— Prime Minister of Israel (@IsraeliPM) October 16, 2026The statement indicated that "serious questions remain" regarding who specifically was responsible for the attack on Levine, emphasizing the presence of "200 Arabs and far-left activists... (and) approximately 40 Israeli youths" at the site of the attack."The investigation must establish the facts, including who initiated the violence," the statement continued. "We will not allow disputed incidents to be exploited to demonize the hundreds of thousands of law-abiding Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria. The facts must determine the conclusions. Not the headlines."Washington Post editor-in-chief Matt Murray also condemned the incident in a statement earlier on Friday, according to N12 News, accusing Israeli settlers of having attacked Levine, whom he emphasized "was wearing prominent identification marks that clearly identified her as a journalist.""We are appalled by this unjustified attack on a journalist who was doing her job," he said. "We call on the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and act on its findings."In addition, the US Embassy in Jerusalem told N12 that it is aware of the incident and is "monitoring the situation.""We condemn criminal violence and call for the investigation and prosecution of those responsible," it said.Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot also responded to the incident in a post on X/Twitter, calling it "unacceptable" and referring to the perpetrators as "violent lawbreakers."התיעוד של פורעי חוק אלימים תוקפים את צלמת ה״וושינגטון פוסט״, היידי לוין (בת ה-64), הוא בלתי מתקבל על הדעת. קומץ הפורעים הזה אינו מייצג את הציבור בישראל. מעשיו של קומץ זה מכתים מדינה שלמה ופוגע קשות בביטחון של אזרחי ישראל ולוחמי צה״ל כולם. אני מגבה את צה״ל בגינוי החד והברור לאירוע. חובה על משטרת ישראל לנקוט בצעדים קשים כלפי האלימות הפושעת הזו.— Gadi Eisenkot - גדי איזנקוט (@gadi_eisenkot) October 16, 2026"This handful of rioters does not represent the public in Israel. The actions of this handful stain an entire nation and severely harm the security of all Israeli citizens and IDF fighters," he said. "I back the IDF in its sharp and clear condemnation of the incident. It is incumbent upon the Israel Police to take harsh measures against this criminal violence."Mateh Binyamin Regional Council accuses PA of bringing terrorists to attack IsraelisThe Mateh Binyamin Regional Council provided a different course of events.According to the council, the Palestinian Authority "led hundreds of anarchists and terrorists into a direct confrontation with Israelis near Abu Falah, all under the cover of the olive harvest.""Footage from the scene shows terrorists launching fireworks directly at people and hurling stones at Israelis, while journalists stand behind them, documenting this deliberate provocation," the council said."The event was orchestrated by the PA; its patrol vehicles were present and highly visible at the scene, even though it is in Area B, where Israel holds responsibility for security," it added."Clashes broke out between Arabs and Israelis, eventually being dispersed by Border Police officers who arrived at the location. According to reports, several activists were injured during the confrontations," the council said.The council did not explicitly comment on Levine's reported wounds.The event was part of four incidents of nationalist-motivated violence and clashes between Israelis and Palestinians which were reported overnight and on Friday morning at several locations across the West Bank, including several olive groves.The incidents reportedly involved vehicles being set on fire, attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters, and attacks on Palestinian homes.In the village of Burin, a confrontation broke out during the olive harvest. Additional incidents were reported in the village of Burqa, east of Ramallah, and in Turmus Ayya. The incidents reportedly included at least four vehicles being set on fire, one of which was a civil defense vehicle, and attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters.In a separate incident, shortly before midnight, settlers reportedly attacked Palestinian homes in the Wadi al-Sheikh area of the town of Beit Ummar, north of Hebron.The Palestinian Red Crescent said that two wounded Palestinians, a 63-year-old woman and a 40-year-old man, had been treated and taken to the hospital. Another Palestinian was reportedly shot in the knee. Israeli security forces arrest fleeing suspect following manhuntIsraeli security forces arrested a suspect after he fled an olive grove near Kafr Kara, Israel Police announced later on Friday.The police and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) conducted a manhunt for the suspect lasting several hours prior to his arrest.An M-16 rifle was also found in the vicinity.

title: Teen kills 4 at Oregon school. And, DOJ sues California over alleged noncitizens
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
A teenager opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Ore. , killing three children — ages 5, 8, and 11 — and a teacher, officials confirmed. A 7-year-old and a 54-year-old were hospitalized. A bystander killed the 16-year-old suspected shooter after following him into Silver Rail Elementary School, according to local officials. The suspected shooter has not been identified. Officials say he was a resident of Bend. He used a "long gun," which is similar to a rifle or shotgun, during the attack. His connection to the school — if any — remains unclear.
A candlelight memorial is seen out front of Silver Rail Elementary School on Oct. 15, 2026, in Bend, Oregon. Mathieu Lewis-Rolland/Getty Images hide caption
The Justice Department is suing California to stop the state from counting ballots that the government claims are from noncitizens. Three weeks before Election Day, the DOJ provided a flash drive containing the names of 20,000 people it suspected of being noncitizens on California's voter rolls to Los Angeles County's top voting official. The DOJ gave him 48 hours to investigate the names or face a lawsuit, which was filed yesterday.
Trump administration lawyers will argue today at a federal appeals court that White House papers belong to Trump rather than the American people. The case could end up in front of the conservative-leaning Supreme Court. The White House's claim comes after a series of actions during Trump's second term that challenged the limits put on the president after the Watergate scandal. For some 200 years, presidents could personally decide what to do with the papers they created in office. Then, Congress established the Presidential Records Act following disputes with Richard Nixon. Until this year, every president has followed this records law. Six months ago, the Trump administration moved to invalidate it . The move came after Trump was indicted on obstruction-of-justice charges for allegedly possessing classified documents at Mar-a-Lago, although a federal judge dismissed the case for technical reasons and the Justice Department later dropped it after Trump won reelection.
by Monika Evstatieva , senior producer on NPR's Investigations team
NPR's investigation finds that stores selling skincare products purchased from Mazal Group have routinely pressured shoppers, including older adults and people with disabilities, into buying expensive skincare products and services they did not want, could not afford or tried to refuse. Collage by Jackie Lay/NPR hide caption
It all began with a tip. A colleague of mine had a friend in Ann Arbor who needed help. When I called her, she told me her elderly mom had been walking through a mall when a salesperson approached her with an eye cream sample. She went into a store called Beauty Essentials in Ann Arbor, Mich., and came out with $5,000 in skincare products she didn't want, tried to refuse, and couldn't return. But, she said, it wasn't an isolated incident. She posted on Facebook and connected with more than 30 people with complaints about the store. She asked me to look into it.
And so began an investigation that took place over more than a year . My reporting partner, Caley Fox Shannon, and I found similar complaints all over the country. We followed the trail, and found a network of mall skincare stores that systematically targeted older adults and people with disabilities across the United States. There was a link between them: one company, the California-based Mazal Group.
Over the past year, we spoke with more than 50 people, including customers who say they were taken advantage of, their family members and former employees. We looked at state and federal court lawsuits, hundreds of online reviews and nearly 500 consumer complaints we got through Freedom of Information Act requests. We went to stores selling products from Mazal Group in Virginia, Maryland and California, as well as the company's Chatsworth, Calif., headquarters.
You can read about what we found in NPR Investigations' whole report here , watch our documentary or listen on Consider This .

title: Tragedy averted as private jet loses door Mid-Air
body: An air crash was averted on Thursday after a CL60 aircraft operated by Triton Aviation lost a door shortly after take-off from the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (NAIA), Abuja, forcing the crew to declare a “Mayday” emergency. The aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was scheduled to fly from Abuja to the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred at about 4:20 p.m. UTC. An incident report obtained by our reporter indicated that the aircraft had taken off from Runway 22 at 4:17 p.m. UTC and was about three nautical miles from the airport, climbing through 3,000 feet, when the crew declared an emergency. According to the report, the crew informed air traffic controllers that a door had opened in flight, prompting the approach radar controller to direct the aircraft back to Abuja for an emergency landing. Following the distress call, the airport’s fire watch room and medical team were alerted and instructed to remain on standby. Fire and emergency personnel were also directed to designated positions at A4 and A5 in preparation for the aircraft’s return. The report stated: “At about 4:29 p.m. UTC, while in contact with the Abuja control tower, the crew asked whether air traffic controllers could confirm if the door was open. “The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft using binoculars, but could not establish the door’s condition because of the aircraft’s position. The crew was subsequently informed that the controller could not confirm the situation visually. “The aircraft landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 p.m. UTC, 14 minutes after the Mayday call.” The report added that after the aircraft landed, the duty controller observed that the door was missing from the fuselage, confirming the seriousness of the incident. The aircraft was subsequently taxied to the international apron extension, where it was parked with the assistance of a marshaller. At about 4:40 p.m. UTC, the crew reported that the marshaller was in sight before the aircraft was positioned in its parking area. Meanwhile, a viral video showed the missing aircraft door was reportedly recovered by farmers in a farmland within Abuja. In the video, a male voice, whose identity could not be established as of the time of filing this report, said the farmers found the door while returning from their farm. “This is what we found as we were returning from our farm. It fell from a plane, but we don’t know much about its identity. As I am sending it to you, sir, just check it,” the voice said. The number of passengers on board the aircraft could not be ascertained as of the time of filing this report. Triton Aviation, the operator of the jet, could also not be reached for comments. When contacted, the Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Michael Achimugu, confirmed the incident but said the agency could not comment on it. He said the incident fell under the purview of the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB). The NSIB also confirmed the serious incident. A source at the bureau said its management had deployed investigators to the scene to conduct further investigations, adding that an official statement would be issued soon.

title: ‘We Pay for It’: Germany Demands Starlink Restrictions in Ukraine Be Lifted
body:
Germany has demanded that restrictions on Starlink satellite communications in Ukraine be lifted, arguing that equipment financed by Berlin must remain operational.
Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany was seeking answers from the US about the disruptions, though it did not yet have a complete picture of their cause, German broadcaster ntv reported.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“These restrictions must be lifted,” Wadephul said , arguing that Germany finances some of the Starlink equipment used in Ukraine.
“And so, of course, we insist that it works if we are paying for it. Ukraine must continue to receive full support,” he said.
Wadephul’s remarks added diplomatic pressure over disruptions to a service Ukrainian forces use for communications, drone operations, and frontline logistics. But Wadephul stopped short of identifying who was responsible.
Germany had questions for the US “that we will clarify,” he said.
Sources in Ukraine’s defense ministry told Kyiv Post on Thursday morning, Oct. 15, that Starshield connectivity while in motion had been restored and remained operational, according to reports from military units. However, the sources did not specify the speeds at which the service was functioning or whether any speed restrictions remained.
The ministry was continuing communications to establish the reasons and circumstances behind the previous day’s restrictions, the sources said.
That update confirmed the resumption of service but did not establish what caused the disruption or how it was resolved.
On Wednesday, ministry sources told Kyiv Post that SpaceX had introduced speed restrictions overnight without advance warning to Ukraine’s defense forces.
They described a limit of 160 kilometers per hour, or about 100 mph, although units reported losing connectivity at speeds ranging from approximately 72 to 161 km/h (45 to 100 mph).
The restrictions hampered drone missions, including interceptor and medium-range strike operations, and reduced capabilities for logistics, reconnaissance, and communications relay.
Ukraine is seeking to raise the operating speed limit to 450 km/h (280 mph) to allow interceptor drones to pursue faster Russian aerial threats, including jet-powered drones.
Dan Rice, president of American University Kyiv and a former special adviser to Ukraine’s military commander-in-chief, warned that such restrictions could have deadly consequences.
Speaking to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty , Rice described the scale of the threat facing Ukrainian air defenses.
“When you have 500 inbound Shaheeds, jet-powered Shaheeds, and I was hit within 400 meters [1,312 feet] twice this week,” he said, “you need to have interceptors going out to protect Ukrainian civilians.”
Rice warned that interference with high-speed interceptor operations could allow Russian drones to reach civilian targets, including schools, hospitals, and residential buildings.
Retired Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said the restrictions also impaired Ukrainian drone missions against Russian military logistics and command facilities approximately 150-250 kilometers (93 to 155 miles) behind Russian lines.
The consequences extend beyond battlefield efficiency.
In an interview with Piers Morgan on Wednesday , President Volodymyr Zelensky said the restrictions had already cost Ukrainian lives.
“People are dying because of his decision,” Zelensky said.
“I’m sure that they knew what they did. Absolutely,” he added.
However, the Ukrainian leader stopped short of identifying who had ordered the restrictions.
“I don’t know, him or somebody pushed him to… I don’t know really,” Zelensky said when asked whether he was angry with Elon Musk.
“We are professionals. If you are losing the speed of Starlink, we understand what’s going on. So they switched off. That’s their decision,” he added.
The controversy has also clarified who ultimately controls the military satellite system.
Starshield is a government-focused version of SpaceX’s Starlink network, developed for military and national security operations. Unlike commercial Starlink, the Starshield services at issue operate under US government control.
Elon Musk, SpaceX’s chief executive, confirmed Wednesday that restrictions on the system were a government decision.
“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk wrote on X .
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: World’s first fielded laser downs drones in Korea test
body: A South Korean laser air defence weapon destroyed all three target drones put up against it during a Republic of Korea Army exercise, at a cost the manufacturer puts at around one dollar fifty a shot, according to the company. Hanwha Systems said its Cheongwang, the Laser Air Defence Weapon Block-I, and a 30kW class vehicle-mounted high energy laser cannon took part in the Army TIGER+ Future Warfare Integrated Combat Exercise run by Republic of Korea Army Headquarters on 14 October. Around five hundred people watched, among them the Chief of Staff of the Republic of Korea Army along with military officials, academics and industry figures. Joohun Shin, head of the Laser Systems Business Centre at Hanwha Systems, said: “Laser weapons are core assets that will fundamentally change the game of air defense. Driven by unmatched technological capability and proven operational performance, we will accelerate our entry into the global market to establish both Cheongwang and the high-mobility, high-power 50kW Laser Armored Vehicle as key next-generation export items for K-Defense.” Cheongwang, whose name means light of the sky, was developed by Hanwha Systems with the Agency for Defense Development and is the first laser weapon of its kind to be fielded operationally anywhere. The company puts the cost of a single engagement at about a dollar fifty and says the system can keep firing for as long as it has power, with no magazine to run down and no resupply chain behind it. A Shahed type attack drone costs tens of thousands of dollars and the missiles fired at it cost far more, so an attacker generating cheap airframes in quantity wins on arithmetic even when every shot works. A laser inverts that, provided it can generate the power, hold the beam on target long enough to burn through, and see through the weather. Hanwha ran a similar demonstration on 16 September at the 2026 Defense Drone Technology Exhibition, where it said Cheongwang neutralised four drones and two uncrewed aircraft in succession in front of domestic and international guests. It also showed a 50kW Laser Armored Vehicle there, a more powerful and more mobile system it is developing in-house for export, and took that vehicle to MSPO in Kielce in September, the largest defence exhibition in eastern Europe. Britain has been working the same ground through DragonFire, the laser directed energy weapon developed by MBDA, Leonardo and QinetiQ with Dstl, which hit aerial targets in trials in the Hebrides in 2024 and is being accelerated towards installation on a Royal Navy Type 45 destroyer. The Strategic Defence Review committed further money to directed energy, and the Army has been trialling laser systems mounted on Wolfhound vehicles. The post World’s first fielded laser downs drones in Korea test first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: US not serious about negotiating with Iran, ambassador to Moscow says
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. The United States is not showing any serious political will to negotiate with Iran, the Islamic Republic’s Ambassador to Moscow Kazem Jalali said.
"Iran has repeatedly affirmed its commitment to actual diplomacy toward achieving a sustainable and long-term settlement even as we cannot see any serious will for actual talks on the opposite side," the Iranian diplomat said, addressing a conference on security in Central Asia and Afghanistan hosted by the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).
According to Jalali, what is happening today in the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait is a direct result of the US and Israeli aggression and the naval blockade against Iran. "Continued use of force and the language of ultimatums will not bring any result to the United States," the ambassador emphasized.

title: Azerbaijan’s SOCAR say they want to resume gas purchases from Russia’s Gazprom
body: Azerbaijan’s state oil company SOCAR is interested in resuming natural gas purchases from Russia’s Gazprom, despite the country’s role as a major gas exporter, SOCAR Vice President Elshad Nasirov said on 16 October. Speaking at the Russian Energy Week forum in Moscow, Nasirov said SOCAR had previously bought gas from Gazprom before becoming a supplier to the Russian company. However, he said there were no specific plans for renewed purchases, and did not provide details on potential volumes or the timing of deliveries. ‘We can proudly say that our cooperation with a giant like Gazprom is a very good example, because SOCAR is probably the only company in the world that first bought gas from Gazprom, then supplied gas to Gazprom, and now wants to buy gas again’, Nasirov said. Asked by journalists how much gas Azerbaijan intends to purchase from Gazprom, Nasirov said there were no specific plans at present. ‘This is simply a fact confirming that we have both bought and sold gas. There are no specific plans’, he said. Azerbaijan’s gas trade with Russia Azerbaijan previously relied on Russian gas to meet part of its domestic demand. In 2006, the country imported approximately 4.48 billion cubic metres of gas from Russia. Imports stopped in 2007 as Azerbaijan expanded domestic production, particularly from the Shah Deniz gas field. Disagreements over gas prices also contributed to the suspension of supplies. The direction of gas trade subsequently reversed, with Azerbaijan beginning to export gas to Russia in 2010. In November 2017, SOCAR and Gazprom signed a contract for the supply of 1.6 billion cubic metres of Russian gas. Azerbaijan imported approximately 349 million cubic metres in 2017 and 999 million cubic metres in 2018, before purchases stopped again in autumn 2018. In November 2022, the two companies signed another agreement covering the supply of up to one billion cubic metres of gas between 15 November 2022 and 1 April 2023. Meanwhile, Azerbaijan has continued to develop its gas exports to international markets. In January 2026, SOCAR announced the start of gas supplies to Germany and Austria. The latest announcement does not include details of a potential new supply agreement, including the volume of gas to be purchased or when deliveries could begin. The Russian Energy Week International Forum is being held in Moscow from 14–16 October, with support from the Russian government, the Ministry of Energy, and the Moscow government. The event is organised by the Roscongress Foundation.

title: Indian embassy in UAE issues warning over fake job offers and visa scams
body: Bogus agencies are targeting Indians with fake job advertisements in the UAE and Europe, luring unsuspecting applicants with false promises of employment and residency in exchange for payment. In an advisory, the Indian embassy in Abu Dhabi and the consulate general of India in Dubai have urged Indians to exercise caution when dealing with private visa and migration agencies based outside India, including some operating in the Emirates. The missions said they have received complaints of agencies advertising third-country employment opportunities and residency visa services. The consulate told The National it has “received a large number of complaints, mostly from southern states of India, directly from individuals or through welfare associations”. “The job offers are mostly for European countries,” a representative said. "Social media is the most common source of such advertisements and in most cases the individuals have transferred their money from India." The missions advised would-be job applicants not to rely solely on social media advertisements or promises from private visa-processing agencies. They should verify visa requirements, application procedures and authorised channels directly with the embassy or consulate of the country they want to visit. Applicants were also told to consult official government websites for the latest immigration information before making payments or sharing personal documents, and were urged to be wary of anyone promising overseas jobs or residency permits in exchange for payment. The latest advisory follows a warning issued by the Indian embassy in Abu Dhabi in August about unauthorised people offering consular services. According to previous warnings, scammers have targeted Indian citizens, particularly blue-collar workers, by posing as agents who claim they can arrange emergency certificates, exit permits, Emirates ID, visa regularisation and employment. In some cases, fraudsters obtain victims' facial images and fingerprint scans under false pretences. They may then misuse this information to conduct financial transactions, open bank accounts or get loans and credit cards in victims' names without their knowledge or consent. Victims could then face financial liabilities and potential legal consequences, including fines, travel bans or imprisonment. The missions have urged Indian citizens to verify the credentials of anyone offering consular or immigration-related services before sharing biometric data or other sensitive personal information. Passport-related scams India's top crime-investigating agency, the Central Bureau of Investigation, also warned citizens on Friday about passport-related fraud involving people impersonating agents or police officials. The CBI said fraudsters may promise faster processing, guaranteed approval or immediate appointments while demanding money and personal information. Some also create lookalike websites of official passport portals to collect application fees, banking details and identity documents. Other scams involve fake police verification calls in which victims are threatened with delays, passport cancellation or legal action unless they pay a fine or disclose personal information. Scammers may also offer fake passport updates, renewals and delivery services to extract money and sensitive data. The CBI reiterated that no agent can guarantee passport approval or promise special access to urgent processing. It offered tips to avoid falling victim to recruitment, visa and passport scams. Do not pay anyone who promises guaranteed passport approval, urgent processing, or a confirmed overseas job Do not click on suspicious links or make payments through unverified websites Never share bank PINs, passwords or other confidential banking information Do not respond to calls threatening passport cancellation, legal action, or police intervention unless you pay a fine Avoid sharing copies of passports, identity documents or biometric information with unknown individuals or unauthorised agencies.

title: JAZA: Does the Philippines have what it takes to win big investments?
body: At a party packed with people who know a thing or two about winning, Ayala’s big boss had a rather inconvenient question for his fellow corporate titans. Everyone wants to bag the next big deal, but does the Philippines even have what it takes to attract those investments in the first place? “We need, I think, an honest conversation among ourselves and with our partners in the public sector of whether we have the talent, whether we have the infrastructure, whether we have the energy, whether we have the regulatory environment and institutional stability needed to attract long-term investment,” Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala (JAZA) said on Thursday, October 15. Quite the conversation starter for a night of cocktails, buttered scallops, honeyed sausage tarts, and plenty of schmoozing and boozing at the Makati Business Club’s (MBC) 45th anniversary bash. But he did, after all, have quite the audience. Among those gathered at the Grand Hyatt Manila were MBC chairman and former Shell Philippines chief Edgar Chua, Aboitiz InfraCapital’s Cosette Canilao, PHINMA’s Ramon del Rosario Jr., shipping magnate Doris Magsaysay Ho, and former Microsoft Philippines CEO Peter Maquera. And he sure had their ear. “As global companies diversify their supply chains, we should think beyond which company, industrial park, or sector secures the next investment. A more important question to ask is whether the Philippines itself is winning,” the Ayala chairman said. And if the country as a whole is to win, JAZA argued, his fellow “fierce competitors in the marketplace” had to work together on the things that make the country attractive to investors in the first place. “We will not always agree. We will have different interests and conflicting views on policy, but we can agree on many of the first principles and, more importantly, identify practical areas where we could all make progress together,” he added. And who better to ask a roomful of business rivals to play nice than JAZA? His uncle Enrique Zobel co-founded MBC and his father served as a longtime trustee. Even in BGC, a little beyond the Makati business district the family helped build, he was hardly away from home. The Philippines has advantages, he said, including its young population, digital economy, and manufacturing base. But actually turning those into better jobs and better lives require businesses to cooperate on shared concerns, like education and affordable electricity . A promising country on paper would only get everyone so far. Play Video Infrastructure projects also needed to be built properly, with “every project and peso fully accountable for.” He didn’t mention corruption, but he didn’t have to, with the headlines still fresh in every businessman and investor’s mind. (READ: Flood control corruption cleanup spooks investors, drags PH growth – World Bank ) Even on the sidelines, the investment chatter wasn’t particularly upbeat. An MBC member familiar with the Jefferies-Regis Partners Philippines Conference, which brought together blue-chip companies and institutional investors earlier this week, told Rappler that turnout was thinner than expected this year, with fewer foreign investors making the trip to Manila. (READ: [READOUT] What a stickier inflation wave could mean for businesses ) A worrying sign, they reckoned. The broader numbers haven’t exactly been encouraging either. Net foreign direct investment inflows fell 23.9% to $4.071 billion in the first seven months of 2026, according to data from the central bank. Could AI and Pax Silica offer some hope? JAZA did mention the US-led technology supply chain initiative in passing as a “major initiative.” But the AI pitch has its share of skeptics at the club. An MBC member told Rappler that earlier meetings had revealed disagreements, with some eager to back AI and hyperscale data centers, while others questioned their enormous water and electricity needs, and whether they would actually bring enough jobs for Filipinos. One participant even reportedly brandished Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas , which raises concerns about AI’s implications for workers, inequality, and the environment. It’s not every day someone brings the Pope to a data center debate. – Rappler.com Must Read High-tech dreams, low-tech reality of the Luzon Economic Corridor

title: What this bankruptcy says about AI startups
body:
You're reading a newsletter from The Indicator from Planet Money. Once a week, we curate our favorite stories and insights on business, finance, economics and why they matter. Subscribe here to get it in your inbox every Friday.
After you win the economics Nobel, what would your first act be? Buy a Corvette? Gloat to your childhood bully? For co-winner Michael Woodford, his first act was … proctor an exam . The DAY that Columbia professor Michael Woodford found out that he and Robert Hall won the economics Nobel, he returned to his class with the pithy title "Cognitive Mechanisms and Economic Behavior" to administer an exam. He was welcomed to the classroom with cheers and applause. He held up his arms in triumph.
Michael Woodford, Columbia University professor and winner of the 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel. Andrew Harrer/Bloomberg via Getty Images hide caption
What to know: Character.ai is a company that allows you to speak with a "companion" — an AI-powered fictional character, historical figure, or whatever you decide to build. It came out just before ChatGPT and quickly went viral in part thanks to its adoption on TikTok. It hit 28 million monthly active users at its peak.
Character.ai had a lot of engagement, a big customer base, lots of talent … and Google promptly picked 'em up for $2.7 billion back in 2024. But Google didn't buy the company and absorb it! No, that traditional " acquihire " model would require all sorts of legal and regulatory approvals. Instead, they hired away the founders (and other big hitters on the team) and bought the nonexclusive license to the technology, leaving the company itself behind. That's called a "reverse acquihire," and it's happened at least six times in the past two years with AI startups. Now this week, Character.ai is filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
Some of the "Characters" available to users Gabby Jones/Bloomberg via Getty Images hide caption
Why it matters: A "reverse acquihire" doesn't leave a company in the greatest position. After the Google deal, Character.ai had to change its business model away from the quite costly LLM training and toward developing AI characters. Its founders were gone. Sure, the shrunken company had $2.7 billion in the bank, but leadership was still looking to raise money as they struggled to monetize their user base.
So is the "reverse acquihire" what caused the pain? Or was it a symptom of a larger issue? Character.ai faced a mountain of litigation over alleged harm to minors plus copyright concerns from Disney. So what's left behind? A once very promising company, which Disney is very excited to pick over for parts of it for $20 million.
What's going on: President Trump signed a deal last week to get diesel from Russia in an effort to lower fuel prices ahead of the midterms. Two weeks ago, we talked in the newsletter about the potential of a diesel export ban to lower prices. It didn't happen. One week ago, we talked again about Trump issuing an executive order to defer a tax from diesel. Now, this!
It's safe to say people were surprised by the move, given Trump signed a Russian sanctions law just last month that looked to tamp down on their energy revenues. Beyond surprise, a bipartisan group of senators is openly calling for the president to rescind the deal. They said it gives Putin the funds to power his war machine and "enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians."
Will this do anything? The same bipartisan group of senators said this deal will mean "limited to no relief to Americans." Goldman Sachs estimated the release of Russian oil would affect wholesale prices by $1 to $2 per barrel. The price of a barrel of diesel is around $200. So a $1 to $2 impact? Neil Atkinson, an independent energy analyst, says, "Frankly, [it's] a rounding error. It makes no fundamental difference to the global diesel market."
What's weirder to Atkinson, though … Russia hasn't really been exporting diesel. Its refineries have been damaged, and it's literally been importing diesel to make up for shortfalls. " So where these barrels of Russian diesel are going to come from to go either to the United States or elsewhere in the global market is a bit of a mystery," said Atkinson.
If you HAVEN'T listened: Reporter Greg Rosalsky opens the piece describing WHAT exactly Michael Woodford and Robert Hall won the economics Nobel for. They helped shape what's known as NEW Keynesian economics by bringing microeconomic principles to the traditional models of John Maynard Keynes. BUT THEN, Greg goes on to explain that the Nobel Prize did not initially include an economics award. No, that changed when the Swedish Central Bank, the oldest central bank in the world, wanted to celebrate its 300th anniversary with a bang. They would fund a new award for economics. It's a fascinating story which you can listen to below.
If you HAVE listened: A leading philosophy of John Maynard Keynes is that governments could fight recessions by boosting spending, and deal with inflation by holding spending back. In the initial draft that didn't make it into the final episode, Greg touched on how STAGFLATION was a central thorn in the side of this concept. Specifically, back in the 1970s, during the Arab oil embargo, the U.S. dealt with the one-two punch of high unemployment and high inflation, bringing about stagflation. It challenged the Keynesian idea that when lots of people are out of work and spending less, inflation comes down. Because at that point, unemployment and inflation rose together. Isn't that nice? Greg Rosalsky writes Planet Money's newsletter … you can catch that here .
Producer Cooper Katz McKim is reading The AGI Chronicles
Man oh man, this is the page-turniest nonfiction book I've read in a while. Kevin Roose, co-host of the upcoming NPR podcast Machine Gods , formerly The New York Times ' Hard Fork , tracks the handful of characters racing to make AI a commercial reality. It is far from a clear-cut story. There's no one character who came up with the idea and executed it … the existence of AI today comes down to many papers, many individual discoveries, and a whole lot of obsession. I didn't realize how much progress had been made in AI prior to 2020 and how concerned many industry leaders were about even creating AI (looking at you, Amodei ) for fear of creating a super-intelligence that moves outside of human control. It's gossip-y, it's matter of fact … I would recommend.
