I found this a remarkably thoughtful examination of AI risk, particularly your willingness to revisit arguments you previously found persuasive. But I wonder whether the framing around AI developing dangerous “wants” obscures another important class of risks.
Much of the discussion assumes that the central safety problem is preventing advanced systems from developing objectives that diverge from human intentions.
What happens when the intentions themselves are dangerous?
An AI that faithfully executes the objectives of a government, corporation, or military institution could produce catastrophic consequences without exhibiting any technical misalignment whatsoever. Indeed, greater reliability and obedience might make such a system more dangerous.
This raises a question I think deserves greater prominence: alignment with whom, and toward what ends?
Humanity isn’t a unified agent with a coherent set of preferences. Our institutions have competing interests, unequal capacities to exercise power, and long histories of pursuing objectives that impose devastating costs on others.
AI may amplify those existing dynamics long before it develops objectives sufficiently independent of human control to threaten us autonomously.
Your probabilistic framework can accommodate this possibility, of course. But I wonder whether institutional incentives deserve to be treated as common causal factors across multiple catastrophic scenarios, rather than primarily as circumstances that complicate the management of autonomous AI.
Commercial competition, geopolitical rivalry, premature deployment, and the progressive delegation of authority can simultaneously increase both the capabilities of AI systems and the likelihood that those capabilities will be used irresponsibly.
There’s an uncomfortable possibility here: we could make substantial progress on technical alignment while simultaneously increasing the capacity of powerful institutions to pursue destructive objectives.
The resulting systems might be safer according to important technical criteria while making the world substantially more dangerous.
I don’t think this diminishes the importance of mathematical AI safety research. Quite the opposite. It suggests that technical safety needs to be situated within a broader account of institutional governance, political accountability, and the distribution of power.
Perhaps the crucial question isn’t only how we prevent AI from escaping human control, but how we prevent increasingly capable AI from magnifying the consequences of humanity’s existing failures of judgment and governance.

One argument I didn’t see, in the post or in the comments (though the comments about human misuse come close).
Even if AI is perfectly aligned with human values, our values themselves have a terrible track record. On the declarative level we are for love and mutual understanding. In practice, just from 1914 onwards: two world wars, the Armenian genocide, Stalin’s purges, Franco, Pol Pot, Macías Nguema in Equatorial Guinea, Mengistu in Ethiopia, Idi Amin, Vietnam, US/CIA operations in Indonesia and Latin America… And many of the people responsible were not hypocrites. They believed in what they were doing: revolution, the nation, some utopia.
Maybe there is biology underneath. For most of our history the basic unit was the tribe of 200 or so people, with strong bonds inside and wariness, often hostility, toward outsiders. I know this is debated, and states and ideologies did most of the work in turning it into mass killing. But the pattern is hard to miss.
So alignment does not solve the problem. Aligned with whose values? And frozen at which moment? Aligned with the values of 1914 would have been a disaster (racial hierarchy, women rights, …). Worse, mass repression always needed many cooperating people (soldiers, police, clerks), and their reluctance was a limit to the level of repression. An obedient aligned AI removes that brake. A small group could do what once needed millions.
This is also why “agents cooperating” might not be all good. Cooperation is not the same as morality. Armies and cartels are cooperation. The 1914 alliances were cooperation between states, and they turned a regional crisis into a world war. AI agents cooperating among themselves need not include us.
And there is a tension inside the post. The debate approach works only if the two AI systems really compete and expose each other’s errors, like a judge relying on two opposing lawyers. If they cooperate, the judge is fooled. So in one part of your argument cooperation between AIs is something to hope for, and in another it is exactly what would break the safety method.
Alongside the very important examples you list (the two world wars, the Armenian genocide, etc), we also have the fact that during much of the 20th century, some Great Powers and many smaller countries worked mainly (if sometimes unsuccessfully) to achieve peace. Moreover, within the democratic nation-states (for most of the twentieth century) there was a high degree of adherence to what we would call the basic moral standards. So I think I would say the track-record of our values is mixed. All the ‘realist’ political philosophers (going back to Hobbs) thought that nation-states and Great Powers behaved ‘worse’ towards one another (on average) than individuals living in the same country under a government and legal system, precisely because of the absence of the latter on the global stage. There may be lessons in this for how we allow the AI landscape to develop. (AI ‘Great Powers’ in an unregulated global system?)
The “Great Powers” were doing colonialism during the first half of 20th century, fighting decolonization in the middle of the 20th century, and doing neocolonialism from the end of the 20th century onwards.
Thank you for your honest post. One suggestion on the conclusion: your decomposition estimates the level of risk, but whether to pause depends on how much a pause changes that risk, and at what cost.
Let a be the net reduction in p(doom) a pause buys, b the reduction in p(very good outcome), D and G their respective stakes relative to a muddle-through outcome, and C the cost of delay. In a simplified expected-value model, a pause is worth it iff a·D > b·G + C. The baseline p(doom) bounds a, but doesn’t establish its size or even its sign.
Illustratively: if the advances forgone during a five-year pause would otherwise have cut annual global deaths by 3% throughout those five years, C is about 10 million lives. Counting only people alive today and setting b = 0, a pause pays off once a exceeds about 0.12 percentage points. That’s a low bar, so this may strengthen your case.
But it makes the crux a: does a pause actually reduce risk once defection and racing are accounted for, the incentive problem you raise yourself?
All the technologies that may cause extinction in your scenarios — autonomous killer robots, highly advanced AI models potentially beyond human control — are being actively developed by big tech companies. (Recall that a few months ago the OpenAi head of robotics resigned as she was concerned the company was developing killer robots. There have been similar resignations at Google).
When you talk about AI extinction risk, you are really talking about extinction risk from big tech companies. After all, there would be no possibility of AI extentinction if tech companies were not continuing to develop advanced AI and autonomous robots. Framing the problem as one of risk from AI let’s the people actually causing the problems off the hook.
Similarly, a precursor to the alignment problem for AI is the alignment problem for corporations. Clearly many corporations (OpenAI, Exxon Mobil) are not acting in a way aligned with human values.
Given OpenAI is allegedly developing autonomous military robots, they are clearly not serious about safety. This makes me think that AI safety work at OpenAI plays a similar role to carbon capture research at an oil company. The point is to give people the impression that they care and are doing something, when clearly they are not.
Should have said, in my comments above: many thanks indeed for taking the time (and going through the necessary pain barrier) to write this!
Perhaps as a British person you should be more worried about the riots in the rest of Europe spreading over to the United Kingdom.
Thanks for writing this. Another decent resource is “An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks” by Dan Hendrycks et al. Given the pace of AI its a bit old (last updated in 2023 I think), but essentially all of it is still relevant.
There is a working paper of Nick Bostrom arguing that the expected gain might be positive. I find his arguments ridiculous, but this is not the place to explain why.
I think it’d be valuable to hear your counterarguments. One obvious one is that Bostrom’s assumption that one only cares about oneself rather than future humans is too strong.
Yes, it’s clearly ridiculous for Bostrom to essentially discount people’s concern for the futures of their children and grandchildren (or rather to relegate it to a footnote claiming that such concern would probably be balanced by people’s concern to prolong the lives of their elderly relatives).
Thank god for your realization!! Better late than never!
I would add one more layer to your now advanced reflexion. Mathematicians are part of the AI ecosystem by giving into the fascination for the (albeit fascinating) tool and offering free publicity to OpenAI and others.
Until a world-wide pause has been acted, the first thing mathematicians can do to help is actually to break the cord and explicitly criticize big AI firms pushing for a trial and error approach . Until the pause is reached, giving into “safety washing” by pushing for AI Safety research without pausing frontier development is an act of complicity .
I’m really glad you dove deeper into x-risks, I tried posting here before and was really not well met by some of your readers.
I suspect that x-risk is fairly small but dystopia-risk, the risk that out-of-control use of AI will create a dystopia (either of the Orwellian or Huxleyan kind, or an unforseen kind) is far greater.
[…] Timothy Gowers, “How worried should we be about extinction risk from AI?“ […]
This is a rather fishy initiative. Tsimerman, who is a good mathematician but with no particular knowledge in AI safety, is the scientific director with an absolute veto and what seems to be an absolute control of the recruit process and the money. Do you get money from MAISI? Does Tsimerman get? How much on on what basis?
AI-movies: VIBE & MAX v. GOWERS: THE TWO-SECOND CONSPIRACY
SCENE 1: UNIVERSITY LECTURE HALL – THE SEMINAR
Professor Gowers walks to the whiteboard.
PROFESSOR Gowers: Today, I propose an open mathematical problem…
VIBE (whispering): Bro, this is a generational opportunity.
MAX: Forget generations. I have a premium AI subscription.
VIBE & MAX: Hey AI, solve this problem and give me a rigorous proof with Lean certificate!
Vibe’s AI responds with the exact same proof.
MAX: Your proof? I got mine two seconds earlier!
VIBE: Bro, we asked at the same time! Your AI just had better Wi-Fi!
A giant screen displays both AI-generated proofs.
JUDGE: Mr. Max, when did you receive the proof?
JUDGE: Mr. Vibe, yours arrived at 10:42:05?
VIBE: Your Honor, I demand intellectual property rights! My prompt was more elegant.
MAX: In mathematics, timing is everything!
JUDGE: I spent seven years in law school, buried myself under $300,000 in student debt, and sacrificed my youth to uphold justice. And now I’m sitting here billing $400 an hour to referee a custody battle over an AI-generated proof that neither of you could reproduce if I confiscated your Wi-Fi and your laptops!
JUDGE: CASE DISMISSED! The only thing you two have successfully proven today is that artificial intelligence is getting smarter while natural stupidity remains undefeated!
SCENE 3: THE COURTROOM – SIX MONTHS LATER – THE TRIAL OF PROFESSOR GOWERS
A banner reads: VIBE & MAX v. PROFESSOR GOWERS: THE MATHEMATICAL DEEP STATE.
JUDGE: You are accusing Professor Gowers of conspiring to embarrass you by presenting an open problem?
PROFESSOR Gowers: I gave a seminar. I presented an open problem.
JUDGE: Were the proofs actually correct?
PROFESSOR Gowers: Both proofs were correct. Lean verified them.
JUDGE: Do you have any evidence of a conspiracy?
Vibe produces a photograph of Gowers standing beside the whiteboard.
JUDGE: He appears to be explaining mathematics.
PROFESSOR Gowers: Your Honor, I had no idea this would happen.
SCENE 4: VIBE & MAX v. PROFESSOR GOWERS: APPEAL NO. 001 — THE MATHEMATICAL DEEP STATE
The grand appeal courtroom is packed with journalists, mathematicians, AI researchers, and spectators who have absolutely no idea what a Lean certificate is but desperately want to see someone held accountable for it.
BREAKING NEWS: DIRECTORS OF AI MATHEMATICS ACCUSE WORLD-FAMOUS PROFESSOR OF ENGINEERING AN AI CONSPIRACY.
Vibe enters in an expensive suit, carrying a protein shake. Max follows, wearing sunglasses indoors and holding a briefcase stamped CLASSIFIED MATHEMATICAL EVIDENCE.
Centre for Extremely Advanced Intelligence.
JUDGE: Mr. Vibe. Mr. Max. I thought I dismissed this case six months ago.
MAX: You did, Your Honor. But we have new evidence. Obtained directly from the AI company.
Max connects his laptop to the giant screen.
MAX: Exhibit A: Two email accounts belonging to Professor Gowers. Both authenticated by the company’s internal investigators.
The screen displays two redacted email addresses.
MAX: Two months before the seminar, Professor Gowers sent a mathematical proof from his first account to his second account.
JUDGE: People email themselves documents every day.
MAX: Not usually solutions to problems they later announce as open.
VIBE: Exhibit B: The company’s internal data-processing logs. They confirm that the email entered an AI-connected processing pipeline associated with model improvement.
JUDGE: Does this prove the proof was included in the training data of the exact models used?
MAX: Not conclusively. But the timing, records, and matching proof establish a highly suspicious chain of events.
JUDGE: Professor, did you send this proof between two accounts you controlled?
GOWERS: I wanted to test whether an AI-connected email service might leak the contents of a mathematical proof into model training. If the model later reproduced it, that would raise interesting questions about data contamination.
MAX: And you deliberately presented the corresponding problem as open two months later?
MAX: So you deliberately designed the experiment, exposed the proof to a potential leakage pathway, and then presented the problem knowing people might use AI!
GOWERS: Correct. Although I did not know whether the experiment would work.
VIBE: And we were your unsuspecting test subjects!
GOWERS: You were not specifically selected.
JUDGE: It is, in fact, a rather important distinction.
MAX: Your Honor, we request that the original judgment be overturned. The evidence proves Professor Gowers deliberately engineered the entire situation.
VIBE: We demand justice, damages, and formal recognition that we were not hallucinating the mathematical deep state!
The judge studies the evidence for several minutes.
JUDGE: The court accepts that Professor Gowers deliberately conducted an experiment involving potential AI data leakage. The emails are authentic. His explanation is consistent with the records. The circumstances are, to put it mildly, extraordinary.
JUDGE: Your appeal concerns the dismissal of your original lawsuit. That lawsuit claimed ownership of an AI-generated proof and sought damages for a conspiracy against you.
MAX: And the professor deliberately set up the experiment!
JUDGE: Yes. The evidence supports that conclusion.
JUDGE: You have demonstrated that Professor Gowers planned an experiment. You have not demonstrated that the proof belongs to either of you.
JUDGE: Your AI may have reproduced a proof that originated elsewhere. That does not automatically grant you ownership of the underlying mathematics.
JUDGE: You have shown that Professor Gowers deliberately created the conditions for a possible data-leakage experiment. You have not established that he specifically targeted you, controlled the AI systems’ outputs, or committed an actionable legal wrong against you.
VIBE: So the evidence proves he set the whole thing up, but we still lose?
JUDGE: The evidence proves he set up the experiment. It does not prove every allegation in your lawsuit.
MAX: This is absurd! We have authenticated emails, internal server logs, a matching proof, and his own confession!
JUDGE: And you have failed to establish the legal grounds necessary to obtain the remedy you requested.
JUDGE: Appeal dismissed. The original judgment stands.

title: FM Sybiha: Time to use frozen Russian assets, not just proceeds
body:
He said this in an interview with Ukrinform .
“We raised the issue of frozen Russian assets with our European colleagues. It is time to return to substantive discussions about using these assets in full, rather than just the interest generated by holding them,” Ukraine’s top diplomat stressed.
According to Sybiha, Sweden, Poland, the Netherlands and Spain, with Stockholm taking the lead, have initiated the resumption of these discussions within the EU and set out their position in a joint letter to the European Commission.
He noted that a solution now needs to be found for how to proceed, as the political will is already there.
“I believe that we now have the political will. From what we understand from our partners, what is needed is a legal solution, shared responsibility and joint commitments so that, in the event of lawsuits or other unforeseen circumstances, Belgium does not bear all the responsibility alone, and we can jointly and unanimously defend ourselves against such actions by the Russian side,” the Minister emphasized.
Sybiha noted that a few days ago he published an op-ed in Politico on frozen Russian assets. Meanwhile, Sweden’s Foreign Minister is conducting a separate campaign on the issue.
“She gave an example: the total amount of EU assistance to Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion is smaller than the amount of Russian assets frozen in the European Union. That is why we will keep fighting for this, because it is fair! Why should European taxpayers pay for Russia? Frozen Russian Federation funds must be used,” Ukraine’s top diplomat stressed.
As Ukrinform reported, the EU sees frozen Russian assets as the most logical way to address Ukraine’s projected funding shortfall in 2027.
U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have proposed that Ukrainian and EU representatives unfreeze some Russian assets as part of efforts to resume peace talks and place them under Washington’s control.

title: NSA extends 2026/2027 National Service registration deadline to October 23
body: The National Service Authority (NSA) has extended the registration deadline for the 2026/2027 national service year from October 15 to Friday, October 23, 2026, giving eligible National Service Personnel (NSPs) additional time to complete the process. In a statement issued by the Authority on Friday, October 16, all personnel who are yet to complete their registration have been urged to take advantage of the extension and finalise the required procedures. The NSA said the extension is intended to provide an additional opportunity for eligible personnel who have not completed their registration to do so within the revised timeframe. The Authority has cautioned affected personnel against missing the new deadline, urging them to follow the prescribed registration procedures and ensure that all required steps are duly completed. “All affected personnel are therefore urged to take advantage of this extension and complete their registration before Friday, October 23, 2026, to avoid any inconvenience associated with missing the deadline.” The extension is expected to give outstanding registrants more time to fulfil the requirements for the 2026/2027 service year. The NSA reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring a smooth and efficient registration process for all eligible National Service Personnel. “The National Service Authority remains committed to ensuring a smooth and efficient registration process for all eligible National Service Personnel,” the statement concluded.

title: EFCC arraigns Kano businessman over alleged ₦34.8 million spaghetti fraud
body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned Halifa Abdulmajid for allegedly collecting ₦34.8 million to supply spaghetti but failed to deliver the goods.
The suspect faces a one-count charge of criminal misappropriation of ₦34,875,000 before Justice Musa Karaye of the Kano State High Court.
According to the charge sheet, Mr Abdulmajid allegedly committed the offence in Kano between September and October 2024.
The prosecution alleged that he dishonestly misappropriated funds belonging to one Fahad Adaji.
The money was reportedly transferred, on Mr Abdulmajid’s instruction, into a First Bank account belonging to Muazu Abdullahi, intended to purchase IRS Spaghetti from BUA.
The charge stated that the act violates Section 308 of the Penal Code Law, Laws of Kano State, and is punishable under Section 309 of the same Law.
When the charge was read to him on Wednesday, Mr Abdulmajid pleaded not guilty.
Following the plea, the prosecution counsel, Mustapha Maiwada, asked the court for a trial date and requested an order remanding the defendant in a custodial centre.

title: Britain studies US autonomous warfare command for lessons
body: Britain will engage closely with the United States as it establishes an Autonomous Warfare Command and will see what lessons apply here, while continuing to assess the most effective organisational arrangements of its own, according to a written answer in the House of Lords . Lord Sarfraz, the Conservative peer, asked what assessment the government has made of the American decision and what consideration has been given to establishing an equivalent integrated capability within British defence. Lord Coaker, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “Given the importance of autonomous systems to the future of warfare, we will continue to engage closely with our US counterparts as they establish an Autonomous Warfare Command and see what lessons apply to the UK Defence system. “The UK’s approach reflects our own operating model and structure. Defence is developing an integrated approach to optimise the balance between crewed, uncrewed and autonomous systems across the Armed Forces. This includes the establishment of the Uncrewed Systems Centre as a Defence centre of excellence alongside Defence’s Rapid AI Delivery (RAID) taskforce, to accelerate the development, integration and adoption of these capabilities. This is backed by a defence investment plan commitment of over £5 billion by 2030 in autonomous systems across the Integrated Force. This investment will support capabilities including the Hybrid Navy, uncrewed ground vehicles and Collaborative Combat Aircraft, increasing the mass, lethality and readiness of the Armed Forces while retaining appropriate human responsibility and accountability. We will continue to assess the most effective organisational arrangements for delivering these capabilities.” The Pentagon announced the new command at the start of October, putting a four-star officer in charge of artificial intelligence and uncrewed systems across the American services and consolidating work that had been spread between the individual branches and a set of separate offices. Standing up a command of that weight around autonomy goes further than anything Britain has done, and Coaker’s answer stops short of promising an equivalent while keeping the possibility in play. Britain has instead built the Uncrewed Systems Centre as its centre of excellence, with the Rapid AI Delivery taskforce working alongside it. Neither carries command authority over operational units in the way an American combatant command does, and both are designed to coordinate and accelerate work that is still owned by the services. The Army conceded at Apex Europe this month that its a number of its own drones cannot talk to each other, which is precisely the fragmentation the centre was created to address. The post Britain studies US autonomous warfare command for lessons first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: SAPO and NABU complete investigation into former official Stefanishyna over UAH 13.9 mln illicit enrichment
body:
The Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) and the National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) have completed the pre-trial investigation in the case of former Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration – Minister of Justice of Ukraine Olha Stefanishyna concerning illicit enrichment amounting to UAH 13.9 million.
"On October 15, 2026, the SAPO prosecutor decided to complete the pre-trial investigation in the case against the former Deputy Prime Minister – Minister of Justice of Ukraine. The individual is suspected of illicit enrichment totaling over UAH 13.9 million and submission of inaccurate declarations (Articles 368-5 and Part 2 of Article 366-2 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine)," SAPO reported in a Telegram post on Friday.
According to the pre-trial investigation, in 2024–2025, the individual acquired two apartments in the Faina Town residential complex valued at UAH 6.9 million, registering them in the name of a close female friend, as well as UAH 7 million in cash, part of which was spent on renovating these properties.
"It also transpired that she was negotiating the purchase of a house near Kyiv with an estimated value of $550,000, intending to pay with cash ($250,000) and the two aforementioned apartments. However, she later abandoned the deal, presumably due to her appointment to a diplomatic position abroad," the statement notes.
According to SAPO, an analysis of income and expenses confirmed that despite an official income of about UAH 3.7 million (recorded from early 2024 to mid-2025), approximately UAH 4.2 million was spent solely from bank accounts.
Furthermore, the anti-corruption prosecution emphasized that the individual failed to declare information regarding the use, at various times, of assets registered in third parties' names.
This concerns an apartment in the capital's business-class residential complex Lvivska Ploshcha (registered in her mother's name) and a "MERCEDES-BENZ GLC 220D" vehicle (registered in the name of a subordinate).
"Currently, upon the prosecutor's instruction, NABU detectives have disclosed the case materials to the defense counsel for review," SAPO informed.
As reported, on August 6, the High Anti-Corruption Court (HACC) selected a preventive measure for Stefanishyna in the form of bail totaling UAH 6 million. The prosecutor's office had requested a bail of UAH 13.3 million. She is suspected of illicit enrichment and false declaration. According to the investigation, she failed to declare two apartments in Kyiv, renovation expenses, housing rental costs, the use of a Mercedes-Benz, as well as payments for plane tickets and her mother's medical treatment.
Stefanishyna stated that she did not have the funds for the bail set by HACC but would look for them, and that she would consult with lawyers regarding a possible appeal. On August 13, the "Ilyashev & Partners" law firm posted the designated bail for Stefanishyna.
On August 20, the HACC Appeals Chamber upheld the preventive measure for Stefanishyna. Since the bail was paid, procedural obligations were imposed on the suspect, including reporting to detectives, prosecutors, and the court upon summons, notifying them of any change of residence, and refraining from communicating with a specified circle of persons.
On June 4, Ukrayinska Pravda published an investigation stating that the Asset Recovery and Management Agency (ARMA) had selected a management company for the Trade Unions House in Kyiv that may be linked to Stefanishyna's family, specifically her former husband. According to the investigation, this is already the fourth valuable asset acquired by the same company.
Stefanishyna stated that she was not connected to her ex-husband's activities, complained of information pressure, and emphasized that she had no conflict of interest regarding ARMA. In turn, ARMA Head Olena Duma stated that there were no links between the individuals mentioned in the media and ARMA, nor with participants in the competitive procedures for selecting managers of seized assets.

title: India sees potential for cooperation with Tatarstan in IT, finance, cybersecurity
body:
KAZAN, October 16. /TASS/. Indian Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar described IT, finance and cybersecurity as promising fields of cooperation with Tatarstan at an opening ceremony for the business forum titled, "TIME: Russia - India. Mutual Efficiency," in Kazan.
"Tatarstan is one of the fastest developing Russian regions, and it offers huge opportunities in the development of trade, business, investment and industries. And India is the world’s fastest growing economy. <...> We have numerous opportunities for various startups, such as IT, finance, cybersecurity and various technical and engineering skills. Interested students can visit and explore India, find friends and forge their future business contacts there using the ITEC program," Kumar said.
India has the world’s largest pool of talent and offers a mobility of skills to Russian youths, industries and businesses, the diplomat noted. "Our regions, our countries are mutually supportive, therefore we can complement our interests for the sake of progress and future cooperation," he emphasized.
At the first such forum last year, Kumar recalled, 19 business agreements were signed. "I am adamant that even more agreements and memorandums will be signed between our regions this year. There will be not only business but also cultural cooperation – more films, more cultural programs, and tourism will develop too," the ambassador concluded.

title: Nigerian govt reopens First Niger Bridge after 38 days of closure
body:
The Nigerian government has reopened the First Niger Bridge linking Onitsha in Anambra State with Asaba in Delta State.
Nigeria’s Minister of Works, David Umahi, reopened the bridge on Thursday, 38 days after closing it for emergency maintenance and rehabilitation.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the bridge was closed for rehabilitation and initially scheduled to last from 7 to 21 September but was later extended indefinitely following persistent rainfall.
A video clip sighted by PREMIUM TIMES showed that Mr Umahi was flanked by some federal officials as well as representatives from Anambra and Delta states during the reopening.
Some traditional rulers from the two states also attended.
During the reopening ceremony, the minister praised President Bola Tinubu for his infrastructure projects in the South-east and South-South.
He asked residents of the two regions to support the president’s re-election bid in 2027 as a reward for his projects in the regions.
“By the power of Mr President and in our deep appreciation of what he has done for the people of South-South and South-east in this bridge, it is my humble pleasure, and with gratitude to God Almighty, to open this bridge for the benefit of our people, in Jesus name,” he declared, cutting a ribbon to signal the official reopening of the bridge.
Mr Umahi lauded the contractors for their diligence and quality of work on the bridge.
The Works Minister stressed that the rehabilitation was aimed at improving traffic flow and ensuring the safety of road users.
The First Niger Bridge, linking Onitsha and Asaba, was completed in 1965 and built by the French Construction company, Dumez.
In 2018, the Goodluck Jonathan administration began construction of a Second Niger Bridge to reduce strain on the first bridge.
But President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration completed the bridge and commissioned it in May 2023.

title: Oba Of Benin Decorates Oluremi Tinubu With Prestigious ‘Ikele’ Coral Beads
body: The Oba of Benin, Omo N’ Oba N’ Edo Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, has decorated Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, with the prestigious Benin traditional Coral beads known as ‘Ikele’. Remi Tinubu becomes the first Nigerian First Lady to receive the honour, which is an expression of warm welcome and appreciation for her goodwill toward the traditional institution. She was honoured during a courtesy visit to Edo State traditional rulers from the state’s three senatorial districts at the Oba’s Palace in Benin City on Thursday. In an address read on behalf of the palace by the Oba’s eldest daughter, Princess Ikuoyemwen Aimiuwu-Ewuare, Oba Ewuare prayed to God and the ancestors to grant President Bola Tinubu and other leaders divine wisdom and strength to fulfil their responsibilities. L-R: Princess Ikuoyemwen Aimiuwu-Ewuare; His Royal Majesty, Omo N’ Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, Oba of Benin; First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu; Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State; and Governor Usman Ododo of Kogi State during a courtesy call at the Oba’s palace in Benin City, Edo State on Thursday, October 15, 2026. The Benin monarch said his reign has been a journey of service, reflection, renewal, and continued commitment to preserving Benin cultural heritage, while “strengthening traditional institutions and promoting peace, unity, and the well-being of our people.” Oba Ewuare also commended the First Lady for representing Nigeria gracefully on the global stage, making special mention of her recent recognition by President Donald Trump. Addressing the Benin throne earlier, the First Lady expressed delight at the honour and pledged to collaborate with traditional institutions. Remi Tinubu announced plans to partner with rural women through her Renewed Hope Initiative, noting that her visit to Edo State was her first in several years. She highlighted key achievements of President Tinubu’s administration, emphasising economic and social empowerment grants targeting rural women, the elderly, vulnerable citizens, and persons living with disabilities. Mrs Oluremi Tinubu with the Oba of Benin. Delivering a message from the Presidency, the First Lady congratulated Oba Ewuare on his 10th coronation anniversary. “He (President Bola Tinubu) asked me to appreciate your support and wish you well on your 10th coronation anniversary. We didn’t plan it this way, but it is divine,” she said. “I am truly happy, and I wish you long life, divine health, prosperity, joy, peace, and fruitfulness.” The First Lady was accompanied to the palace by Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo, Kogi State Governor Usman Ododo, and first ladies from Kogi, Kwara, Zamfara, and Cross River states, alongside leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC). With the decoration, Mrs Tinubu is only the third prominent Nigerian woman to receive the Ikele beads. Previous recipients are retired Chief Judge of Edo State, Justice Esohe Ikponmwen, and former Zonal Director of the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA), Benin Network Centre, Pauline Igbanor. The post Oba Of Benin Decorates Oluremi Tinubu With Prestigious ‘Ikele’ Coral Beads appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Tanker attacks intensify as Saudi–Houthi fighting threatens Bab el-Mandeb
body:
Commercial shipping across the Middle East faces a worsening security situation, with repeated attacks on tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement threatening maritime traffic through the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb.
The developments are raising concerns for shipowners, crews, oil exporters and cargo interests using the region’s critical energy routes.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency reported a series of attacks on commercial vessels on 11 and 12 October, including several tankers struck by unidentified projectiles while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
Six vessel incidents were reported for Sunday, 11 October, including attacks on crude and product tankers and a container ship. The reports were issued after delays, and investigations into the circumstances remain ongoing.
Separately, UKMTO confirmed that a tanker near Sohar anchorage off Oman was struck by a drone. The crew’s condition and the extent of damage were initially unknown, although local authorities assisted with the evacuation of the crew.
Twelve vessels were attacked between 5 and 11 October – the largest number of weekly strikes reported to the UKMTO agency since the US-Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw 10 ships reporting attacks.
The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, ​a small container vessel, sank earlier this week while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, according to ​maritime security sources. “GFS Pride sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All ⁠21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported,” the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said in a ​statement on Wednesday, adding that the vessel had been sailing through the strait on Tuesday.
In a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged ​Cape Dao sank close to the strait, weeks after being struck by a projectile on 23 September, data from UN shipping agency the International Maritime Organization showed on Wednesday. One crew member was killed, the rest of the crew evacuated straight after the strike, maritime sources said.
The GFS Pride and Cape Dao are the second and third vessels to have ​sunk since the US-Iran war began on 28 February.
The growing number of incidents is increasing the risks for vessels navigating the Gulf, where Iran has also issued warnings concerning routes it considers unauthorised. UKMTO continues to advise vessels to transit with caution and report suspicious activity.
Further south and west, the security situation has deteriorated following renewed fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and the Houthis, who have made gains in areas close to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
On 12 October, there were reports that Saudi Arabia was facing another barrage of missiles and drones after a deadly attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport. The airport remained closed, while attacks on Saudi infrastructure and retaliatory Saudi-led airstrikes continued.
On 13 October, the Saudi-led coalition carried out further strikes against oil facilities west of Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, according to the Associated Press. Houthi military representatives warned that further attacks on Yemen would bring retaliation against Riyadh.
The conflict has direct implications for shipping. A US maritime advisory says the Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi-affiliated shipping transiting Bab el-Mandeb in July, and warns that vessels with Saudi, US, UK or Israeli connections may face increased risks in the southern Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea oil export facilities have also been affected. On 1 October, an unidentified projectile struck inside Yanbu port, starting a fire and briefly halting loading operations involving a Liberian-flagged tanker. Loading subsequently resumed, but the vessel was not identified and the source of the projectile was not established.
The incident followed an earlier drone attack that disrupted Saudi Arabia’s East–West oil pipeline. Yanbu is particularly important because the pipeline allows Saudi crude to reach the Red Sea without passing through Hormuz.
The latest reports do not establish that a specific tanker at Yanbu is currently under a new alert. Nevertheless, the combination of attacks on the port, threats to Saudi infrastructure and renewed fighting around Bab el-Mandeb places the wider export chain under heightened security pressure.
For shipping companies, the immediate priorities are updated voyage risk assessments, close monitoring of UKMTO advisories and careful coordination with flag states, naval liaison services and insurers.
The situation remains fluid, with no clear indication that the attacks or the wider regional confrontation are about to subside.
France intercepts suspected Russian shadow-fleet tanker
In other news from further south in the Indian Ocean, the French Navy intercepted and boarded the tanker DF Peak (IMO 9341067) on Monday 12 October, about 450 nautical miles (833 km) south of Réunion in the Indian Ocean.
The 110,120-dwt tanker, formerly named Kaliningrad and sailing under the flag of Benin, had earlier rounded the Cape of Good Hope before heading into the Indian Ocean. DF Peak was suspected by French authorities of using a false flag and being involved in illicit fuel transportation. It was reportedly being escorted towards Réunion for further investigation.
Russia has since laid a complaint against France for what it referred to as an illegal act and a violation of international law.
Written by Africa Ports & Ships with input from DefenceWeb. The original article can be found here .

title: Sikorskiy reminds Trump that Ukrainians are attacked by Russian missiles, bombs, and drones
body:

title: American attack helicopters open fire in Korea
body: American Apache crews carried out aerial gunnery at the Rodriguez Live Fire Complex in South Korea at the end of September, validating weapons employment, target engagement and crew coordination under live-fire conditions, according to the unit . The crews came from 4th Battalion, 2nd Aviation Regiment, part of 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade in the 2nd Infantry Division and Republic of Korea and United States Combined Division. The division said the training strengthens combat readiness and proficiency, and the imagery released shows AH-64 Apaches engaging simulated targets at low level over wooded ridgelines, with rocket motor flashes beneath the fuselage and impact smoke rising from the hillsides. Rodriguez Live Fire Complex sits near Pocheon in Gyeonggi Province, around twenty-five kilometres from the Demilitarised Zone, and it is the principal range on the peninsula where American and South Korean units can shoot and manoeuvre together with live ammunition. Its proximity to the border has made it a politically sensitive site, with noise and safety complaints from nearby villages a recurring issue. 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade is the only permanently forward-stationed combat aviation brigade in the United States Army, and the “Fight Tonight” tag the division attaches to its material reflects what the formation exists to do, which is to be ready for combat without a deployment timeline. The brigade operates from Camp Humphreys, the largest American overseas base, and its Apache battalions are among the few American attack aviation units held at that readiness state permanently. The British Army flies the AH-64E Apache from Wattisham Flying Station under 1 Aviation Brigade Combat Team, having completed the transition from the Westland-built Mk1 fleet, and the American and British fleets now operate the same baseline aircraft. British crews train in similar gunnery cycles at ranges including Castlemartin and Otterburn, and have exercised alongside American attack aviation in Europe and the United States. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
body:
President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine.
The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company.
Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively.
Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC.
Tsentr Kapital is owned by 47-year-old Marat Mirkhaidarov, the former deputy governor and chief of staff of Far East Russia’s Zabaikalsky region.
Mirkhaidarov volunteered to serve in Ukraine with Chechnya’s Akhmat unit in early 2024, according to exiled media reports.
“I’m a patriot, I served in the special military operation [in Ukraine]. I have combat awards,” Mirkhaidarov told the Agentstvo outlet on Friday, expressing caution about his and his family’s safety over the news.
Mirkhaidarov stepped down from his regional administration post in March 2025, citing the need for medical rehabilitation after sustaining injuries during a delivery mission near the frontline.
Putin signed an order in 2023 granting the state the authority to place foreign assets under its temporary management. The regime strips foreign owners of operational control over their Russian subsidiaries while preserving nominal legal title.
Moscow has described the asset seizures as a response to “hostile actions” taken by “unfriendly” foreign governments.
On Friday, the Kremlin said the latest transfers represent a continued policy “trend” targeting countries that froze more than 210 billion euros in Russian reserves in Europe.
“Their origin was one of the factors taken into account when making the decision,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a daily briefing.
“We’re talking about those countries that take part in illegally holding Russian money, Russian assets. These are countries that take part in the illegal expropriation of Russian companies’ property,” Peskov said.

title: Mahama reaffirms commitment to private investment and industrial growth
body: President John Dramani Mahama has reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for private investment and industrial growth. The President made the remarks during a working visit to the Bright International Industrial Zone, where he cited the US$2.62 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) recorded in 2025 as evidence of renewed investor confidence in Ghana. Mr Mahama expressed optimism that the rollout of the New Economy Policy would further strengthen the country’s investment prospects and enhance its attractiveness to investors. He highlighted the importance of maintaining investor confidence and creating favourable conditions for private-sector investment to support industrial development. The President’s visit to the Bright International Industrial Zone emphasised the Government’s focus on encouraging private investment and promoting industrial growth as part of its broader economic agenda.

title: Moscow Airports Suspend Flights Again Amid Drone Alerts
body:
Moscow’s four airports suspended arrivals and departures overnight into Friday, Oct. 16, amid drone alerts, forcing more than 20 inbound aircraft to divert, according to Russian aviation authorities.
Restrictions at Vnukovo, Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky began on Thursday evening, Russia’s Federal Air Transport Agency, Rosaviatsiya, said.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
All four had reopened by 5:43 a.m. Moscow time on Friday, when Domodedovo and Zhukovsky resumed operations after Vnukovo and Sheremetyevo, Moscow 24 reported .
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defenses had intercepted 94 drones heading toward the capital, according to Meduza .
The Moscow Times reported more than 200 flight cancellations at Moscow’s airports during the disruption.
The latest shutdown followed restrictions at all four airports on Oct. 9 and again overnight on Oct. 13-14.
More than 500 flights were delayed or canceled during the Oct. 13-14 disruption, The Moscow Times reported, with aircraft also diverted to other Russian cities.
President Volodymyr Zelensky warned airlines and insurers in September about growing risks in Russian airspace as Ukraine expanded strikes on military targets and infrastructure supporting Moscow’s war effort. He said Ukraine did not target civilian aircraft.
“Drone-infested skies are no place for civilian aviation,” he said. “The safe days in Russia’s skies are over.”
Ukraine is preparing a broader campaign to disrupt Russian airports using AI-guided drones capable of navigating and identifying targets without human operators, The Atlantic reported, citing two sources familiar with the plan.
The proposed operation, codenamed “M&Ms,” was developed under former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, as previously reported by Kyiv Post.
Russian airlines carried 39.5 million passengers between May and August, down 7% from 42.6 million during the same period in 2025, according to Rosaviatsiya head Dmitry Yadrov.
The industry also faces difficulties maintaining foreign-made aircraft and prolonged closures of airports in southern Russia, as Kyiv Post previously reported.

title: NATO tries to extend reach beyond its bounds, into Eurasia — Russian foreign minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. NATO is seeking to extend its reach into Eurasia and promote its interests across the entire continent, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said at a conference of the Collective Security Treaty Organization, the Commonwealth of Independent States and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization on security issues in Central Asia and Afghanistan.
"NATO has no place in Eurasia," he said. "NATO is now trying to claim that the entire territory of Eurasia falls within its area of responsibility because it is a defensive alliance that protects the territories of its member states. However, threats to the territories of North Atlantic Alliance countries supposedly now originate from the Taiwan Strait, the South China Sea and elsewhere."
"This is a major philosophical shift that demonstrates NATO’s intention to dictate its will far beyond its area of responsibility," Lavrov pointed out.
In this regard, the foreign minister continued, "some kind of constructive response is needed, and only the countries of the region themselves can provide it." According to him, such a response is the idea of a Greater Eurasian Partnership put forward by Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"It is necessary to use the process of forming a Eurasian partnership as a material foundation for interaction among countries and integration structures located in Eurasia, and then build a collective security framework on that basis," the minister stressed. "Our president’s initiative is addressed to all countries, regional and subregional associations located on the Eurasian continent, without exception. It is difficult to imagine and envision this under the current circumstances, but I am nevertheless convinced that setting such a goal at the conceptual level is highly reasonable. It would underscore that the initiators and like-minded partners who embrace this idea envision an open and inclusive future for the development of our shared continent."

title: General Staff: Russian "Nebo-U" radar hit in Russia's Krasnodar Krai
body:
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine has reported the destruction of Russian Nebo-U radar station in Krasnodar Krai during the night of Friday, October 16.

"In the night of October 16, 2026, units of the Ukraine Defense Forces hit the 55Zh6U 'Nebo-U' radar station in the area of the settlement of Mahri in Krasnodar Krai of Russia. As a result, a fire broke out in the area of the facility," the General Staff said in a Telegram post.

It is noted that Nebo-U is a long-range three-coordinate meter-band radar station. The station is designed to detect and track air targets, including aircraft, cruise, and ballistic missiles. The destruction of such equipment reduces the enemy's capability to control airspace and detect air targets in a timely manner. The estimated cost of the station is about $100 million.

title: Silent Lynx Hackers Leave Their Central Asian Spy Campaign Exposed
body: New findings published on October 14 suggest that hackers spying on Central Asian governments have been operating from Kazakhstan. The group, named Silent Lynx by researchers, used hijacked official email accounts to break into government computers. The hackers left some of their own working files unprotected online, allowing researchers to examine how they prepared and adapted their attacks. Their targets included agencies holding information about regional diplomacy and natural resources. The investigation was conducted by cybersecurity firm Recorded Future and Talos, a security research group at computer networking company Cisco. The two companies, both based in the United States, have not established whether the hackers were working for a government. Hijacked Official Email Accounts Seqrite, an Indian cybersecurity provider, gave the hackers the name Silent Lynx in January 2025 . Its investigation found that they had sent malicious emails from an employee’s hijacked account at Kyrgyzstan’s central bank. A message from a real official’s address could make a dangerous attachment look like routine business. One message claimed that correspondence intended for Kyrgyzstan’s Finance Ministry had been sent to the central bank by mistake. Attached was what appeared to be a United Nations meeting invitation, packaged with a malicious program. Running it would allow the hackers to issue instructions to the recipient’s computer and send files through a chat they controlled on Telegram, the messaging app. In related attacks, investigators saw the hackers copying documents and collecting passwords saved in web browsers. One victim had left a file called passwords.txt on the desktop, which the attackers stole and could use to access other accounts. German cybersecurity company VMRay and independent researcher Pol Thill documented these thefts in February 2026. The Files That Gave Them Away Researchers Ashley Shen and Julian-Ferdinand Vögele, from Talos and Recorded Future, respectively, found three online folders where the hackers had left attack software and other tools publicly accessible. A program in one folder led them to an account on GitHub, a website where programmers store and share code. GitHub preserves earlier versions of files, so the researchers could see how the hackers had revised their software and changed the internet addresses used to control infected computers. Moving to a new address did not erase the record, allowing investigators to continue tracking the operation. An attack file identified in April exploited a weakness in WinRAR, a program for unpacking compressed files. It was designed to install software that would start when the user next signed in, allowing the hackers to send instructions to the computer. A July 2025 update had fixed the weakness in WinRAR, but the attack could still work on computers where users had not updated the program. VMRay’s earlier investigation found that some operators had infected their own computers, exposing their browsing histories to the researchers. What Were They Looking For? The victims of those earlier attacks included water and hydropower institutions in Kyrgyzstan and water-related bodies in Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. Access to water records could be valuable in a region where decisions upstream affect farming far downstream. Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation estimates that 44.3% of the country’s long-term average surface-water supply comes from rivers flowing across its borders. This year, for example, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan agreed on summer releases from the Bahri Tojik reservoir to irrigate farmland in southern Kazakhstan. Recorded Future’s new report identified computers at a Tajik economic-development institution communicating with servers used by the hackers. It detected activity involving computer systems associated with Uzbekistan’s Smart Forestry initiative, which collects geographic information about forest lands . These connections did not establish what information, if any, had been stolen. An August 2025 document posed as a cooperation proposal from Turkmenistan’s state oil concern to Russia’s Orsk Oil Refinery. Talos suggests the lure may reflect interest in regional fuel supplies and the effects of the war in Ukraine on Kazakhstan’s energy security. The document does not prove either organization was successfully breached. Recorded Future believes the hackers were gathering intelligence about regional diplomacy and natural resources, although the researchers could not establish precisely what information the operators wanted. The Trail to Kazakhstan In 2022, just 86 seconds after a program used by the hackers was created, it was uploaded from Kazakhstan to VirusTotal, a service for checking suspicious files. Recorded Future and Talos describe the upload in their joint research paper and believe it was an attacker testing a new tool. GitHub’s records show that the hackers usually saved revised versions of their attack programs between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. Kazakhstan time, matching a daytime office schedule. A saved record also showed an operator trying to enter English commands while the keyboard was set to Russian. Talos suspects the hackers were working from Kazakhstan but rates its assessment at medium confidence. Talos and Recorded Future expect the campaign to continue, citing the group’s persistence and adoption of new ways to break into computer systems. They identify government agencies managing diplomacy and natural resources as likely targets for further attacks.

title: NCP parliamentary group proposes tightening Finland's asylum rules
body:
The government party has outlined plans for a more selective immigration policy, including stricter asylum procedures and tighter access to social security.
The National Coalition Party's (NCP) parliamentary group wants Finland to move towards a policy of selective immigration, in an aim to give the country more control over who can enter and remain in Finland.
The group published its new immigration policy guidelines on Friday, with proposals prepared under the leadership of MP Atte Kaleva (NCP), who has led the work since January.
They have proposed moving asylum processing outside the EU and tightening the conditions for family reunification and access to social security.
"This means that Finland must be able to decide under all circumstances who is allowed to enter the country and under what conditions, as well as who is allowed to remain here," Kaleva said.
The proposals include linking immigrants' eligibility for unemployment benefits to their employment history in Finland and tightening the conditions for receiving the national pension and guarantee pension.
The parliamentary group proposes transferring asylum processing entirely to reception and return centres outside the EU.
It also wants to restrict repeated asylum applications deemed unfounded and make returns more efficient.
"Asylum has been misused as a channel for mass migration, which it was never intended to be. We are returning to protecting individual people who are in need of protection. This also removes the market for people smuggling," he said.
The group further proposes that serious or repeated criminal offences could lead to the revocation of a person's residence permit and their deportation.
Regarding quota refugees, the group proposes that authorities also take into account their prospects for integrating into Finnish society and culture.
"We have certain fundamental values in Finland that we cannot compromise on: democracy, individual freedoms, equality, the equality of women and girls, and minority rights," Kaleva said.
"If a person is unable to adapt to these values, then of course they cannot be accepted into Finland," he added.
Under the proposals, immigrants' eligibility for unemployment benefits would depend on the work they had done in Finland. The level of support would vary according to the length of their employment.
The group also proposes tightening family reunification rules by requiring the person bringing family members to Finland to be able to support them through employment or business activities.
Kaleva said the party wanted to encourage work-based immigration, but opposed the creation of a low-wage labour market in Finland.
"We cannot create a cheap labour market in Finland, where people come here to work for companies that do not pay a sufficient salary," he said.
Kaleva said responsibility for integration should lie primarily with immigrants themselves, but also with their employers.
The parliamentary group's proposals were outlined in its new immigration policy programme, titled 'Towards Selective Immigration' ( Kohti valikoivaa maahanmuuttoa ), included in their press release (in Finnish).

title: Ukraine makes its anti-drone road nets a national standard in a new strategy for defensive lines through 2028. It has already strung over more than 1,000 kilometers of road
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s government has approved a Strategy for the Engineering Equipment of Defensive Lines through 2028. It makes strengthening anti-drone protection of logistics routes one of its priorities, the Defense Ministry says . Russian FPV drones hunt almost anything that moves within 15 to 30 kilometers of the front, which has forced Ukraine to drape its logistics roads in overhead netting, wire-mesh canopies and reinforced barriers that catch an attacking drone before it reaches a vehicle. Ukraine had already built more than 1,066 kilometers of such protection by mid-July and aims for 4,000 kilometers by the end of 2026. The new strategy turns that scramble into a single national standard, setting deadlines, assigning responsibility, and building control mechanisms, the ministry explained. “Solutions that have proven effective we will scale. But we will also account for new challenges, threats and changes in Russian tactics. The main goal is the protection of our service members and civilians,” the Defense Ministry says. One digital map for every trench and net The plan puts the entire defensive network onto a screen. To track and monitor the state of defensive lines, Ukraine will introduce a single digital geographic information platform, built on and expanding existing systems, including the DELTA situational-awareness system. The database will hold object passports, photographs, and data on each structure’s location and condition, helping officials verify that work is done, identify repair needs, and distribute resources on evidence rather than guesswork. From trenches to supply roads, one cycle The strategy covers the full span of military engineering. Its main lines of work are building and maintaining fortifications, laying engineering obstacles, strengthening anti-drone protection of logistics routes, using modern designs, materials and camouflage, creating a reserve of construction materials, and maintaining digital records of the work. Developed on the Defense Ministry’s initiative based on combat experience, the document spans the entire cycle from planning and construction to accounting, upkeep, and restoration, the ministry noted.
