title: Bear crash and drone strike cost Russia three more aircraft
body: Russia lost three tactical and strategic aircraft in the space of a week, a Tu-95MS bomber that crashed after multiple engine failures on a training flight and two fighters destroyed by a Ukrainian one-way attack drone at an airbase five hundred kilometres from Ukraine, according to the latest UK Defence Intelligence update on the situation in Ukraine. The update said: “Over the course of one week, Russia suffered three tactical and strategic aircraft losses. These airframes have been involved in strike campaigns against Ukraine. “On 29 September 2026 Russia’s Long Range Aviation fleet lost one of its workhorse Tu-95MS BEAR H on a training flight shortly after take-off in eastern Russia. The BEAR H suffered multiple engine failures before crashing. These aircraft have been used extensively to strike Ukraine over the course of the conflict, almost certainly creating a significant maintenance burden on the fleet. “On 04 October 2026, a Ukrainian one-way attack uncrewed aerial vehicle strike destroyed a Su-35S FLANKER M multi-role fighter and Su-34 FULLBACK fighter-bomber and a munitions depot at Khanskaya airbase, Russia, 500km from Ukraine. “FULLBACK aircraft are used on daily operations to launch glide munitions into Ukraine. Analysis of commercial satellite imagery dated 04 October 2026 identified the attack had destroyed two fighter aircraft, cratered the parking apron and the taxiway, destroyed one building and destroyed and damaged two munitions’ depots. “Russia has lost more than 100 fighter aircraft in the Ukraine conflict since February 2022.” Russia will find the Bear the harder of the two losses to absorb, because production of the Tu-95MS ended in the early nineteen nineties. They fly the Kh-101 cruise missile strikes that have hit Ukrainian cities through the war, launching from well inside Russian airspace and turning for home without entering contested air. Khanskaya sits in the Republic of Adygea in southern Russia, well outside the range at which Russian commanders had been willing to disperse aircraft earlier in the war. Ukraine’s long-range one-way attack drones have steadily pushed that calculation back, and airfields that were treated as rear areas have had to adopt the revetments, decoys and dispersal that frontline bases adopted years ago. The post Bear crash and drone strike cost Russia three more aircraft first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Senate passes bill backing Akwa Ibom’s federal university of technology
body:
The Senate has passed a bill seeking to provide a legal framework for the Federal University of Technology, Ikot Abasi (FUTIA), Akwa Ibom State, five years after it was established.
The bill, sponsored by Ekong Sampson, senator representing Akwa Ibom South Senatorial District, was passed on Thursday after consideration of its provisions.
Samuel Udoma, Mr Sampson’s media aide, announced the development in a Facebook post on Thursday, describing the legislation as a significant step towards securing the university’s legal status.
The university’s Vice-Chancellor, Leo Daniel, welcomed the passage, describing it as “the best gift of the year” from the National Assembly to the institution.
The development comes as FUTIA expands its academic offerings, having recently secured approval from the National Universities Commission (NUC) to commence 12 additional degree programmes from the 2026/2027 academic session.
FUTIA was among the federal tertiary institutions approved by former President Muhammadu Buhari in June 2021. However, the university was established without an Act of Parliament.
Mr Sampson sponsored the bill to address the gap and provide the institution with legal backing for its administration and operations.
According to the university, the legislation will strengthen its institutional foundation and support its mandate to advance technology-driven education, research, innovation and sustainable development.
The bill’s passage followed legislative consideration at the National Assembly, including a public hearing at which stakeholders submitted memoranda in support of the proposed legislation.
Senate President Godswill Akpabio, who presided over Thursday’s plenary, emphasised the institution’s potential contribution beyond Nigeria.
Mr Akpabio said the university would serve “the global community, not just Nigerians,” while commending the 10th Senate for its commitment to education-focused legislation.
Earlier, Muntari Dandutse, chairman of the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, presented the committee’s report on the bill.
Mr Dandutse said the establishment of FUTIA and other tertiary institutions would deepen Nigerians’ access to technology-based higher education.
Following clause-by-clause consideration, the Senate read the bill for the third time and passed it.
The chamber also passed bills establishing the Federal University of Health Sciences, Funtua, Katsina State, and the Federal University of Technology, Babura, Jigawa State.
In a separate development, the NUC approved 12 additional degree programmes at FUTIA following a successful resource verification visit to the university.
A statement posted on Facebook and signed by the university registrar, Offiongita Nkang, said the approval was conveyed in an NUC letter dated 11 September 2026.
The newly approved programmes include biomedical engineering, computer engineering, materials and metallurgical engineering, mechatronics engineering, chemistry, industrial chemistry, environmental management technology, biotechnology, environmental health science, health information management, community health science and estate management.
The approval brings the number of NUC-approved programmes at the university to 36, according to the institution.
The university commenced its pioneer academic session in 2023/2024.
The vice-chancellor said the expansion reflected the institution’s commitment to widening access to higher education and strengthening teaching, research, manpower development and community service.
Mr Daniel, described by the university as Nigeria’s first professor of aeronautics and astronautics, pledged that FUTIA would continue to introduce programmes aligned with present and future educational needs.
He thanked the management team, academic board, governing council and other stakeholders for supporting the institution’s development.
The university advised candidates who sat for the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination and wish to study the newly approved courses to change their course choices through the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board’s Central Admissions Processing System.
Candidates who did not initially select FUTIA as their first-choice institution but scored at least 160 can also apply by changing their first-choice institution to the university.
Mr Sampson has also sponsored a bill seeking to establish the Federal University of Medical Sciences in Eket, which remains before the Senate.
He has advocated the full university status of the University of Maritime Studies, Oron, as part of efforts to strengthen tertiary education across the three federal constituencies in Akwa Ibom South.
FUTIA’s establishment in 2021 generated controversy over its location, resulting in exchanges between Ita Enang, then a presidential aide, and the administration of former Governor Udom Emmanuel of Akwa Ibom.
PREMIUM TIMES reported the disagreement in August 2021. Mr Enang is now Nigeria’s ambassador to Germany.
With the Senate’s passage of the bill, the legislative process at the National Assembly has been concluded. The bill is expected to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

title: ‘We have been used and dumped’ – NDC’s James Agbey warns over grassroots neglect
body: An operative of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), James Agbey, has warned that the party risks alienating its grassroots supporters unless government appointees address concerns about neglect and a lack of economic opportunities. In a statement dated Friday, October 16, Mr Agbey accused appointees of overlooking activists and cadres who worked to secure the party’s return to power in the 2024 elections. “The feeling out there at the base is that ‘we have been used and dumped’,” he said. Mr Agbey claimed that many party activists were struggling with unemployment and financial hardship, while some appointees were prioritising relatives and close associates over those who supported the party during its years in opposition. “Everything seems to have changed after the elections. Appointees are now prioritising their families and close allies, some of whom were not even part of the struggle,” he alleged. He said the concerns required practical intervention rather than occasional handouts or promises of future support. “All that these party activists are asking for is opportunities to be able to fend for themselves,” he stated. Mr Agbey urged government appointees to engage with the party’s support base and take concrete steps to address their concerns. He warned that unresolved grievances could weaken loyalty and lead dissatisfied activists to turn against the government in a future election. “Our support for the NDC must not be taken for granted,” he cautioned. The statement did not provide figures to substantiate his claim that the party’s support base was dwindling or identify the appointees accused of favouring relatives and associates. Mr Agbey nevertheless maintained that the leadership needed to act urgently to prevent growing frustration from damaging the party’s electoral prospects. “I call for urgent action or we will have ourselves to blame come the electioneering season,” he said.

title: Lukashenko announces impending inspection of Belarusian territorial defense forces
body:
MINSK, October 16. /TASS/. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko has announced a coming inspection of the country’s militia and territorial defense forces, according to the Telegram channel Pul Pervogo, which is affiliated with the Belarusian leader’s press service.
"This is a matter of the utmost importance," the channel quoted the president as saying, adding that the people’s militia and territorial defense forces will be inspected shortly.
"We will soon put this entire nationwide system on its toes, this chain of command, for the purpose of inspection. We’ll see how the people’s militia operates and how the territorial defense forces function. The territorial defense forces will protect major life-support facilities within their districts. And, of course, these functions will also overlap [with those of the people’s militia]," the BelTA news agency quoted Lukashenko as saying.
The Belarusian leader emphasized that every rural council, comprising up to 20 villages where people live, must have a support force. "God forbid an enemy should come - these people must be able to defend themselves and their families. If they (the enemies) come to us with the sword, you know… This small unit (the people’s militia) is very important," Lukashenko said.

title: Defence to automate a fifth of its back-office functions
body: The Ministry of Defence is committed to automating at least twenty per cent of its Human Resources, Finance and Commercial functions by July 2028 and to moving Regular personnel out of administrative work and into front-line roles, according to a written answer in the House of Lords . Lord Sarfraz, the Conservative peer, asked how many military personnel have been released from back-office roles to front-line roles as a result of automation since the publication of the Strategic Defence Review in 2025. Lord Coaker, Minister of State for Defence, said: “The Department remains committed to maximising the operational effectiveness of the Armed Forces and ensuring that Defence personnel are focused on activity that best supports front-line outcomes. As set out in the Strategic Defence Review, Defence is taking forward work to move Regular personnel from administrative activity into front-line roles and to automate at least 20% of Human Resources, Finance and Commercial functions by July 2028. “This commitment is being delivered through the Defence Reform and Efficiency Plan, including the Corporate Services Modernisation programme, which is redesigning and modernising Defence’s People, Finance and Commercial services. The programme is simplifying policy and processes, standardising activity, consolidating services where appropriate and introducing modern digital tools to reduce manual work, strengthen access to reliable management information and improve the user experience. This will reduce the back-office burden, improve productivity and release capacity for front-line activity while maintaining effective support to all personnel.” July 2028 gives the department a little under two years from now to hit the target. The post Defence to automate a fifth of its back-office functions first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: US claim on collapse of Iranian economy not realized
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 16 (MNA) – Reacting to the remarks of the US secretary of state who had claimed Iran's economy would collapse, Tehran's provisional Friday Prayers Leader said, “Not only Iran’s economy did not collapse, but also became stronger, viable."
Speaking at his sermon of Friday prayers in Tehran, Ayatollah Seyyed Ahmad Khatemi stated that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said that Iran's economy would collapse within two weeks, but not only its economy did not collapse, but also became more dynamic and viable.
“This is not just our view. This is while that the head of the World Economic Forum (WEF) also confirms Iran has managed to bring the situation under control in the best form possible over the past month, and that the coming year will be a brilliant year for the Iranian nation in economic terms," the senior cleric emphasized.
The United States has failed to achieve its sinister goal in the imposed war waged against the noble people of the country, Khatami underlined.
The interim Friday Prayers then pointed to the shaky political situation of US President Donald Trump, stating, "These days, Trump is campaigning for his party. Wherever he has gone with this aim, he has faced public protest; in a way that he was interrupted five times during one of his speeches.”
Ayatollah Khatami considered this incident as a sign of protest against the American president, noting, “Even inside America, he is opposed and his popularity rating has been plummeted and has reached less than 40%.”
Elsewhere in his remarks, he pointed to the powerful Armed Forces of the country who gave an unforgettable lesson to the delusional US president, so that the US Navy fleet was forced to flee to a position several hundred kilometers away from the Iranian territory and this shows extreme power of the country on he international stages.
He seized this opportunity to thank the courageous and brave Iranian Armed Forces and also resistance of the noble people of the country in the face of the US and Israeli aggression against the country.
The US officials' prediction regarding the collapse of Iran's economy did not and will not materialize forever, he reiterated.

title: Ghana defender Marvin Senaya begins training ahead of comeback
body: Black Stars fullback Marvin Senaya has returned to light training on grass as he aims to return to competitive action following a muscle injury sustained during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Senaya suffered a hamstring injury during Ghana’s Round of 32 clash against Colombia in July and has been out since the new season commenced. The injury has forced the Ghanaian fullback to miss the opening seven league matches for AJ Auxerre. His return to on-pitch running shows progression in his recovery. However, a definite return to competitive action has not been confirmed. Senaya was a standout player for Ghana during the 2026 World Cup, earning praise for his performances during the campaign. His eventual return to match fitness will be a bright spot for Auxerre, while the Black Stars will also hope to utilise the defender for upcoming international fixtures once he full recovers.

title: US misunderstands Iranian people, Tehran’s envoy says
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. The United States has a mistaken understanding of the Iranian people, while millions of Iranians have officially registered to participate in the country’s defense, Tehran’s Ambassador to Moscow Kazem Jalali said.
"The US government has a wrong impression and understanding of the Iranian people. Our people always stand their ground and don’t doubt for a second when it comes to defending their land. More than 33 million Iranians have officially registered to take part in the country’s defense, and they are ready to resist any new act of aggression, he noted, addressing a conference on security issues in Central Asia and Afghanistan involving the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).

title: External management introduced for firms from countries holding Russian assets — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. External management is being introduced primarily for companies from countries that are unfriendly in the full sense of the word, that are unlawfully holding Russian assets and expropriating Russian property, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing.
"This refers to countries that are participating in the unlawful holding of Russian funds, Russian assets, and are taking part in the unlawful expropriation of property belonging to Russian companies," he said. "In other words, unfriendly in the full sense of the word," Peskov added.
Earlier, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree placing the Russian assets of flooring manufacturer Tarkett, as well as those of Ontex, the owner of the Helen Harper diaper brand, and three foreign packaging companies, under external management.
The Kremlin has said that the move is not aimed at a change of ownership, adding that the mechanism of external management is designed to prevent the suspension of operations at key production facilities affiliated with Western companies for political reasons due to pressure from the governments of unfriendly countries.

title: AG orders Cuban/SA military co-operation project to end
body:
South Africa’s Auditor-General (AG) – government’s financial watchdog when it comes to protecting the public purse – has instructed the SA National Defence Force (SANDF) to end Project Kgala.
It in 2025 succeeded the Cuban/South African military co-operation agreement Project Thusano, and like its predecessor, has been shrouded in controversy. This has involved costs of technical services and training arrangements long opposed by Democratic Alliance (DA) Member of Parliament (MP) Chris Hattingh at Parliamentary oversight level.
This week Rear Admiral James Matshimane, SA Navy (SAN) Head of Policy, Strategy and Planning, told Parliament that “an instruction has already been given that we should stop”. He added that training courses currently underway would finish before Kgala is officially concluded.
Chairperson of Portfolio Committee on Defence and Military Veterans Dakota Legoete subsequently called for a formal, phased plan that sets out exactly when the remaining Project Kgala courses would finish. He said Project Kgala should be included in a “remedial audit action plan” that would, for example, specify when the last student would leave the programme.
DefenceWeb in May reported on the Auditor-General finding on Project Kgala, in the wake of a legal opinion from the Office of the Chief State Law Advisor (OCSLA), that Kgala be ended.
Hattingh agrees the announcement of Kgala ending doesn’t mean it’s a completed shutdown saying completion of student qualifications needs a lawful plan – “it cannot become an excuse for indefinite irregular expenditure”. On this count he maintains a termination instruction, a full reconciliation of expenditure and a costed exit plan must be decided on and produced for public scrutiny.
Hattingh said the African National Congress (ANC) “obsession” with Cuba consumed billions of rands at a time when the SANDF struggled to maintain equipment and fund essential operations.
“In March 2025, the Department [of Defence] told Parliament that Thusano had cost approximately R3.04 billion over a decade. The AG reported R1.699 billion in disclosed irregular expenditure. Kgala was presented as the solution, yet the reporting on it identifies a further R278.6 million in irregular expenditure under the successor arrangement.
“The DA warned Parliament on 12 March 2025 that changing Thusano’s name would not change the laws governing public procurement. Defence nevertheless assured the committee that irregular expenditure would not recur. Those assurances now demand an explanation from the officials who gave them and the leadership responsible for implementation. Proof that the ANC’s idea of ‘cost-effectiveness’ is selling South African jobs to Cuba,” part of Hattingh’s reaction statement reads.
Elaborating, he added Kgala costs extend beyond payments to Cuban specialists – one of which was a nearly R34 million charter flight carrying more than 200 SANDF personnel, including senior officers and students, to Cuba for a graduation ceremony. “The latest reported Kgala expenditure includes R100.3 million for aircraft chartering. Defence must disclose the flights concerned and establish whether the previously exposed charter forms part of that amount,” he said.
Hattingh does not see Kgala as finished, saying costs, among others, go beyond payments to Cuban specialists with training outcomes needing examination. One of these is medical where, according to him, the Caribbean island’s medical qualifications do not automatically entitle returning graduates to practise medicine in South Africa. They must satisfy South African registration and clinical requirements.
“The AG reported just six of the first cohort of 21 medical students successfully completed the initial 18-month integration course at the University of Pretoria. Expensive overseas training must deliver recognised qualifications and usable skills,” he added.
On technical services Maluleke’s public institution found Cuban technical services cost substantially more than their comparable South African equivalents, denying skilled South Africans work opportunities. Hattingh said Minister Angie Motshekga’s Department of Defence (DoD)/SANDF cannot justify neglecting domestic artisans, engineers, training institutions and defence companies while committing scarce resources to arrangements whose value remains inadequately demonstrated.
He will, in line with his allotted oversight function in Parliament, watch General Rudzani Maphwanya’s SANDF closely to ensure its dealings with Cuba comply with legal requirements – “another name change or transfer to a different budget cannot substitute accountability”.

title: Police remove DPO after suspected cultists renovate station
body:
The Police Command in Rivers State has removed the divisional police officer in charge of Abuloma Division and the officer overseeing its police outpost following allegations that suspected cultists renovated the facility.
The command also ordered a full investigation into the circumstances surrounding the renovation and the alleged involvement of police officers
The police spokesperson in Rivers State, Blessing Agabe, disclosed this in a statement posted on Facebook on Friday, following a viral video showing alleged cultists at the police outpost during what appeared to be a handover ceremony.
The video , which circulated on Facebook, shows men dressed in black, white, and red shirts at the facility. Some police officers were also seen taking photographs with the suspected cultists during the event.
A Facebook user identified the group as “Aro Bagger” and claimed that the police station was unveiled as part of the group’s activities to mark its 2026 “Humanitarian Day celebration” on 15 October.
The police said it had taken cognisance of the reports and condemned any action that could undermine the integrity, discipline, nd professional standards of the Nigeria Police Force.
It warned that police facilities must not become platforms for suspected criminal groups seeking public recognition, legitimacy, or influence.
Ms Agabe said the Commissioner of Police in Rivers, Olugbenga Adepoju, ordered an investigation to establish the identities and backgrounds of those who financed or facilitated the renovation, the officers who authorised the project, and whether the required procedures were followed.
The investigation will also “determine whether any police officer breached professional standards or compromised the integrity of the force,” said the police.
The command, however, acknowledged that “legitimate community support for improving police facilities is permitted under Section 26(1)(d) of the Nigeria Police Act 2020, which provides for gifts and contributions to the Police General Fund.”
It stressed that such assistance must not compromise police independence, professional standards or security.
“No donation or assistance confers immunity from investigation or prosecution,” the statement said.
The statement added that the police would take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against anyone found culpable after the investigation.
It reiterated its commitment to fighting cultism and organised crime and urged residents to remain calm and provide credible information to support security operations across the state.

title: 3 dialysis machines delivered to Ed Daein Centre in Darfur
body: The Federal Ministry of Health under the Tasis government has delivered three dialysis machines to the dialysis center in Ed Daein in Sudan’s East Darfur State following a shutdown that lasted more than a year and left 24 patients dead. Ed Daein Hospital was subjected to aerial attacks by the Sudanese army in March 2025, destroying its buildings and completely suspending its services. Speaking during the handover of the machines, Minister of Roads and Bridges Dr Khalid Ahmed Aseel described the army’s targeting of Ed Daein Hospital, which he said was intended to disable an essential service institution, as a humanitarian crime. “Providing healthcare is a fundamental part of the Tasis government’s responsibilities and reaffirms the ‘recovery’ slogan it has been promoting in recent days,” he said. For his part, Federal Undersecretary of Health Al-Amin Daoud paid tribute to the medical staff who continued working at Ed Daein Hospital despite repeated attacks. “We pledge to provide free healthcare services to residents, including primary healthcare, maternal and child health services, dialysis treatment, and care at rural hospitals,” he said. “The ministry is prepared to respond to public health emergencies, including cholera and measles outbreaks, and work to contain their spread.” Meanwhile, East Darfur’s Director-General of Health, al-Azraq Hassan Humida, said the dialysis center had suspended operations in 2024 following an aerial attack on the hospital. Services subsequently resumed at Ed Daein Hospital, but a second attack in March 2025 killed more than 70 patients, he said. “All patients receiving dialysis at the center have since died as a result of the interruption of treatment,” he stated. He expressed hope that the equipment will enable services to resume. The post 3 dialysis machines delivered to Ed Daein Centre in Darfur appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: 'I was innocent': Former Dubai resident gives first interview after five-year detention in Iraq
body: A former Dubai resident detained for five years in Iraq over a contract dispute will take time to adjust to freedom and is determined to fight for vindication after the “dark times” he endured. Australian engineer Robert Pether was released from prison in Baghdad in June last year but was barred from leaving the country due to financial claims linked to a case over a contract dispute between his employer and authorities in Iraq. “The concept of freedom is still kicking in for me because it's been a long time and I'm still adjusting,” Mr Pether, 50, told The National in his first interview since returning to Dublin on Monday. Spending time with family who now live in Ireland will be his main priority. He will soon have surgery to treat high-risk skin cancer, which deteriorated while he was in prison. “I'm having surgery in the next few days,” he said. “But it will be fixed, there's no doubt about that. We caught it in time.” 'No innocent person should suffer this' He will consult lawyers over the next few months to address the “huge injustice ” he suffered. Mr Pether and his Egyptian co-worker Khaled Radwan, both of whom lived in Dubai, travelled to Baghdad in April 2021 and were locked up four months later. They were fined $12 million over a contract dispute between their employer CME Consulting and the Central Bank of Iraq. “I'm looking for accountability,” he told The National . “I was innocent when I was arrested. We did nothing wrong. “What was done to us was not reasonable, was not justice. So there does need to be accountability. I'm not at a stage where I'm going to identify who we're looking at for that accountability. I will let lawyers keep working on that.” Mr Pether did not share details of the legal case he plans to pursue and is aware of the challenging road ahead. “It will all be made known when the time is right. What we went through, no one, no innocent person should have to be subjected to … that is not something that you can just snap your fingers and say it's finished. “There needs to be some balance and that's where we're seeking accountability among the people who caused this, the people who are truly responsible for it … so that we feel more vindicated.” 'Don't give in' Mr Pether sought to give strength to others who have been wrongly incarcerated and their families. “Do not give up. That's really all I could tell them. Do not give in. You have to keep fighting,” he told The National . “There is an end. There is a way through … arbitrary detention is completely unjust but unfortunately it still happens. It will continue to happen. You just have to be strong enough to get through it.” The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention in 2021 deemed that Mr Pether’s detention breached international law and said he was being used as leverage in a commercial dispute. Mr Pether said his pursuit of justice also aims to deter those who consider detain innocent people unjustly. “The fact that we did suffer a huge injustice … it's going to be a long path but it's one that needs to be crossed,” he said. “This is not just for me, this is for other people … because it will happen again. I will not be the last … if we do bring in some measures of accountability and a way to achieve accountability, it will help the next person. And perhaps give people thought, to not put people into arbitrary detention.” His first priority is his family and he will then set aside time with lawyers. “In terms of actually making something happen, it will take months or years,” Mr Pether said. “I'm prepared for that, as is my wife. We've already discussed it, this is part of the healing process for us.” Not if but how to survive prison Conversations with his wife, Desree, and children, Flynn, Oscar and Nala, gave him courage . Speaking to former hostage Terry Waite, the Archbishop of Canterbury's special envoy kidnapped in Beirut in 1987 and held in captivity for five years – four of those in solitary confinement – helped him make crucial choices to draw on his inner resilience to survive his prison ordeal. “Terry and I started talking soon after my incarceration,” Mr Pether said. “The very first discussion we had, he said that I needed to make some hard decisions, and I had to decide how I was going to survive. There was never any question of if, it was always how.” Building mental fortitude, distancing himself from other prisoners and trying to keep tight control of his emotions proved to be his lifeline. “I personally decided I'd be better off isolating myself, relying on myself and my own internal strength,” Mr Pether told The National . His wife Desree and the embassy sent over books and immersing himself in reading took him away from the prison walls. After his release from jail last year, Mr Pether lived in a secure compound and his reading continued to give clarity of mind. “Reading books was a form of escapism that helped me build up my strength,” he said. “Basically that was how I got through the years in prison and the last 12 months when I was hidden away somewhere quietly and I had a few people I would speak to daily and catch up with … “I’m a fairly voracious reader, so anything I could get my hands on, I was reading. It was a way to fill in time and also a way to keep my brain moving, so that I could think about things more clearly.” Family lifeline The Pether family have spoken about being robbed of sharing personal milestones, from graduations to birthdays. “There were a lot of dark times but we got through them,” he said. “My wife used to prop me up when I was really down. There were times it was a roller coaster … each time it went down, it went further down and that was hard because then you had to drag yourself back up from there.” He initially thought the case would be resolved quickly, then as months and years passed there were times he lost hope. “I'll be honest, there were times when I did question that – 'will I actually go home?’” Mr Pether said. “It was a matter of trying to avoid the really dark patches, keeping the mental strength to know I would go home. It was just a question of when.” Conversations with his wife and children encouraged him to keep going. “My family was always on my mind, my wife especially, and there was never any question of not getting back,” he said. “What she was doing was not just fighting for my freedom. She was also propping up myself, our children, holding our family together. And it was her strength, sharing her strength with me, that helped.”

title: Le Pen announces readiness to visit Ukraine
body:
Far-right French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who previously stated that she would not support further funding for Ukraine if she comes to power, has continued a remote debate with President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

"I have nothing, personally, against Zelenskyy, and if he wishes for us to discuss, I will gladly come to Ukraine," she wrote on the social media platform X on Friday.

"But we no longer have the financial means to provide aid that has cost us up to 6 billion euros per year so far," she emphasized.

Earlier, in an interview with the Financial Times, Zelenskyy commented on her statement, stressing that France and its industry stand to lose a lot if support for Ukraine is cut off. Zelenskyy noted that the technological experience of the Ukrainian army is crucial for partners, particularly the United Kingdom, the United States, and France. "And, in my opinion, French industry can only win thanks to these technologies, thanks to this cooperation and join…

title: WACOT Renews Strategic Partnership with Edo Govt to Drive Agricultural Transformation
body: Oluchi Chibuzor WACOT Limited, has extended its agreement with the Edo State Government on fertilizer production through the Edo State Fertilizer and Chemical Company Limited (ESFCCL) in Auchi. The partnership which commenced in 2017, reaffirms both parties’ commitment to boosting local fertilizer production, supporting smallholder farmers, and advancing Nigeria’s food security. Speaking on the significance of the facility from an industry perspective, the President of the Fertilizer Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) and Director, Corporate Affairs, TGI Group Mr. Sadiq Kassim, said: “The Auchi facility is of strategic importance to Nigeria’s fertilizer industry and national food security. It is the only plant in the South-South with the capability to produce tailored, crop-specific fertilizer blends suited to the region’s soil requirements. The facility also has the capability to produce specialised chemical blends to meet the specific needs of the North-East, where security challenges have made establishing fertilizer production facilities particularly difficult.” Also commenting on the renewed partnership, the Managing Director of WACOT Limited, Mr. Naveen Chaurasia, said: “The renewal of this agreement is a strong statement of our long-term commitment to Edo State and to Nigeria’s agricultural transformation. Since 2017, we have demonstrated that a well-managed public-private partnership can revive moribund assets and deliver real value.” Speaking on behalf of the Edo State government, Commissioner, Ministry of Business, Trade and Investments, Omoh Anabor, added: “This agreement involving the Edo State Government, ESFCCL and WACOT Limited represents far more than a formal transaction. It is a strategic step towards positioning Edo State as a leading destination for investment and industrial growth. This partnership demonstrates our readiness to work with credible private sector partners to unlock economic opportunities, support farmers through improved access to agricultural inputs, strengthen food security, create jobs and enterprise opportunities across Auchi and the wider Edo State.”

title: Europe Has No Starlink Replacement as Ukraine Faces Satellite Disruptions
body:
Europe cannot replace Starlink anytime soon, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned Friday, as disruptions to Elon Musk’s satellite network raised concerns over Ukraine’s battlefield communications.
“Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine and unfortunately in the short term Europe can’t replace this capability,” Kallas told reporters ahead of an EU summit attended by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Ukraine relies on Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, for battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and interceptor drones used to shoot down Russian attack drones.
Starlink’s satellite network is unmatched in scale, while its business model and portable, affordable terminals give it a major advantage over competitors that rely on bulkier, more expensive equipment.
Kyiv reported restrictions on military Starlink connections this week, with Ukrainian officials reporting slower speeds on some terminals on Wednesday. Musk said any disruption was the responsibility of the US government , not his SpaceX company.
Kallas said the European Defence Agency had mapped the critical military capabilities Europe lacks and must develop.
“We need to fill these gaps as soon as possible,” she said.
Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs acknowledged that Europe was not yet equipped to provide a full alternative.
“Starlink is the key for Ukraine actually to fight or fight back,” he told reporters on Friday, according to AFP. Europe has some comparable capabilities, but not enough to meet Ukraine’s needs.
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten told AFP he had discussed the issue with French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday, focusing on how European countries could provide more satellite communications services in the near future.
The European Commission is negotiating Ukraine’s participation in GOVSATCOM , an EU program that pools satellite resources to provide secure communications for government users.
“We are currently in talks with Ukraine to fully associate Ukraine to GOVSATCOM,” Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said on Wednesday.
The system could give Kyiv another way to maintain secure communications during Russian attacks on infrastructure and disruptions to conventional networks. But Brussels has yet to confirm whether it can match Starlink’s capabilities for combat operations.
The EU could add commercial satellite services as early as 2027, potentially helping meet military needs, Regnier said. Its longer-term plan, the IRIS² constellation of more than 300 satellites, is expected to become fully operational in 2029.
Until then, Ukraine remains heavily reliant on Starlink – and Europe has no immediate replacement for a system critical to its war effort.
The European discussions have gained urgency after restrictions detected overnight on Oct. 13-14 disrupted Ukrainian drone operations .
Ukrainian defense ministry sources said units received no advance warning and reported connections dropping at different movement speeds, approximately 72 to 161 kilometers per hour (45 to 100 miles per hour).
The ministry contacted the US, SpaceX, and NATO partners while checking backup communications channels.
The disruption affected interceptor and medium-range strike drones, alongside reconnaissance, logistics, and communications relay missions.
The reported speed limits concern how fast a terminal is moving, rather than its internet download speed.
Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said on Wednesday evening that connectivity at speeds of up to 160 kilometers per hour (99 miles per hour) was being restored , while calling for Starshield’s speed restriction to be removed entirely.
That partial restoration does not resolve every operational requirement. Two Ukrainian officials told RFE/RL that connections had improved below the threshold, but restrictions continued to complicate interception of Russia’s jet-powered drones.
One Ukrainian source said operating speeds needed to reach at least 450 kilometers per hour (280 miles per hour).
President Volodymyr Zelensky has accused those responsible of deliberately restricting the service during Russian attacks , saying the disruption weakened Ukraine’s defenses and endangered civilians. Who authorized the restrictions remains disputed.
Musk said Starshield systems are controlled by the US government and that their operational limits are determined by the US military and ultimately the president. A senior White House official, however, told Axios that the Trump administration was not involved.
According to Reuters , Europe has no ready-made replacement that Ukrainian troops can immediately attach to their drones.
Eutelsat already provides connectivity in Ukraine through its low Earth orbit and geostationary networks.
But independent satellite consultant Christian Freiherr von der Ropp told Reuters that OneWeb faces capacity and performance constraints, while terminal cost, weight, size, and power consumption limit frontline suitability.
Switching would also require replacing thousands of terminals: Starlink equipment uses proprietary technology and cannot simply connect to OneWeb.
European political pressure to develop alternatives is growing. In a statement on Thursday, Oct. 15, Renew Europe President Valérie Hayer urged EU leaders to strengthen support for Ukraine and address dependence on American satellite services.
“Recent days have also shown the urgent need for a European alternative to Starlink,” she said.
Russia could deploy an alternative to Starlink across the front line within a year , Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert “Madyar” Brovdi warned in May.
Russia’s main project is Rassvet, developed by Russian company Bureau 1440. The company launched 16 spacecraft in March 2026, while six Rassvet satellites were in orbit at the time, according to Russian media outlet Kommersant.
Despite the limited constellation, Ukrainian defense outlet Militarnyi reported that the satellites’ regular passes over Ukraine could provide usable coverage for some frontline applications. However, Rassvet remains far behind Starlink in scale and established operational capability.
Russian troops have also relied on alternative equipment, including terminals referred to as “Gazprom.” In an intercepted conversation published by Kyiv Post in February, a Russian serviceman dismissed one such terminal as “ f**king shit .”
Starlink operates more than 7,800 satellites, while Russia is still building its network. Moscow’s ability to expand Rassvet and improve its terminals could nevertheless become a growing concern for Ukraine, particularly as both sides depend increasingly on satellite connectivity to control drones and coordinate battlefield operations.
Alisa is the Head of News and a correspondent at Kyiv Post, where she leads the newsroom’s coverage of breaking events and global developments. With over seven years of experience in TV journalism, Alisa has reported on international and Ukrainian politics, making complex stories easier to understand. Back in September 2022, Alisa joined the Kyiv Post team.

title: Kremlin calls external management of firms from unfriendly states continued trend
body:
MOSCOW, October 16. /TASS/. The introduction of external management for a number of companies from unfriendly countries that has taken place, can be described as a continuation of an existing trend, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing.
"This is a continuation of a trend. All those companies are from unfriendly countries, and their origin was one of the factors taken into account when the decision was made," he said.
Earlier, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree placing the Russian assets of flooring manufacturer Tarkett, as well as those of Ontex, the owner of the Helen Harper diaper brand, and three foreign packaging companies, under external management.

title: Russia pushes its drone war into Volyn Oblast on NATO border, cutting power to 370,000 as strikes creep toward EU
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia is pushing its drone war westward, into a Ukrainian region that borders NATO. Russian drones attacked Volyn Oblast through the night of 16 October, hitting civilian and critical infrastructure and leaving 370,000 subscribers without power, regional administration head Roman Romaniuk says . Volyn borders Poland, a NATO member, and Belarus, a Russian ally. Russia’s jet-powered drones keep flying farther west, and now the strikes reach deeper into the center and the EU-facing frontier too. Moscow launched more than 850 Shahed drones at Ukraine in about a day and a half, including a record roughly 360 on the central Kirovohrad Oblast, precisely as a speed cap on Starlink degraded the interceptor drones Ukraine’s air defense relies on. Moscow escalates its attacks after winning sanctions relief from the diesel deal of US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin and sensing pressure on Ukraine, exploiting the moment its defenses were artificially restricted. “Russia takes advantage of every such moment and must be held accountable for what it does,” Zelenskyy says, noting the skies had not been clear for a single hour. A night that turned deadly in the west In Volyn Oblast, the damage was concrete and lethal. Debris fell on a power line in the central Lutsk community, cutting electricity and disrupting water supply, and the city lost power entirely with public transport halted, Lutsk council secretary Andrii Razumovskyi says . The heaviest toll came in Manevychi, where a drone hit the private enterprise Agrofrukt LTD, killing one person and injuring eight. By 10:46 AM, the fire there was contained , and residents were asked to seal windows, doors, and vents due to the risk of an ammonia release from a damaged facility. A capital-to-border map of the same assault Throughout the day, Russia has struck Kyiv and its region, and the Dnipropetrovsk, Odesa, Rivne, Kharkiv and Donetsk regions, along with Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Poltava and Ivano-Frankivsk. By reaching western border regions at once, Russia is widening the pressure on civilians across the country and edging closer to the EU. Read also One Ukraine out-produced third of EU’s steel.
