title: Haley Stevens is everywhere — except on the trail for El-Sayed
body: Haley Stevens is highly visible in the wake of her Senate primary loss: Meeting with the Dalai Lama , crashing “ TMZ Live ” with her new fiancee, getting spoofed on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon. One place she hasn’t been spotted: alongside her former rival Abdul El-Sayed. Even though the representative quickly endorsed El-Sayed after their bruising Aug. 4 primary, she’s done little to help him since. That absence is becoming more conspicuous in the closing weeks of a crucial Senate contest, as some of her old supporters continue to vocally resist backing him. In an interview, Stevens said El-Sayed is building a “new coalition” in the race against GOP former Rep. Mike Rogers — and suggested it’s not her place to push some of her more skeptical supporters into joining it. When asked if she was encouraging her former donors to help El-Sayed, she said she believes her role this election is to “be part of the coordinated campaign, support where I can,” mentioning Michigan House races. When asked again if she would push donors to back him, she responded: “That’s Elissa’s thing,” referring to Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), who has been fundraising for El-Sayed. “I didn't win a Senate primary,” she continued. “It's not like a salty grapes deal or anything.” Stevens said she’d checked in with El-Sayed’s team, but hadn’t met with the candidate himself recently because she’d been traveling. “There's changing dynamics, and there's a new coalition that Abdul has built, and some people are a die-hard part of it, and some people are not. We’re seeing some constituent community pain coming out,” Stevens said, referencing resistance to El-Sayed among some Black and Jewish voters who backed her in the primary. “Rogers is working the Black community harder and more successfully than we have ever seen a Republican do or at least that I can remember — ever," Stevens said. “But we’re also seeing Abdul go up to the UP [Upper Peninsula] and we’re seeing him fill venues in rural Michigan and it’s very real in terms of this coalition he’s built,” she added. El-Sayed ran particularly strongly during the primary with young voters and in the state’s large Arab-American community, as well as in some rural, more populist parts of the state, and is working hard to expand that coalition in the general election. Stevens’ remarks come as some of her former backers and financial boosters continue to publicly withhold support from El-Sayed and in some cases openly embrace his Republican rival . The ruptures are most visible among the Jewish and Black communities that largely broke for Stevens, and point to enduring friction within Michigan Democrats’ traditional coalition after a bitter primary that she could be in a unique position to mend. Debbie Rosenman, the chair of Birmingham-Bloomfield Area Democratic Party Club in Stevens’ backyard and an El-Sayed supporter, said Stevens has been “absent” on the trail and said she was “very concerned” her coalition is not coalescing around El-Sayed. “I feel that that could change with more of her public support,” Rosenman said. El-Sayed’s campaign said the former rivals’ teams keep in close touch and noted several Stevens staffers joined the nominee’s team after the primary. “The Abdul campaign is grateful for Congresswoman Stevens’ immediate and sustained support,” El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner said in a statement. El-Sayed has worked to repair relationships with Black and Jewish leaders. He has endorsements from several of them and is campaigning with prominent Democrats from both communities, including former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris and Slotkin, who is Jewish. He has made more than two dozen visits to Black churches and participated in more than 100 events and meetings with Black leaders , according to his campaign. He has hired a liaison to the Jewish community, keeps in regular contact with Jewish leaders and has apologized for his controversial remark after a synagogue attack in West Bloomfield in the spring that “hurt people hurt people.” “I take very seriously that I'm going to represent a large community of Jewish Michiganders, and I want them to know that I'm committed to their safety and their well being, even if there are points in foreign policy on which we might disagree,” El-Sayed said in an interview. Not everyone has come around. David Kramer, Stevens’ primary campaign chair and a vice chair of the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus who introduced Stevens to her fiance , is now working with Nonnegotiable Michigan , a group of Jewish leaders who have pledged to withhold their support from El-Sayed unless he adjusts his approach to Israel. Kramer, a prominent Democratic fundraiser in the state who has also previously worked with Slotkin and Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, told POLITICO he’s not tapping his donor network for the general election and estimated he’s left upward of seven figures on the table that he could have raised to boost El-Sayed. Brian Hermelin, a normally Democratic donor who backed Stevens in the primary and leads the Jewish Federation of Detroit, co-hosted a fundraiser for Republican nominee Mike Rogers shortly after the primary that raised roughly $200,000. Rogers’ campaign has attempted to capitalize on those cracks by launching a “Democrats for Mike Rogers” group and making overtures to Jewish and Black voters. Bobby Schostak, a former Michigan GOP chair who is serving as Rogers’ finance chair, estimated the Republican’s campaign has brought in roughly $3 million to $4 million since the primary from “nontraditional Republican donors” across the country, including Democrats. “The Democratic Party is still divided,” said Democrat Mary Waters, a Black Detroit city councilor who’s met with both El-Sayed and Rogers but remains undecided. “People are still so torn about what it is that they want to do.” Joe Tate, a Black state representative from Detroit who supported Stevens, acknowledged there has been some lingering apprehension around El-Sayed. But he said Stevens’ endorsement of El-Sayed helped convince him to back the candidate and predicted Democratic voters would largely stand by their party, too. El-Sayed’s donor network may look different from Stevens’, but he’s still posted big numbers. He raised nearly $33 million from July through September, which included some raised before the Aug. 4 primary, compared to Rogers’ nearly $10 million, and has been outspending Rogers on the airwaves. Some of El-Sayed’s prominent surrogates have also taken steps to court apprehensive Democrats. Jewish leaders like former Rep. Andy Levin, a former synagogue president who Stevens defeated in a 2022 primary, are holding house parties with voters coordinated by the grassroots group Michigan Jews for Democracy. Slotkin has privately pressed senators and donors to boost El-Sayed’s bid. That includes hosting a fundraiser for El-Sayed in Washington, D.C., in late September with donors who she described as initially “skeptical” of the nominee. “I talked to them about why I thought it was important and how I don't agree with Abdul on everything … but we agree on the really important things, and that's putting a check and balance on this president,” Slotkin told POLITICO in a brief hallway interview on Capitol Hill the next day. “And they donated.”

title: Saab to build new flight control computer for Gripen
body: Saab has won an order worth 1.3 billion Swedish kronor, around £100 million, from the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration to develop a new generation flight control computer for Gripen, with deliveries planned during 2030, according to the company. The new computer will replace the version currently flying, and Saab said it has been designed to meet long-term requirements for availability, performance and security of supply. The work will be carried out in close cooperation with FMV, the Swedish procurement agency. Marcus Wandt, head of Saab’s business area Aeronautics, said: “We look forward to continuing our close collaboration with FMV. The new flight control computer will contribute to Gripen’s capability and performance for decades to come.” Saab described the flight control computer as a central component in Gripen’s flight control system, contributing to safe and precise manoeuvring of the aircraft. That understates it. Gripen is aerodynamically unstable by design, a configuration chosen to make it more agile, and the aircraft is only controllable because the flight control system makes continuous corrections faster than a pilot could. A flight control computer designed in the 1990s runs on processors and components that stopped being made years ago, and keeping a fleet airworthy eventually means buying obsolete parts from brokers or redesigning the box. Sweden is choosing to redesign it, and specifying a new one now lets the design use components the country can be confident of sourcing through the 2050s, which is how long Gripen E is expected to serve. The order follows a pattern set earlier this month, when Saab reached an agreement with GKN Aerospace covering the Gripen engine, the RM16 that GKN’s Swedish operation builds from the General Electric F414 under licence. Taken with this contract, Sweden is working methodically through the parts of Gripen that depend on foreign supply chains and bringing what it can under domestic control. Gripen E has had a strong run commercially over the past few years. Brazil is building the type under licence, Thailand has ordered it, Peru signed for a batch last year, and Ukraine and Sweden have signed a letter of intent covering a potential order of up to a hundred or more aircraft. The British connection runs through GKN Aerospace, headquartered in the United Kingdom, whose Trollhättan site in Sweden produces the Gripen engine, and through Saab’s growing British footprint. The post Saab to build new flight control computer for Gripen first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Google Boosts News, Link Visibility In AI Mode
body: Google announced Thursday it will start displaying links to websites and articles more prominently and higher up in search results powered by artificial intelligence (AI), as brands and news publishers warn of a sharp decline in their traffic. The Alphabet subsidiary began integrating more AI features in its search results over two years ago. In May 2024, it launched AI Overviews, where Google generates summarised answers to search queries, rather than only showing links as it historically did. Then in March 2025, Google added AI Mode, which opens in a separate window and provides a more comprehensive answer and more links than AI Overviews. Now, contextual links will be featured “more frequently” and higher up in AI-generated search content. Google will also expand worldwide its link “carousel”, which are cards displayed directly below AI Overviews that show headlines with images for relevant articles. The algorithm will prioritise articles from sites a user has previously identified as “preferred sources”, and it will also be able to pull in content from relevant social media posts and other forums. Google will also make links displayed at the end of AI-generated summaries “more engaging and prominent” for users who want to “dig deeper”. During its second-quarter 2025 results, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said that AI Overviews had more than two billion monthly users in over 200 countries. Several studies have shown that replacing traditional search with AI summaries significantly reduces the rate at which users open the suggested links. According to a report by consultancy Chartbeat, news website publishers saw a 40 per cent drop in traffic coming from Google between July 2025 and July 2026. In August, Apig, a group representing daily newspapers in France, alerted the Competition Authority that AI summaries were in breach of agreements reached with news publishers in 2022. AFP The post Google Boosts News, Link Visibility In AI Mode appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Gunmen abduct Catholic priest in Benue
body: A Catholic priest, Reverend Father John Inalegwu Otache, has been reportedly kidnapped by gunmen along the Otobi Amejo-Ajegbe road in Ohimini Local Government Area of Benue State. Otache, the Parish Priest of St. Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume, was said to have been abducted on Tuesday while returning from Otukpo. The Catholic Diocese of Otukpo confirmed the abduction in a statement issued on Friday and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor, Reverend Father Joseph Aboyi Itodo. The statement said the Bishop of the diocese, Most Rev. Michael Ekwoyi Apochi, was deeply pained by the incident and called on Christians and people of goodwill to pray for the priest’s safe and speedy release. Soldiers feared killed repelling terrorists in Borno Man sentenced to death in Kogi for killing friend It also stated that efforts were being intensified to secure the priest’s release as the abduction marks the second time a priest serving at St. Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume, was kidnapped. Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) for Benue command, DSP Peter Aondongu, however, said the command was investigating the reported abduction. “I dont have that report yet. They said he was coming from Ohimini and going to Otukpo. He is a Catholic priest, a Reverend Father. They said it happened on Tuesday. “Yes, They confirmed it. I can confirm that it happened on Tuesday. He has not been rescued yet. Our teams are still making efforts to rescue him,” Aondongu said.

title: Population of rare Hainan gibbons gradually increasing — newspaper
body:
HAIKOU /China/, October 16. /TASS/. The small population of rare gibbons in the southern Chinese province of Hainan is gradually increasing, Hainan Ribao reported.
According to the newspaper, there are now 44 gibbons on the island, comprising seven groups, compared to 35 five years ago. The local ecosystem continues to recover and thrive. Since the establishment of the Hainan Rainforest National Park on October 12, 2021, scientists have discovered 91 new species of wild flora and fauna within its boundaries.
The article pointed out that the International Union for Conservation of Nature has recognized Hainan’s gibbon conservation model as an exemplary model for protecting rare species. Thus, the global community has adopted the experience of China’s southernmost province to restore biodiversity in other regions of the world.
Hainan Ribao noted that the abovementioned forest park effectively protects more than 95% of the territory where trees have virtually remained untouched by human activity, which comprises 55% of the island’s natural forest. The Chinese authorities provide round-the-clock monitoring and control of this area, including through the use of satellite data. According to official statistics, the Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) of this region increased by nearly 4.4 billion yuan, or about $655 million, from 2019 to 2024.
The newspaper emphasized that a 466-kilometer tourist route encircles the forest park. It connects nine provincial administrative units and boosts revenue for local companies operating in the culture and tourism sectors.
Hainan gibbons inhabit the central and southern parts of the island. They prefer to live in the tree canopy about ten meters high, making it difficult to monitor these primates that do not reproduce well in captivity. These mammals feed on both plant matter and small animals. In China, they are under the vigilant protection of the state.

title: 2027: CSO Coalition Cautions Enugu Guber Candidates, Demands Issue-Based Campaigns
body: Kasim Sumaina in Abuja The Coalition of Civil Society Groups for Good Governance (CCSGG) Thursday cautioned governorship candidates in Enugu State against inflammatory politics and smear campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging them to present verifiable development agendas to the electorate. The coalition, which said it comprises over 52 civil society organisations committed to promoting accountability and good governance, stated this at a world press conference themed: “Enugu State and the Politics of 2027: Putting the Record Straight.” in Abuja Addressing journalists on behalf of coalition, Comrade Okpanachi Jacob, said the group intervention became necessary following the controversy surrounding the incident at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu, on October 10, 2026, involving supporters of the National Democratic Congress (NDC). He noted that the group investigated the matter after statements attributed to the NDC governorship candidate, Sir Christian Chinyeaka Ohaa, and others, which linked the Enugu State Government to the incident. The coalition described the suggestion that a political rally was to be held at an international airport as deeply concerning and inconsistent with established standards for aviation security. It noted that according to accounts released by the Enugu State Government and the Enugu State Police Command, the NDC had publicised a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the airport, was advised to secure approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), but allegedly proceeded without such approval, leading to a confrontation when security personnel restricted access. The coalition therefore posed five questions to the NDC to answer in public interest, stating: “Did the party obtain formal approval from the appropriate federal airport authorities for the gathering? If approval was obtained, will the party publish it for public scrutiny? What instructions were given to party members concerning access to the airport? Why was a large political gathering planned for a sensitive federal facility? What credible evidence directly connects Governor Peter Mbah or any identified state official to the confrontation? “Freedom of association and peaceful assembly are constitutional democratic rights. However, those rights must be exercised lawfully and responsibly. Political enthusiasm does not override aviation security,” the coalition said. It urged politicians to desist from disseminating misleading information, stressing that airports are sensitive federal facilities whose security and operations must not be compromised by partisan activities. The coalition said Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah is not above criticism, noting that citizens, opposition parties and journalists have the right to question his policies, scrutinise public expenditure and demand transparency. However, it said criticism must be based on facts and not on demonisation or allegations unsupported by evidence. “Accusation without evidence is not accountability. It is political blackmail capable of inflaming passions, misleading the public and undermining the peace and security of Enugu State,” the group said. The group stressed that opposition status does not confer immunity from regulations governing airports, political gatherings and public order. Adding: “It said all political parties must notify appropriate authorities of major public activities, comply with lawful security requirements and ensure members do not engage in violence or destruction of public property. It also called on security agencies to remain professional, impartial and proportionate, ensuring a level playing field for all parties while respecting citizens’ rights to peaceful assembly. The coalition warned against importing thugs, arming supporters, spreading unfounded security alarms or manufacturing confrontations for propaganda, urging security agencies to investigate reports of attempts to recruit armed persons ahead of 2027.

title: UK Sends Ukraine More Storm Shadow Missiles as US Presses Kyiv to Halt Strikes
body:
Britain is supplying Ukraine with additional Storm Shadow cruise missiles to counter Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure before winter, as London backs Kyiv’s ability to strike targets inside Russia despite US pressure to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed replenishing the missile stocks during their meeting in London on Wednesday, Oct. 14.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
London considers strikes on Russian facilities used to launch attacks against Ukrainian civilians and infrastructure a defensive measure, the sources said.
They pointed to Russia’s increased production of jet-powered drones and missiles, saying Ukraine needed the means to counter the growing threat.
The British position contrasts with that of US President Donald Trump’s administration, which has demanded that Ukraine stop drone attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Ukraine resumed those attacks on Thursday, Oct. 15, in response to continuing Russian strikes on its energy infrastructure.
Trump called Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries a “disgrace” and accused Kyiv of driving up global energy prices, even as Moscow continued attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
“ Well, I think that’s a disgrace ,” Trump told Newsmax in an interview published on Thursday, when asked about Ukraine’s decision to resume attacks on Russian refineries.
However, energy analysts say Trump’s deal to resume Russian diesel exports is unlikely to significantly lower fuel prices, as the main driver of the global price surge has been the US-Israel war with Iran, which has disrupted oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
According to Bloomberg’s sources, London does not believe Kyiv should stop striking Russia while Moscow continues attacking Ukraine.
The distinction concerns both the targets and the broader question of Ukraine’s right to respond: the reported British position supports attacks on facilities enabling Russian strikes, while Washington has specifically pressed Kyiv to spare refineries.
Britain began supplying Storm Shadow missiles to Ukraine in 2023. Their use was initially restricted to targets within Ukraine, including Russian-occupied territory. Ukrainian forces first used them against military targets inside Russia in late 2024.
Manufactured by MBDA , Storm Shadow is an air-launched cruise missile designed to strike high-value targets. It flies at low altitude to reduce detection, and the manufacturer lists its range as more than 250 kilometers, or about 155 miles.
Bloomberg also reported that Burnham announced plans in August to share technical information and designs for long-range missiles to support assembly in Ukraine, as establishing that production capability would take time.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Ukrainian drone operators use Alyoshki as training ground — ombudsman
body:
GENICHESK, October 16. /TASS/. The Ukrainian armed forces’ unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operators in Kherson are testing their skills by carrying out strikes against civilians in Alyoshki, Sergey Georgiev, the regional human rights commissioner, told TASS.
"I have information from our military personnel and intelligence sources that they have indeed been taking, and continue to take periodically, exams, operating from Kherson, practicing on civilians in high-rise buildings – how to fly into building entrances and how to operate in densely-packed areas," he said.
On September 21, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the humanitarian situation in Alyoshki as critical, saying that shelling and drone attacks by Kiev had made it impossible to deliver food and medicine to the city. On October 9, the presidents of Russia and the United States held a telephone conversation. During his conversation with Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin reported that regarding concerns about the humanitarian situation in Alyoshki, in the Kherson Region, it was agreed that Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova would remain in regular contact with Melania Trump’s staff.

title: You don't need psychic powers to see Obama is an 'antisemitism superspreader' - opinion
body: Barack Obama was never a friend of Israel. Some people were foolish enough to believe otherwise, but I was convinced from day one. And it hardly required psychic powers to see the signs. Red flags were there throughout his presidency, but this week the mask of this Nobel Peace Prize laureate finally slipped, and in the most shocking way.According to Irish media, Obama - speaking about the Israel-Palestinian conflict at an event in Belfast - said it was “undeniable” that Jews who settled in Palestine to escape persecution “took land off people and they were excessive. And those people understandably said, 'This is injustice and I want my land back.'”Read those words again, and consider who spoke them. The problem is not merely that Obama said it. It is that countless people will believe it precisely because Obama said it.This was not some 5th grader history student speaking. This was a two-term president of the United States, a man who remains one of the most influential figures on the planet, with hundreds of millions of social media followers.When Obama speaks, people listen. Millions of them. Including young, impressionable people who may know little about Jewish history and the history of this land.Obama: An 'antisemitism superspreader'In one fell swoop, Obama, either knowingly or through astonishing ignorance, peddled one of the most pernicious myths about Jews and Zionism - a myth which perhaps more than any other has been responsible for a century of conflict, tens of thousands of Jews killed, and many more times that of Arabs. All because of this false claim that the Jews stole the land.If this is what Obama truly believes, then, in my view, he is an antisemitism superspreader.Well, Barack Hussein Obama, let me put you right.It is not “undeniable” that Jews “took land off people”. It is, in fact, very deniable, because it is quite simply untrue. You do not need to be a professor of Middle Eastern history to understand that the Jewish people have maintained a connection with the Land of Israel for more than 3,000 years. We are not strangers who have appeared here out of nowhere. Jews who more recently settled in waves of aliyah did not steal the land, as you inferred, but bought it legally from Arabs, even paying exorbitant prices. Don't take my word for it - you can check for yourself in Ottoman and British documents.And what exactly was it “excessive” that, according to you, the Jews did? Flee from gas chambers? Were my own parents “excessive” when they escaped to Palestine in 1932 because Hitler was round the corner? They bought their own home, by the way.A wolf in sheep's clothingAnd it is not just these latest remarks that should outrage every Jew. I have long believed that Obama felt a deep disdain for Israel. He always was, to my mind, a wolf in sheep's clothing.His last major act as president was to throw Israel under the bus when he let a resolution condemning Israel pass at the UN. Nor has Israel forgotten that he was responsible for the disastrous nuclear agreement with Iran, a country which wants to destroy ours. Thankfully President Trump tore it up.I warned about Barack Obama for years. He is not merely a disgrace in my eyes. He is dangerous. And this week, I believe he proved exactly why.Uri Geller is one of the world's most investigated proclaimed psychics and has been the source of fierce controversy for decades. He was one of Israel's first international celebrities and is now the owner of the Uri Geller Museum in Old Jaffa. Learn more at www.urigellermuseum.com. Follow him on X at @theurigeller. His opinions are his own.

title: Rivers: DPO removed over alleged renovation of police station by cultists
body: The Rivers State Police Command has suspended the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in charge of Abuloma Division and the DPO overseeing a police outpost in the area of their duties following allegations that suspected cultists renovated the police facility. In a statement on Friday, Police spokesperson in Rivers State, ASP Agabe Blessing Kaborlo, announced the removal of the DPO, saying the action is based on the trending social media report and a video in circulation alleging that suspected vikings cult group members were allowed to renovate the police facility. Though the identities of the affected officers were not disclosed, the police spokesperson said they were queried and relieved of their duties, pending an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. She also stated that the police investigation would determine the identities and backgrounds of the individuals or groups that financed or facilitated the renovation, the officers who authorised or approved the project, and whether due procedures were followed. ‘Why Tinubu deserves second term’ Man sentenced to death in Kogi for killing friend Daily Trust gathered that the development followed a video shared by a popular anti-cultism social media platform, Naija Confra, purportedly showing suspected Vikings cult members chanting their slogans in front of the Abuloma Police Outpost and taking photographs with police officers inside the facility on Thursday. The incident reportedly occurred on October 15, a date associated with the annual anniversary celebration of the Vikings confraternity. Reacting to the development, the command condemned any action or association capable of compromising the integrity, discipline and professional standards of the Nigeria Police Force or conferring legitimacy on suspected cult groups and other unlawful organisations. It maintained that police facilities were public institutions established to protect citizens and enforce the law, stressing that they must not become platforms for criminal groups to seek public recognition or influence. The statement said, “The Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Adepoju, had ordered a full investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and verify the allegations. “According to the command, the investigation will determine the identities and backgrounds of the individuals or groups that financed or facilitated the renovation, the officers who authorised or approved the project, and whether due procedures were followed. “It will also establish whether any police personnel breached professional standards, compromised the integrity of the Force or were involved in the incident. “The command, however, acknowledged that legitimate community support for the improvement of police facilities was permissible under Section 26(1)(d) of the Nigeria Police Act, 2020, which provides for gifts and contributions to the Police General Fund. “But such assistance must not compromise police independence, professional standards or security, the investigation would determine whether the necessary approvals were obtained and appropriate checks conducted on those who financed or facilitated the renovation. “The Command will not condone unprofessional conduct, compromise or any form of improper association with criminal elements by any police officer. All personnel are expected to uphold the highest standards of discipline, integrity and accountability in the discharge of their duties. “The Command remains committed to professionalism, transparency, the protection of lives and property, and the fight against cultism and organised crime. Appropriate disciplinary and legal action will be taken against anyone found culpable, in line with the outcome of the investigation and extant laws. “Members of the public are urged to remain calm and continue to support the Police with credible and timely information to enhance security across Rivers State.”

title: UNDP urges stronger early warning to prevent conflict
body: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has called for stronger early warning and response mechanisms to identify harmful narratives and prevent them from escalating into conflict in South Sudan. Dr. Ligane Massamba Sene, UNDP Senior Economic Governance Advisor, made the remarks on Tuesday during a three-day workshop in Juba to establish a national multi-agency coordination platform to address hate speech and disinformation. “Harmful narratives can provide warning signs of rising tensions. When they signal an organized area and address it carefully, they create an opportunity for timely engagement before tensions escalate,” he said. “Prevention therefore requires attention to the information being circulated and to prevent these mistrusts and divisions that allow harmful narratives to gain traction.” He said hate speech and disinformation were closely linked to peacebuilding challenges in South Sudan, where narratives promoting exclusion and spreading false information could weaken reconciliation efforts and increase tensions between communities. The UNDP official stressed that no single institution could effectively address the challenge, calling for cooperation among government institutions, civil society organizations, media professionals, community and religious leaders, women’s and youth organizations, and relevant security and justice actors. “Its value relies on its ability to translate information into practical action, identifying emerging risks, verifying information, agreeing on appropriate responses and follow-up on their effectiveness,” he said. Massamba said possible responses could include credible public communication, fact-checking, community dialogue, mediation and referrals to relevant institutions when harmful narratives are linked to violence. He also emphasized the importance of strengthening national ownership and institutional capacity to ensure that prevention efforts respond to South Sudan’s local realities. The UNDP official called for stronger connections between the proposed national platform and existing regional early warning mechanisms to improve information sharing and responses to threats that cross national borders. He further urged stakeholders to ensure that women, young people and marginalized communities participate meaningfully in shaping the platform’s priorities and responses. Their involvement, he said, could help identify risks that might otherwise be overlooked and ensure that interventions reflect the experiences of affected communities. According to Massamba, the success of the initiative would depend on sustained cooperation, timely responses, stronger institutional capacity and transparency with the communities being served. For his party, Riek Kok, Director General for Multilateral Affairs at the foreign ministry, called for a coordinated national effort to combat hate speech and disinformation, saying the responsibility should not be left to individual institutions. “Combating hate speech is not the responsibility of one person or a national institution alone, but it is our responsibility as a nation,” he said. He warned that false information and harmful narratives could incite hostility, deepen social divisions and undermine public confidence in government institutions. “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation recognizes that countering hate speech and disinformation is not solely a domestic responsibility,” he stated. “It also requires international cooperation, constructive engagement and the exchange of best practices.” The post UNDP urges stronger early warning to prevent conflict appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Tesla's new Roadster makes a flying debut, hitting 60 MPH in under a second
body:
Tesla unveiled its long-anticipated Roadster on Thursday during a dramatic event in which the vehicle used compressed-air thrusters to fly off a ramp and perform a midair maneuver.
Tesla unveiled its long-anticipated Roadster on Thursday during a dramatic event in which the vehicle used compressed-air thrusters to fly off a ramp and perform a midair maneuver.
The vehicle was seen flying, performing a midair flip and accelerating from zero to 60 mph in under a second.
"Turns out the future does have flying cars," Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas.
Vice President of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy added, "Flying cars are real."
ELON MUSK CALLS WAYMO CARS 'PET DESTROYERS' AS ROBOTAXI RIVALS CLASH OVER SAFETY
Tesla officially unveiled its redesigned, next-generation Roadster on Oct. 15, 2026, during a dramatic livestreamed event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas. (Tesla/X)
The jaw-dropping showcase featured the new Roadster accelerating up a massive curved ramp and using a fan-based suction system to remain attached until it was completely upside down before using integrated cold-gas thrusters developed in collaboration with SpaceX to launch off the ramp, flip in midair and land safely back on the ground.
In another demonstration, the Roadster launched over a lineup of cars and a semi-truck, performing a midair flip before landing safely on the other side.
Musk said certain versions of the Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph in less than one second and reach a top speed of more than 230 mph. During the event, Tesla demonstrated a Roadster accelerating to 60 mph in under a second.

Nearly a decade after the Roadster's initial 2017 concept debut, the vehicle left audiences in awe with the gravity-defying demonstration that deployed SpaceX’s rocket technology.
"Today, Roadster presents a new moment in history – the best of the last human-driven cars," Tesla wrote on X.
Tesla executives announced at Thursday's event that production would begin in 2028.

title: Nigerians Can Grow Capital, Assets Through Cooperatives, Says Adesope
body: Nigerians can grow their capital, assets and income through cooperative societies, the newly elected President of The Bodija (Ibadan) Unique Cooperative Investment & Credit Society, Mr Olufemi Adesope, has said. Adesope urged managers of cooperative societies to encourage members to save and invest more consistently while developing attractive investment products and expanding their investment portfolios to ensure continuous growth in capital, assets, income and members’ return on investment. He made the call while assuming office for the 2026/2027 Cooperative Year at the society’s ninth Annual General Meeting held at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan. Describing his new responsibility as a call to duty, Adesope said, “We must build on our successes, learn from our experiences and deliberately position Unique Cooperative Society for greater heights.” Speaking on the theme of the AGM, ‘Building Bridges, Empowering Members: Cooperatives in the Digital Age,’ he called for a shift from dependence on traditional cooperative activities to identifying viable businesses, property investments, community projects and other sustainable income-generating opportunities. “The Society should continuously ask: ‘What new opportunities can create additional value for our members?’” he said. Adesope also stressed the need to build relationships with credible financial institutions, professional organisations, businesses, technology companies, other cooperatives and development institutions. He called for continuous training of members and leaders in financial literacy, investment, entrepreneurship, leadership and digital skills. On the need to adapt to developments in the financial world, the new president advocated the digitalisation and automation of the society’s operations. He said this should cover member registration, savings, loans, investment monitoring, communication, reporting and performance tracking. “Technology should make the Society faster, more transparent, accessible and efficient,” he said. Adesope, while commending the Board of Trustees, including the society’s foundation president and past president, Mr Olusegun Sanni and Mr Gbolahan Arogundade, respectively, for their guidance, wisdom and continuing support, said the new leadership would maintain the highest standards of transparency, prudent financial management, risk control and accountability. He also called for measurable annual targets for membership, savings, investments, income, assets and member benefits, with regular performance reviews to ensure progress. “ Our goal must not merely be to preserve what we have built, but to continuously grow, improve and create greater value for every member,” he said. Also speaking at the AGM, the keynote speaker, Professor Sulaiman Adesina Yusuf of the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Ibadan, advised people seeking steady financial growth to join cooperative and credit societies and pool resources with others. Yusuf, a professor of agricultural economics, urged members to participate regularly in the growth process and allow their collective investments to grow over time. Speaking on the theme, ‘Building Bridges, Empowering Members: Cooperatives in the Digital Age,’ he challenged cooperative leaders to avoid the pitfalls of the past by embracing digital transformation to encourage more people to join their societies. However, he cautioned that the human element of cooperative societies must not be overlooked in the drive towards digitalisation. “Let us be honest with each other: a digital notice is not the same thing as meaningful participation. An app cannot manufacture trust,” he said. Yusuf explained that technology could strengthen transparency and accountability by enabling members to access their balances, decisions and records. “What it can do, if we build it honestly, is make trust visible: a balance a member can check, a decision a member can read, a record a member can request. “Technology can support accountability. It cannot take responsibility for it. That responsibility still belongs to us, the leadership and the membership of this cooperative.”

title: Ghana’s crude oil production rebounds by 30% after five years of decline
body: Minister of Energy and Green Transition, John Abdulai Jinapor, says Ghana’s crude oil production has risen by about 30 per cent, after five years of declining output. Speaking at African Energy Week 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa, Mr Jinapor credited the recovery to renewed development activities following a US$2 billion memorandum of understanding signed in 2025 with Kosmos Energy, a partner in the Jubilee oilfield. The Jubilee and Tweneboa-Enyenra-Ntomme (TEN) field agreement includes licence extensions to 2040. It is designed to stimulate further investment, increase oil production and improve the supply of affordable natural gas for domestic electricity generation. The revised development plan for the Jubilee field will see up to 20 further wells drilled. Mr Jinapor said the agreement had moved from commitment to implementation, with the government approving the revised development plan and work commencing. He noted that the production increase represented a significant turnaround after years of sustained decline. Recent operational updates from Kosmos Energy point to another drilling campaign (up to 10 wells) planned for the Jubilee partnership in 2027-2028, with the campaign due to start in mid-2027. The company reported average gross production of approximately 72,000 barrels of oil per day from the Jubilee field in the second quarter of 2026. Two additional wells, J76 and J77, came on stream in June and July, respectively. Kosmos Energy has also maintained a group capital expenditure budget of US$350 million for 2026. Beyond crude oil production, the agreement is intended to bolster Ghana’s domestic gas supply and advance the country’s wider energy security agenda. Speaking alongside Mr Jinapor, Kosmos Energy Chief Executive Officer Andy Inglis said extending the licences gave the company the long-term certainty needed to commit further investment, particularly in technology and gas development. Mr Inglis explained that the partnership also emphasised supplying affordable natural gas to Ghana, noting that energy security must be accompanied by affordability for consumers and businesses. Mr Jinapor said the Jubilee agreement could serve as a model for others in the upstream petroleum sector to follow in attracting investment. He stated the government was actively working to build investor confidence through a series of mutually beneficial agreements and reforms designed to make the sector more competitive. The Minister said Ghana already has agreements in place with Chevron and is engaging with Shell and CNOOC, explaining that the government looks forward to increased investment as a result of these engagements. He also mentioned that reforms to the country’s petroleum fiscal regime were in the pipeline to improve the investment climate. The proposed reforms had the blessing of both the Energy and Finance Ministers and were on track to go to Cabinet and then to Parliament. Mr Jinapor also confirmed that talks with Petrobras had progressed, with both parties considering finalising an agreement. He added that the government was working towards an agreement with Chevron, subject to the necessary parliamentary approval. The government’s renewed engagement with existing and prospective operators is part of a wider effort to reverse the slide in production, attract fresh capital, and further cement Ghana’s position as an investment destination in the upstream petroleum sector.

title: Sanctions working: FM Sybiha urges allies to maintain pressure on Russia
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said this in an interview with Ukrinform .
“It is also important not to pause sanctions policy: rather than waiting for new packages to be adopted, sanctions should be imposed continuously, in a targeted, focused and sector-specific manner, because this is producing results. Whatever Russia may say, sanctions are working, and we know that. They will gradually have a critical impact on the Russian economy. Even if the Russians circumvent sanctions, even if they adapt, this still hurts any economy – all the more so the economy of a country waging such aggression,” the Foreign Minister stressed.
According to Sybiha, Ukraine is proposing tougher restrictions on Russia’s “shadow fleet,” including a complete ban on maritime services and sanctions against the captains of such vessels.
“This is also a very sensitive issue. We know that many captains refuse to work on shadow fleet tankers because doing so poses a serious reputational risk. We will continue working in this area,” Ukraine’s top diplomat said.
Kyiv is also calling for a ban on the transit of Russian grain and other agricultural products through Europe, including Baltic ports, as well as further restrictions on Russian banks’ access to the SWIFT system.
“Russia still uses SWIFT, and Russian banks need to be disconnected from the system to the greatest extent possible. It is important to keep up the pressure on Russia to ensure that these sanctions have a truly shocking and devastating effect. There is still room to do more,” Sybiha said.
He stressed that sanctions pressure must raise the cost of Russia’s continued aggression. According to Ukrainian estimates, the war costs Russia about $1 billion a day.
“Putin understands only strength. To seriously force him to negotiate, pressure is needed, and the cost of continued military action must be raised,” the minister said, citing sanctions, the use of frozen Russian assets, international isolation and restrictions on access to technology as tools of such pressure.
Sybiha recalled that an EU sanctions package covering around 1,600 individuals and legal entities was adopted at a meeting of EU Foreign Ministers in Luxembourg. He said particular attention was paid to Russia’s defense industry and efforts to counter sanctions evasion.
The Ukrainian Foreign Minister also criticized the decision to remove Russian oligarchs Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from the EU sanctions list. Ukraine, he said, will seek to have both men reinstated and is proposing sanctions against more than ten other Russian oligarchs linked to Russia’s military-industrial complex and Putin’s inner circle.
Sybiha added that the United Kingdom had assured Ukraine it intended to maintain sanctions against Usmanov and Fridman. He emphasized that Kyiv would continue working with its partners to strengthen and expand restrictions against Russia.
As Ukrinform reported, the Council of the EU adopted additional restrictive measures against 1,569 individuals and entities linked to Russia’s military-industrial complex.

title: Britain too slow to blame Russia for attacks
body: Britain is applying a criminal standard of proof before attributing sabotage and arson to Russia when a civil one would do, and the delay is leaving companies supplying Ukraine without the warning they need, a Labour MP has told the UK Defence Journal. Graeme Downie, the member for Dunfermline and Dollar and author of The Putin Tax report, was asked why Estonia blamed Russia within days for an arson attack on a drone manufacturer last month while British investigations into comparable incidents run for far longer. “We’ve seen other NATO countries like Estonia blaming Russia and attributing blame within days without the need to publish all of the raw intelligence,” he said. “I honestly don’t know why the UK is so much slower. We must be so much quicker in attributing this stuff and not wait for it to be perfect. Wait till you’re pretty sure.” His proposed fix is a change in the standard of proof that gets applied to this kind of incident. “Rather than apply the criminal bar of beyond reasonable doubt, you probably apply a civil legal bar of overwhelming evidence, and on the balance of probabilities, that’s how I would prefer to see it,” he said. “And we seem to apply the criminal level, and I just don’t think that’s necessarily appropriate when you’re talking about this kind of stuff, because it delays it.” He argued that the usual reason for caution does not apply when the suspects are beyond reach. “Let’s be honest, much like we saw in Salisbury, we ain’t ever getting any of these Russian people responsible into court. So I don’t think we need to worry as much about prejudicing inquiries.” Downie accepted that cyber attribution is harder than attributing a fire. “The UK on cyber attacks, it genuinely is really hard to track that stuff and find out where it originated and who did it and everything else. So it is harder, but I think we’ve got to do much better.” He described the government’s attribution of last month’s incident at RAF Fairford to Iran as a step in the right direction, with a caveat about why it happened when it did. “I think the UK government move this week with the Iranian activity at RAF Fairford is the beginnings of that,” he said, “although how much of that was because Donald Trump kind of tipped the hand and left them with little choice, but nonetheless that speedier attribution.” The practical cost of slow attribution falls on businesses. Asked whether British companies supplying Ukraine should be worried after the arson attack on a Leyton warehouse linked to Ukrainian aid, he drew a distinction. “I think it’s not they should be worried, but they should be aware,” he said. “More publication of that attack, more publicising of that attack and what it was, would have signalled to those companies that are helping supply Ukraine that they need to get protection. I don’t know if they get any protection advice. I suspect they don’t. If they’re supporting Ukraine, I suspect they don’t get that kind of advice or information unless they’re fulfilling a government piece of work, and then they’ll have different rules. But no, I don’t think they do get the protection that they need, or the advice that they need in information.” On subsea infrastructure, which the report covers alongside Russian submarine activity around British cables, he was unequivocal. “The threat to subsea infrastructure is entirely real. We’ve seen that there was the sabotage rehearsal near Svalbard. That infrastructure threat is very real.” He said he had raised it repeatedly through the Energy Security and Net Zero Committee, and cited how another NATO member has responded. “In Romania they’ve changed their rules of engagement to allow them to protect the Neptun gas facility, and they actually have intercepted a Russian marine drone in that area over the last couple of months. So the threat to subsea infrastructure, both energy and those internet cables, is massive. Even if they’re down for just a few minutes, the cost to the UK economy would be massive. There would be the harm to confidence if those networks don’t come back up very quickly.” The Leyton warehouse fire in March 2024 destroyed a unit connected to a business sending aid and equipment to Ukraine. Men were later convicted over the attack, which prosecutors told the Old Bailey had been organised on behalf of the Wagner group. Britain attributed the September incident at RAF Fairford to direction by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps earlier this month. The Putin Tax puts the cost of Russian hostile activity to the British economy at between £2 billion and £2.5 billion and makes four recommendations, among them that the Ministry of Defence begin costing physical attacks. The post Britain too slow to blame Russia for attacks first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Yemen government will remain in Aden despite Houthi attack, says official
body: Yemen 's southern port city of Aden will remain the centre of government operations despite a deadly Houthi attack on the city's presidential palace , an official told The National on Friday. Marwan Ali Noman, political adviser to Yemen's Foreign Minister Afrah Al Zouba, said the Iran-backed Houthi rebels will not succeed in disrupting public life or undermining state authority as the government pushes ahead with a military and political campaign against them. Mr Al Noman said the government will continue to function from Aden despite security pressures and repeated Houthi attempts to destabilise areas under its control. At least five security personnel were killed and 16 others injured when Houthi missiles struck the presidential palace in Aden on Thursday, Yemen's Health Ministry said. It was the first time the Houthis had targeted Al Maashiq Palace, the seat of the Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government, since fighting in Yemen resumed last month after a four-year lull. “The government condemns in the strongest terms possible this terrorist attack, and reaffirms that such acts of violence and intimidation will not deter it from fulfilling its constitutional responsibilities, protecting its citizens and safeguarding state institutions,” Mr Al Noman said. The government instructed military and security authorities to take the necessary measures to “protect state institutions, confront terrorist threats and respond appropriately to the sources of those threats” following the attack. Mr Al Noman said the government remains committed to advancing Operation Dawn of Yemen, a campaign launched this month to regain control of the entire country, including the capital Sanaa that the rebels seized in 2014, and to restore state institutions. Government forces backed by the Saudi-led coalition have partially reversed Houthi advances along the Red Sea coast in south-west Yemen. The rebels have imposed a siege on the city of Taiz , creating severe shortages of food, fuel and other essentials. The Houthis have also launched repeated missile and drone attacks on airports and oil sites in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, killing 19 people and injuring hundreds. Most of the casualties were from a strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on October 10. On Friday, the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's government intercepted and destroyed a drone launched towards Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said. On Thursday, Syria's Foreign Minister Asaad Al Shibani visited Riyadh and held talks with Saudi officials, following a visit by President Ahmad Al Shara earlier in the month. They discussed “bilateral relations and regional developments”, the Saudi state news agency reported. Mr Al Shara's visit led to reports that Riyadh had asked Damascus to send troops to support the kingdom against the Houthis in Yemen, a claim Syria strongly denied.

title: Nzema East launches Responsible Cooperative Mining Programme to tackle environmental destruction
body: The government has launched the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme in the Nzema East Municipality of the Western Region to promote safer, more organised, and environmentally responsible small-scale mining. The programme will be implemented in Akangoo, Axim-Agona and Adelekezo, where it is expected to strengthen mining cooperatives, improve compliance with mining regulations and protect water bodies, farmlands and vegetation from the effects of irresponsible mining. Minister for Lands and Natural Resources Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah said the environmental destruction caused by irresponsible mining underscores the need for more sustainable approaches to mineral extraction. Addressing the launch, Mr Buah cited damage to forest reserves and pollution of water bodies as major concerns, warning that the destruction of natural resources has created significant challenges for water treatment and environmental restoration. He said Ghana had 118 forest reserves, 44 of which he described as destroyed, while also highlighting the scale of pollution affecting the country’s water resources. “How do we destroy what has been keeping us alive?” he asked, pointing to the substantial financial resources required to reclaim degraded lands and restore damaged ecosystems. Small-scale mining remains an important source of employment and income for households and businesses in mining communities. However, the Minerals Commission has acknowledged that irresponsible operations have contributed to the degradation of farmlands, pollution of water bodies, destruction of vegetation and threats to public health. Deputy Director of the Minerals Commission Emmanuel Kwamena Anyimah said the priority must be to ensure that mineral resources are extracted legally, safely and sustainably. “The challenge before us, therefore, is not simply how to mine our minerals, but how to mine them responsibly, legally, safely, and sustainably,” he said. The Commission says it will continue to promote lawful mining, strengthen regulatory oversight, improve occupational health and safety, and support initiatives that enhance the organisation and performance of small-scale mining operators. Acting National Coordinator of the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme, Sheihu Siddiq, said the cooperative society would receive support to comply with regulatory standards and improve its operational capacity. The support is expected to cover mine safety, appropriate processing technologies, responsible water management and the rehabilitation of degraded mining areas. Mr Siddiq urged members of the cooperative to operate strictly within their authorised concession and comply with all applicable regulatory requirements. He said the initiative offered an opportunity to demonstrate that small-scale mining could be organised and profitable while meeting environmental and safety standards. Member of Parliament for the area, Kofi Arko Nokoe, also welcomed efforts to bring licensing services closer to mining communities and strengthen local monitoring through municipal security structures. He said responsible mining must deliver tangible benefits to host communities through decent jobs and sustainable livelihoods, while ensuring the protection of rivers and farmlands and the restoration of mined lands. The launch places renewed attention on the challenge of balancing the economic importance of small-scale mining with the need to protect the environment. For the beneficiary communities, the programme’s success will depend on how effectively the cooperative model translates into lawful mining operations, safer working conditions, stronger local accountability and measurable improvements in environmental protection.

title: The Arts Edit replay: Inside Christie's first fine art auction in Abu Dhabi
body: Ahead of Christie’s first fine art auction in Abu Dhabi, The National explored the works going under the hammer, the growth of the emirate’s art scene and how collectors, museums and auction houses are establishing Abu Dhabi as an international art centre. The discussion and Q&A, guided by moderator William Mullally , arts and culture editor at The National, included Sultan Sooud Al Qassemi , founder of the Barjeel Art Foundation and Ridha Moumni, Chairman of Middle East & Africa at Christie's. Together, the panel examined the pieces up for auction, the stories behind their creation and took insightful questions from the audience.

body:

country’s U-23 Greco-Roman wrestling team, Major General Ahmad Vahidi underlined that winning the title of championship serves as yet another clear testament to an enduring truth.

title: Friday, 16 October 2026
body: Regional The UN Leaders' Summit has started in Yerevan. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, the leaders of Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Iran, Georgia are among those in attendance. Guterres urged Armenia and Azerbaijan to implement the provisions of the peace agreement during the press conference in Yerevan. The UN Secretary-General added that this naturally included the issue of detained persons. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said that he intends to sign a peace agreement with Azerbaijan by 2031. This is when the next parliamentary elections are set to take place in Armenia. Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan said that, in contrast to the Armenian Constitution, the issue of enclaves and exclaves does not pose an obstacle to the peace process between Armenia and Azerbaijan. The comments came after Pashinyan said earlier this week that neither country should have enclaves or exclaves. Armenia Pashinyan has established a working group to discuss the efficiency of the South Caucasus Railway concession management with Russia and to identify potential solutions within three months. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said he believes that the next meeting of foreign ministers within the ‘3+3’ regional format — Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Russia, Turkey, and Iran — could be held in Azerbaijan, followed by a meeting in Yerevan. Azerbaijan Two brothers have reportedly been detained in Nakhchivan over the hijab school ban issue. According to their relatives, who spoke to Meydan TV , the brothers were taken to the police after protesting against their children being barred from attending school wearing hijabs. Both brothers were reportedly sentenced to 25 days of administrative detention. It is unclear under which legal provision the sentences were handed down. Azerbaijan’s Parliament has issued a statement warning that hybrid attacks against the country have escalated. According to the statement, investigations conducted in cooperation with relevant state agencies have identified activities aimed at manipulating public opinion, polarising society, and undermining trust in state institutions. On Thursday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan told journalists that the ‘unbreakable bond’ between the leaders of Turkey and Azerbaijan would continue to exist ‘in the strongest possible way’, while also acknowledging that there were problems between the two countries. A few hours after Fidan’s remarks, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan shared a post on X about education and the Maarif Foundation. Georgia The Georgian Prosecutor’s Office announced yesterday that Vato Kipiani and Avtandil Bilanashvili, known as ‘Katsro’, had been detained and charged. Both are figures who the media have linked to the criminal underworld for years. A prisoner died at Kutaisi Prison No 2 on 9 October. The Special Penitentiary Service said yesterday that the prisoner fell from the upper bunk of a bunk bed in his cell and landed face down on the floor. He received medical assistance, but could not be saved. Viktor Japaridze, an MP elected to parliament on the Georgian Dream list and a member of the People’s Power party, has sold his 52% stake in POSTV , a TV channel sanctioned by the UK, for ₾1,000 ($380). Giorgi Shengelia, who previously managed Japaridze’s stake, is now the new majority owner of the TV channel. The court has decided to keep Iranian activist Mohammad Mahdi Rahimian in immigration detention. The Migration Department must make a final decision within three months on whether to deport him or grant him asylum or another legal status. South Ossetia Russia will assist South Ossetia in establishing a data centre, developing fibre-optic infrastructure and modern mobile communications, and digitising public services. South Ossetian President Marat Kambolov announced this following a meeting with Russian Minister of Digital Development, Communications, and Mass Media Maksut Shadaev. President Marat Kambolov has made the first appointments to South Ossetia’s new government. The North Caucasus The Daghestani Parliament has elected Fyodor Shchukin as Head of the republic. He received 78 of the 87 votes cast by lawmakers. Shchukin had served as acting Head of the republic since May 2026. Russian President Vladimir Putin replaced the republic’s leadership following devastating floods. Security forces in Chechnya are detaining relatives of Arbi Khaskhanov, who fled his military unit. He is currently in Slovakia, where he is seeking protection. RFE/RL reported this, citing Austrian human rights activist Roza Dunaeva. The Supreme Court of Daghestan has increased the sentences of former police officers Shamil Aliyev and Ramazan Saipulaev in a case involving the torture of local resident Yulduz Kurashova and the fabrication of a criminal case against her. The court replaced their suspended sentences with prison terms. This is the fourth time the verdict has been reviewed. A court in Nalchik has fined 29-year-old Eduard Udovydchenko ₽31,000 ($370) for ‘discrediting’ the army. According to the court ruling, Udovydchenko posted ‘text comments’ in a public Telegram channel that included the phrases ‘waging war on hospitals, schools and maternity hospitals’ and ‘drug addicts and alcoholics’. title: Morning strikes on Kharkiv kill 2, injure 19
body:
On Monday morning, Russian UAVs attacked the Osnovyanskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, and Industrialnyi districts of Kharkiv, killing two people and injuring 19 others, Head of the Regional Military Administration Oleh Synehubov reported.

"At this moment, two dead are known – a 71-year-old woman and a 58-year-old man. Sincere condolences to their family and friends. A total of 19 people were affected: 12 sustained injuries, 5 suffered an acute stress reaction," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

Synehubov added that the energy system was among the targeted infrastructure.

title: Writing Books with AI: How Do Manually Written Books Stay Relevant?
body:
Last updated Updated: Oct 20, 2026 by Simon SpÃ¤ti Â· Created Created: Sep 20, 2023 Â· 4 min read Â· growing Note status Growing. Worked on quite a bit, still rough. Expect bullets, gaps and views that update. Estimated from edit history Â· 2 sessions over 3 days Â· 656 words Â· How my notes grow Recent changes Oct 20 last week +223 / â0 words Oct 17 2 weeks ago published Â· 433 words
AI-generated content is rising, if you have been on any social media platform, you have noticed that everywhere, but it’s not only social media, it’s articles, videos, and even books.
The rise of AI-generated e-book releases- I’m sure the grey number is much higher. Original Source , shared on Reddit
The more interesting question also: how is it in printed books?
A lot also has to do with trusting the author. If you started writing before AI, people trust you more because it’s manually written . But also, there must be a way to still write today without getting lost in the AI flood.
I also find it concerning that AWS is restricted to 3 books per day (that was in 2023!), shouldn’t that be much lower? Amazon restricts authors from self-publishing more than three books a day after AI concerns | Books | The Guardian , this was 2023-09-20
Who writes more than one book a year? This is insane.
It seems that Amazon has no way of sorting out AI books - on the Amazon Hot New Releases in Data Warehouse today, I see three books already clearly generated by AI.
Just a couple of hours later, 4 out of top 5 is AI genearted covers, so it gets updated quick.
Some of these authors write a lot - see this author: img_Writing books with AI- Study_1792495677736.webp
So if the cover is already AI-generated, you can clearly know what’s inside the book.
Amazon, please, can you not promote them as hot new releases? No offense to the authors, but when you spend years writing it, why wouldn’t you want a nice cover (or maybe you haven’t spent the years…). Just an observation today.
I had an AI generate a cover initially too , but that was for an unfinished book and just when I started and when I focused on the writing, which is a good thing, but if you publish your life’s work on Amazon , then clearly you want something nice, might be initially helped with AI-Design skills. Still, you want to alter it to make it yours, right?
Good thing there’s still people writing manually , see Tim Ferriss :
Updated opinion 7 months later, but with the same messate at 2026-10-15 : I’m working on this new book right now and it’s like I am not using AI to write for me because if I do that, I’m done . […]. . But if you want to retain a function, a cognitive ability, be very careful about what you outsource. Why I Refuse to Let AI Write My Next Book
Me included, but the question is: how long will people withstand the temptation of doing the hard work of spending all the time? And again, how do we avoid the real books getting under with the flood?
Though I certainly don’t have the answer, and I can only guess, I still think being true to yourself, writing from the heart , something you experienced, having a soul and character in your writing, and having conviction as Harry Dry said so nicely, is some thing that help. Otherwise I think we just have to wait until people are tired of reading generate text, even if good (though for writing, I haven’t come across yet), but what’s the point?
Time will tell, as always. Do you have a better answer? Write me, discuss in the link below. I’d like to know.
