title: C. Equatoria prioritizes peace, security ahead of December elections
body: The Central Equatoria State caretaker government has prioritized peace, security, public finance management, and service delivery as it begins implementing its policy agenda under Governor Augustino Jadalla Kamilo Wani. Speaking to journalists on Thursday after the first ordinary Council of Ministers meeting, Joseph Pitia Kenyi, the state minister of Information, said the council adopted the policy priorities, including maintaining government operations and ensuring peaceful, credible and orderly elections. “The main agenda that the Council discussed is the policy of His Excellency the Governor-Caretaker of Central Equatoria State. One of them is the responsibility of maintaining continuity of the government, peaceful, credible and orderly elections,” he said. “We shall maintain peace and security, unity and reconciliation. It is a collective responsibility of the Government of Central Equatoria State and public service delivery and institutional coordination.” Pitia said the Council of Ministers had adopted a policy on public finance and revenue mobilization, tasking the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Investment with overseeing the management of government resources. “The Council has listened to the policy and adopted the public finance and revenue mobilization policy,” he said. He added that the finance ministry was expected to take responsibility for government resources during the caretaker administration. “The Council also encourages the minister of finance, as a caretaker government, to take charge of the resources of the government,” Pitia said. The information minister said the Ministry of Local Government and Law Enforcement had also been tasked with strengthening security across counties and communities as the country prepares for elections. He called on communities to remain calm and support efforts to maintain stability. “Let the communities remain calm and wait for elections,” Pitia added. He said the Council directed the Ministry of Agriculture to raise awareness about the possibility of drought and encourage communities to take preventive measures. He said food security remained essential, particularly amid concerns about possible climate-related challenges and the wider global situation. “So, the Council has directed the Minister of Agriculture to raise awareness among the communities so that we take appropriate measures to address the risks,” he said. The Council also discussed land management, with Pitia saying the governor had directed that land be administered appropriately to enable residents to acquire it through proper procedures. “The Council also listens to the policy, and the governor has directed that land be managed so that people may appropriately acquire the land,” he said. On education, the minister said the education ministry was directed to document government schools to improve oversight and support access to education. The post C. Equatoria prioritizes peace, security ahead of December elections appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Burtsev returns to NovaPay to lead corporate business development
body:
Hlib Burtsev, who headed business development at Post Finance LLC (now NovaPay) from 2017 to 2020, has returned to the international financial service provider NovaPay (operating under the NovaPay trademark, with NovaPay Credit LLC as the issuer). He will lead the company’s corporate business development, overseeing the B2B segment and the creation of financial solutions for entrepreneurs and companies.
"The corporate segment is a key part of NovaPay’s development. Burtsev’s experience in the banking sector, fintech, and business development will strengthen our team and help us execute these plans," said NovaPay CEO Ihor Prykhodko, as quoted in the press release.
The company noted that Burtsev brings over 20 years of management experience in the banking and fintech sectors. During his previous tenure at NovaPay (2017–2020), he worked on the company’s strategy, the development of payment services, and the creation of its proprietary fintech platform. Most recently, he was responsible for business development at TAS Link.
In his new role, Burtsev will be responsible for the growth and financial performance of the corporate business—covering everything from customer experience and product development to commercial strategy, digital solutions, and the efficiency of business processes.
NovaPay emphasized that this appointment is part of the company’s ongoing efforts to expand its financial services for various business segments and to develop tailored offerings for corporate clients. NovaPay was founded in 2001 as an international financial service provider within the Nova group (Nova Poshta), offering financial services both online and offline at Nova Poshta branches. In 2023, it became the first non-banking financial institution in Ukraine to receive an expanded license from the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU), enabling it to open accounts and issue payment cards.

title: Ghana included in WHO lead-testing programme as questions remain over local exposure risks
body: Ghana is among six sub-Saharan African countries selected for support to strengthen laboratory capacity for blood lead testing under a World Health Organisation (WHO) initiative, as concerns grow over the health risks posed by exposure to the toxic metal. The programme aims to improve the monitoring and early detection of lead exposure. However, the WHO’s latest announcement does not provide figures on the number of people tested through the initiative in Ghana or the results recorded so far. The announcement comes amid evidence of widespread exposure among young children in the country. A survey conducted by the Ghana Health Service, Pure Earth and UNICEF found that 52% of children under five in Ghana had elevated blood lead levels, according to a report published by the Ghana News Agency in September 2026. The finding highlights the importance of identifying the sources of exposure and strengthening measures to protect children. Lead is a toxic metal that can damage several body systems. Children are particularly vulnerable because their brains and nervous systems are still developing. Why lead exposure matters The WHO says lead exposure can occur through contaminated paint, cookware, cosmetics, spices, informal recycling and industrial pollution, among other sources. The metal can affect the brain, kidneys and cardiovascular system. In children, exposure can cause lasting damage to brain development and affect learning, behaviour and intellectual development. The WHO says there is no level of lead exposure known to be without harmful effects. Even relatively low exposure can cause irreversible damage. In adults, lead exposure is associated with cardiovascular and kidney disease. The health effects may not be immediately apparent, making it difficult to identify some cases without appropriate testing. The WHO estimates that lead exposure was responsible for more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year, primarily through cardiovascular effects based on global health burden data. The WHO says laboratory capacity building and technical support under the Lead Poisoning Prevention Initiative will cover Ghana, Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, South Africa and Tanzania, alongside Brazil, Nepal and five states in India. The initiative is intended to strengthen blood lead testing so that health authorities can monitor exposure and identify affected people. The WHO’s announcement does not specify how many laboratories in Ghana will receive support, when implementation will begin locally or how many people are expected to be tested. Separately, Ghana is taking steps to address contamination by heavy metals in food. In September 2026, the Ghana News Agency reported that the country had launched a national strategic plan for heavy metals reduction in food covering 2026 to 2030. The plan seeks to strengthen food safety regulation, surveillance, laboratory capacity and public awareness, including measures addressing lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic. The report also cited findings of lead contamination in some consumer products and food-related materials. WHO calls for action at the source “Lead poisoning should not be stealing children’s potential in 2026,” said Bruce Gordon, Director a.i. of the WHO’s Department of Environment, Climate Change and One Health. “We know where many exposures come from and we know how to prevent them. Countries now need to move upstream, removing lead from products and environments before it reaches a child’s bloodstream. WHO is working with governments and partners to help turn that evidence into action,” Bruce added. The WHO is urging governments to strengthen regulations, enforce safety standards, improve monitoring and surveillance, and eliminate lead hazards from products and environments. It also recommends safer industrial practices and waste management systems, stronger public awareness and better capacity to manage poisoning cases. Despite decades of progress, fewer than half of countries had confirmed legally binding controls on lead paint in the WHO’s latest published global assessment . The WHO says its member states have mandated the development of a Global Action Plan on Lead Mitigation, which is scheduled to be presented to the World Health Assembly in 2027. The agency also plans to launch its PREVENT Technical Package on Lead Poisoning Prevention in 2027. The package is expected to provide practical guidance on identifying major sources of exposure, choosing effective interventions, strengthening regulations and tracking progress. The initiatives form part of a broader effort to shift from detecting lead exposure to preventing it. For Ghana, key questions remain about the implementation of the WHO-supported laboratory programme, the availability of blood lead testing, the sources of exposure affecting children and the enforcement of relevant safety standards. The WHO says preventing lead exposure can protect children’s development, reduce the burden of disease and bring wider social and economic benefits.

title: Hamzat: African Govts, Private Sector Must Increase Investment in Digital Infrastructure
body: Kayode Tokede The Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Hamzat, has demanded of African governments and the private sector to increase investment in digital infrastructure, stressing that the continent’s major challenge in technological development is not a lack of innovation but the inability to scale successful ideas to reach millions of people across the continent. Hamzat, who was speaking recently at the fifth edition of Texcellence in Lagos, said African countries must dismantle bureaucratic bottlenecks, establish predictable policies and implement institutional reforms that would enable technology-driven businesses to grow and deliver widespread economic and social benefits. The event, themed ‘Accelerating Africa’s Digital Future Lacks Direction and a Sustained Force,’ brought together stakeholders to discuss strategies for strengthening the continent’s digital economy. Texcellence is an annual tech summit attracting public and private sectors with technology experts. The fifth edition attracted international speakers from some African countries like Uganda, Kenya, South Africa among others. Hamzat said governments must provide reliable infrastructure, predictable regulations and adequate funding to enable technology businesses to grow and deliver measurable benefits to citizens. He outlined measures being taken by Lagos State to accelerate digital development and called for stronger collaboration between government and the private sector. Hamzat stated: “Africa does not have an innovation problem. I will repeat that again. Africa does not have an innovation problem. We have a scaling problem. And it goes across all sectors.” He cited CWG, a Nigerian technology company that began operations in Lagos in 1992, as an example of how businesses could grow in a supportive environment. He said the company had expanded from a computer warehouse with six employees to a business listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), with subsidiaries in Ghana and Uganda and clients across Africa. According to him, CWG’s growth demonstrated the importance of a large market and a stable business environment that rewarded excellence and encouraged long-term investment. The deputy governor disclosed that Lagos had adopted a shared fibre-optic infrastructure model to reduce duplication of telecommunications facilities, with about 3,000 kilometres of fibre laid and plans for a unified 6,000-kilometre network backed by an additional $22million investment. He added that more than seven million residents had enrolled in the state’s residents’ identity management system, while smart cameras installed along major roads were helping with traffic monitoring. On improving the business environment, Hamzat said the state introduced an electronic physical planning permit system in April, allowing applicants to process and track permits online. He said the initiative had reduced the steps required to obtain permits from 29 to seven without increasing statutory fees. Hamzat also disclosed that the Lagos State Science, Research and Innovation Council had supported 18 researchers and more than 75 start-ups. He said the government was proposing legislation to dedicate a fixed portion of its annual budget to research, development and innovation. The founder of CWG and Texcellence host, Austin Okere, noted that the desire to address poor customer service and unreliable technology delivery inspired him to establish the company, which has grown into a major player in Nigeria’s information technology industry. He said he founded CWG after becoming dissatisfied with the failure of his former employer to meet delivery commitments to customers, warning that businesses risk losing their reputation when they fail to keep their promises. He added that the company’s commitment to developing Nigeria’s technology industry informed the establishment of the CWG Academy, which trains professionals not only for the company but also for its customers and competitors. According to him, the initiative was introduced partly in response to the departure of skilled Nigerian technology professionals to international companies entering the local market. He explained that Texcellence was created to bring technology companies, governments, customers and other stakeholders together to discuss how Africa could strengthen its digital infrastructure and accelerate technological development. While speaking with journalists, the Chief Operating Officer of CWG , Mr. Afolabi Sobande, advocated greater investment in indigenous technology development, stressing that Africa has the capacity to develop solutions to its challenges rather than depend continually on imported technologies. He said the annual conference, which began in 2021, was established to stimulate conversations about Africa’s capacity to drive technological development and encourage stakeholders to explore solutions that could address the continent’s needs.

title: Oil prices ease but head for another weekly gain on Middle East supply concerns
body: Oil prices eased on Friday but were still headed for another weekly increase on lingering Middle East supply concerns and as global efforts to boost crude stockpiles continue. Brent, the benchmark for two thirds of the world's oil, declined 0.77 per cent to $105.10 a barrel at 12.59pm UAE time. WTI, the gauge that tracks US crude, retreated nearly 1 per cent to $97.04. For the week, Brent is set to add 0.32 per cent, while WTI is on track to jump by more than 5.6 per cent. Global energy prices remain volatile and elevated as the war in Iran, now in its eighth month, continues to choke energy supplies. That has prompted moves to ensure ample supplies globally. On Thursday, the International Energy Agency said its March pledge to release crude oil stocks will exceed its target. It will accelerate the release of the remaining supplies as global efforts to tame soaring energy prices continue. The Paris-based agency also pointed out that exports out of the Middle East have recovered to pre-crisis levels and that oil storage globally is not tight. Gulf oil producers, meanwhile, have pushed tanker transfers as far as India’s coast and slashed prices to keep crude flowing to Asia, as the makeshift export network around the Strait of Hormuz buckles under congestion and persistent attacks . There were 82 Ship-to-ship transfers in India's Gulf of Kutch last month, equivalent to about 680,000 barrels per day, shipping analytics company Vortexa said. Refined products accounted for about 65 per cent of the volume, with crude making up the remainder. Current oil market levels “still seem to be somewhat lofty compared to market realities … [but] we are not running out of oil, as flows out of the Middle East have largely recovered. Instead of tilting the oil market into a deficit, the Iran war has mainly erased the surplus that had been built in 2025", said Norbert Rucker, head of economics and next-generation research at Swiss lender Julius Baer. G7 leaders pledged this month to accelerate the IEA's co-ordinated emergency stock release by releasing 100 million barrels of diesel and other reserves to help stabilise markets. And in a surprise move last week, US President Donald Trump's administration lifted sanctions to enable Russia to supply millions of barrels of diesel to global markets. The IEA on Wednesday warned that the global diesel shortage triggered by the Iran war is set to persist well into next year, with depleted inventories not expected to recover until the second half of 2027. Meanwhile, questions have been raised over the validity of Mr Trump's declaration of an “ energy ceasefire ” between Russia and Ukraine, after Moscow offered no confirmation of such a truce and Russian strikes hit Ukrainian power plants within hours of the announcement.

title: Pakistan's Asian Games final star Hasan Nawaz added to Desert Vipers squad for ILT20 2026
body: Hasan Nawaz became the fifth Pakistan player to join the Desert Vipers squad ahead of the fifth season of the DP World International League T20 (ILT20). Nawaz returns to the Vipers dugout after his debut season with the franchise in the title-winning campaign last term. The middle order batter replaces England’s Aneurin Donald who has been selected for England’s upcoming T20 series in Australia. The 24-year-old batter will enter the tournament high on confidence, having come close to the Asian Games T20 gold medal in Japan. During the title match against a full-strength Indian team, Nawaz smashed 96 from 51 balls as Pakistan almost chased down the target of 212, losing by 19 runs. Last month, Nawaz scored 47 in the final to help Antigua and Barbuda win the Caribbean Premier League title. Pakistan, meanwhile, completed a T20 series win at home against Sri Lanka this month. Now, as many as five Pakistan international stars will be competing for the Desert Vipers when the ILT20 kicks off on November 21. Once a Viper, always a Viper 🐍 Hassan Nawaz returns to our squad as a replacement for Aneurin Donald 💚 [Desert Vipers | Fangs Out | DP World ILT20 Season 5] pic.twitter.com/EetmWV4l8Q — Desert Vipers (@TheDesertVipers) October 16, 2026 Nawaz joins Babar Azam , Naseem Shah, Fakhar Zaman and Shadab Khan in the Vipers team. Interestingly, Desert Vipers are the only franchise not under Indian ownership and face no competition while recruiting Pakistan players. “The fact we have been able to secure the services of Hasan as his replacement is fantastic from our perspective,” Desert Vipers CEO Phil Oliver said. “He was a key member of the Vipers squad in our successful Season 4 and so he will slot in very easily to our set-up. And, on top of that, he has been in terrific form this year, scoring runs for the Quetta franchise in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) and then being a vital component of the Antigua and Barbuda franchise’s run to the Caribbean Premier League (CPL) title. “We look forward to welcoming Hasan back to the Vipers for Season 5 and hope he will play his part as we look to go back-to-back in the upcoming tournament.” The Vipers begin their title defence on the opening day of Season 5, playing MI Emirates at the Dubai International Stadium. The ILT20 runs from November 21 to December 20.

title: Koretsky: 100% reservation provides opportunities for major manipulations
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky states that 100% reservation for enterprises creates opportunities for significant manipulation, a problem that has grown to a large scale.
"100% reservation provides opportunities for major manipulations. If you have 100%, it means you can endlessly expand your staff and reserve people: and it doesn't matter whether a person is a repair worker or not, an energy worker or not. And this system has already reached a large scale, unfortunately. Therefore, this is the only reason why we are looking at the 100% barrier – to modify it or leave it as it is. Because, unfortunately, there are many abuses," Koretsky said during the "Question Time with the Government" in the Verkhovna Rada on Friday.
The Prime Minister noted that additional reservations continue to be granted by the tens of thousands monthly at such enterprises.
"It is necessary to separate criticality and the economic block. Because wages and the absence of tax debt do not always mean that an enterprise is critical. Criticality is the defense capability and life support of the state," he added.
To substantiate his words, Koretsky gave an example of a contractor performing work for an energy company, where only 20 out of 100 employees actually carry out the subcontract for that company, yet all 100 are reserved.
Earlier, the Prime Minister stated that when modifying the reservation system, there will be no radical changes for critical enterprises in the defense and energy sectors.
"The resolution is being processed, it will definitely be finalized, adopted, and published. There is no betrayal there. All details will follow once they are made public and all relevant decisions are made," he said.
As reported, on October 13, the Cabinet of Ministers adopted the resolution On certain issues of organizing the reservation of persons subject to military service during mobilization and in wartime, introducing changes to the reservation system. As of today, the resolution has not been published.
Earlier, MP Yaroslav Zheleznyak published a draft government resolution providing for the reduction of reservation limits for the defense-industrial complex and energy sector from 100% to 85%, for municipal enterprises from 75% to 60%, as well as changing the calculation base for the 50% quota and creating a Coordination Center under the Cabinet of Ministers. According to his data, the Coordination Center was proposed to be established with 17 members, including representatives of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), the Main Directorate of Intelligence (GUR), the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine (SZRU), and the National Police. Without a positive recommendation from this body, enterprises would not be able to obtain the status of critically important or a reservation quota exceeding 50%, with the center also having the authority to recommend revoking such status, while clear deadlines, criteria, and appeal mechanisms were absent in the document.
A group of MPs from all parliamentary factions appealed to Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky demanding the cancellation of plans to create a Coordination Center for Organizing Reservation.
Chairman of the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, MP Oleksandr Fediyenko, emphasized that the creation of a new agency risks causing delays in reservation procedures for enterprises in the defense-industrial complex, energy, and critical infrastructure, threatening the non-fulfillment of state contracts.

title: Kyiv Starts Heating Hospitals and Schools as Repairs Delay Parts of City
body:
Kyiv began supplying heat to hospitals, schools and kindergartens on Friday, Oct. 16, while repairs to a damaged energy facility delayed connections in parts of two left-bank districts, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
In a Telegram post , Klitschko said facilities would be connected at their managers’ request. Parts of Dniprovskyi and Darnytskyi districts remain excluded while repairs continue.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
He did not announce when heating would start in residential buildings or when the damaged facility would return to service.
The Darnytsia combined heat and power plant , which supplied heating to both districts, was devastated by Russian strikes on Feb. 3. Klitschko did not identify the facility undergoing repairs in his latest announcement.
Russian forces targeted Kyiv’s three main combined heat and power plants again overnight on Oct. 13-14. All three had stopped generating electricity , Ekonomichna Pravda reported on Oct. 15, citing energy-company sources, as previously reported by Kyiv Post.
The loss of electricity generation at those plants does not establish that heating is unavailable throughout Kyiv, which also relies on other heating facilities.
In an Oct. 14 update, Klitschko said Kyiv had prepared nearly 700 generators and 70 mobile boiler units for water and heating facilities. The city had also built three diesel power stations.
Hospitals have 480 generators, while 15 medical facilities have their own water wells, he said. Eleven hospitals have independent heating, with plans to increase that number to 21 by the end of the year.
Residential buildings have also acquired more than 6,000 generators, inverters and batteries through municipal programs.
Russian attacks repeatedly disrupted heating and electricity supplies in Kyiv last winter. On Jan. 24, Klitschko said nearly 6,000 homes had lost heating after a major strike damaged critical infrastructure.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Controller and Accountant-General pays promotion arrears to 56,003 GES teachers ahead of deadline
body: The Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) has paid promotion-related salary adjustments and arrears to 56,003 Ghana Education Service (GES) teachers, completing the payments ahead of the October 16 deadline agreed between the government and teacher unions. The teacher unions were on strike for over a week, but called it off after the government intervened and assured them of payment. In a statement issued by the CAGD and signed by its Head of Public Relations, Cephas N. Dosoo, on October 16, the CAGD said the payments covered teachers whose promotion records had been submitted by the GES and successfully verified to meet payroll requirements. Providing a breakdown of the payments, the statement indicated that 49,725 teachers received their payments on October 15, alongside their October salaries, covering salary adjustments and arrears dating from January 1, while a further 6,278 teachers were paid in September 2026. “Of this number, 49,725 received their payments on 15 October 2026, together with their October salaries. These payments covered salary adjustments and arrears from 1 January 2026. A further 6,278 teachers were paid in September 2026,” it said It added that the payments were completed ahead of the deadline agreed between Government representatives and teacher unions at a meeting held at the Ministry of Education on 2 October 2026. “The payments were completed ahead of the 16 October 2026 deadline agreed between Government representatives and teacher unions at a meeting held at the Ministry of Education on 2 October 2026,” the statement added. The Department explained that, out of approximately 80,000 teachers reported to have been promoted, the GES had processed and submitted supporting documents for 56,633 for verification and payment. According to the statement, the CAGD verified and paid 56,003 teachers, while 630 cases remain pending due to issues identified during the verification process. “CAGD awaits the resolution of these issues by GES for the payments to be effected,” the statement noted. It further disclosed that the remaining 23,367 promoted teachers were yet to be processed by the GES, with the relevant supporting documents still to be submitted to the Department. “The remaining 23,367 teachers are yet to be processed and relevant documents submitted by GES,” the statement said. The CAGD maintained that all teachers whose records met the necessary criteria had been paid, stating that, “it has therefore completed payment for all teachers whose submitted records met the payroll requirements.” It further assured affected teachers that it would process outstanding eligible payments promptly once the necessary corrections were made or complete, accurate documentation was received and verified. “The Department remains committed to processing outstanding eligible payments promptly once the necessary corrections are made or complete and accurate documents are received and verified,” the statement said. The Department expressed appreciation to the GES, teacher unions, and the participating ministries and agencies for their co-operation in facilitating the payment process.

title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: We will win the trophy – Samson Deen
body: Ghana National Paralympic Committee president Samson Deen is confident the Black Challenge can win the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Ghana have been drawn in Group D alongside Angola, Colombia and Iraq, but Deen believes the reigning African champions have the quality to lift the trophy. “I’ll stand on behalf of the team and tell you that we’ll win the World Cup,” he said. “I’ve told them they have to win it, and we’ll do everything in our capacity to go there and win. Whatever we need to do, we’ll do it. “Unless God says maybe winning won’t be good for us, but we know God is on our side and we have the best team in the world.” The Black Challenge are expected to travel to Turkey this month for a training camp before heading to Mexico for the world championship. Ghana will be aiming to build on their continental success as they prepare to compete against some of the world’s best amputee football teams. Deen’s comments underline the team’s ambition as preparations continue ahead of the tournament.

title: 4 Russian drones violate Moldovan airspace during overnight attack against Ukraine
body:
Yet another series of Russian drone incursions into Moldova's airspace was recorded during the latest overnight attack against Ukraine, Moldova's Defense Ministry reported on Oct. 16.
Between 11:02 p.m. on Oct. 15 and 3:46 a.m. local time on Oct. 16, Moldova's Defense Ministry s aid three Russian drones crossed into the country's territory before returning to Ukraine's airspace.
A fourth drone entered at 5:59 a.m. and reentered again at 6:09 a.m. before turning back to Ukraine.
The incidents underscore the growing security risks posed to Moldova and the region by Russia's war against neighboring Ukraine.
Russian aerial incursions into Moldovan territory during attacks against Ukraine are becoming alarmingly routine, with five Russian drones and missiles exploding on Moldova's territory on Oct. 3 alone.
Chisinau has repeatedly raised the alarm about these airspace violations, with Moldovan President Maia Sandu declaring that Russia's war against Ukraine is "dangerously reaching Moldova."
Moldova announced plans on Oct. 7 to build shelters at border crossings to protect border guards and people nearby in response to growing incursions.
The announcement came after the Moldovan Border Police reported on Oct. 5 that a projectile fired during a Russian attack against Ukraine ricocheted and struck a passenger bus and a border control booth at the Palanca-Maiaky-Udobne crossing, lightly injuring a border guard.
Russia also struck border crossings between Ukraine and nearby Romania in early September.

title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: We want to make the continent proud – Black Challenge coach
body: Ghana’s Amputee National Team head coach, Richard Obeng, says the Black Challenge are determined to make Ghana and the African continent proud at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The team held a training session at Mensah Sarbah Park at the University of Ghana on Thursday as preparations intensified for the tournament. All 15 players named in Ghana’s squad were present as the team worked to improve their fitness and sharpen their readiness ahead of the competition. Speaking to JoySports, Obeng said the players were making good progress as they build towards the tournament. “Training has been good. The boys are on course, and we’re bringing them back into shape and to their peak.” Ghana have been drawn in Group D alongside Angola, Iraq and Colombia and face a challenging route to the knockout stage. Obeng insists the team will approach every match with the same level of determination, stressing that there will be no room for complacency. “We’re not going to have it easy from the group stage. Every game we play is a final,” he said. “That is how we’ve psyched our minds, from the technical team to the playing body. Every team we face is a final game for us, one we are supposed to win to make ourselves, our families, Ghanaians and the continent as a whole proud.” The Black Challenge are scheduled to travel to Turkey for a camping exercise before proceeding to Mexico for the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup.

title: Unpacking the Haze: What Is Floating in Palau’s Air and When Will It Clear?
body: By L.N. Reklai KOROR, Palau (Oct. 15, 2026) For the past three months, a thick, gray haze has hung over the islands of Palau. It has blocked our views of the ocean, darkened our skies, and left many asking what is going to clear our air. A detailed six-month record released by scientists at the Palau Atmospheric Observatory (PAO)—located in downtown Koror on the campus of Palau Community College (PCC)—explains where this smoke comes from, what it is doing to our health and environment, and when it will finally leave. Palau sunrises and sunsets reflect red sun due to the persistent haze. Photo credit: Yobch Toribiong 1. What Is the Exact Cause of the Haze, and Can We Do Anything About It? The primary cause of the haze is smoldering forest and peatland fires in Southeast Asia and neighboring regions , not local land clearing. While Palau recorded 16 brush fires during dry conditions in August 2026, scientific monitoring confirms that local fires are far too small to create this amount of thick smoke. Satellite tracking by NASA and European space agencies shows massive fire clusters burning across: Indonesia: Drained peatlands in Sumatra and Central/West Kalimantan. Papua New Guinea: Agricultural burning belts across the southern lowlands. Northern Australia: Large coastal brush fires. Because tropical peat fires burn slowly underground with low oxygen, they produce huge amounts of smoke, carbon monoxide gas, and fine organic soot. Can we do anything local to stop it? No. Because the smoke originates thousands of miles away across international borders, local actions in Palau cannot stop the fires. The only immediate actions Palauans can take are personal protection measures : Limit outdoor exercise and heavy physical activity on hazy days. Keep doors and windows closed when possible to keep fine indoor air clean. Use N95-rated face masks when spending extended time outside. Avoid starting local brush or trash fires, which add extra smoke to our already overloaded air. 2. How Is the Haze Carried to Palau, and When Will It End? The smoke travels to Palau on a seasonal “wind highway”. Every year between July and October, lower-level winds shift and blow from the southwest. This year, an unusually strong El Niño weather pattern caused severe drought across Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and the Western Pacific. The dry weather allowed forests to burn uncontrollably while drying up the heavy rainstorms that normally wash smoke out of the sky. The southwesterly winds picked up this undiluted smoke and carried it direct northeast across the Celebes and Philippine Seas straight into Palau. When will it end? In November, regional wind patterns undergo a seasonal shift to northeasterly trade winds. By December and through the spring, upper winds blow from the pristine, open Pacific Ocean where there are no fires. Once these trade winds return, the wind conduit bringing smoke from Indonesia will shut off, restoring Palau’s clean ocean air. 3. What Kind of Particles Are in the Haze, and How Do They Affect the Human Body? Testing by the PAO, using advanced lasers, research balloons, and spectrometers in Koror and Malakal, revealed three main dangerous substances in our air: Refractory Black Carbon (Soot): Fine, dark carbon particles produced by burning wood and organic matter. Organic Matter Aerosols: Microscopic liquid drops and chemical compounds released from smoldering peat soils. Carbon Monoxide (CO): An odorless, invisible toxic gas. Under normal conditions, rural Babeldaob has very clean air with low soot levels (about 40 nanograms per cubic meter). In August 2026, soot levels in downtown Koror spiked to 14 times higher than normal , with extreme peaks reaching 22 times higher than baseline levels . How do these affect the human body? Lungs and Breathing: Fine soot particles (PM2.5) are tiny enough to bypass the body’s natural filters in the nose and throat. They travel deep into the lungs, causing coughing, throat irritation, asthma flare-ups, and bronchitis. Bloodstream and Heart: The smallest fine particles pass directly through lung tissue into the blood. This forces the heart to work harder, increasing the risk of irregular heartbeats, high blood pressure, and heart attacks. Headaches and Fatigue: Elevated carbon monoxide levels reduce the blood’s ability to carry oxygen around the body, leading to dizziness, headaches, and tiredness. Vulnerable Groups: Children, elderly residents, pregnant women, and people with existing heart or respiratory conditions face the highest health risks. 4. What Is the Impact of Prolonged Exposure on Humans, Land Plants, and Marine Life? Impact on Humans Living in fine particle pollution for months strains the cardiovascular and respiratory systems. Prolonged exposure can cause reduced lung capacity, permanent lung tissue damage, chronic bronchitis, and an increased risk of long-term heart and lung diseases. Impact on Flora (Land Plants and Forests) Reduced Photosynthesis: Thick haze blocks natural sunlight, preventing trees and farm crops from absorbing the light energy they need to make food. Clogged Stomata: Fine soot settles on leaves, physically clogging the tiny pores ( stomata ) plants use to breathe, which slows plant growth and weakens forest health. Impact on Fauna (Land Animals and Birds) Animals inhale the same fine particles, suffering respiratory distress and reduced stamina similar to humans. Impact on Marine Life (Coral Reefs and Lagoon) Shading Coral Reefs: Corals rely on microscopic algae living inside them ( zooxanthellae ) that require sunlight to survive. Prolonged gloom from smoke reduces light penetration through lagoon waters, stressing corals. Ocean Surface Chemistry: As soot and chemical compounds slowly settle onto the ocean surface (wet and dry deposition), they alter the water’s local surface chemistry, potentially harming sensitive plankton and marine organisms at the base of the ocean food chain. 5. What Will Make the Haze Go Away? The haze requires two specific weather changes to fully clear: The November Wind Shift: The arrival of the seasonal monsoonal reversal. When winds turn to blow from the northeast, they will blow clean ocean air across Palau and push Indonesian smoke away from the archipelago. Heavy Rainstorms (Wet Scavenging): As El Niño conditions weaken, returning tropical rainstorms over the ocean will wash soot and organic particles out of the atmosphere before they can travel far. Until the wind direction turns next month, residents across Koror and Babeldaob are advised to take sensible precautions outdoors. Data and observational findings sourced directly from the joint research report by the Palau Atmospheric Observatory (PAO), Coral Reef Research Foundation (CRRF), Alfred Wegener Institute (AWI), University of Bremen, and Palau Community College (PCC) . The post Unpacking the Haze: What Is Floating in Palau’s Air and When Will It Clear? appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Zelensky to discuss energy, air defense and financial support in Brussels
body:
The Ukrainian President made the statemen t after arriving at the EU summit during a joint media appearance with the Presidents of the European Council and European Commission, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
“Of course, we want to end this war as soon as possible. Now, we do not see signals from Russian side that they are ready to end this war. That is why we have to prepare for the winter. Winter package is not only energy, it is also air defense and funding,” Zelensky said.
He clarified that the financial assistance would cover not only this year but also next year.
The President thanked EU leaders for opening two negotiating clusters and expressed hope that two more could be opened by the end of the year.
“Thank you for two [negotiating] clusters. We will work and do everything to open two last clusters by the end of the year. I am sure that we will do it,” Zelensky said.
He stressed that he was grateful for the European Union’s tremendous support – from the European Council, the European Commission and the leaders of EU member states, who have been helping Ukraine since the beginning of the war.
“It is crucial, and we count on the support,” the head of state said.
As reported, today the leaders of EU member states will discuss issues related to Ukraine and hear from President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Zelensky’s schedule also includes a number of bilateral meetings, including with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa, and European leaders.
On October 13, at an intergovernmental conference in Luxembourg, the EU officially opened two more negotiating clusters in Ukraine’s EU accession talks.

title: Do Americans own the president's papers? Appeals court to weigh in
body:
A flag featuring Donald Trump waves amid a group of supporters near Mar-a-Lago, Fla., in 2024. Alon Skuy/Getty Images hide caption
President Trump has famously pushed the bounds of executive power since he returned to the White House. In arguments Friday before a federal appeals court in Washington, administration lawyers will make an especially bold claim: that papers created in the White House belong to Donald Trump, not to the American people. The move comes amid a series of actions under Trump's second term to test the limits put in place after the Watergate scandal, and could be another case that ends up at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.
Six months ago, the Justice Department moved to invalidate the Presidential Records Act, a federal law in place since 1978. Conservative lawyer Michael Edney cast the move in a long line of other attempts to pare back statutes from that era.
"This is a story about a post-Watergate, overbroad statutory incursion into the prerogatives of the executive branch," Edney said in a recent webinar sponsored by the Federalist Society.
For some 200 years, presidents could decide for themselves what to do with the papers they created in office, until disputes with Richard Nixon prompted Congress to weigh in. Every president since then has complied with the records law, until this year.
"The Presidential Records Act is unconstitutional and a clear violation of the separation of powers," said White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis.
The White House's reinterpretation of the act comes after Trump was indicted on obstruction of justice charges for allegedly stockpiling classified documents in a bathroom, ballroom and office at his Mar-a-Lago resort. A federal judge threw out the case for technical reasons, related to the appointment of the prosecutor, and the Justice Department ultimately dropped the case after Trump won reelection.
Nikhel Sus is chief counsel for Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a watchdog group that sued over the Trump move.
"If the courts were to accept it, and we are hopeful that they will not, it would mean the people really have no right of access to the president's papers and that would be a major loss for archivists, historians and to the American people writ large," Sus said.
Senior U.S. District Judge John Bates, an appointee of former President George W. Bush , ruled against the Trump White House this year, in a decision that opened with a passage from George Orwell's dystopian novel 1984: "Who controls the past controls the future; who controls the present controls the past," the judge wrote.
Three judges from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit will consider the issue on Friday.
The Trump administration said in court papers that keeping all those records imposes a burden on the White House and that it could chill advisers from having honest conversations with the president.
But former government officials say being able to consult these papers is essential.
"Access to the records on national security issues of former presidents is really vital for the continuity of our government," said John Bellinger, who served as legal adviser to the National Security Council under George W. Bush.
Bellinger said he and other members of Bush's staff sometimes requested the papers of President Bill Clinton, to understand conversations Clinton had with world leaders and members of Congress.
"Often the only record of what a president has said to a foreign leader — or perhaps even more important, what a foreign leader, friend or foe, has said to the president of the United States — is in a written document," Bellinger said.
To not be able to see those papers, he said, will leave future presidents at a "terrible disadvantage."
Edney, who also worked for Bush's National Security Council and Justice Department, said he believed that Congress could probably pass a "thoughtful" records preservation statute. He said parts of the current Presidential Records Act that provide Congress with automatic access and presume the records will be publicly disclosed are "constitutionally problematic."
Edney said he has some doubts about whether the watchdog groups suing to challenge Trump's move actually have legal standing to proceed.
But the Trump administration appears to have breezed past those concerns, because they have a higher goal in mind.
"They want this to go to the Supreme Court," Edney said. "I think they want this resolved at a time of their choosing, with arguments of their choosing, and a court of their choosing, and with the Solicitor General's office that's making their arguments, as opposed to a subsequent administration."

title: Remembering Oscar-winning actor Eva Marie Saint
body:
Saint, who died Oct. 6, studied at the Actors Studio and was best known for her roles in On the Waterfront and the Hitchcock film North by Northwest. Originally broadcast in 2000.
DAVE DAVIES, HOST: This is FRESH AIR. I'm Dave Davies. The actress Eva Marie Saint, best known for two very different roles in "On The Waterfront" and "North By Northwest," died last week. She was 102 years old. She won an Academy Award in 1955 for her movie debut in "On The Waterfront," playing the shy, parochial school-educated young woman opposite longshoreman Marlon Brando. Here they are on a first date. (SOUNDBITE OF FILM, "ON THE WATERFRONT") MARLON BRANDO: (As Terry Malloy) What do you really care, am I right? EVA MARIE SAINT: (As Edie Doyle) Shouldn't everybody care about everybody else? BRANDO: (As Terry Malloy) Oh, what a fruitcake you are. SAINT: (As Edie Doyle) I mean, isn't everybody a part of everybody else? BRANDO: (As Terry Malloy) And you really believe that drool? SAINT: (As Edie Doyle) Yes, I do. DAVIES: She co-starred with Cary Grant in the Hitchcock thriller "North By Northwest," playing a femme fatale. (SOUNDBITE OF FILM, "NORTH BY NORTHWEST") SAINT: (As Eve Kendall) I'm a big girl. title: 'Everything got worse': Gen Z express frustration, regret after Trump vote
body:
President Trump speaks at a campaign rally in San Antonio on Oct. 7. Trump made big inroads with young voters in 2024, but some of that support appears to be waning. Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
📲 Follow the midterms & more in the NPR App .
Gen Z Americans were a key part of President Trump's winning coalition in 2024. Nearly two years later — and with early voting underway in multiple states for the midterms — some of that youth support has faded.
That sentiment was on display in a focus group, conducted last week, of eight Generation Z Trump voters, who reported varying degrees of unhappiness and disappointment over the state of politics, with some going as far as to say they regret supporting Trump in 2024.
The conversation was conducted virtually by Navigator Research , a left-leaning polling group. Participants ranged in age from 20 to 29 and spanned five states: Florida, Mississippi, Ohio, Texas and South Carolina — places Trump won by double digits in the last election. Two of those states, Texas and Ohio , are home to competitive races that could be key to control of the Senate .
For participants who now regret their vote for Trump, much of their frustration centers on what they see as a string of failed promises. When asked to give the president's job performance a letter grade, a majority of participants, 6 out of 8, assigned him a grade of either D or F, while two selected C.
"I just feel like nothing went correctly. I just feel like everything got worse," said John, a 29-year-old Black man from Florida. (Participants agreed to be part of the focus group on the condition that they be identified by only their first names.)
John, who identifies as a Republican and has voted for Trump since 2016, gave the president an F and said he now plans to support Democratic candidates this fall, in large part because of the strain he has felt from rising costs.
"I'm willing to give the other side a chance," he added. "I don't think they're going to make a total change. But things are just horrible right now for me. So I feel like even if they make one or two small changes, it will probably benefit me."
Though the focus group is not a nationally representative survey, the frustrations shared by participants echoed polling conducted by Navigator this month, which found that more than a third of Gen Zers — those under age 30 — who voted for Trump now regret having done so, higher than older generations.
Trump's rising unpopularity among young voters isn't in a vacuum. He has also lost ground with other key groups that shifted right in 2024, notably independents and Latino voters — and in a year when the Republican Party is facing political headwinds, it's unclear whether that expanded coalition from two years ago can show up at the same strength now.
While some voters, like John in Florida, do feel compelled to vote blue this cycle in response to Trump, 4 of the 8 who took part in the focus group said they still planned to back Republicans this year. Three said they'd vote for Democrats; one participant said she was still deciding.
Matthew, a 25-year-old Black man living in Texas, said he doesn't regret his support for the president and gave him a C grade.
"I feel like he's done a really good job closing the border," he said. "I also do appreciate his efforts in trying to end some of the conflicts that began under the last administration, besides the fact that the Iran conflict hasn't really worked the best, from my perspective."
He plans to vote in the midterm elections and argued that Trump will be able to carry out more of his agenda if Republicans can secure a larger majority in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, although national polls indicate that the GOP is more likely to lose seats.
Courtney, a 20-year-old white woman based in South Carolina, said she doesn't regret her vote for Trump in 2024 and overall aligns with Republicans, but she did admit she has grown more distrustful of both major political parties, particularly on foreign policy.
"I just really do feel like we would be in this situation either way. … Education, the economy, everything else would be so much better if we weren't pumping money out into other countries that aren't ours," she said, referring to U.S. aid for Israel and the decision to go to war with Iran.
"I don't think it matters what side you vote on — that's why I voted red, because I agree with those policies more — but at the end of the day, what we do in the Middle East is going to be not at all up to [the] party [in power]," she said during the focus group.
That sense of political disaffection may underscore a growing challenge for both Republicans and Democrats moving forward as both try to repair ties with this generation.
"As we see people regret their vote for Trump, sour on the Republican Party and Republican policies, that doesn't necessarily mean that they're swinging right over to Democrats," said Melissa Toufanian, the managing director at Navigator.
Toufanian points to Navigator's own polling , which has found that even as the GOP has lost trust on economic issues, "it's not a one-for-one with Democrats gaining that trust."
"A lot of people are moving to this middle, this category that 'I don't trust either party,'" she said. "We are seeing people who are becoming increasingly pessimistic about our political parties and our political system, and they're not feeling strongly that either party can really deliver for them."
