title: Who was Tenzing Norgay? The real story behind Apple TV's Everest film
body: On May 29, 1953, two men stood at the summit of Mount Everest, becoming the first people confirmed to have reached the top of the world's highest mountain. One was Edmund Hillary , a New Zealand mountaineer whose name would become synonymous with the historic achievement. The other was Tenzing Norgay , an experienced Sherpa climber who had spent years attempting to conquer the mountain. Their extraordinary journey is the subject of Tenzing , a new Apple TV film that shifts the spotlight towards the man whose role in one of mountaineering's greatest achievements has not always received equal attention. Directed by Jennifer Peedom, the film stars Genden Phuntsok as Norgay, Tom Hiddleston as Hillary and Willem Dafoe as John Hunt, the British expedition leader. It was released in select cinemas on October 9 and begins streaming globally on Apple TV on Friday. But Tenzing is more than a recreation of the dangerous climb. It also explores the cultural divisions within the expedition, Norgay's determination to be recognised as a mountaineer rather than simply a guide, and his deeply personal relationship with Everest . Who was Tenzing Norgay? Born around 1914, Norgay came from a Sherpa family in the Himalayan region, although details of his birthplace remain disputed. Accounts of his early life differ, with some placing his birth in Nepal and others in Tibet . What is clear is that he grew up close to the mountains that would come to define his life. He eventually moved to Darjeeling in India, which had become an important base for mountaineering expeditions attempting to explore the Himalayas . Norgay began working on Everest expeditions in 1935, initially carrying supplies for foreign climbers. Over the following years, he developed into an exceptionally skilled mountaineer, learning to navigate treacherous terrain and work at altitudes where even breathing became difficult. Despite being unable to read or write, he spoke several languages and became an important figure in organising and leading Sherpa climbing teams. By the time he joined the British expedition in 1953, Norgay had already attempted to reach Everest's summit six times. A year earlier, he had come close during a Swiss expedition alongside Raymond Lambert, reaching approximately 8,600 metres before being forced to turn back. His seventh attempt, alongside Hillary, would finally prove successful. How does Apple TV's Tenzing tell his story? Unlike many accounts of the 1953 expedition, which have traditionally focused on Hillary or the wider British effort, Tenzing approaches the historic climb from Norgay's perspective. The film follows his determination to be recognised as a full member of the expedition, rather than simply someone employed to assist the western climbers. His wife Dawa, played by Thinley Lhamo, is portrayed as an important source of encouragement, while Caitríona Balfe plays expedition secretary Jill Henderson, who supports his efforts to secure a place on the climbing team. Australian filmmaker Peedom, whose previous work includes the 2015 documentary Sherpa , has described the film as an opportunity to place Norgay at the centre of a story in which he has often been overshadowed. To prepare for their roles, Phuntsok and Hiddleston travelled to Nepal and trekked towards Everest Base Camp , meeting Sherpa mountaineers and learning more about the region and its climbing history. Norgay's son Norbu Tenzing is an executive producer of the film, bringing a direct family connection to the production. Tenzing is now streaming on Apple TV

title: Matchbox: The Movie (Apple TV)
body: Inspired by Mattel’s Matchbox toy cars, this action-adventure stars John Cena as Sean, an undercover CIA agent who returns to his small hometown after a long absence and reunites with the group of childhood friends he once led. title: Investor confidence in Gulf remains strong despite war, says World Economic Forum's regional chief
body: Investor confidence in the region remains strong despite the fall-out from the Iran war , with efforts to diversify economies helping to shield them from the crisis, a senior World Economic Forum official has said. Kelsey Goodman, head of Middle East and North Africa at the World Economic Forum (WEF), told The National that the region’s economic fundamentals remained solid despite geopolitical uncertainty. Her comments come as the International Monetary Fund sharply downgraded its 2026 growth forecasts for Gulf economies amid the effects of the war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. “There’s still widespread investor confidence in the region,” Ms Goodman said. “The fundamentals are solid even if the surrounding area is uncertain, but it calls for the need for dialogue and co-operation and hopefully a return to peace and resiliency in the region.” Speaking at the Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders in Dubai , which concluded on Thursday, Ms Goodman said efforts to diversify Gulf economies had helped them withstand recent shocks and would be crucial to their recovery. “Diversification really is key, and the companies and the economies that have been able to have already built in diversity into their plan are the ones that have been most resilient," she said. "Resiliency is something that you have to prepare for. It's not something that you can build only in times of crisis.” Foresight simulations were carried out at the meeting on Thursday, in which participants rehearsed responses to unfolding geopolitical and technological crises. “This meeting has really emphasised that dialogue and co-operation are not luxuries for easy times. They're essential precisely when the world is at its most complicated,” said Ms Goodman. Even with this in mind, she said the mood at the meeting was positive. “I think it speaks to the resiliency of Dubai, and we hope that the participants are leaving with a message of hope and renewed belief in the power of moving from foresight into action,” she said. Economic diversification into AI In recent years, the UAE has prioritised artificial intelligence investments, with trillions of dollars earmarked for the technology, including building data centres. A newly published WEF report showed the potential of artificial intelligence in unlocking upwards of $1 trillion by 2030 in the region. Ms Goodman believes the investments countries are making in the AI sphere could return, but that regional uncertainty creates more barriers to reaching these goals. “For the economies to realise this value, it's going to take a lot of co-operation across all sectors of society,” she said. “That's going to include long-term planning from governments, but also having the regulation, the energy infrastructure, and the business applications for these new technologies.” Impacted labour markets While blocked trade routes have affected shipping and petrol prices have risen, Ms Goodman said the war's impact on the travel and tourism sector could also affect labour markets, especially given the high numbers of migrant workers in the country. The UAE workforce is made up of approximately 8.7 million migrant workers. “The Gulf really relies on a very mobile labour market with a lot of connections outside the region,” she said. “These are areas where there could potentially be short a ges.”

title: FM Sybiha: Ukraine plans to buy weapons from Poland by year-end using EUR 125M loan
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke about this in an interview with Ukrinform .
According to him, the Polish side has decided to provide a €125 million loan for the purchase of weapons from a Polish manufacturer. He noted that this was confirmed to him by Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, and that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk had also discussed the matter.
“We understand that, for example, the Piorun MANPADS is an extremely effective weapon. Ukraine is interested in purchasing this weaponry using the loan. We are currently discussing how to finalize this agreement. I hope this will happen in the near future—by the end of the year—since there is political will for it, and funds have been allocated in Poland’s budget,” Sybiha said.
He added that this issue is currently being resolved at the level of the finance and defense ministries of both countries, specifically regarding the list of products that Ukraine will purchase from Poland.
The head of Ukrainian diplomacy emphasized that such cooperation is beneficial to both sides. According to him, it is also beneficial for Poland, as the funds will support its defense-industrial complex, and the products supplied to Ukraine will be tested on the battlefield. This will mean that they will be improved, and thanks to positive feedback from Ukrainians, this will undoubtedly help Polish products enter new markets and expand their reach.
Sybiha also emphasized Ukraine’s readiness to deepen defense cooperation with Poland, in particular to conclude the “Drone Deal”—an agreement on cooperation in the field of unmanned systems. He noted that it will be signed once both sides have agreed on the terms.
“What matters here is the substance, not the timeline, but we are ready. Joint production is also important, and we are ready for that as well. Poland is one of the largest recipients of the European SAFE program. Here, too, we are ready to work together on a mutually beneficial basis,” the head of Ukrainian diplomacy emphasized.
Sybiha noted that during his visit to Warsaw, he discussed the entire agenda of Ukrainian-Polish relations with his Polish counterpart, Radosław Sikorski, including joint defense projects.
“I’ve said this before: we’ve managed to normalize bilateral relations after the well-known difficulties. That is how it should be between strategic partners, because we must be able to share the joy of joint achievements, but also jointly overcome the difficulties that arise,” the Ukrainian minister stated.
As reported by Ukrinform, Sybiha participated in the Warsaw Security Forum on Octo ber 13.

title: 'Shoot the Jews': Two years after Sinwar's death, IDF releases letter from Sinwar's 10-year-old son
body: The IDF released a letter on Thursday, written by Yahya Sinwar's son Ibrahim at the start of the Israel-Hamas War, in which the then-10-year-old expressed his desire to hold a Kalashnikov rifle and "shoot the Jews."The letter, which was addressed to his father, was recovered by IDF soldiers in Gaza in 2024, the military said, releasing it ahead of the second anniversary of Sinwar's death.Written on lined paper, the letter featured a Spider-Man sticker in its lower-left corner. The image of the Marvel superhero appeared alongside the child's handwritten message about making weapons and his desire to “shoot the Jews.”The 10-year-old's letter also depicted drawings of weapons, tanks, and missiles. The IDF did not comment specifically on the Spider-Man sticker.In the letter, Ibrahim wrote that he missed his father and wished he could “hug you [Yahya Sinwar] and see you victorious.”He also described making pistols, tanks, and Kalashnikovs out of paper and cardboard in his spare time.“I wish to grow up, hold a Kalashnikov, and shoot the Jews,” Ibrahim wrote.He also asked his father when he would return home to sleep with his arms around him and hoped the war would end and that his father would be safe.“Oh Lord, may the war end and may I see you well. May God protect you, Dad. All I ask of you is your prayers.”Sinwar's 'murderous ideology' reflected in his son, IDF saysThe IDF said the letter and drawings illustrated "Sinwar's murderous ideology is reflected in the upbringing of his children, revealing the impact of Hamas' values of hatred and violence on the younger generation in the Gaza Strip."Sinwar, who led Hamas in Gaza and was considered one of the main architects of the October 7, 2023, massacre, was killed by Israeli soldiers in Rafah two years ago, on October 16, 2024.

title: Preparations for 2027 ​Asian ​Cup ​in Saudi Arabia 'progressing according to schedule'
body: The local organising ​committee of the 2027 Asian Cup said preparations for hosting the continental tournament in Saudi Arabia are going ahead as per schedule despite recent attacks in the kingdom. Saudi Arabia saw a number of events called off or postponed as fighting intensified between the kingdom and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels. Multiple attacks on airports in the country forced the Six Kings men's tennis tournament , scheduled for October 21-24, and the Fifa Esports final, set for October 16-25, to be postponed. Three matches in the Saudi Pro League this weekend were rescheduled to later in the season due to “logistical considerations”. Earlier, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said ‌it was open to the idea of ⁠delaying the Asian Cup until ​2028 if needed. The continental tournament is scheduled to ​kick ‌off on January 7 across venues in Riyadh, Jeddah ⁠and Al Khobar. However, ⁠the tournament's local organising committee said preparations are going ahead according to schedule. The Local Organising Committee for the AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027™️ confirms the continuation of preparations for the tournament pic.twitter.com/Jqlf9dtZyg — Saudi 2027 (@saudi2027) October 15, 2026 “Preparations across all organisational and operational areas are progressing according to the approved schedule, including work on venues, facilities and supporting services,” ​the organising committee ‌said, adding ⁠that the tournament ​remains on track to ​be ‌held from January 7 to ⁠February 5, 2027. “The LOC ⁠will continue to monitor ​developments relevant to the tournament and ​ensure ‌the appropriate conditions are in place for its successful ⁠delivery.” Earlier this week, AFC president Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said the confederation was in “no hurry” to decide ​whether the tournament needed to be postponed. “We ​can wait until the end of November. Things can change very quickly for ‌better or worse in the region and ⁠it is question of seeing what happens,” Al Khalifa told ​reporters in Zurich during the Fifa Council meeting. The Korea Football Association (KFA) said it was in ⁠communication with the AFC. “We are closely monitoring the situation in Saudi Arabia and plan to continue discussions regarding overall developments,” the KFA said in a statement. The previous Asian Cup was ​delayed by a year after China withdrew as hosts because of Covid-19 restrictions, with Qatar stepping in to stage the tournament in early 2024. Saudi International postponed The Asian Tour postponed its ​season-ending ​Saudi International ​⁠in the aftermath of ⁠attacks in Riyadh. "The decision to postpone was taken following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and ensuring the event is delivered to a standard befitting its international stature," an Asian Tour statement said. The $5 million ​flagship event, which is ‌sponsored by the ⁠Saudi Public Investment ​Fund (PIF), was scheduled to take ​place ‌at Riyadh Golf Club from November 18 ⁠to 21. "The PIF Saudi International is ⁠one of the most important events on the Asian Tour calendar and we look forward to seeing our players ​compete in Riyadh in the future," Asian Tour Commissioner Cho Minn Thant said.

title: Iran urges UK not to conceal its insecurity role in West Asia
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 16 (MNA) – Iranian foreign ministry spokesman has called on the British government not to conceal its destructive role in insecurity in the West Asian region by deflecting blame.
In response to the remarks raised by British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who labeled Iran’s defensive actions as "aggression", Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei, in a post on his X account late on Thursday, wrote that the UK government cannot conceal its destructive role in spread of insecurity in the West Asia by deflecting blame.
"The chaos engulfing our region is the consequence of unlawful interventions, including those backed or contributed to by the UK," he emphasized.
For the UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to portray Iran as the “aggressor” after two rounds of unlawful aggression against it in just nine months, even as it pursued negotiations, is a grotesque reversal of victim and aggressor, he said, adding, "It marks yet another low in the UK’s long record of hostile campaigns against Iran."
Baghaei pointed out, "It is as absurd as portraying Nazi Germany as a “defender of peace” while casting the UK and its allies in WWII as the aggressors!"

title: Iraqi parliament approves key cabinet posts, including US-sanctioned deputy PM
body: Iraq’s parliament voted to fill a series of long‑vacant cabinet posts late on Thursday, completing Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi’s government and approving a deputy prime minister who is under US sanctions . The government formation process has been completed five months after Mr Al Zaidi took office, with 11 key positions approved at a full parliamentary session in Baghdad. Those included the country's Defence Minister, Nayef Al Shammari, and Interior Minister Yasir Al Maliki. Mr Al Zaidi said in a statement that the completion of his cabinet marked the start of “accelerated, diligent work” and pledged to push ahead with the government’s policies . He said the regional conflict had posed exceptional economic and security challenges to Iraq. Politicians also endorsed Laith Al Khazali as one of three deputy prime ministers. He is the brother of Qais Al Khazali, leader of the Iran‑backed Asaib Ahl Al Haq militia. The US designated the group as a foreign terrorist organisation in 2020 and has accused it of attacks on US and coalition forces. Both brothers were named “specially designated global terrorists” and Laith was arrested by US forces in 2007 over allegations related to a January attack in Karbala that killed five American soldiers. Parliament approved two other deputy prime ministers – Mohammed Ali Tamim of the Sunni Taqadum Party and Asas Coalition leader Muhsin Al Mandalawi. Votes were postponed for the nominee for migration and displacement minister owing to disagreement among parties, politicians said. The nomination of Mr Al Khazali drew sharp criticism from Washington. Republican Representative Joe Wilson condemned the appointment , describing him as an “Iranian puppet whose militia killed Americans and Iraqis". “He is no better than ISIS, maybe even worse. It is outrageous but sadly not shocking that he has been appointed deputy PM of Iraq,” Mr Wilson wrote on X. Another controversial name is Mr Al Maliki, the son-in-law of former prime minister Nouri Al Maliki. When he was in power, Iraq lost nearly a third of its territory to ISIS in 2014, a collapse that ultimately forced him to resign. He is known to have strong connections with Iran and is often described as an influential power-broker in Iraqi politics. The nomination raises questions about how Iraq will manage its ties with the US. Sajad Jiyad, an Iraq expert with the Century Foundation, told The National that Shiite parties within the ruling coalition appear confident the appointments will not trigger a major rupture with Washington. Mr Jiyad said the move to nominate Mr Al Khazali might be to encourage other Iran‑aligned factions to integrate into state structures and dissolve their armed wings, by signalling that participation in formal politics can lead to senior government posts. Asaib Ahl Al Haq has grown into one of Iraq’s most influential Shia parties, now holding both ministerial positions and a deputy premiership. Mr Al Zaidi's government has pledged to introduce economic ⁠reforms and anti-corruption measures, as well as taking steps to strengthen state institutions. But many challenges lie ahead, including rebuilding an economy hit by regional instability, ​tackling endemic corruption and bringing Iran-backed armed groups under greater state control.

title: Zelensky meets Danish PM to discuss air defense and financial stability
body:
This was reported by the Office of the President, according to Ukrinform.
The leaders discussed in detail the threats posed by Russian escalation, particularly against Ukraine’s energy sector.
“It is clear that Russia has interpreted signals regarding the easing of sanctions as a green light to continue attacking residential buildings, substations, and any other infrastructure that supports normal life. It is now of the utmost importance for everyone in Europe to mobilize to provide additional protection against this brutal terror as winter approaches,” Volodymyr Zelensky noted.
The president emphasized that Ukraine’s top priority is air defense—primarily anti-ballistic defense and anything that helps intercept “Shahed” drones.
Volodymyr Zelensky and Mette Frederiksen also discussed how Denmark could provide financial support to bolster Ukraine’s resilience. They agreed that their teams would continue working on this at their respective levels.
As reported by Ukrinform, Volodymyr Zelensky discussed with the Belgian prime minister additional deliveries of F-16 fighter jets and ammunition for th em.

title: Ukraine Plans More Powerful Drone Campaign to Paralyze Russian Airports – The Atlantic
body:
Ukraine is preparing to escalate its campaign to disrupt Russian airports, deploying AI-guided drones capable of evading air defenses and striking aviation infrastructure directly.
The operation, codenamed “M&Ms,” was developed under former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and envisioned using small, low-cost drones capable of navigating and identifying targets without human operators, according to two sources familiar with the plan.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The drones would carry detailed maps and images of designated targets, allowing their onboard computers to compare live camera footage with stored data. Once a target was identified, a drone would dive into it and detonate without requiring further confirmation from an operator, the report said.
The upcoming operation is expected to be significantly more aggressive, with drones that do not depend on US intelligence and could soon enter mass production, Ukrainian officials told The Atlantic .
The Ukrainian official also said a drone prototype had already been used in combat in the Donbas, although development is ongoing. The drones have not yet been deployed against Russian airports.
The current campaign has already disrupted air travel across Moscow. Between Oct. 3 and 9, Russian airports canceled 345 flights and delayed nearly 4,000, with some passengers facing waits of 10 hours or more.
On Oct. 10, another 692 flights were delayed and 93 canceled. On Oct. 14, 238 flights were delayed and 124 canceled. Moscow’s airport network was shut down for an average of around three hours daily, according to the report.
Even Russian President Vladimir Putin’s plane was reportedly unable to land in Moscow on Oct. 9 while returning from Turkmenistan, as two of the capital’s four airports were closed for seven hours during a drone attack.
Prolonged airport shutdowns could force international carriers, including Turkish Airlines and Emirates, to reconsider flights to the Russian capital, disrupting a key connection between Russia’s political elite and the outside world.
The plan was reportedly presented to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in early 2026. Although he raised concerns about risks to civilian aircraft, passengers and airport workers, he allowed preparations to continue, according to The Atlantic’s earlier report.
The planned escalation comes amid growing tensions between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
Last week, on Oct. 9, Trump announced an agreement for Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets, drawing criticism from US lawmakers and European allies.
Zelensky described the deal as a “ simple victory ” for the Kremlin in an interview with British broadcaster Piers Morgan on Wednesday.
“It’s a pity that we are losing a strong partner,” Zelensky said.
He also accused Trump of taking Russia’s side in the war, arguing that Washington should remain neutral rather than favor Moscow.
“This is our country, our body, our home, our children,” Zelensky said. “That’s why it’s painful when Trump chooses one side.”
Trump called for a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure and announced what he called a mutual energy ceasefire.
However, Russia continued striking Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, with missile and drone attacks leaving hundreds of thousands of people without electricity.
Ukraine had temporarily suspended strikes on Russian refineries at Washington’s request. Kyiv argued that any energy truce must apply to both sides, rather than restrict Ukraine’s ability to retaliate while Moscow continues attacking its power grid.
On Oct. 14, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times that Kyiv would no longer observe the pause in refinery strikes.
“The block [on attacking refineries] is out. We’re done,” Zelensky said.
Ukraine struck an oil refinery in Russia’s Ryazan Oblast early on Oct. 15, triggering a fire at the facility about 300 kilometers (186 miles) southeast of Moscow.
Later that day, Trump called Ukraine’s decision to resume refinery strikes a “disgrace,” accusing Kyiv of driving up global energy prices in an interview with Newsmax.
“Well, I think that’s a disgrace,” Trump said when asked about the renewed attacks.
Energy analysts, however, say Trump’s deal to resume Russian diesel exports is unlikely to significantly lower fuel prices.
The main driver of the global price surge has been the US-Israel war with Iran, which has disrupted oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump also portrayed Zelensky as a greater obstacle to ending Russia’s war against Ukraine than Putin.
“It should end soon. I think they actually both would like to see it end,” Trump said. “But I think I find Zelensky to be more difficult to deal with than Putin.”
Zelensky met NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Brussels on Oct. 15 and held talks with European leaders ahead of the EU summit, seeking continued military and political support for Ukraine.
“Don’t attack us. Don’t kill our children. We will stop attacking your diesel,” Zelensky said in an Oct. 11 interview with ABC News, outlining Kyiv’s position on a reciprocal energy ceasefire.
Trump, however, has not publicly objected to Ukrainian attacks on Russian airports or data centers, which Ukrainian forces targeted last week, The Atlantic reported.
When Trump first called Zelensky last month, he reportedly suggested that Kyiv could strike targets other than oil refineries.
“There are many other targets,” Trump said.
According to The Atlantic, Trump is becoming less interested in mediating between Moscow and Kyiv and increasingly appears to be pursuing a deal on the Kremlin’s behalf.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: If Iran rights not respected, Hormuz Strait to remain closed
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 16 (MNA) – Army Commander-in-Chief Major General Amir Hatami has said should the inalienable rights of the Iranian nation are not observed, restrictions regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz will continue.
He made the remarks at the closing ceremony of the 11th National Itikaf (Religious & Spiritual Seclusion with Divine) Congress and 8th International Scientific, Literary and Artistic Itikaf Festival, held at Imam Ali (AS) Officers’ Academy’s Mosque in Tehran late on Thursday, emphasizing that if enemy fails to respect the rights of the Irania nation, restrictions will continue in the Strait of Hormuz.
Mejor General Hatami termed four pillars of Iran’s power as: "people, the Armed Forces, the governance structures, and its geopolitical position", stressing that all these components have caused the enemy’s calculations to completely fail.
Referring to the role played by the noble people of the country during the early days of the outbreak of war imposed by US and Israel against the country, he added, “Relying on their own capabilities, the noble nation of the Islamic Iran entered the fray spontaneously and this issue has also been emphasized by Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei.”
He stressed that the strait is under the complete supervision of Iran’s armed forces. The western section is managed by the IRGC Navy, while the eastern section and the Sea of Oman are controlled by the Army Navy. Claims that the waterway is open are false, he said. Traffic has been sharply restricted, and no hostile vessel has been able to enter Iranian maritime zones in the area except for a few that were engaged with multiple firings.
Generally speaking, people played a leading and outstanding role, in the war imposed against the country, in thwarting the enemies’ miscalculations and plots, the Army chief commander highlighted.
Hatami termed the Armed Forces as the second component of the country's power, stating, "The Armed Forces responded to the enemy with full force, and in the very early hours of the war, salvoes of missiles were fired towards the enemy’s positions.”
The Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) continued their operations despite the martyrdom of a large number of commanders and officials and these events did not hinder the ongoing operational activities of the Armed Forces, General Hatami emphasized.
Should the enemy fail to respect the rights of the Iranian nation, restrictions regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz will continue, he reiterated.
Iranian forces seized operational control of the Strait of Hormuz in response to the start of the US-Israeli aggression on February 28. Tehran has repeatedly stated that coordinated passage is possible only for non-hostile vessels after authorization from Iranian authorities, while hostile shipping linked to the aggressors remains barred. Illegal routes created by violators have also been targeted for closure.

title: Finland to introduce mobile phone emergency alert system in November
body:
A new system will send emergency warnings directly to mobile phones in affected areas, without requiring users to install an app or share personal information.
Emergency warnings will be sent directly to mobile phones in Finland under a new system called FI-Alert, according to the Ministry of Interior in a press release .
The system will complement Finland's existing emergency warnings by enabling authorities to send alerts almost instantly to phones in specific affected areas.
Currently, emergency warnings are available through the 112 Suomi and Yle apps, radio and television broadcasts, teletext page 112, and the 112.fi and yle.fi websites. Authorities can also use public warning sirens.
The new system is being introduced as authorities seek to improve their ability to reach the public quickly during emergencies, amid a changing security situation.
FI-Alert is based on Cell Broadcast technology and the EU Alert concept.
Such technology allows mobile phones to receive alerts without users having to share personal information, such as their phone number or location data.
The only requirements are that the phone is switched on and configured to receive Cell Broadcast messages. No app needs to be installed in advance, and users do not need to subscribe to the service.
The technology uses a distinctive sound to draw attention to alerts, even when a phone is set to silent. Messages appear on the phone screen automatically and remain there until the user acknowledges them.
The ministry has previously stated that the system is suited to emergency situations because it does not place the same strain on mobile networks as mass text-message distribution.
Similar systems are already in use or being developed in several European countries, and the Ministry of the Interior says the technology is becoming the most common way of using mobile phones to warn the public.
In August, the government proposed amending the law on emergency warnings to allow alerts to be sent using Cell Broadcast technology. President Alexander Stubb is expected to approve this legislation on Friday and bring it into force at the beginning of November.

title: The Folders Programming Language
body:
Created 2015 | Updated 2026 | One of Forty-Four Esolangs , by the creator of Rivulet and Velato Where directories are code and drive space is infinite About Folders is a non-textual language, where code is expressed in containment and order alone. The names of the folders are ignored, apart from alphabetical ordering. In other words, they are pure ordered trees . Inspired by the Whitespace language, Folders is devoted to the idea of dematerialized code. It began with the question What is more empty than a file with no visible text? The empty folder is clutter, an appendage with no purpose. In git, it is ignored entirely (for this reason, it is suggested that Folders programs put .gitignore files in their deepest reaches). Folders began as a Windows language. In Windows, folders are an even more extreme measure of emptiness: they take up no disk space at all. For proof, create 352,449 folders and get properties on it. In this way, Folders offers not only a dematerialized approach to code but also infinite storage capacity. Keep all your data encoded in folder names and never worry about running out of space again. For those who use other operating systems, the emulator below gives some of the experience of how Folders manages data and code. The original implementation can be found on github . Encoding Each command folder has at least one child folder. The number of subfolders in the first folder (alphabetically) indicates the type of command; any arguments are indicated in a second folder; some commands require a third folder. Expressions are the same: the number of folders in the first sub-folder determine what kind of expression it is. The full Language Spec is below . Temporary data is stored as folders; unlike Folders code, it is the name of the folder that stores the data. Animation of Program Parsing Here a program is built one folder at a time, starting with the outermost folder. Each folder's first subfolder fills in before the rest, setting what it means; after every folder is added, the program is read again as pseudocode. Strings change letter by letter as their bits are filled in. Folders FS The Folders interpreter does not create temp files; anything not held immediately in memory is stored as a set of temp folders. Unlike Folders code, the name of the folder stores the data itself. The prefered I/O of Folders is another set of folders. This means you can encode all your data in folders, bypassing the "material realm" of files entirely and giving you infinite disk space (attempt at your own risk). Folders lang for code, Folders FS for data storage. Temp folders from several Folders programs Visualizations A Folders program is a nil-terminated nested list . Its simplest form is pure containment and order, like this all-array JSON: [[[[],[]],[],[[]]],[[[],[]],[],[[],[]]],[[[],[]],[],[[],[],[]]],[[[],[]],[],[[],[],[],[]]],[[[],[],[]],[[]],[[[],[],[],[],[]],[],[[[],[],[],[]]]]],[[[],[],[]],[[],[]],[[[],[],[],[],[]],[],[[[],[],[],[[]]]]]],[[[],[],[]],[[],[],[],[]],[[[],[],[],[],[]],[],[[[],[],[],[]]]]],[[[]],[[[],[],[],[],[],[],[],[]],[[],[[],[],[],[]]],[[[],[],[],[],[]],[],[[[],[],[],[[]]],[[[]],[[]],[[]],[]]]]],[[[[],[],[],[]],[[],[[]]]],[[[],[],[],[]],[[[],[],[],[],[]],[[],[],[]],[[[[]],[],[[]],[]]]]],[[[],[],[]],[[],[],[]],[[[]],[[],[[]]],[[],[[],[]]]]],[[[],[],[]],[[]],[[],[[],[]]]],[[[],[],[]],[[],[]],[[],[[],[],[]]]],[[[],[],[]],[[],[],[],[]],[[[]],[[],[[],[],[],[]]],[[[],[],[],[],[]],[],[[[],[],[],[[]]]]]]]]]] Fibonacci Program That is also how the JS emulator saves/reads Folders programs. However, other systems of visualization are possible. Folders programs are content as structure and can be applied to raw data of any type. Here is a Truth Machine as a contour map. The thicker lines are containers, and the order of folders is read starting at the upper left (NW corner) and proceeding counter-clockwise. Truth Machine Truth Machine (Detail) Other visualizations might be a family tree (with all single parents), a botanical branching structure (like a splitting stalk of wheat), or the paths through a maze. Truth Machine Simple Echo The red dots indicate a threshhold from a container to a single child. Language Spec The language itself is a very simple imperative language with a short list of semantic rules. For Commands and Expressions, the number of folders in their first child folder determines their use. Types are used directly. Commands Command # of Folders Details if 0 folders Second sub-folder holds expression, third holds list of commands while 1 folder Second sub-folder holds expression, third holds list of commands declare 2 folders Second sub-folder holds type, third holds var name (in number of folders) let 3 folders Second holds var name (in number of folders), third holds expression print 4 folders Second sub-folder holds expression input 5 folders Second sub-folder holds var name Expressions Type # of Folders Details variable 0 folders Second sub-folder holds var name add 1 folder Second sub-folder holds first expression to add, third holds second expression subtract 2 folders Second sub-folder holds first expression to subtract, third holds second expression multiply 3 folders Second sub-folder holds first expression to multiply, third holds second expression divide 4 folders Second sub-folder holds first expression to divide, third holds second expression literal value 5 folders Second sub-folder holds the type of the value (e.g. two folders for a string, third holds the value) equal to 6 folders Second and third folders hold expressions to compare greater than 7 folders Second and third folders hold expressions to compare less than 8 folders Second and third folders hold expressions to compare Types Type # of Folders float 1 folder string 2 folders char 3 folders Links Discussed on Hacker News (2026): https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50114342 The reference compiler on github: https://github.com/rottytooth/Folders
