Google is updating its AI search results to make inline links appear “higher up in responses more frequently,” according to a blog post . The company’s search results from AI Overviews and AI Mode give you answers in a customized view instead of the traditional list of links, but there are concerns that the format reduces traffic to publishers . Google says it’s been making “continued and substantial increases to the presence of inline links in our AI experiences,” and this new change will help ensure “ensure key sources are easily clickable right when you need them.”
The company is announcing several other changes to highlight links and publishers within its AI results. For sites that are among a few for a specific task or certain information — an example image from Google highlights a query about an airline refund — Google is testing showing the relevant links at the top of a response with context. For “timely” articles, the company is now rolling out the link carousels announced in May to more locations and languages. Google is making links at the end of a query “more engaging and prominent, with image thumbnails and a more clickable design.” And it’s now testing clickable links in AI mode to search profiles for publishers and creators.
Google also says that more than 400 publishers are participating in its “News AI” pilot program, which it announced in December . The licensing program pays publishers for “the delivery and use of enhanced content to develop new AI features,” including “in-depth article overviews on Google News publisher pages,” and Axios , CNN , and the Financial Times are among the partners that are newly onboard, according to Google.

title: Why would Hezbollah admit its explosives were smuggled into Lebanon? - analysis
body: Hezbollah appeared to admit on Thursday that it is the owner of more than 500 kilograms of explosives that were seized by Lebanese authorities.It appears that this is one of several recent attempts at smuggling explosives, and conflicting information is circulating. Nevertheless, Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has called for “no leniency” and for “truth and accountability” in this incident.“The vehicle and its cargo belong to the resistance,” Hezbollah lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said. He noted that his organization also called for the immediate release of those arrested over the seizure, according to the AFP and Reuters.This marks a rare admission by Hezbollah and follows several days of questions about the shipment of explosives. Al-Ain media, based in the United Arab Emirates, noted that “the Lebanese Hezbollah party has acknowledged that a shipment of explosive materials seized by Lebanese authorities this week belongs to it.”Fadlallah indicated that the explosives belong to “the party,” which is a euphemism for Hezbollah.Shipment seized by Lebanese army carried C4 plastic explosives“Lebanese authorities opened investigations that began with the judicial police and expanded to include military intelligence and the information branch of the Internal Security Forces,” Al-Ain added, based on a Reuters report.This follows a shipment that was seized earlier this week. Reports indicated the shipment had been smuggled from Syria. At the time, the Lebanese army claimed it had found the explosive materials in the Qasr area of Hermel, packed inside bags and prepared for smuggling from Syrian territory into Lebanese territory. Lebanon attempted to make it appear that the smugglers had fled to Syria. It was not clear whether this was true. Damascus has halted attempts by Hezbollah to smuggle weapons through Syria over the past year.The reports this week said that the explosive material consisted of C4 and that it had been moved by donkey. It was unclear from reports how many donkeys were used to move the material.Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam praised Lebanon's efforts to identify “all those involved and the parties behind the shipment and to determine their plans and objectives, in preparation for referring them to the judiciary,” Al-Ain media noted. The same report said that Lebanon and Syria are trying to prevent smuggling along their roughly 330 km. of shared border, where there are dozens of illegal crossings.Lebanese authorities seem to want to make a show of cracking down on explosives smuggled to Hezbollah. However, they don't want to actually mention Hezbollah by name. The goal may be to indicate to the US that Lebanon is doing “something” to stop smuggling.It's convenient for Lebanon to make it seem that the smugglers flee to Syria, which means they need not be charged with crimes in Lebanon. This narrative can also be used to depict Syria negatively.Hezbollah invaded Syria in 2012 to back the Assad regime against Syrian rebels. When it fell in 2024, Hezbollah had to flee Syria. Since then, there have been discussions about whether Syria might intervene against Hezbollah in Lebanon. While some in the Trump administration discussed this, Damascus appears reluctant to intervene, as it is still rebuilding after years of war.Salam said this week, “It has become known that a few days ago, a truck was stopped in the town of Zahle, heading from the Bekaa Valley to the Greater Beirut area, containing hundreds of kilograms of explosives, including the highly explosive C-4 substance.” The Lebanese president praised the actions of the security forces.“I understand the anxiety gripping the Lebanese people upon the news of this truck's interception and the materials it was transporting, especially since C-4 has been used in several of the infamous political assassinations in modern Lebanese history,” Salam said.'We will not relent in pursuing the investigation... identify every individual involved'“But from my position as head of government, I call on all Lebanese to rest assured that we will not relent in pursuing the investigation and expanding it to identify every individual involved in this criminal operation, as well as those behind them, uncover their plans and objectives and bring them all to justice to receive the punishment they deserve.”The reality in Lebanon is that Hezbollah appears to be challenging Salam. They know that the politicians in Lebanon are afraid to condemn Hezbollah. The terror organization wants to see if it can continue to get away with smuggling.The smuggling incident comes amid an attempt to intimidate Lebanon's Ambassador to the United States, Nada Hamadeh Moawad. A complaint about her was filed with Lebanon's military judiciary by a lawyer believed to be pro-Hezbollah. The US has been critical of this complaint.Naharnet media in Lebanon said that the “state Commissioner to the Military Court Judge Claude Ghanem has decided to dismiss the complaint filed by pro-Hezbollah lawyer Hassan Bazzi against Lebanese Ambassador to the US Nada Hamadeh Moawad, MTV reported on Thursday.”Hezbollah's aim is to attempt to intimidate Lebanese officials who meet with American and Israeli officials.It is worth noting, Naharnet added, that “Lebanon's boycott law, adopted in 1955, prohibits direct and indirect dealings with Israeli individuals or entities, including commercial, financial, and cultural institutions. It carries prison sentences ranging from several years to harsher penalties under the broader criminal code.”The current situation in Lebanon is that Hezbollah remains in the country and is a threat.Despite rounds of talks, the Lebanese government is not able to rein in Hezbollah, and it continues to challenge the state. It wants to show that it can continue to stockpile explosives.The group was likely linked to the Beirut Port blast in 2020, but was never held accountable. Hezbollah also murdered former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafic Hariri in 2005 and was not held accountable, despite years of investigation.

title: Iran facing growing insurgency in separatist, largely Sunni, Sistan-Balochistan region - analysis
body: Iran continues to clash with rebels in its Balochistan region, according to numerous reports. This follows several weeks of growing unrest in the region – the Sistan and Balochistan province of Iran. Little is known about the situation because media is not allowed in the area, and Iran keeps a tight lid on information. Nevertheless, videos that have appeared over the last two weeks, along with reports, appear to indicate a growing insurgency.Recently, an Iranian commander and a police officer were reportedly killed in clashes. Haalvsh, a human rights group, said that “both casualties were from Zabol district.” It identified them as “Afsaneh Aqila, a female commander of the all-women's Basij unit in Mehrestan County and Mohammad Ali Shahriari, a male police officer.”On October 1, videos shared on social media showed smoke billowing from fighting in the area of Zahedan city.Now, the Kurdish media outlet Rudaw has reported that “Iranian forces deployed around 40 additional vehicles to Taftan county in southeastern Sistan and Balochistan province on Tuesday, a Baluch rights monitor reported, as clashes between Iranian security forces and militants continue.”A human rights group that covers the Baloch region said it has documented the arrival of more regime forces to the region, as well as fighting between the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and local rebels. “As the clashes intensified, approximately 40 additional military vehicles carrying reinforcements were reportedly dispatched to the area on Tuesday,” Rudaw said.Iranian security forces suffer casualties amid clashes with Baloch rebelsThe reports indicated that not much is known about the results of the clashes, notably the number of casualties on both sides. “The reported deployment of reinforcements and other details have not been independently verified,” it said.However, Rudaw added, “More than a dozen Iranian military and police personnel were killed or wounded in four attacks over a 24-hour period last week, according to Haalvsh.”Iranian state media also reported on the clashes. The regime views the Baloch rebels as “terrorists.” Fars News in Iran, which is linked to the IRGC, described clashes on Tuesday, saying “initial reports indicated that several militants had been killed during the operation. The reported casualties could not be independently verified, and it was unclear whether the incident was connected to the clashes in Taftan.”TodayPress.TV, a media organization based in Azerbaijan, noted that “a bloody crackdown by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is reportedly unfolding in the Sistan and Balochistan region, where assassinations are being carried out almost daily.”It added: “Several militant groups have joined forces in the region and claim to be fighting for control of all of Iran. However, at least one of these groups has historically been associated with Baloch separatism and follows a distinctly conservative Sunni ideology.”Reports point to escalating IRGC crackdown in BalochistanTodayPress.TV noted the scale of the fighting: “IRGC members, Basij forces, clerics affiliated with the regime, and foreign militants have been targeted. Police stations, military bases, and checkpoints have come under attack, while patrols have also been targeted. Clashes have reportedly extended as far as Kerman Province.”Meanwhile, The Arab Weekly asked whether fighting might become Iran's “Achilles heel.” This indicates that many people in the region are watching closely what happens in southeastern Iran, some 10 months after the Islamic Republic's brutal crackdown on protests in January 2026, with tens of thousands of people murdered.The Arab Weekly explained: “Sistan and Balochistan Province lies in Iran's far southeast and is the country's second-largest province by area, after Kerman. It consists of two main regions: Sistan, whose population is predominantly Shia, and Balochistan, which is considerably larger than Sistan, accounts for most of the province's territory, and has a predominantly Sunni population.”It added that “if we classify the regions inhabited by Iran's non-Persian national and ethnic communities according to their national identities and geographical characteristics, rather than the country's official administrative divisions, we can speak of Balochistan as a distinct region within Iran.“This region extends beyond the Baloch-inhabited areas of Sistan and Balochistan Province to include parts of Kerman Province where Baloch communities also live,” The Arab Weekly said.Iran launches new operations as Baloch insurgency continuesIran's IRGC continues to portray itself as able to “dismantle” what it calls “terrorist cells” in the Balochistan region.A recent report at Al-Monitor said, “Iran's IRGC announced a new operation against armed militants in the southeastern province of Sistan and Baluchistan, which is witnessing almost daily attacks and clashes.” The Baloch groups in southeastern Iran include the Sunni militant group Jaish al-Adl.Meanwhile, across the border in Pakistan, Baloch armed groups are fighting the Pakistani government. This week, the Baloch Liberation Army in Pakistan said it had carried out numerous attacks.On Monday, that army was reported to have “carried out 16 organized and intense attacks against the occupying Pakistani military in various regions of Balochistan over the past six days, inflicting severe personnel and material losses on the enemy.”

title: Ship Fuel Market Fragments as Middle East Conflict Hits Trade
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran, May 22, 2026. Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS
(Bloomberg) — Shipowners are facing an increasingly fragmented fuel market as disruptions triggered by the Middle East conflict raise concerns about the availability and quality of supply.
Ships can’t always refuel at familiar ports if they’re forced on longer journeys around Africa and diverted to the Atlantic Basin to avoid escalating hostilities near the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. That’s turned other locations into so-called bunkering hubs and driven up fuel prices.
“No one can treat bunkering as a routine, last-minute decision anymore,” said Frederik Guttormsen, Asia Pacific president at Stolt-Nielsen Ltd., an operator of 167 tankers that transport chemicals worldwide. “We’re securing fuel earlier and tracking availability and lead times at key ports because the risk is now as much about prompt supply as about price.”
Middle East oil flows are coming under renewed strain from recent attacks in the region, including on vessels transiting Hormuz. The disruptions are pushing oil and bunker prices higher, Guttormsen said. He made the comments on the sidelines of a shipping conference in Singapore known as Sibcon.
Singapore, the world’s biggest ship-refueling hub, continues to see growth, while vessels are tending to avoid Fujairah on the east coast of the United Arab Emirates, south of Hormuz. Other locations seeing higher bunkering demand since the US-Iran war include Port Louis in Mauritius, South Africa, West Africa, Brazil, Sri Lanka and Pakistan, according to participants at Sibcon.
Bunkering at less familiar ports may expose shipowners to smaller or less reputable sellers, as well as wider price disparities between locations. Differences can reflect factors including fuel sourcing, access to on-spec feedstock and the availability of support services needed to ensure quality and compliance.
“In this market, procurement needs to be much more structured,” said Kenneth Dam, executive director and global head of bunkering at TFG Marine, a major trader and supplier of ship fuels. Vessels are also refueling more frequently and taking smaller volumes at each stop to avoid locking in too much fuel at a particular price and port, he said.
Disruptions are also becoming more frequent, leading to vessel diversions that are shifting fuel demand to other locations, said Peter Grünwaldt, head of bunkering at tanker owner Hafnia Ltd. and co-chief executive officer of bunker trader Seascale Energy. “We’re making sure we have fuel available at these ports,” he said.

title: NRC IRAP Invests $135M in Defence and Dual-Use Technologies
body: Supporting Canadian innovators to scale technologies, strengthen supply chains and compete globally A strong and innovative defence sector is vital to Canada’s security, economic resilience and sovereignty. By investing in the development of made-in-Canada technologies, the Government of Canada is strengthening domestic supply chains, accelerating innovation, building capacity in critical sectors, and positioning small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to succeed in global markets. The Honourable Mélanie Joly, Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions, announced that the National Research Council of Canada Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP) has invested more than $135 million in defence and dual-use technologies since launching Defence Industry Assist (DI Assist). The initiative helps Canadian businesses understand the defence market and procurement processes, explore early-stage R&D ideas and refine, test or validate technologies that are closer to completion. READ: Larus Receives $800K from NRC IRAP to Advance ScenarioGPT From cybersecurity and communications infrastructure, to maritime and underwater systems, aerospace, drones and space, Canadian SMEs are advancing the critical technologies that will strengthen our economic and national sovereignty. Since its launch in January 2026, DI Assist has helped 860 Canadian SMEs, enabled over 540 innovation projects and supported more than 2,300 jobs across Canada. DI Assist supports innovation across all 10 key sovereign capabilities identified in Canada’s Defence Industrial Strategy (DIS). The investment and initiatives under the DIS are helping create 125,000 jobs, increase Canada’s defence exports by 50%, and position Canada’s defence economy at its strongest level in decades. Through NRC IRAP expertise, networks, and targeted funding, DI Assist is helping Canadian companies bring strategic technologies to market, support high-quality jobs, strengthen Canada’s industrial and innovation capacity, and contribute to Canada’s defence and security objectives. “In an increasingly dangerous and complex world, our government is investing in Canadian expertise to build a stronger and more resilient defence industrial base. Through NRC IRAP’s long-standing relationships with innovative Canadian businesses and its national reach, DI Assist has invested in Canadian companies who are building Canada’s defence future, innovating cutting-edge technologies, and contributing to Canada’s defence and security priorities.” — The Honourable Mélanie Joly, Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions “Canadian SMEs play a critical role in developing technologies that drive economic growth and national security. Building on the National Research Council of Canada’s long-standing role in advancing defence and security research, DI Assist is helping innovative businesses bring new ideas to market, strengthen Canada’s industrial capabilities and create opportunities across the country.” — Mitch Davies, President, National Research Council of Canada ADDITIONAL INFO In January 2026, the Government of Canada announced a $241 million investment in NRC IRAP to launch Defence Industry Assist (DI Assist), which has since provided advisory services and funding to 860 Canadian SMEs and supported more than 2,300 jobs. Seventy-nine percent of supported businesses have fewer than 50 employees, and about half were incorporated within the last 10 years. Nearly one-quarter are owned or led by women. For more than 75 years, NRC IRAP has supported Canadian business through its network of more than 250 industrial technology advisors who provided advisory services and funding to over 10,800 innovative Canadian SMEs in 2025-26. Under Canada’s Defence Industrial Strategy , the NRC is investing over $900 million to develop aerospace defence capabilities, support Canadian SMEs developing technologies for civilian and military purposes, and accelerate quantum technologies and defence applications. Canadian SMEs looking to explore DI Assist opportunities are encouraged to visit the website for more information. title: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ
body:
The Wall Street Journal reported that a company co-founded by Bo Hines benefited from the passage of the GENIUS stablecoin bill.
Bo Hines, previously a crypto adviser to US President Donald Trump who later joined stablecoin issuer Tether, reportedly kept a stake in a company that profited from the passage of a stablecoin bill when he was still at the White House.
According to a Wednesday report from The Wall Street Journal, Hines had a one-third stake in the investment company he co-founded, Nxum, while pushing US lawmakers to pass the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins, or GENIUS, Act. The legislation reportedly came amid Nxum receiving $6.3 million as part of a deal with stablecoin issuer Tether, behind the USDt (USDT) token, with the first payment going through while Hines was still serving in government.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Hines kept in contact with his partners at Nxum, updating them on progress with the GENIUS Act through the Signal app while serving as Trump’s crypto adviser.
He also reportedly pressed the Nxum partners to label any Republican lawmakers opposing the stablecoin bill as “undermining the president” and “bought and paid for by democratic shills like Coinbase and a16z.” Hines joined Tether as a “strategic adviser” in August 2025, becoming CEO of its US arm the following month.
The reported deal between a former White House official and a crypto company continues to shine a spotlight on accusations that Trump and his family and staff are personally benefitting from laws they help to draft and pass. The president disclosed earning $1.4 billion from investments tied to digital assets in 2025, which included millions of dollars from his family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial, behind the issuance of the USD1 stablecoin.
Related: EU lawmakers push crypto onto anti-corruption agenda
The GENIUS Act passed Congress and was signed into law in July 2025 in a ceremony attended by many cryptocurrency executives, including those behind stablecoins like Tether and Circle. Hines was in attendance and personally recognized by Trump at the event.
Though it was signed into law in 2025, the GENIUS stablecoin bill requires rules from government agencies overseeing the tokens, including the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Federal Reserve Board and Treasury Department. The law is scheduled to go into effect in January 2027.
Cointelegraph reached out to Tether for comment on the accusations in the report but did not receive an immediate response.
Several figures previously in government have left to become executives or advisers to digital asset companies. In addition to Hines joining Tether, Summer Mersinger, a former commissioner with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), resigned her position three years before her term was scheduled to end for a position as CEO of the crypto advocacy group Blockchain Association.
On Wednesday, Solidus Labs announced that Kevin Webb, a former CFTC senior counsel and adviser to former Commissioner Brian Quintenz, would join the fintech company as its vice president of policy. Webb isn’t the first former commissioner at the company, as the CFTC’s Dawn Stump left the agency in 2022 to join Solidus as a “strategic adviser.”

title: Zelensky Seeks Greater NATO Support as Starlink Restrictions Strain US Ties
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky opened his Brussels visit on Thursday, Oct. 15 by meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, urging allies for steady weapons deliveries as Russia continues increasing its strikes on Ukraine’s energy and civilian infrastructure nationwide.
The discussions centered on ballistic missile interceptors, ammunition for Ukraine’s F-16 fighter jets and new air defense packages from partners; all critically important as the country prepares for its fifth winter of war.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“All of these are significant challenges, especially against the backdrop of restrictions on Starlink’s operation in Ukraine,” Zelensky said , “which is why it is very important that defense supplies from NATO partners continue.”
The President arrived in Brussels to attend the European Council summit.
His schedule also includes meetings with French President Emmanuel Macron, the prime ministers of Poland, Denmark and Belgium, and an audience with King Philippe of Belgium.
On Friday, Oct. 16 he is set to meet the presidents of the European Council and European Commission, as well as the prime ministers of Hungary, Finland and Sweden.
Russia responded to the latest effort by US President Donald Trump to enforce a ceasefire by launching fresh waves of attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid, residential buildings and other critical infrastructure.
According to Zelensky, Russian forces carried out several ballistic missile barrages in recent days while Shahed attack drones remained in Ukrainian airspace almost continuously, with close to 1,000 drones launched since the start of Wednesday, Oct. 14.
Trump declared an immediate energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv on Oct. 11 on Truth Social media, claiming both sides had agreed, and called on Ukraine to stop its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Although neither side formally agreed and Ukrainian authorities appeared to find out about the truce by the news circulating online, Kyiv had refrained from striking Russia’s power infrastructure.
However, Russia increased its strikes significantly in recent days, with Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov saying on Oct. 14 that the truce was never defined, so Russia cannot be accused of breaking it .
His remarks came as Moscow’s latest strikes on Kyiv and Kharkiv’s power plants left at least 600,000 Ukrainian citizens without electricity.
Zelensky has since lifted Ukraine’s self-imposed pause on those strikes. “The block [on attacking refineries] is out. We’re done,” he told The Financial Times .
The pressure on Ukraine’s defenses is growing as Starlink satellite service faces restrictions in the country, making continued NATO supplies especially critical.
Overnight on Oct. 13-14, the US aerospace giant Starlink and its owner Elon Musk tweaked parameters and limited terminals above 160 kilometers per hour (roughly 100 miles per hour), disrupting Kyiv’s drone operations.
The move particularly crippled Ukraine’s key mid-range strike drones, used in strikes on Russian logistics.
It also disabled interceptor drones, used by Ukraine’s Defense Forces against Russian jet-powered Shaheds that are significantly harder to intercept due to their speed, reaching up to 400-600 kilometers per hour (250-370 miles per hour).
“It is clear that the Russians are trying to exploit problems with Starlink’s operation in Ukraine, as interceptor drones rely significantly on this connection,” Zelensky said after meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in London.
Around the same time, Musk said on Oct. 14 that the US military – including Trump himself – decides speed limits on Ukraine’s military Starshield terminals, not SpaceX.
US intelligence officials told Ukraine’s embassy in Washington that information sharing would stop immediately if Kyiv kept striking Russian energy targets, The Washington Post reported on Oct. 14, citing a person familiar with the matter.
The source said sharing had not been fully cut off.
Zelensky confirmed the warning reached the military rather than him directly. “They said this to my generals, not to me.”
Trump, for his part, insisted cooperation continues and denied that the US cut off intelligence , although Ukrainian forces received no partner warnings of Russian ballistic missile launches toward Kyiv on two consecutive nights at the beginning of the week.
Concerns about intelligence sharing grew after media reports that US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had warned Ukrainian negotiators during talks in Miami on Oct. 9 that Washington could suspend intelligence sharing should Kyiv continue targeting Russia’s energy infrastructure.
While the Ukrainian delegation was in Miami hoping to reach a breakthrough and broker an end to Russia’s aggression, Trump abruptly announced that he signed a diesel deal with the Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Shortly after, the US Treasury Department authorized the sale and import of Russian diesel fuel through April 7, 2027.
The new license came only three weeks after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law on Sept. 18, appearing to completely disregard the bill intended to target Russia’s energy and defense industries, as well as networks close to the Kremlin leader.
A bipartisan group of 12 US senators signed a joint letter on Oct. 13, urging Trump to rescind his diesel agreement with Putin, calling it a gift to Moscow and a betrayal of Ukraine.
They also joined Zelensky’s month-long appeals to utilize the sweeping sanctions.

title: More on Anthropic's Scion ripping off Mononoke
body:
Update: Nick G. from Anthropic has responded on Hacker News , and sufficient attribution has been added to Anthropic’s blog post. I stand by my posts as of the time I wrote them.
In response to yesterday’s post about Anthropic’s Scion ripping off Mononoke, I received a number of questions and concerns. Here’s a followup to answer the big ones.
This was a ripoff. My post yesterday was trying to be as charitable as possible given what I knew, and in particular that the similarity to Mononoke was mostly unintentional and the lack of credit was the result of not doing due diligence. However, after publishing the post I privately received confirmation that Scion intentionally and blatantly ripped off Mononoke, and in particular that there was overlap in personnel. There is no chance that this was an unintentional homage. This is something I had a hunch about but was not comfortable saying yesterday, given what I knew back then.
The resemblance is much deeper than just the notion of derived data. Some people pointed out that derived data is just an index, which is a well-known concept. I want to clarify that derived data was merely the most striking resemblance. It goes much deeper than that, and extends to the entire data model, as well as a number of the structures built around it.
Here is how Anthropic describes Scion changesets:
Mononoke has the same concept; we call it a Bonsai changeset. In the same Oxide materials from 2022, here’s how I described them:
They are exactly the same. Even the name “Scion” reverses the syllables of “Bonsai” and drops the “B”! This might be a coincidence, or might not.
For derived data, I also wanted to draw attention to the kinds of indexes being built, such as for blame. Needing to do this is a natural consequence of the Bonsai data model, so it’s not surprising that indexes need to be built; I was drawing attention to the striking similarity in terminology and framing, because that was indeed how we used to think about it during my time on Meta’s source control team.
Another set of resemblances is in the server-side API to do version control queries and mutations with. This was implemented in Mononoke, but I believe other systems before Mononoke had it as well, so I’m not going to claim novelty. But if what you did is point Claude at Mononoke and asked it to rebuild that, you would probably design something very similar.
The Bonsai data model is wildly contrarian. I want to emphasize that the prevailing wisdom in source control is Git-like data models. Building a write-ahead log-style Merkle DAG was very far away from what anyone else was doing in 2018, and required solving several hard problems along the way such as how to perform server-side rebases (to my knowledge, one of several novel algorithms in Mononoke). While I was leading the team effort to design and implement the model in 2018, I personally had to justify it to several layers of management at Meta. It is quite rare for skip levels to get pulled in to discuss a system’s data model in depth.
The Bonsai data model is also wildly successful. At this point, almost a decade later, the model has been stretched far outside its initial design parameters, and it’s still chugging along. The team effort to build it remains one of my proudest career achivements. Given the overlap in personnel, there is no reasonable way the Scion team could not have known about this. (Which is why they quite reasonably copied it!) This brings us to my next point:
The problem is attribution, not copying. I mentioned this in my original post, but I am completely fine with good ideas being copied. I am not fine with the serial numbers being accidentally stripped off, and I am certainly not fine with them being intentionally stripped off.
Crediting Sapling for “hard-won lessons” is not enough. Several people pointed out that Mononoke is part of the Sapling ecosystem. The problem here is that Sapling can mean either the VCS client ( sl , originally forked from hg ) or the system as a whole. If you were previously on Meta’s source control team, you absolutely know the difference between the two. Besides, the resemblance is much, much deeper than merely “hard-won lessons”. The Lore VCS can claim inspiration from Mononoke, but it differs in several ways as well. Scion’s resemblance to Mononoke goes well beyond that, and merely crediting Sapling (not even Mononoke) with “hard-won lessons” is dishonest. (And specifically, I would expect the Scion changeset section to mention Bonsai changesets as the thing they are copied from.)
This makes Anthropic’s achievement significantly less impressive. Anyone who’s put a distributed system into production knows how many issues tend to crop up during the productionizing process. “Our LLM built this thing, productionized it, and dealt with all the attendant challenges over 5 months” is a significantly more compelling narrative than “the source control team at Meta had spent 10 years building and productionizing this system, and we were able to point our LLM at it and rebuild it in 5 months”.
…and yet, it is still quite an achievement. Being able to point to an existing system and rebuild it in this short a period is still quite stunning. It is shocking to me that Anthropic didn’t just say they copied Mononoke and rebuilt it in 5 months. That is still noteworthy, even if it isn’t as grand. Surely they knew they would be called out?
It is always good to situate your work in the larger context. We all stand on the shoulders of giants! There is nothing wrong with borrowing and adapting existing work to new contexts — that is the vast majority of what I do as an engineer. When you position your work as derivative, you are acknowledging those that came before you, as you hope to be acknowledged by those who come after you.
There is nothing without the team. On a personal note, it’s been many years since I worked on Mononoke. There is a team that still carries the torch forward all these years later, solving new and existing problems, including many I’m sure are my fault. Anthropic ripping the Bonsai data model off hit me hard, but spare a thought for the team working on it now: those who were most directly plagiarized. Imagine how they must feel about their work being deliberately copied wholesale and intentionally presented as someone else’s.
It’s been two days since I first posted about this on Bluesky and Linkedin, and I haven’t seen an update to the original post yet. This remains yet another shameful example of large AI companies appropriating the commons and presenting others’ work as their own. I don’t know what it will take to rebuild bridges from here, but my default assumption now is that Anthropic’s public engineering presentations are largely bad-faith ripoffs. That’s a shame.

title: Abacus AI Honest Review: Key Criticisms, Facts & What Users Should Know
body:
This review highlights the main critiques of Abacus AI, its price, user reviews, reliability of workflows, and real-life use cases to assist you in evaluating its advantages and disadvantages.
Online reviews and competitor reviews of Abacus AI present two distinct perspectives on the platform. Generally speaking, positive reviews can be found among those users who make extensive use of the platform and value the wide variety of AI models, agents, and cost-effectiveness of the platform. However, negative reviews can highlight the challenges and confusion associated with using credits, pricing, learning curve, and some workflow-related issues. Analysis of both perspectives will allow one to get a better understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of the platform.
This article studies Abacus AI through Reddit discussions, positive and negative user reviews, and video walkthroughs to find out how users perceive and utilize the platform. In addition, the review of the platform's features, pricing, credit system, and product ecosystem is conducted to add depth to the analysis.
It is necessary to conduct an honest review of Abacus AI that will cover its main strengths and weaknesses and answer the most common criticisms.
Abacus AI is a technical workspace that combines various AI models and functions under one umbrella. One can use this workspace for writing, data analysis, generating images and videos, coding, and much more.
ChatLLM makes a great start for beginners in AI technology. The app basically gives you access to various models of providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google through one interface so that you can toggle between these models without accessing multiple applications.
Even though many people draw comparisons between Abacus AI, ChatGPT, and Claude, it should be kept in mind that these two platforms are designed to serve different purposes. While ChatGPT and Claude specialize in conversational AI, Abacus AI covers a broader area of individual and commercial needs in the form of various AI capabilities.
The ideal option would depend on your needs: if you seek assistance in conversational AI, you might go for ChatGPT and Claude; however, if you are looking for multiple AI capabilities and models in one place, then you should consider Abacus AI.
The following table explains the ecosystem of Abacus AI and their respective uses.
Several common complaints about its user interface, pricing, credit system, and suitability for various kinds of tasks are noted both in reviews and on forums. Here are the significant criticisms to consider.
Complex interface: Some users find the platform difficult to navigate because it offers many tools and features in one place.
Model identification: Switching between AI models can make it harder to track which model was used in previous conversations.
Steep learning curve: Advanced features, particularly AI agents and workflow creation, may take time to understand.
Developer-focused experience: Some tools are easier to use if you have technical knowledge, although basic ChatLLM features are accessible to general users.
Uncertainty around credit consumption: Users sometimes find it difficult to predict how many credits a task will require, particularly for complex agent workflows.
Credits running out quickly: Tasks involving extensive research, coding, or multiple agent steps can consume credits faster than expected.
Usage pacing limits: The platform's credit pacing rules can affect how users access their remaining monthly allowance throughout the billing cycle.
Budgeting concerns: Unpredictable usage can make it harder for individuals and businesses to estimate their monthly costs.
Pricing changes: Changes between introductory offers and regular subscription prices can create confusion if users do not review the billing terms.
Incomplete tasks: AI agents may occasionally stop before completing a workflow or produce results that need further work.
Credits consumed during failed runs: Users may be concerned about credit usage when an agent encounters an error or fails to complete a task.
Complex workflows: Multi-step tasks can require additional instructions, monitoring, and troubleshooting to achieve the expected result.
Integration requirements: Businesses may need to check whether their existing tools and preferred integrations are supported before adopting the platform.
Limited ready-made workflows for some use cases: Teams looking for preconfigured solutions for customer support, IT, or other specialized functions may need to configure their own workflows.
Analytics and monitoring: Businesses with specific reporting requirements should evaluate whether the available monitoring and analytics features meet their needs.
Different business requirements: A platform designed to support many types of AI work may not offer the same specialised experience as a tool built for one particular function.
"Only suitable for hobbyists and developers, not business teams" (criticism appearing in some comparative reviews)
Support response times: Some users report delays or responses that do not fully resolve their issues.
Cancellation and billing: Online discussions include complaints about subscription cancellations and unexpected charges. These reports should be assessed individually rather than treated as evidence of a widespread problem.
Understanding subscription terms: Users should check renewal dates, credit allowances, plan limits, and cancellation policies before subscribing.
Agent hallucinations during web search or research tasks: Some users report that the agent retrieves inaccurate information during autonomous web research runs.
"Scam" or "deceptive billing" language in some reviews:
The following are some examples that show how Abacus AI can be used in real-world scenarios such as website creation, mobile application development, automation of processes, invoicing, analytics, software testing, and even research. Some of the capabilities of Abacus AI, possible uses, and crucial considerations prior to using its generated output have been highlighted below.
It is a multiple-page website with a built-in payment feature, capable of assisting businesses launch offers and testing consumer demand.
A similar example. “App with Stripe Payments” is related to workshop sign-ups and payment processing.
Generating a checkout page is just one part of building a working payment-enabled website. It must also handle successful , failed or post payment functions.
The Build a Mobile App example showcases a fitness application with daily objectives, workouts, and progress monitoring.
Some other examples in the catalog are: Running Coach, Meditation Coach, Expense Tracker, and Mobile Games.
For instance, the Running Coach app claims to support live GPS tracking and background mode. It should be tested on a real device to prove that it functions as expected beyond a demo.
Example of Vibe Code CRM involves creating a customer relationship management.
Catalog contains such features as employee directories, vacation tracking, and apps with user roles and permissions.
Development of CRM is a good example because the core workflows in this type of software can be clearly outlined. As the number of integrations, permissions, and business rules increases, more thorough testing of the application is needed.
Invoice Processing API example shows how to extract the vendor information, amounts, due dates, and details for each item in a PDF document or image.
Another example, Invoice Data Extractor, gives a description of the process of conversion of the extracted information to a validated CSV file.
The key benefit of invoice automation is not only the extraction of text from the PDF but the creation of consistent information with some questionable fields for further human validation.
Revenue Analytics Pro offers automated Excel analytics aimed at finding patterns and growth opportunities in revenue.
Other examples are financial modeling, churn analysis, product classification, and annual report dashboards.
For instance, the definition of revenue needs to be specified prior to any analysis. Invoiced revenue, recognized revenue, and collected revenue are different things. Even a perfectly made chart will be misinterpreted if the wrong metric is used. Consequently, the quality of AI-supported analytics depends on the precision of the calculations and the information provided.
Multi-Agent Code Review is a case when several AI agents check the latest ten pull requests simultaneously. These agents find potential bugs, inefficiencies, missing tests and security flaws in order to prepare their suggestions for improvement and corresponding pull requests.
The parallel processing may help in reviewing several changes at once and increasing the range of automated reviews. Still, the problem of resolving contradictory suggestions and verification of the right functioning of the suggested patch with other parts of the software remains.
An example of the AI QA Engineer showcases how to test an application through emulated user interactions and create reports on possible broken workflow.
There are also individual samples for navigating, submitting forms, permissions testing, and evaluating user interface.
The example of Landing Page Testing gives us a more concrete sample as it tests form submission, email verification and creation of issues in Jira. Such type of testing can give more valuable information than just stating that the application works.
Example of the Automated Browser Workflow involves scheduled processes such as logging in, downloading invoices, and uploading information into Google Sheets.
A second example is the E-Commerce Price Watch that mainly revolves around price watching of competitors, taking screenshots, identifying any change, and emailing CSV reports.
These workflows need to have an error handling process defined in advance. For instance, if the automatic login procedure does not succeed, there needs to be a mechanism that raises the alert about the issue instead of generating an empty spreadsheet as the result.
Some of the entries in the catalog relate to robotics research into investment, market entry presentations, education reports, and scientific research.
The Parallelised Equity Research example is an analysis of 50 companies within the S&P 500 index and the creation of a portfolio of ten stocks.
The same applies to presentations and research reports. Creating presentation slides or information summaries is not equivalent to verification of all claims made in the generated output. It is up to users to verify underlying sources and ensure that the information is up-to-date and distinguish between the facts and assumptions or AI interpretation.
Abacus AI would suit individuals and organizations who want to go beyond just text generation and question answering using AI technology. The unique features of multiple models, AI agents, application development, data analytics, and workflow automation make this platform an ideal choice for those who wish to integrate multiple AI functions on a single platform.
Abacus AI provides a multifunctional AI platform, where one can find such functionalities as access to models, autonomous agents, code support, applications, data analysis, and media creation. All these features may be helpful for users who need to use various tools provided by artificial intelligence in their work.
Flexibility in terms of functionalities offered is the main advantage of this platform. However, it also means that some functionalities need to be learned for using the platform. The pay-by-the-credit system enables the usage of various features; however, people working with intensive agent workflows or media generation need to control their expenses.
Some issues raised in public reviews also indicate areas where improvement is needed. They are related to unpredictability in costs, workflow, and client support. These factors should be considered along with the positive experiences of some people.
To have the best experience, begin with those that apply to your work, try out complicated functions before depending on them, and check on the present subscription plan. This will make it easy for you to appreciate both strengths and weaknesses of the platform.
In conclusion, Abacus AI is a good choice for people who require a general AI working environment. The strength of the product will depend on whether the tools and workflow meet your needs.
This user-led demo shows how the whole platform works with live demonstrations of ChatLLM model switching, task performance by the agents, creation of images and videos, and the API access layer including live credit monitoring:
The review explains not only where the platform excelled, but also where the platform needed work. This is more helpful than a staged presentation, and gives you a true idea of what it is really like to use the platform on a daily basis.
Many different kinds of AI exist, including models like ChatLLM, AI agents, programming skills, application development, data analysis, and media production. All of these kinds of AI may prove useful for people who wish to control several workflows using AI in one platform.
It can be considered testing it out for those who frequently use different capabilities of this application. It will depend on how often you use it and whether your monthly credits are enough.
Credits are the amount used on the platform, which varies based on the actions that one takes. Certain basic text actions will consume less credits than complex coding, interacting with AI agents or creating media.
Yes. Novices can use ChatLLM for their everyday writing, research, and documentation. As the user gets acquainted with the tool, he can experiment with agents, coding, and workflow automation. Moreover, additional capabilities might need further experimentation.
The agents could be utilized to execute complex tasks, coding, doing research work, and developing applications. The dependability of the agents will depend on the complexity of the task, the instructions, the tools at hand, and the quality of the outcome. It is also important to test intermediate and final outcomes.
People provide their own reviews regarding the services; some of them like the diversity of offered instruments, but other people have troubles with spending of credit, processing of workflows or any other help. Reviews can be useful for revealing weaknesses, but personal experience is not a universal one.
Yes. Agents and applications can be helpful in accomplishing various tasks like document processing, research, and data analysis. Organizations need to define what they require from an integration and then test it out along with making sure that there are enough security measures in place..
The first step is to define the job at hand, provide proper context for it, and divide the complex workflow into smaller steps. Credit usage monitoring would also be beneficial, along with the selection of the proper level of effort required to complete the job.
The user will need to assess the number of tools needed, the cost of subscription, number of credits per month, Agent restrictions, the integration list, and the degree of workflow analysis required. It might be more helpful for companies that need diverse capabilities from AI compared to those who just need the chatbots occasionally.
Those who create and have applications for AI will perhaps get more out of the rich ecosystem of AI than those who simply use it. There may be people who would be helped by a specific platform for finding a chatbot.

Join the celebration online by sharing responses with #ShareYourSpark for a chance to win an ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark laptop signed by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. See the campaign and official rules . See What Reviewers Are Saying From local AI workflows to creative apps and gaming, see what reviewers are saying about RTX Spark — then experience it at a launch celebration. “The fact that NVIDIA, Microsoft and their partners have delivered such a capable, compatible and polished platform even in its first at-bat should put the rest of the PC industry on notice.” — Tom’s Hardware “I tested NVIDIA’s RTX Spark for gaming and local AI – the performance absolutely stunned me.” — TrustedReviews , UK “I’m very happy to report that performance is actually looking really good when it comes to AI, gaming and creative workflows.” — Microcenter “[RTX Spark] is a different species of computer that has arrived early. It is a statement of intent from NVIDIA about where computing is going — trading raw benchmarking crowns for the ability to carry a self-rewriting, fully autonomous, CUDA-accelerated digital brain in your backpack.” — Tom’s Guide “One of the most impressive parts of the launch is how many apps NVIDIA has worked with to ensure optimisation with the Spark technology.” — Creative Bloq Independent testing from Artificial Analysis offers an early look at the powerful local AI performance RTX Spark brings to a laptop. Walk-in entry; no advance registration required. Seoul — COEX East Lobby, 513 Yeongdong-daero . title: Meta ships Muse Spark Open, its answer to China’s best open-weight models
body: Meta on Thursday launched Muse Spark Open, a new 816B open model (with 42B active parameters) that the company argues is the “most capable US open-weight model to date.” The new model is available through the APIs of Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter, and Together AI. And since it’s an open model, you can also download the weights from Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face, and Microsoft’s Foundry Model Catalog. Open Weights, semi-open license Overall, Muse Spark Open, which features the industry-standard 1 million token window, looks to be an extremely capable model that, depending on the benchmark, is on par with or beats some of the best Chinese models. Like with some of the newer Chinese models , though, the weights may be open but the license doesn’t tell the same story. Meta is launching the new model under the “ Muse Model License .” This license, Meta says, has “limited commercial terms, which allow many developers to use the model for free.” Specifically, this means any company that has more than $20 million in gross revenue during any consecutive twelve-month period must “notify Meta and enter into a separate written agreement with Meta before offering the Software or any Derivatives as part of that Model as a Service business.” Muse Spark Open — weights releasing today — runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple. pic.twitter.com/U2wJNrKBOg — Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) October 15, 2026 Any company using the model must also “prominently display ‘Built with Muse Spark Open’ in the user interface of each product or service” that uses the model or a derivative model that was created, trained, fine-tuned, or distilled from Muse Spark Open. Overall, this looks a lot like the license that Moonshot uses for Kimi K3, for example. Internal use and building the model into your own product are free, and the license’s usage policy bars military and critical infrastructure deployments, a carve-out Meta added for the U.S. government with Llama in 2024. Unlike Anthropic’s new usage policy for Claude , though, you can abuse the model as much as you want. Benchmarks The company says it built the new model for “coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.” The two U.S. models Muse Spark Open competes with are essentially Thinking Machines’ Inkling and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3 Ultra. In Meta’s own benchmarks, its new model beats them across the board — often by 20 points or more. Credit: Meta. The closer fight, however, is with Chinese open models that many developers already run today. Spark Open leads Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, and Qwen3.8 on the agentic and tool-use benchmarks, including JobBench and MCP-Atlas, and roughly ties them on SciCode. Coding is where it trails. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, Kimi K3 scores 85.0 and GLM 5.3 83.9 against Spark Open’s 76.4. On DeepSWE 1.1, the spread is 68 to 60. That’s the same gap Meta acknowledged when it launched the closed version of Spark in April, and it doesn’t look like it’s made much progress since. muse spark open. why 2026 won't be like 1984  pic.twitter.com/jYnOSfZf9u — Alexandr Wang (@alexandr_wang) October 15, 2026 Muse Spark Open on the Mac you can’t afford You’re unlikely to run an 816B model locally, but if you have two new Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips and 512 GB, Meta says you could link them and use MLX to run the model on them. The company did just that to run Muse Code, powered by Muse Spark, and ship updates to the Ice Cubes Mastodon client, for example. Apple doesn’t currently sell the 512 GB Mac Studio to mere mortals, but in a few weeks, you will be able to buy two of those machines for the price of a compact car . The post Meta ships Muse Spark Open, its answer to China’s best open-weight models appeared first on The New Stack .

title: US Army to stand up second expeditionary cyber battalion in coming months
body: The Army will soon double the number of battalions it uses to train and deploy expeditionary cyberspace and electromagnetic warfare teams, according to the Army. Head of Army Cyber Command Lt. Gen. Christopher Eubank on Monday at the Association of the United States Army conference in Washington gave an approximate timeline for when the service would be delivering the new unit devoted to the exact same mission as the 11th Cyber Battalion, dubbed the Leviathans. “It should start standing up in earnest within the next couple months, and it will be an exact replica of the 11th Cyber Warfare Battalion,” Eubank said. The new battalion will achieve initial operating capability within the next year and from there work toward full operational capability, according to the Cyber Command leader. The battalion is currently working on behalf of Joint Task Force–Southern Border, providing radio frequency-enabled cyber effects as directed by the division commander, Eubank said. The Leviathans was activated on Oct. 16, 2022, as the first scalable expeditionary capability to handle the Army’s current and future cyberspace objectives. It was built with the specific intention of rolling out non-lethal and non-kinetic effects that include cyberspace and electronic warfare assets. Its previous iteration, the 915th Cyber Warfare Battalion, was activated on June 6, 2018, before being renamed during the 11th Cyber Battalion’s activation. At the time of the battalion’s creation, the Army said it planned to have 12 expeditionary teams it could deploy under the 11th Cyber Battalion by September 2027. The service has labeled the battalion the first of its kind. “Just as Gen. Patton led the modernization of tank warfare into WWII, the leaders and soldiers of the 11th Cyber Battalion spearhead concept development for the delivery of CEMA [cyber electromagnetic activity] combat power to the tactical edge of the contemporary battlefield,” said Lt. Col. Lou Etienne, who led the 11th Cyber Battalion until June 25. Developers from 11th Cyber Command worked alongside the Cyber Solutions Development unit within the 780th Military Intelligence Brigade to develop new drone technology between July 2025 and July 2026. The partnership project was performed to support the Army’s “Transforming in Contact” initiative, which delivers new unmanned technology to soldiers to track their feedback in real time as they utilize it in the field. The 11th Cyber Battalion also participated in a demonstration at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, from August. 5-8, simultaneously deploying three new Army technologies and proving their efficacy in diffusing electromagnetic threats from enemies.

title: Venezuela's Oil Recovery Gains Momentum as New Drilling Rigs Arrive
body: Eleven new 550-horsepower workover rigs will work in Venezuela's oil fields this month. According to North American Blue Energy Partners NABEP, which announced the deployment on 13 October, they are the first new mobile repair-and-maintenance units to enter the country's fields in more than 15 years. Two 1,500-horsepower drilling rigs arrived on 7 October, with more equipment to follow. The company says it has now bought 60 rigs, 30 steam boilers and 70 pieces of heavy machinery, which it describes as the country's largest heavy-equipment fleet.  On its own, a rig delivery is a small item. Its significance lies in what it is attached to. NABEP says its production has grown from 18,000 barrels per day to more than 200,000 in two years, backed by about $1 billion in company-funded investment, a figure it first published on 31 August when it announced its agreement with the US government. "NABEP is making serious and steady progress in increasing oil production," said Alejandro Betancourt, the company's founder and chief executive. The new rigs are the physical means by which that number is supposed to keep rising.  The timing matters. Oil markets lack barrels they can rely on. Brent is holding above $100, tanker attacks around the Strait of Hormuz keep coming, and freight and insurance costs are at record levels. Refiners from the US Gulf Coast to India want heavy crude that does not have to pass a chokepoint, and India's imports of Venezuelan oil have just reached a seven-year high. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven reserves and produces about 1 million barrels per day, a third of what it once did. The question every operator now crowding into Caracas faces is the same how quickly can idle capacity be turned into barrels  Related Europe's Gas Prices Close to 2022 High as Hormuz LNG Flows Remain Limited  Two sets of numbers, one direction  NABEP is the company at the center of the agreement with the US Departments of State and War announced on 31 August, which covers 17 fields and, according to the company's announcement of the deal, the rights to commercialize more than 65 billion barrels of P1 reserves. Most coverage since has dealt with the structure of that deal, and on 1 October the ranking Democrats on five House committees and subcommittees asked for more information about it. Those are legitimate questions about governance. They are separate from the operating question, which is whether the barrels are real.  On that question, two sources point the same way. The company's own figure, published in its 31 August announcement of the agreement and repeated on 13 October, is that production has risen from approximately 18,000 barrels per day to more than 200,000 in two years. The company dates that baseline to January 2024. It counts the PetroZamora fields on Lake Maracaibo in the state where it found them before it formally took over their operation that April. Independently, Rystad Energy assesses that production across operations associated with NABEP has risen from 90,000 barrels per day at the end of 2024 to 200,000 today.  The two measure different things over different periods. The company's figure runs from January 2024, before most of its current portfolio was in place; Rystad's starts at the end of that year and covers everything associated with the company, not just what it operates directly. They should not be set against each other. What gives the trend its weight is that an independent estimate and the operator's own books both arrive at the same place around 200,000 barrels per day, more than double where they stood at the start of 2025.  PetroZamora the clearest case  The most detailed part of the record is in the west. PetroZamora comprises the Bachaquero, Lagunillas and Ceuta fields, some of the oldest producing acreage in the Maracaibo basin. NABEP has operated them since April 2024. According to the company, the fields were producing about 18,000 barrels per day at the start of that year, about 23,000 on the day it took over in April, and 25,000 on average in that first month. By mid-2026 they were producing 100,000.  That is a fourfold increase in a little over two years, from fields that had been in decline for years. No new reservoir was found. The oil was there, the wells were there, and much of the surface infrastructure was there. What was missing was the capital, equipment, and operating discipline to keep them running.  The company's account of how it achieved the increase is unglamorous, which makes it more credible. Gas compression plants at Ceuta that had stopped running were restarted, the first in June 2024 and another in May 2025. Portable steam generators were put to work at Bachaquero and Lagunillas, where heavy crude does not flow without heat. Service rigs and well-rehabilitation barges returned to existing wells. Each step added a few thousand barrels. The workover rigs announced this week use the same method at greater scale a workover rig moves from well to well, fixing what has failed and bringing production back one well at a time.  This is how brownfield recovery works anywhere, from the North Sea to southern Iraq. Gains come from hundreds of small interventions, sustained month after month, and they hold only for as long as the equipment and the people stay in place.  What it says about the wider recovery  The PetroZamora record matters beyond one company because it tests an assumption that has shaped a decade of commentary on Venezuela that the sector's decline was so deep that recovery would take a generation and tens of billions of dollars before the first additional barrel appeared.  The evidence points to something more practical. A large share of Venezuela's lost production sits in existing fields with known geology. Where an operator has applied capital, equipment and experienced crews, output has responded within months. That is a faster and cheaper route to supply than any greenfield project, and it is the route now open to every operator returning to the country.  That does not mean the rest will be easy. The August agreement is expected, in the company's words, to involve $100 billion of investment in production capacity and infrastructure, and NABEP's stated near-term goal is to lift output above one million barrels per day. The first figure is a program to be funded in stages, not capital already deployed; the second would mean extending what has been done on a handful of assets to 17, including greenfield blocks in the Orinoco Belt that are a different engineering task from reviving wells on Lake Maracaibo. Heavy-oil production also depends on diluent, power, and export logistics that no single company controls, and monthly output will not move in a straight line.  Betancourt has worked in Venezuela's oil sector for years, and the company's approach reflects that. It is run as an operating business the emphasis is on rigs, steam, compression and well work, and on the sequence in which they are applied. PetroZamora's production record measures that approach, and it is the measure by which he and the company should be judged as the portfolio grows.  NABEP is not the whole of Venezuela's recovery and should not be presented as such. Other operators are raising output in the west and in the Orinoco Belt, and the policy changes in Caracas and Washington that reopened the sector apply to all of them. NABEP offers a dated, field-level record showing the method works, plus a fleet of equipment to apply it more widely.  The fields and the towns around them  Higher output also changes the economy around the fields. NABEP says it directly employs more than 5,000 people and supports more than 10,000 contract workers in Venezuela. Every restarted compression plant and every well brought back needs contractors, transport, maintenance crews, catering, and spare parts. On the eastern shore of Lake Maracaibo, where towns such as Lagunillas and Bachaquero were built around the oil industry and declined with it, that activity reaches local businesses long before national statistics register it. Those are the engineers, technicians, and service workers Venezuela will need if the recovery is to last.  What to watch  Three things will show whether this trajectory holds. The first is whether PetroZamora stays near 100,000 barrels per day through the coming year, since holding a level is harder than reaching it. The second is whether independent trackers such as Rystad and the vessel-tracking firms keep confirming what the company reports. The third is how quickly the new rigs translate into volume from the first of the fourteen further assets.  For a market paying more than $100 for crude and counting every tanker that clears Hormuz, the conclusion is practical. Venezuela's additional barrels do not depend on a discovery or a technological breakthrough. They depend on operators doing in other fields what has already been done on Lake Maracaibo, and on the rigs to do it with.  By Cyril Widdershoven for Oilprice.com

title: Black Forest Labs' open-weights image model FLUX 3 Image Klein runs on consumer GPUs with just 8 GB of VRAM
body:
Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6-billion-parameter open-weights model for text-to-image generation, image editing, and generation with up to ten reference images. It supports native 4K output, pixel-accurate editing, and bounding boxes for element placement. Black Forest Labs says it scores the highest Elo ratings among all open models in internal testing, beating closed competitors Ideogram V4.5 and even BFL's own FLUX.2 [pro] . It gains 91 Elo points over FLUX.2 [klein] with 38 percent fewer parameters than that model's 9 billion.
An INT8 build lets it run on NVIDIA GPUs with just 8 GB of VRAM, generating an image in under 9 seconds on an RTX 4070. The weights ship under the FLUX Kommunity License , free for commercial use by companies making under $5 million annually. The model is also available through the BFL API at $0.009 per 1,000 images, as a Playground , on Hugging Face Spaces , and locally via ComfyUI and Diffusers . LoRA training works from day one through Ostris AI Toolkit and NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel .

title: TSMC chip capacity is ‘fierce’ battleground for AI customers, amid record quarter
body:
As Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s record quarter makes clear, demand from chipmakers shows no sign of slowing down. In fact, TSMC can't manufacture quickly enough.
The artificial intelligence boom has created unending need for space on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, and it could put a chokehold on the entire industry's ability to scale. Last year, TSMC said it had the capacity to make more than 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers. But customers want more.
"The competition is extremely fierce," said Jordan Klein, an analyst at Mizuho Securities. "It's a game of who can get the most leverage and supply."
TSMC makes the vast majority of the world's most advanced semiconductors, the graphics processors and central processors from Nvidia , AMD and Broadcom that are necessary for running AI workloads. Now a growing number of tech firms – Apple , Google , Amazon , Microsoft , Meta and OpenAI – also rely on TSMC to make custom in-house AI accelerators.
TSMC North American CEO Sajiv Dalal told CNBC he gets at least 10 calls a day about wafer capacity. TSMC posted record profit for a sixth straight quarter on Thursday and expects fourth-quarter revenue to be 58% higher than a year earlier, driven by strong demand for its advanced chipmaking technologies.
If compute demand continues to grow at the current rate over the next 12 to 18 months, Klein said capacity constraints at TSMC could threaten some of the industry's massive infrastructure investments and the "aggressive revenue growth targets" from the AI companies. U.S. hyperscalers are projecting well over $700 billion in capital expenditures this year, and analysts expect that figure to jump in 2027.
AI ambitions are also threatened by a global shortage of memory chips. The logic chips that TSMC manufactures are more complex and expensive to produce. That means GPU and CPU leaders like Nvidia and AMD work out lengthy contracts and bespoke deals with TSMC behind closed doors years in advance. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su have both visited Taiwan multiple times this year.
Sid Sheth, CEO of AI chip startup D-Matrix, has fostered a relationship with TSMC for more than 20 years, and his company relies on TSMC to manufacture its processors.
For TSMC customers, many roads lead to Kevin Zhang, a senior vice president of the Taiwanese company and a central figure in determining which chipmakers get access to its coveted factory lines.
He's "currently probably the most popular person on the planet," Sheth said in an interview. Sheth said that Jerry Qubain, D-Matrix's vice president of manufacturing, has been visiting TSMC since 1992 and goes to Taiwan three to four times a year.
"This was even before Nvidia was founded," Sheth said. "That's a good example of a person we brought on board because of the relationships he has at TSMC." Qubain joined D-Matrix in 2024. TSMC declined to participate in this story.
TSMC had 534 customers in 2025. While it doesn't name or rank them, its top 10 customers accounted for 78% of net revenue , with its top two bringing in 19% and 17%, respectively.
That leaves startups competing for capacity against customers with far bigger orders. Sheth said TSMC is "selective," but has an incentive to back promising newcomers.
"They were very supportive of Nvidia and Broadcom when they were very young companies, and now these are their biggest customers today," Sheth said. "They want to see a repeat of that."
TSMC is hustling to bring much more capacity online, with new fabs in Taiwan, Japan and Arizona — it's making advanced chips in the U.S. for the first time. In July, TSMC announced it was adding $100 billion and "several more" fabs to the six planned in Arizona, bringing its total commitment to $265 billion. TSMC is also reportedly considering an entirely new fab location in Texas.
All of this will take years to come online. In the meantime, analysts say TSMC is adding tools like ASML's extreme ultraviolet lithography machines to existing factories to ramp up capacity. ASML smashed profit expectations in its earnings report Wednesday and said customers are interested in placing orders through 2030.
TSMC isn't the only option. Capacity constraints create an opening for the other two leading advanced chip manufacturers, Samsung and Intel , to win customers.
"People want a second source to be able to twist TSMC's arm and keep them honest on pricing," Dan Hutcheson, an analyst at TechInsights, told CNBC.
That second source might be Intel, the only U.S.-based advanced logic manufacturer. Although its foundry business has been struggling with delays and setbacks for years, Hutcheson says all the big chipmakers are now testing there.
Trade association SEMI expects 102 new chip fabs will come online globally by 2029, including 15 in the U.S. and 78 in Asia. China is the primary growth engine, expected to nearly triple capacity by 2030. In a race to catch up, American fab investments are projected to more than double by 2029.
With an increasing Arizona presence and "extremely fierce" competition for wafer capacity, Klein says TSMC is "one of the best strategically positioned companies on the face of the planet."

title: Sweden revisits digital krona as ECB advances digital euro plans
body:
Sweden’s Riksbank has recommended that lawmakers prepare for a possible digital krona, citing concerns over foreign-currency stablecoins and the future of domestic payments.
Sweden’s central bank is revisiting the possibility of introducing a digital krona, citing the European Central Bank’s (ECB) progress toward a digital euro and the growing use of stablecoins as reasons to reconsider a central bank digital currency (CBDC).
In an Oct. 7 letter to parliament’s Finance Committee, published Thursday, the Riksbank urged lawmakers to begin preparing legislation for a potential digital krona, three years after a government inquiry concluded there was insufficient need for one.
The letter pointed to the ECB’s planned digital euro pilot in 2027 and a potential public launch in 2029. According to the Riksbank, Sweden’s payment system could become less competitive without a comparable digital version of its own currency.
The central bank also identified the growing use of foreign-currency stablecoins, particularly those pegged to the US dollar, as a longer-term concern, though it sees the near-term risk as limited.
“If stablecoins pegged to foreign currencies are considered attractive as a means of payment, the use of the Swedish krona could come under pressure even within Sweden’s borders,” the letter read.
The Riksbank estimates that introducing a digital krona would take at least five years, excluding the time required for legislative changes. For this reason, it recommends beginning legal preparations now, even if Sweden ultimately decides against launching a CBDC.
