title: Copper price falls for third day as US inflation shock, easing Chile strike risk spur selloff
body: Copper dropped to its lowest in 10 days on Thursday as hotter-than-expected US inflation revived talk of another Federal Reserve rate hike, a rout in Asian chip stocks spread to the metals complex and a deal at Escondida took the most immediate supply risk off the table. Comex copper for December delivery fell 1.2% to $6.5810 a pound (about $14,508 a tonne) by late morning in New York, after trading as low as $6.5245 earlier in the session. The most-active contract is now 4.5% below the record settlement of $6.89 set on September 9 and heading for a third straight daily loss, the longest losing streak since June. In London, three-month copper eased 0.9% to $14,360 a tonne in official trading after touching $14,289, the weakest since October 5. Cash copper settled at $14,751 on Wednesday, $116 over the three-month price, and LME inventories have fallen to 228,000 tonnes, down 8% since the start of the month. The most-traded contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange lost 1.9% to 108,940 yuan ($16,276) a tonne. Click on chart for live prices. “Two things are happening at the same time: the easing worries of supply and the strong inflation report,” Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, told Reuters. “That was too much for the market to chew in one go and some profit-taking is emerging.” The technical picture is deteriorating too, Hansen said, with copper challenging an uptrend that began in March and edging below its 50-day moving average. US consumer prices accelerated in September at the fastest pace in five months, Wednesday’s data showed, putting a rate hike later this month back on the table and lifting the Bloomberg Dollar Index to its highest since May 2025. Higher rates hurt metals twice over, by cooling demand and raising the cost of carrying inventory, and the market was already nervous about the other pillar of this year’s rally. South Korea’s Kospi fell almost 8% on Thursday, dropping into a bear market as investors questioned how long the artificial intelligence spending boom can last, and the memory-chip selloff that began earlier in the week spread across Asian tech. “For copper, it’s a double whammy of the AI trade coming under pressure from the sell-off in chip stocks, and the impact of rising Fed rate hike odds,” Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, told Reuters. Sucden Financial expects “the firm dollar and renewed rate pressure to keep the complex defensive, with copper’s remaining supply risks offering only very limited support,” its analysts wrote in a note. Escondida signs, Antofagasta stalls Those supply risks shrank on Wednesday afternoon, when supervisors at BHP’s Escondida in Chile ratified the agreement their union had struck with the company hours earlier, removing the threat of a stoppage at the world’s largest copper mine. Unionized workers at Antofagasta’s Centinela remain on strike, and the open pit at Codelco’s El Teniente is still shut after last week’s landslide, but the 5% of Chilean output that GEM Mining Consulting rated at risk a week ago has narrowed considerably. Antofagasta itself reported a 7% rise in third-quarter copper production and held its 2026 guidance of 625,000 to 655,000 tonnes despite the Centinela strike, but it was the year after that spooked investors. The company now expects 630,000 to 690,000 tonnes in 2027 , below its original 650,000 to 700,000 tonnes and short of BMO Capital Markets’ 703,000-tonne estimate, and lifted its cash cost guidance on higher diesel prices. The outlook “implies no growth on the original guidance for 2026,” RBC analysts wrote, despite better grades at Los Pelambres and the Centinela expansion coming on stream. Tariff odds fade with the spread The selloff has also drained what was left of the tariff premium in the Comex curve. December copper in New York settled on Wednesday just $49 a tonne over the LME three-month official price, down from a gap of about $175 on Tuesday, and on Macquarie’s arithmetic that puts the market-implied odds of a 15% import duty arriving on schedule in January at roughly 2%, against the 10% the bank read into the spread at the end of September. That is the “very binary” setup the bank described in its latest quarterly, in which a decision against a tariff would see the Comex price “collapse, taking the LME price with it” and surplus US stocks reappear in LME warehouses. Macquarie counts a 223,000-tonne surplus this year and surpluses above 700,000 tonnes a year from 2027, a view the International Copper Study Group broadly shares with its forecast of a 368,000-tonne surplus next year , while BMO argues that the near-2 million tonnes sitting in the United States is China’s strategic reserve relocated rather than surplus, and has copper averaging $14,675 next year. Miners follow the metal lower Copper producers fell with the metal on Thursday. Freeport-McMoRan dropped 2.4% to a $98 billion market value and Southern Copper 2.4% to $165 billion, with BHP down 1.4% at $213 billion, Rio Tinto 1.3% lower and First Quantum off 1.7%. Lundin Mining lost 1.0% and Ivanhoe Mines 1.5%, while Teck Resources, up 0.5%, was the only major copper producer in positive territory. Freeport has now shed 5.5% over the past week. Antofagasta was the day’s casualty, down 6.4% to £33.40 in London for a market value of close to £33 billion, taking its loss over the past week to 10%. The stock is now flat for 2026, as is First Quantum, against gains of 41% for Southern Copper, 37% for Glencore, 36% for BHP and Teck, and 34% for Freeport. Polish state miner KGHM, up 2.4%, bucked the trend after the EU put its $2.4 billion of copper projects on a fast track last week. Comex copper is up about 17% in 2026. Top 50 mining companies take $264 billion hit as gold trade unwinds, lithium stocks exit (With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)

title: The technical actions needed to ensure the continuity of UTC
body:
Working together to promote and advance the global comparability of measurements
The General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM), at its 28th meeting, recalling that the CGPM, when adopting Resolution 2 “On the definition of time scales” at its 26th meeting (2018), confirmed that Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is a time scale produced by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) with the same rate as International Atomic Time (TAI), but differing from TAI only by an integral number of seconds, stated that UTC is the only recommended time scale for international reference and the basis of civil time in most countries, the CGPM, when adopting Resolution 4 “On the use and future development of UTC” at its 27th meeting (2022), recalled that the offset by an integral number of seconds is due to the agreement maintained between UTC and the time scale describing the angular rotation of the Earth (UT1), decided that the maximum value for the difference |UT1-UTC| will be increased in, or before, 2035, to ensure the continuity of UTC for at least a century, requested the CIPM to draft a resolution for the 28th meeting of the CGPM (2026), recognizing that industrial users and the synchronization needs of national critical infrastructures, for example transportation, energy distribution, telecommunication, and space projects require UTC to be continuous without any future adjustment, for some applications it is necessary to fix a maximum value for the difference |UT1-UTC| to appropriately design the software underlying operational systems, in many countries there are differences of more than one hour between local apparent solar time and civil time due to the choice of time zone, and changes of an hour are regularly introduced when daylight-saving time is used, further recognizing that users of UT1 can find information on the value of the difference UT1-UTC in the Global Navigation Satellite Services (GNSS) navigation messages, and internet services provided by the International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service (IERS), National Metrology Institutes (NMIs), and other services, the International Telecommunication Union Radiocommunication Sector (ITU-R), through its Working Party 7A, is studying possible updates of the code for the transmission of the difference UT1-UTC by radio stations and Resolution 655 (REV.WRC-23) resolved to “establish a transition period for implementation and allow for the possibility to disseminate the increased difference between UT1 and UTC via radiocommunication system until 2035, but no later than 2040, in cases where existing equipment cannot be replaced earlier”, noting that a workshop organized by the Consultative Committee for Time and Frequency (CCTF) and IERS in March 2025, which included experts on Earth rotation, estimated that the probability of a negative leap second will increase rapidly in the near future, reaching a 30 % probability by 2035, a negative leap second has not previously been applied, and it is considered to pose a high risk of causing anomalies and disruption to critical infrastructures that are largely unprepared, and the preparation would create, for the industries that rely on time synchronization, a need for financial investment, whose amount is estimated to be similar to their preparations for the millennium bug, the growing influence of IoT (Internet of Things) technologies, dispersed multi-sensor systems, smart grids, and virtual services for contemporary society, creates an increasing risk of malfunction in operation of systems and services with the insertion of any leap second, especially with a negative one, the use of different mitigation methods for leap second introductions by global service providers in their server systems, in order to avoid time steps, leads to inconsistency in timing between different systems and in the disseminated time and frequency, which do not conform to the SI unit, international organizations including the International Telecommunication Union Telecommunication Standardization Sector (ITU-T), the International Union of Radio Science (URSI), international working groups such as the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 1588, and individual industry representatives have provided formal statements to the BIPM on the need to bring forward the implementation of UTC as a continuous time scale to avoid the risk of the insertion of a negative leap second, the additional risk of a delay in updating UTC could cause some user organizations to change their reference time scales to, for example, a GNSS time instead of UTC, seriously compromising the concept of international standardization in metrology, welcoming the excellent collaboration between the BIPM and the ITU-R and the endorsement of CGPM Resolution 4 (2022) at the World Radiocommunication Conference by Resolution 655 (REV.WRC 2023), the support and engagement of the IERS to take all necessary measures to change its operational provision for, and its announcement of, leap seconds according to the CGPM resolutions, decides that continuous UTC will become effective on 20 May 2027, the maximum value for the difference |UT1-UTC| will be 3 600 seconds (1 hour), ensuring the long term continuity for UTC for several centuries, requests the BIPM to continue to collaborate with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), International Astronomical Union (IAU), International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics (IUGG), IERS, and other organizations that may be impacted by this decision in order to inform users and support the application of this decision, continue to monitor the value of UT1-UTC, its estimated evolution and modelling as determined by the IERS, inform the CIPM regularly on the evolution of the value of UT1-UTC, and to continue to work with the Regional Metrology Organizations, the NMIs, and users to promote the understanding of the importance of a continuous UTC and its prompt and efficient provision to the users.
The General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM), at its 28th meeting,

title: Yemen warns Saudi airspace, airports unsafe
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 15 (MNA) – Yemen's armed forces spokesman Yahya Saree renewed a warning to airlines, airport staff and passengers that Saudi airspace and airports are unsafe, with Mecca and Medina airports exempt.
Yemen's armed forces spokesman Yahya Saree renewed a warning to airlines, airport staff and passengers over the use of Saudi airspace and airports, declaring them areas of operation exposed to possible attacks.
Saree said Saudi airports and airspace are targets for Yemen's armed forces. Mecca and Medina airports are exempt from the warning, he said.
The warning follows recent missile and drone attacks by Yemen's armed forces that hit targets in Saudi Arabia, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Khamis Mushait air base, according to the statement reported by Reuters.

title: Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open model built to run enterprise AI agents nonstop
body:
Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open multimodal model with 120 billion parameters built for enterprise agents. Two compact Bolt models designed to bring AI agents to local PCs and edge devices are launching alongside it.
Nvidia built Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for specialized agents that run continuously in the background, processing text, images, documents, and videos.
As the company explains in a technical blog post , it uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture where only 12 billion of the 120 billion parameters are active per token. Nvidia developed the model with the Nemotron Coalition , a group that includes Mistral AI, Thinking Machines Lab, Perplexity, and Black Forest Labs. Ad
Two smaller models for local hardware ship at the same time. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB runs agent tasks on local machines, while the smaller Bolt E4B 4GB targets fast voice assistants and will follow later this month. Both models offer the "highest intelligence per gigabyte of memory," Nvidia claims. Ad
Super VL and Bolt join the existing Nemotron lineup. Lightning, released in August , is built for high throughput, while Ultra tackles tough reasoning tasks. Every variant is optimized for Nvidia hardware.
Nvidia distilled Super VL from Nemotron 3 Ultra, its largest reasoning model. On tasks where an agent follows instructions, calls tools, works through multi-step business processes, or analyzes images, Super VL is supposed to match Ultra's accuracy with only about one-fifth the parameters. In agent tests from Hermes and LangChain, it actually scores higher than Ultra, according to Nvidia, and it also beats its predecessor Nemotron 3 Super on the coding benchmarks SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench. Ad
On a single GPU, Super VL delivers up to five times the throughput of other open models of similar size on agent tasks, according to Nvidia, citing the Artificial Analysis leaderboard. In an independent test by EXO Labs on the DGX Spark, no other model was both more accurate and faster. That speed advantage pays off when agents need to grind through large task volumes over days or weeks.
Against closed frontier models, Nvidia is pitching Super VL to companies that want to fine-tune with their own data and run the model on their own servers, free from a provider's terms of service. Nvidia says that could appeal to an insurer that continuously screens claims for fraud, or a financial services firm that scores creditworthiness by its own criteria. For customization, the company provides its NeMo framework, Python pipelines, and open datasets. Ad
Nvidia compresses Super VL with its 4-bit NVFP4 format. On Blackwell GPUs, the model runs entirely in 4-bit precision, while older cards store only the weights at 4 bits and handle math at 16 bits. Sensitive parts of the model keep higher precision. To prevent quality loss, Nvidia trained the compressed version to match the uncompressed original's outputs. Ad
A built-in draft component proposes several tokens ahead of time, which the main model then verifies in a single forward pass. On the DGX Spark, Nvidia recommends its own LiLiCorr method instead, which evaluates all draft tokens together for more coherent output. Nvidia says this approach speeds up text generation by up to 2.3x compared to running without speculative drafts.
Agents send the same instructions, tool descriptions, and conversation history with every request, so Super VL caches the computations for these recurring parts rather than rerunning them each time. Nvidia's inference software Dynamo also routes requests from the same session to the GPU that already holds that session's cache. On 16 B200 GPUs, this lets Super VL serve eight times as many concurrent users, and time to first token drops by 85 percent.
For vision, Nvidia focused on the kind of material agents encounter in daily work, including OCR, tables, charts, multi-page documents, and videos. Super VL can interpret a chart, link it to a table elsewhere in the same document, and summarize both without needing a separate image model.
On the chart benchmark CharXiv, Super VL scores 80.8 percent, according to Nvidia, while the older Nemotron 3 Nano Omni hit 63 percent. When the model can also run Python code, the score rises to 84 percent. On the OCRBench v2 leaderboard, it ranks among the best open models, Nvidia says.
Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a stripped-down version of Super VL built as a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts model where only 9 of its 74 billion parameters are active per step. To squeeze it into 24 GB of memory, Nvidia applies aggressive 2-bit quantization to the weights.
Bolt handles everyday local tasks where an agent needs to work through multiple steps, call tools, or search the web. Users can have it write and debug code or figure out which PC components fit their system, according to Nvidia.
The model is optimized for Nvidia's RTX Spark, a new chip for AI-capable Windows laptops , and the DGX Spark, a compact AI workstation with up to 128 GB of shared memory . It also runs on GeForce RTX PCs, DGX Station, and RTX PRO workstations, and supports llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, and vLLM.
Even with heavy compression, 24 GB is a high bar. Only pricey high-end hardware offers that much memory, and at current GPU prices, most consumers can't justify the cost. For now, the local agent is aimed at developers and owners of powerful workstations.
For weaker devices, Nvidia has Bolt E4B 4GB planned, though it hasn't shipped yet. It's designed to run on GeForce RTX cards, Jetson modules, and RTX/DGX Spark, powering voice assistants, interactive characters, or device interfaces. The model is supposed to hold natural conversations while using tools across multiple turns and staying aware of what's happening in the current app.
Dozens of organizations are already fine-tuning Super VL for their own needs, Nvidia says, mainly in industries with heavy document loads and sensitive data. Scale AI adapted the model for an agent that handles vendor credits at media company Skydance, with costs expected to drop to one-fortieth and response time to one-fifth. Ramp uses the model to turn photos of receipts into structured data and expects ten times faster responses. EY uses it for acquisition due diligence, and Hebbia for analyzing credit agreements.
A second wave of adopters comes from cybersecurity. AI21 fine-tuned Super VL for security firm Alice, which uses it to analyze threats and vulnerabilities, with accuracy improving by 40 percent according to Nvidia. Dream uses the model to hunt for vulnerabilities, and CrowdStrike is building agents to defend enterprise networks. Salesforce plans to automate government workflows, R1 is auditing medical billing, and Perplexity, Dassault Systèmes, and Mercor are also using the model.
Nvidia is releasing the weights in a base version, a post-trained version, and a 4-bit compressed version, along with the datasets and training recipes and reinforcement learning environments. That makes Super VL more open than many open-weight models, which typically only share the weights.
The model was trained on over 25 trillion tokens during pre-training and continued pre-training, Nvidia says, with post-training and reinforcement learning adding roughly four million examples across about 100 open training environments.
On Hugging Face, Nvidia is also releasing several datasets that other developers can use to train or fine-tune their own models. They cover how agents use tools, follow instructions, handle long texts, and understand images, while other datasets deal with finance, safety, and fairness.
One dataset targets languages spoken in India. Nvidia built it with the Indian Institute of Technology Madras and its AI lab AI4Bharat, and it contains about 2.83 trillion tokens of text in 22 Indian languages.
Super VL runs on desktop systems like DGX Spark, DGX Station, RTX PRO, and RTX, on Jetson modules in edge devices, and in data centers and the cloud. Through Nvidia NIM, enterprises get the model as a ready-to-deploy microservice with validated configs and support, with updates planned every two weeks. Weights are available on Hugging Face for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB .
Nvidia releases the models openly but tunes them for its own products, from data center servers to workstations. Anyone who wants to get the most out of Nemotron ends up buying Nvidia hardware.
The strategy behind Nvidia's open models is self-serving. The more companies run their own open models, the greater the demand for compute hardware, and open models will likely stay optimized for Nvidia for the foreseeable future. Meanwhile, companies like Meta, Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI are building their own chips and optimizing models for those instead. To push the spread of open AI models further, Nvidia recently invested $12.9 billion in Hugging Face , one of the most important platforms for developing and sharing them.

title: EIA Says US Crude Inventories Down Nearly 9 Million Barrels
body:
Oil Prices Plunge 7% as U.S. and Iran Signal Room for Diplomacy
Julianne Geiger is a veteran energy journalist and market analyst with more than a decade of experience covering the global oil and gas sector. Her…
Crude oil inventories in the United States saw a decrease of 8.6 million barrels during the week ending October 9, according to new data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) released on Thursday. The decrease brings commercial stockpiles to 415.6 million barrels, according to government data, which is now 3% above the five-year average for this time of year.
The EIA’s data release follows API’s figures that were released a day earlier, which reported that crude oil inventories had fallen by 11.12 million barrels in the period.
Crude futures were trading down at 11:24 a.m. in New York. Brent futures were trading at $105.72 per barrel—down $0.34 (-0.32%) on the day but up roughly $4 per barrel from this same time last week. In contrast, WTI was up on the day, by $1.92 per barrel (+2.02%) on Thursday morning at $97.01 , up about $7 per barrel since this time last week.
For total motor gasoline, the EIA reported that inventories increased by 3.5 million barrels, after gaining 400,000 barrels in the week prior. The most recent figures showed that average daily gasoline production averaged 9.2 million barrels. For middle distillates, inventories decreased by 2.5 million with production decreasing to an average of 5.2 million barrels daily. Distillate inventories are now 12% below the five-year average.
Total products supplied—a proxy for U.S. oil demand—averaged 21.1 million barrels per day over the last four weeks, up 2% compared to the same period last year. Gasoline demand averaged 8.7 million barrels per day over the last four weeks, with the distillate four-week average supplied at 4.0 million barrels—down 0.2% year over year.

title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
body:
Pengfei Tian, Maxwell L. Bileschi, Zoi Tsangalidou, Sukhdeep Singh and Lucy J. Colwell
New antibiotics are urgently needed to help with rising levels of antimicrobial resistance, but searching for new therapeutics is often a slow, labor-intensive process. With Google Antigravity, our agentic development platform, this process can now be made easier.
Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench that empowers biologists to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize promising targets quickly, compressing what used to be a fragmented search over multiple databases into a single session. It also helps researchers scan through millions of previously uncharacterized proteins in the UniProt database using ProtNLM, a model that predicts biological function from amino acid sequences.
This technical walkthrough shows how biologists used Google Antigravity to uncover a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate which has predicted activity against the pathogens involved in respiratory tract infections. The lead identified here is now undergoing wet-lab validation.
Rising antimicrobial resistance is one of the most pressing global health crises of our time and could result in an estimated 10 million annual deaths globally by 2050. To prevent this, we urgently need to discover novel therapeutics. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), particularly bacteriocins, offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics because they have naturally evolved to target fundamental vulnerabilities in competing bacteria, from cell envelopes to essential intracellular machinery, making it difficult for pathogens to develop resistance.
The exponential growth of genomic and metagenomic sequencing has populated global databases with billions of natural amino acid sequences. This pool of natural data has already produced globally used bacteriocins like Nisin, alongside recent genome-mined breakthroughs such as Darobactin, Dynobactin, and Lariocidin.
Many, however, remain locked within the unannotated "dark matter" of protein databases, with their function uncharacterized because they arenât similar to known proteins. For example, the world's leading public resource of protein sequence and functional information, UniProt , holds millions of sequences with unknown functionality, transferred directly from genome sequencing projects.
To bridge this gap, Google developed ProtNLM (Protein Natural Language Model) , a deep learning model trained to directly read the underlying evolutionary âgrammarâ of amino acid sequences. This allows the model to predict biological function directly from raw protein sequences, enriching millions of previously unnamed UniProt entries with high-confidence functional labels.
Overview of the ProtNLM pipeline translating raw amino acid sequences into natural-language biological annotations for unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries. The functional annotation scope of the system covers protein names, function comments, subcellular locations, and GO terms, in addition to keywords.
Scientific discovery is rarely a single step process; finding viable candidate proteins requires human intuition and iteration to incorporate new empirical evidence. Working in Antigravity, the researcher and AI agent begin by setting a focused biological goal: find and computationally validate novel AMPs in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae . During an interactive, multi-turn session the researcher steers the scientific strategy, deciding which questions to ask and what evidence to collect, while the agent handles the heavy lifting of cross-database orchestration, structural analysis, and literature synthesis.
The agent queries the database and filters millions of entries down to a handful of candidates worthy of attention. Here, the agent finds a bacteriocin (Uniprot ID: A0A0U0D591 ) with a length of 97 amino acids from the Lactococcin 972 family.
To verify the novelty of this discovery, the researcher guides the agent to interrogate the candidate against curated knowledge in Swiss-Prot via the EMBL-EBI NCBI-BLAST service and confirm this peptide has no meaningful sequence homolog among manually reviewed proteins.
The researcher steers the analysis towards structural evidence. The agent retrieves the candidateâs 3D model from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, querying it against experimentally determined structures to identify remote homologs, and superimposing the models to assess similarity. Here, the structural evidence corroborates ProtNLMâs prediction by showing the candidate's fold closely matches an experimentally determined bacteriocin. The structure viewer in Antigravity allows this structural analysis to be seamlessly performed in one place.
Reading the biological context around a gene:
The agent looks beyond the molecule itself to its genomic neighborhood, reasoning over whether the surrounding machinery supports the AMP hypothesis. Inspecting the flanking genes, it spots a revealing pattern: our previously uncharacterized candidate sits at the upstream of a tightly coupled operon, just 6 base pairs ahead of a ABC transporter permease and its potential partner ATP-binding protein, alongside another annotated bacteriocin and an XRE transcriptional regulator. This provides strong contextual evidence that it is part of a working bacteriocin system.
Building a mechanistic hypothesis from the literature :
By reviewing the existing literature, the agent proposes how the molecule might act and what pathogens it might act on. In this case, existing evidence suggests a mechanism of action targeting bacterial cell division, and a predicted potency spectrum spanning several drug-resistant pathogens.
Finally, the agent translates its in silico findings into an actionable bench protocol, spanning protein expression, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, target engagement, and in vitro toxicity testing, bridging the gap from computational prediction to wet-lab experiment. This step is already in motion: this candidate - along with several others discovered through the same pipeline - are now in wet-lab validation, where experimental results will provide the ultimate test of the agent's analysis.
The candidate we uncover in this walkthrough represents a biologically plausible lead backed by structural and genomic evidence but it still requires wet lab validation. What makes this meaningful is how dramatically it lowers the barrier to everyday biological workflows, turning days of fragmented database triage into a single collaborative session. While this session focused on a narrow amino acid window in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae , researchers can take the conversation in any direction, such as layering in new filtering criteria, exploring different sequence lengths, or targeting other priority pathogens. By broadening the search from human commensals to environmental microbes and beyond, scientists can guide the agent across UniProt to discover novel AMP candidates at scale.
A protein's 3D structure can help us understand its biological function. Examining a candidateâs predicted fold in space is key. To provide this end-to-end workflow in a single workspace, we are introducing the Biomolecular Structure Viewer , a 3D visualization tool embedded directly into Antigravity.
The researcher and agent work together over a shared visual state. As the agent retrieves structures from AlphaFold Database or the scientistâs own predictions, it can dynamically drive the viewer. For instance, it can highlight key functional regions to visually explain its hypotheses. Crucially, this awareness flows both ways: actions like highlighting specific residues or pinning notes directly onto a binding pocket are synchronised back to the agent. A researcher can simply mark a region of interest in 3D space and ask, for example, "How might this Î²-strand affect Lipid II binding?", allowing the agent to immediately reason over the exact structural context the scientist is looking at.
The Biomolecular Structure Viewer inside Antigravity showing the AlphaFold-predicted structure of the candidate bacteriocin, giving the researcher and agent a shared 3D canvas to inspect and annotate functional regions.
Historically, uncovering insights like those in the workflow demonstrated above required fragmented and specialised software: writing custom scripts to query databases, manually exporting files to 3D modelling programs, managing disconnected genomic tools and working with multiple experts to design the wet lab assays. Because wet-lab validation remains resource-intensive, narrowing the search space to only the highest-confidence leads upfront is critical. Using Google Antigravity allows researchers to navigate the vast biological search space efficiently while leveraging accurate protein function predictions from a domain-specific model.
Google Antigravity executes this end-to-end scientific reasoning in one place. This allows scientists to spend more time evaluating high-quality hypotheses, running experiments in the lab and solving research challenges.
We would like to acknowledge the contributions of the following team members: Maria Gabriela Cardoso, Victoria Johnston, Lexi Walker, Gena Hong, James King, Richard Green, Filip Radlinski, Artem Sobolev, Michael V. LeVine, Ruijie K. Zhang, Zachary Wu, Luca Schulz, Amy Danson, Tristan Oliver Kwan, Ryan Krueger, Oleg Kovalevskiy, Doug Fritz, Yunhan Xu, Sebastian Nowozin. Special thanks to Stephanie Lo from EMBL-EBI for her valuable feedback.

title: DOJ sues California over alleged non-citizens on voter rolls
body:
California officials say DOJ's attempt to intervene is legally baseless.
The Justice Department filed suit against California Thursday accusing the state of failing to review a list of alleged non-citizens that President Donald Trump's administration claims were sent mail-in ballots for next month's midterm election, according to court records.
The lawsuit comes just 48 hours after a top Justice Department official demanded California voting officials access a password-protected thumb drive that it said contained thousands of names of potential non-citizens believed to be on the state's voter registration list.
The letters from acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter were sent to the Los Angeles County Clerk and California Secretary of State on Tuesday, and gave a two-day deadline for the officials to confirm they were conducting a review and also moving to segregate any potential ballots that may have been returned from individuals whose names were on the thumb drive.
But officials in California characterized the request as legally baseless and a last-ditch effort by the Trump administration to intervene in the state's election process, despite facing more than two dozen straight losses in court over the past year in its efforts to compel states to hand over their voter rolls.
"The USDOJ's relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections," California Secretary of State Shirley Weber said. "California has robust state law requirements that only U.S. citizens can register to vote and that any non-eligible registrants are removed from the State’s voter rolls. My office and California election officials remain committed -- as always -- to ensuring a fair and smooth 2026 General Election."
The LA County Clerk separately said in a statement they would refuse to access contents of the thumb drive -- which was delivered to the office with a password attached on a sticky note -- "because doing so would conflict with established data privacy and information security protocols."
"We do not consider the device a secure medium," LA County Clerk Dean Logan said in the statement. "Additionally, the letter does not specify the number of individuals involved or describe the information contained in the records."
The Justice Department contends in its lawsuit that it is not requesting a "purge" of the state's voter rolls or to cancel votes, and instead is asking a judge to compel the state to set aside ballots that are from individuals on its list of alleged "likely" non-citizens.
The lawsuit also marks a strategic shift for the department by declining to involve officials from the Civil Rights Division, which has suffered an unbroken string of legal defeats seeking voter rolls from states based on federal civil rights statutes.
Instead, Thursday's lawsuit was filed by senior officials in the deputy attorney general's office and hinges on the federal supremacy clause -- arguing that the department has an obligation to intervene to prevent the state from permitting non-citizens to vote in federal elections.
But it's not ultimately clear how many of the names identified by DOJ as "likely" non-citizens on the voter rolls may prove to be legitimate.
In a previous exchange with officials in Nevada, for instance, the state conducted a review of 185 individuals that the Department of Homeland Security claimed were potential non-citizens on the voter rolls only to determine that every individual on the list was a lawful citizen.
The lawsuit marks the latest effort by the Trump administration to sow doubt on the integrity of the upcoming elections by pushing claims that non-citizens will seek to vote in mass numbers -- despite evidence and criminal prosecution levels showing such instances remain rare.

title: Trump Weighs Lifting Shadow Fleet Sanctions as Tanker Rates Soar
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
A U.S. military helicopter crew observes the sanctioned oil tanker Bertha during a right-of-visit boarding operation in the Indian Ocean. The interdiction marks the tenth vessel targeted in Washington’s expanding crackdown on shadow fleet oil shipments. Department of War photo
WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) – The Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
The discussions are happening days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump’s fellow Republicans in the US Senate.
Both Zelenskiy and the US senators called that move a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide Russia with revenue to keep funding its war in Ukraine.
The new talks center on the United States potentially allowing “legal oil” to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said. That means crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by Washington rather than Russian and Iranian oil, which are under punitive measures.
The goal is to get more refined products and crude out of the Gulf, the official said.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a video to the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh this week that the administration was talking about easing the sanctions on shadow fleet vessels in an effort to cut record freight rates that have cut into demand for US crude, according to Energy Aspects, a research group.
Bits of the talk were broadcast on social media, but Reuters was not able to obtain the full video or a transcript. The Department of Energy said it was not available.
Companies seeking to use the sanctioned vessels would have to apply to the US Treasury Department to use the vessels, the official said.
The Department of Energy said any move to relieve sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help Russia to move oil or oil products. The Treasury Department referred questions to the Department of Energy.
But Trump’s push to move Russian diesel to global markets quickly could put pressure on the departments to allow shipment via the vessels.
The White House did not respond immediately to a request for comment.
High oil and fuel prices are a risk for Trump in the November 3 midterm elections in which Republicans are hoping to maintain control of both chambers of Congress. He lifted the sanctions on Russian diesel through April 7.
Tanker freight rates have soared to record highs as the wars in Iran and Ukraine have stoked inflation and put US crude oil out of reach for Asian refiners, pushing them to ?seek alternatives from the Middle East and Latin America.
Energy Aspects said in a note to clients that easing the sanctions on the shadow fleet would not greatly impact freight rates but could allow more movement of oil in the Middle East.
Lifting the sanctions on the tankers that are mostly old and not well maintained is “unlikely to add meaningful mainstream fleet capacity overnight, especially as most tankers sanctioned over Russian or Venezuelan links have been actively trading over the past three months,” it said in the note.
Easing the restrictions “could make a small number of additional tankers available for certain (Strait of) Hormuz shuttle runs,” in the waterway between Iran and Oman.
Lifting the measures is unlikely to result in a broad easing of freight rates as ship insurers will still be bound by EU and UK regulations, maritime industry sources said.
(Reporting by Timothy Gardner and Jarrett Renshaw; Additional reporting by Jonathan Saul and Dmitry Zhdannikov in London; Editing by Jamie Freed)
